harness never rewrites history that has been pushed.

### 7.6 Stuck detection, breakers and budgets

**L4-IMP-008** A task is *stuck* when any holds: result `status: blocked`; two consecutive attempts with an identical
worktree diff hash; the same normalised failure fingerprint (`test id + error class`, or gate name + first error line
with numbers/paths normalised) `budgets.same_error_repeats` times; `max_task_attempts` reached **in one phase on one profile**
(red, green and the single phase of a chore task each have their own budget; `breaker.tripped` names the phase; with a later usable profile the phase moves first, L4-IMP-017). A stuck task without
questions triggers one short "state your blocking questions" call; if that yields none, the unit goes to `halted`
with a `breaker.tripped` event. A `blocked` result with no question (none given, or all dropped as malformed) still raises one ambiguous question made from its summary (L4-IMP-021). After a result failure (L4-IMP-021) the retry prompt MUST carry the reason of L4-IMP-021 and the `result values:` line (after normalization no result failure carries a validation error or an allowed-values list). When the harness checks of the step do not pass, a result `partial` or `failed` without
`questions` counts as a failed attempt and triggers the one-shot questions call [V 2×, spikes/03]; when they pass, the
step is accepted whatever the status (L4-IMP-005). When green ends `blocked`, the harness snapshots the worktree
to the WIP branch (L4-IMP-011) and resets the unit worktree to the red commit before recording the questions [I].

**L4-IMP-045** The harness SHALL identify a Python test by its file and qualified name (`test_x`, or `Class.test_x` for a method a
module-level class defines or inherits from a class of the same file), never by bare name. Its definition SHALL be every
statement binding the name in its defining scope, dumped without positions, docstrings normalised, so decorators,
parametrisation, requested fixtures and body count and layout does not. A second binding SHALL be a change.

**L4-IMP-046** The comparison SHALL include every binding of the file a pre-existing test reaches: the module names it reads (a local,
a nested parameter or a comprehension variable is none), the fixtures it requests or names in `usefixtures`,
transitively; every autouse fixture, `pytestmark`, module setup and `pytest_*` name; for a method, its class's
decorators, bases and non-test members. An import SHALL count as its source, so a widened import line is no change.

**L4-IMP-047** A test gone from its file SHALL count as moved only when a test that did not exist under that file and name before has
the same definition and the same closure (L4-IMP-046) at the later revision in a changed file; each such test SHALL
stand for at most one gone test. Every other gone test SHALL be deleted.

**L4-IMP-048** After `classify_red` accepts a red step, the harness SHALL compare every test that existed at the step's base in each
test file the step changed (L4-IMP-045..047). A changed, rebound, unparsable or deleted one SHALL fail the attempt with
`guard.test_tamper{phase: "red", rule: "pre-existing test", action: "rejected"}`, nothing committed, and a reason and
excerpt that name each test and say what to do. A `[test-infra]` task and the task's stale tests SHALL be exempt. This
comparison reads Python tests; one of another language that red changed, deleted or renamed fails in `classify_red` as
`red broke existing tests`, unless the reviewed text names it with `path::name` (L4-IMP-089), which excuses a change that
makes it fail at red.

**L4-IMP-082** Red changes in place the existing tests the reviewed text names. A red step SHALL be allowed to change the body,
decorators or parametrisation of a Python test that existed at its base when the task's reviewed text (the block of
L4-IMP-014: the unit folder has the digest an active plan froze, or the same block is on the base branch) or the text of
a criterion the task cites explicitly (its `_Requirements:_` line) names it, by `<path>::<name>` (or
`<path>::<Class>::<name>`, an optional `[...]` suffix ignored) or by a test name that exactly one test file at the base
defines (a name that two files define names none, and is kept with `named in <n> test files: write <path>::<name>`). A
criterion's text counts only when the source is an activated plan's digest or the unit folder is the same on the base
branch; a fix unit and a follow-up unit name nothing. At most 5 tests SHALL be named per task, the first in path and name
order (`more than 5 existing tests named` for the rest). A named test MUST NOT be deleted, bound again or left
unparsable by red: the step is rejected as in L4-IMP-048. A named test red changed is no regression of `classify_red` (it
may fail after red like a red test, and it is no new test), and after green it MUST pass like every red test. The red
prompt SHALL list the named tests under `# Existing tests this task changes in place`, and the red template's version
SHALL be 13. When the attempt is accepted, the harness SHALL record the named tests red changed as
`tests.superseded{task, tests, criteria: [], reason: "named_by_task", source}` (the stale tests keep their event, now with
`reason: "stale"`; from 0.4.43 the event has `language: "python"`), and the verifier SHALL allow and list them as it does
stale tests: `<id> (named by the task text, <source>)`; unlike a stale test, a named test an earlier red step added stays
among the tests the verifier expects. Every other existing test MUST stay protected. A test of a file that is not Python is
named with a backticked `path::name` and follows L4-IMP-089; the judge is told which named tests red changed (L4-VER-068).

**L4-IMP-049** Each top-level statement of a test file that is not a plain definition (`guards._defines_only`, where a fixture that is
not autouse also counts as plain) SHALL be a part of the pseudo-name `<module>`, which every test of the file reaches;
each such statement of a class body SHALL be a part of `<Class>`, which every test of the class reaches. An attribute,
`globals()` or `vars()` assignment, a `setattr` call or a class attribute that replaces a test SHALL be a change.

**L4-IMP-017** A task phase that fails on one profile moves to the next usable profile of the chain. The configuration SHALL have the key `implementer.escalate_after` (an integer, at least 0, default 2). `0` means that
no task moves.

A failed attempt is an attempt that the implementer loop counts against `max_task_attempts`: a harness check that does
not pass, a result failure of L4-IMP-021, or an agent run that ends with a status that is not `ok` and not a limit. It SHALL
count against the profile that ran it. A limit (L4-AVL-006), a silent stop (L4-IMP-087, a limit of kind `silent`), a `blocked` result, the question about a frozen test
that hangs, and a check held as inconclusive with a `harness` question (L4-IMP-063) MUST NOT count, and MUST NOT
start an escalation.

Every phase moves: red, green and single (a chore task). After a failed attempt of phase P of task T, in the unit's own task loop and in the tasks of a fix unit or a follow-up unit, the harness SHALL try to move P to another
profile when all of these hold:
- `escalate_after` is at least 1 and less than `implementer.max_task_attempts`;
- the current profile has failed at least `escalate_after` attempts of P of T;
- `roles.implementer` lists a profile after the current one.

The move SHALL select the first usable profile after the current one in `roles.implementer`, by profile name, with the
checks of every selection (serves, cool-down, the probe ladder or its cache, the login lock). Two profiles of the same
adapter, provider or vendor are two profiles. The selection:
- MUST NOT park the unit, MUST NOT record `availability.unavailable`, and MUST NOT cool down the profile that failed;
- MUST NOT take a profile when, with it added to the unit's implementer profiles, no profile of `roles.judges`, or of a
  non-empty `roles.verifier_agent`, would pass the independence rule of `verifier.independence` (L4-VER-001); with
  `verifier.independence: none` this check takes every profile;
- SHALL record `availability.selected{role: implementer, selected, escalated_from}` with no `fallback_from`, so that the
  new profile is an implementer profile of the unit for the judge veto.

When a profile is taken, the harness SHALL record `implementer.escalated{task, phase, from, to, failures, attempt}`
(`failures`: the failed attempts of `from` in P; `attempt`: the number of the next step). The next attempt of P SHALL
run on that profile in a fresh session. Its prompt SHALL carry a previous-attempt block that names the profile it
replaces and lists, oldest first, the reason of every failed attempt of P of T on earlier profiles, each cut at 1000
characters. When no profile is taken, the harness SHALL record `implementer.escalation_skipped{task, phase, from,
reason}`, and P SHALL stay on the current profile. The harness SHALL try again after each later failed attempt of
that profile.

Each profile SHALL have its own count of failed attempts per phase. The unit SHALL halt on `max_task_attempts` only
when the current profile has failed `max_task_attempts` attempts of P. The step key `<task>/<phase>/<attempt>` SHALL
count across profiles.

The task SHALL keep the profile for its later phases in that run. The next task, and every task of a later run, SHALL
start on the run's selected profile. The run's selected profile, and the profile that the fix loop reads, MUST NOT
change. A limit on a step of the moved profile SHALL cool that profile (not the run's), and the task SHALL go on as
after any limit (L4-AVL-006).

The tasks of a fix unit move like those of the unit's own loop (0.4.40, change 88): the fix loop asks the orchestrator's selection step, the task's child workbench is rebuilt on the chosen profile with the baselines carried over and the previous-attempt block, the task's own profile ends with the task (also when it raises), and the next task of the fix unit starts on the run's selected profile again. A single step counts its attempts with the green ones (its step keys are `<task>/single/<n>`), and failures of earlier runs move a chore of a follow-up unit before its first attempt (L4-IMP-075). A held check, a `blocked` result and a limit never count and never start a move. Without the orchestrator's selection step in the hook context, a fix unit's task stays on its profile.

**A fix chore that changed nothing is not done (0.4.45).** A fix chore (a `[chore]` task of a fix unit, `run_single` with
kind `fix`) attempt in which a guard put back every edit and no other file changed SHALL fail with `nothing changed: the
guard put back every edit (<paths>)`, and its changes are discarded. A path counts as put back when the test-path freeze
or the frozen-file restore put it back, or when any other guard of the step wrote a `guard.*` note for it (a protected
path, a runner configuration, a link); the ledger, `tasks.md` and held files do not count as a change. A chore for a CI
job (ci-evidence D11, D12: `chore_ci_job`) SHALL keep its rule and commit the put-back chore, because `ci_not_fixed` reads
it; a retake (`retake`) SHALL take `_already_done` as the refactor and test chores do; a step that edited nothing at all
keeps today's rule. [V, a consumer's fix task was ticked done after its only edit, to a frozen test, was put back, in a
commit of `tasks.md` and the ledger alone]

**L4-IMP-018** A person sees which profiles ran a task and why it moved. `task.attempt_failed` SHALL carry `profile`, and its `attempt` SHALL be the step's attempt number. `breaker.tripped`
for `max_task_attempts` SHALL carry `profiles`, a list of `{profile, failures}` in the order the profiles ran the
phase; `attempts` SHALL stay the failed attempts of the phase. When two or more profiles ran the phase, the halt
detail SHALL be `task <k>: max_task_attempts (<n>) reached in <phase> on <p1> (<f1>), <p2> (<f2>); last failure:
<reason>`. With one profile it MUST stay as before.

The progress log SHALL print:
- for `implementer.escalated`: `task <k> <phase>: escalated from <from> to <to> after <n> failed attempts`;
- for `implementer.escalation_skipped`, as a warning: `task <k> <phase>: <from> failed <n> attempts; no later profile
  can take it (<reason>); it stays on <from>`;
- for `task.attempt_failed` with `profile`: `task <k> <phase> attempt <n> failed on <profile>: <reason>`;
- for `breaker.tripped` with two or more profiles: `halted: max_task_attempts (task <k>: <p1> <f1>, <p2> <f2>)`;
- for `availability.selected` with `escalated_from`: the selection line ending `→ selected, escalated from <from>`.

An event without the new fields SHALL print as before.

The doctor SHALL have the check CFG-009 (warn). It SHALL fail when `roles.implementer` has two or more profiles and
`implementer.escalate_after` is neither 0 nor less than `implementer.max_task_attempts`, and when two profiles of
`roles.implementer` have the same adapter and the same model. Each failure names the keys or the profiles, and the fix
line says what to set. A chain of one profile SHALL pass.

**L4-IMP-009** Per-unit budgets MUST be enforced by the harness itself from adapter-reported usage (Claude's
`--max-budget-usd` does not count cost restored on `--resume` [V, research/06]): `max_iterations_per_unit`,
`max_cost_usd_per_unit`, `no_progress_iterations` (no task newly done, unchanged cumulative diff hash), oscillation (a
diff hash recurring A→B→A). Any breach → `halted`, exit 13. Per-run cost for claude-code = `total_cost_usd` − the last
total recorded for that `session_id` (the value is session-cumulative on `--resume` [V, spikes/01: 0.0845 → 0.0955]).
OpenCode `step_finish.cost` is nominal (reported for unbilled free-tier calls; `0` for Zen) [V, spikes/02]. Codex
reports tokens only [V, spikes/03]. Budgets for opencode and codex profiles MUST bound iterations and wall time, and
codex budgets are token or plan-window budgets.

**L4-IMP-013** Budgets stay ledger-counted and cannot be reset by dispatch inputs. `l4 resume` (members only) records
`unit.resumed{by, reason}`, which resets the breaker counters (`no_progress`, `same_error`, oscillation) and the
verifier's consecutive-internal-error counter, and optionally
`budget.extended{iterations, cost_usd, fix_rounds, by, reason}`; the state fold adds extensions to the configured
limits. A unit halted on a budget, or escalated after `max_fix_rounds`, therefore needs an explicit extension to
continue — `l4 resume` without one is refused with a message naming the exhausted budget. The fix-round extension is built
(M1.13): `--extend-fix-rounds N` records `budget.extended{fix_rounds: N}` before `unit.resumed`, the fold sums it
(`UnitState.fix_rounds_extra`) and the verifier's limit is `verifier.max_fix_rounds` plus that sum; the extension is never
reset by a later resume. An escalated unit that still has rounds left (three verifier errors, a fix unit that could not be
created) resumes without one, and the unit goes back to `verifying`. `--extend-iterations` and `--extend-cost` are still
refused. A member's `l4:resume` label is the extension for an escalated unit, fixed at one round (L4-CI-004).
The feedback-round extension is built the same way (L4-FBK-006): `--extend-feedback-rounds N` records
`budget.extended{feedback_rounds: N}` before `unit.resumed`, the fold sums it (`UnitState.feedback_rounds_extra`) and the
feedback limit is `feedback.max_rounds` plus that sum. A unit escalated at the feedback limit
(`phase.changed{reason: "feedback_rounds_exhausted"}`) needs it, and `l4 resume` without it is refused with a message
naming `feedback.max_rounds`; a fix-round extension does not release it, and the label gives it one feedback round instead
of a fix round.

### 7.7 Sessions, WIP and time budget

**L4-IMP-010** The adapter session id MUST be persisted to the ledger as soon as it is known (preset when the CLI
allows it). On restart, the same session is resumed only if the same adapter is selected, `implementer.session_resume`
permits, and the session store exists; otherwise a fresh session starts with a "previous attempt" section (last
checkpoint commit, WIP diff summary, last failure). [V, spikes/01: the preset `--session-id` was honoured 8/8, and
`--resume` keeps the id and returns `structured_output`; resume costs about $0.01–0.02 on Sonnet. Codex
`exec resume` stays U.]

**L4-IMP-011** While an agent runs, the harness MUST snapshot the worktree every `wip_snapshot_interval` into a commit
built from a temporary index and push it to the WIP branch (never the unit branch), with the platform's
non-triggering push mode (§16).

**L4-IMP-012** The harness MUST compute a soft deadline (`ci.time_budget` − `soft_deadline_margin`; `auto` uses 6 h
for GitHub-hosted, 3 h for GitLab.com-hosted runners [V], the job's own timeout otherwise). It MUST NOT start a phase
whose estimate exceeds the remaining time, MUST send SIGINT (not SIGTERM — Claude exits 143 mid-turn on SIGTERM [V])
to a running agent at the soft deadline, push the WIP snapshot and ledger, dispatch a continuation (§16.4) and exit 10.

*Implemented now:* the check between units, and inside a unit the job's start, the check before each step, the stop, the
hand-back, the continuation and the halt of a step that never fits (L4-IMP-066 to L4-IMP-071, L4-IMP-075). The deadline
counts from the job's start: `L4_JOB_STARTED_AT` (the first step `job start` of the GitHub templates), else GitLab's
`CI_JOB_STARTED_AT`, else the start of the run. Before each unit after the first, `l4 run` computes the time left to the
soft deadline (`CI_JOB_TIMEOUT` for `auto` on GitLab; `L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, which the GitHub template sets from the
job's `timeout-minutes`, on GitHub, L4-GHP-003; `ci.time_budget` otherwise) and starts no unit when none is left or when
the longest unit it has already run would not fit; the units left are listed in `outcome.json` as `not started: soft
deadline (…)`, untouched, and the run exits 10 (or a more severe code of a unit). Before each implementer step and each
verification round the run compares the time left with the step's estimate (`step.timed` records, at least 10 minutes),
and a step that does not fit is not started. At the soft deadline every agent, CLI judge and gate that the unit's run
has running gets SIGINT, then SIGKILL after 5 s; the step is handed back with `deadline.reached`, no attempt counted and
no phase change, the ledger and the unit branch are pushed, `run.finished` records `reason: soft deadline: …`, the run
exits 10 and one continuation follows. A step stopped twice halts the unit with `deadline_repeated`. With no known
budget every unit and step runs. *Still to do:* the push of the WIP snapshot (M2, with fencing): the work of a stopped
step is lost, and the next run does the step again.

---


**L4-IMP-023** A heartbeat line shows that an implementer agent works.

The configuration SHALL have the key `implementer.heartbeat` (a duration or `0`, default `2m`). A value other than `0`
MUST be at least `30s`. `0` turns the heartbeat off.

While an implementer agent step runs, the harness SHALL log one INFO line on the `l4` logger every
`implementer.heartbeat`, starting one interval after the agent starts. The line SHALL have the form of the progress
trace (`<unit> [<fix unit>] <message>`) with the message
`task <k> <phase> attempt <n>: <profile> working <elapsed>, <c> tool calls, last activity <t> ago`, where `<c>` is the
count of the stream reader (L4-FAC-012) and `<t>` the time since the agent's last stdout line. When the stream shows
open tool calls, the line SHALL end with `, <m> tool call(s) open for <t>`, where `<t>` is the age of the oldest open
call. For a profile whose adapter has no stream reader (`command`), the message SHALL be
`task <k> <phase> attempt <n>: <profile> working <elapsed>`. Times SHALL be written as `<s>s` under one minute,
`<m>m` under one hour, else `<h>h <m>m`.

The heartbeat MUST NOT be a ledger event, and the line MUST NOT hold text from the agent's stream: only the task, the
phase, the attempt, the profile name, counts and times. An error in the heartbeat MUST NOT end or change the agent
step. The `step.started` progress line SHALL be printed at INFO.

**L4-IMP-024** An idle agent is stopped with a clear reason, and a step that reaches its time limit says so.

The configuration SHALL have the key `implementer.idle_timeout` (a duration or `0`, default `10m`). A value other than
`0` MUST be at least `1m`. `0` turns the idle watchdog off. The key SHALL replace the fixed stall limit of the
implementer step: the harness MUST NOT have a second idle threshold for it.

An implementer agent is idle when its stdout has had no line for `implementer.idle_timeout` and its stream reader
(L4-FAC-012) shows no open tool call. The harness SHALL then send SIGINT to the agent's process group, and SIGKILL to
the group when it still runs 5 seconds later, also when the agent prints lines in those 5 seconds. The run's status
stays `timeout`. The harness MUST NOT use the run's
`interrupt` event for this, which is the soft deadline's and gives the status `cancelled`.

The harness SHALL then record `agent.idle{task, phase, attempt, profile, silent_s, tool_calls, silent, reason?}` before
`agent.finished` (`silent` is true for a silent stop, L4-IMP-087, and false otherwise; `reason` is set when the stop was
the task's second silent stop), and the attempt SHALL fail with the reason `the agent showed no activity for <idle_timeout>
(implementer.idle_timeout), so L4 stopped it`, except for a silent stop, which is a limit of its profile and no attempt
(L4-IMP-087). An attempt that ends with status `timeout` without the idle mark SHALL
fail with `the agent step reached its time limit (<limit>)`, where the limit is the step's wall-clock limit (30m).
Both are failed attempts as before, but for a silent stop: they count against the profile for the escalation
(L4-IMP-017) and against `implementer.max_task_attempts`, and they are not limits (no cool-down). An idle stop with no
tool call and more than one implementer profile is a silent stop and is not counted. The progress log SHALL print
`agent.idle` at WARNING as `task <k> <phase> attempt <n>: no activity from <profile> for <idle_timeout>; L4 stopped it
(implementer.idle_timeout)`, with the suffix `; no tool call was made, so it is a limit of the profile, not a failed
attempt` for a silent stop and `; <reason>, so it counts as a failed attempt` for the task's second.

While a tool call is open in the stream, the idle clock MUST NOT stop the agent; the step's wall-clock limit still
applies.

**L4-IMP-025** The modules a test imports are found under every import root.

The harness SHALL look up the modules a test imports under these import roots: the repository root, `src`, every
directory named `src`, and every directory that holds a `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py` or `setup.cfg` together with that
directory's `src`. The lookup serves the zero-value run of the pre-satisfied criteria (L4-IMP-002), the head stubs of
run (b), the audit sampling (step 4a) and the proof of tests that people or a test chore wrote (step 4). The
directories SHALL come from git's tracked files and its untracked files that are not ignored, so an ignored virtual
environment is not searched. A dotted name SHALL resolve to `<root>/<dotted as path>.py` and
`<root>/<dotted as path>/__init__.py` under every root where that file exists with the exact case. Every match SHALL
be varied: Python takes the first one on its path, which the harness cannot know, and varying a copy the test does not
import changes nothing. A match under the test globs SHALL NOT be varied. A repository whose modules sit under the root
or `src` gets the same modules as before. [V: a consumer repository's uv workspace keeps each member's code under
`packages/<name>/src/<namespace>/<name>/`, and before this rule no zero-value run there ever had a module to vary.]

**L4-IMP-026** The zero-value variant of a generator or a context manager still behaves as one.

A function decorated with `contextmanager` or `asynccontextmanager` (under any module name) SHALL get the zero-value
body `yield <the zero value of T>` for its `Iterator[T]` or `Generator[T, …]` annotation (`yield None` without one), so
that `with f() as x:` enters, `x` is the zero value, and an exception of the block still reaches the caller. Any other
function whose own body has a `yield` SHALL get an empty generator. A function annotated to return
`AbstractContextManager` or `ContextManager` (or their async forms) SHALL return `contextlib.nullcontext()`, and one
annotated `Iterator`, `Iterable` or `Generator` SHALL return an empty iterator. The rule holds for a red stub, which
has no `yield`: the decorator and the annotation decide. The `vacuous` message SHALL tell how to test a context
manager: assert on what it yields, or on its effects after the block. [V: a consumer repository's unit halted after
five red attempts on a `@contextmanager` stub whose zero-value variant `return None` made every `with` raise a
`TypeError` before the test body ran, so no test could fail by assertion.]

**L4-IMP-060** A variant run is judged against the real run. Every variant run (run (b), the pre-satisfied zero-value
run, the base run, `test-at-red`, the audit's run and the extra proofs' runs) SHALL pass
`--continue-on-collection-errors` and SHALL be judged per test against the real run: a test that failed by assertion
is a proof; one that passed, or failed by another error, is none; one the run did not run (absent from the report, or
skipped only there), and every test of a run with no report or no executed test, is inconclusive. A criterion is
confirmed when any of its tests is a proof, inconclusive when none is and any is inconclusive, and not discriminating
only when every one of its tests ran and none is a proof. A reason SHALL quote the first `E` line when there is one,
cut at 300 characters; the raw text is redacted first and cut after, so no prefix of a secret survives.
In a zero-value run (the pre-satisfied run, run (b) and the test chore's run; not the base run, which only confirms) a test the unit's own
files made unrunnable is **no proof**, never inconclusive, as a setup assertion in the unit's own fixture is a proof (L4-IMP-002): a test
that skipped only there, one absent because its module's collection error failed at a statement of the unit's own test module that is not an
import (whatever the deepest frame: a pre-existing helper the agent's module calls raised), and one whose module collected but lost the id (a `parametrize` over a production answer). Only a failing import statement of the
own test module (a production module that failed to import) leaves a test inconclusive. Without this rule an agent could turn "not discriminating" into a held task, and a person's
`accept` into a pass, with a test that skips itself on the zero answer. `run_with_code_of` returns the gate result, so "no test" and "no report" differ.
[V: a consumer repository, harness 0.4.14, task 3.1: the pre-satisfied run ended `Interrupted: 45 errors during
collection` and ran 0 tests, and the message said "its tests still pass"; the base run stopped at the first collection
error; nine red attempts on four profiles halted the unit.]

**L4-IMP-061** Zeroing keeps what imports need. When the harness zeroes every public function, one annotated to return
`Callable` or `type` (also `X | None` or `Optional[X]` of them, also as a string) SHALL keep its body only when a module of the varied set
applies it at import time, as a decorator or decorator factory or by a call in a module-level or class-level statement: the zero value of a
decorator factory is not a value a test can meet, it breaks the import of a module that applies the decorator while its class body runs. A
callable-returning function that nothing applies at import is zeroed like any other, so an honest test of it keeps its proof, and a test that failed by assertion in ANY pass counts: while a candidate has no proof and the first pass kept something by annotation, one more pass keeps nothing by annotation and counts for proofs only (a decorator factory under test). When a zero-value run leaves a candidate inconclusive, the harness SHALL keep the zeroed functions
called on the failing lines of the run's new collection errors and of setup assertions outside the unit's files, and those called by the
module-level statements of a production or pre-existing test-support module whose import failed (`_CFG = load()` above `RATE = _CFG["rate"]`; never the unit's own files), and run again: at most twice, only when a new function is kept, at most 50 functions, recording `zero.kept{gate, rerun,
cause, functions}`. [V: the same halt: `@telemetry.traced("…")` applied in a class body received `None`:
`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable`.]

**L4-IMP-062** A dependency check is held for a person, never passed. A pre-satisfied criterion whose every candidate test is *dependency only* (its function uses no name
bound to a repository module, no definition of its file beyond a constant, no fixture beyond pytest's built-ins and its own `parametrize`, no code reached by a string
(`importorskip`, `import_module`, `__import__`, `getfixturevalue`, `sys.modules`), and reads a dependency's version with a literal name) SHALL be inconclusive with the reason
"its tests import no project module: the zero-value check cannot judge them", with no variant run: the task is held with a `harness` question (L4-IMP-063) and nothing is ever
recorded `via: not_applicable` (old ledgers that carry it are still read). A person may `accept`; an agent only where `clarifier.answer_by_agents` is true. The classifier only chooses the message: any other test
with no project import stays refuted (`not discriminating`) as on 0.4.15, so neither outcome is a pass and its precision is no safety rule. [V: a consumer repository, task 3.1: a test that pins
a dependency's version passes on the zero values and at the base alike; round-3 review: no static rule on the test's shape could tell a pin from `version(x) != ""`.]

**L4-IMP-063** An inconclusive check holds the task with a harness question. When every unconfirmed criterion of a red
step (the pre-satisfied check, or run (b)), or every corrected test of `test-at-red`, is inconclusive, the harness SHALL
discard the step's changes, record `check.inconclusive{task, phase, check, criteria, tests, reason, runs, kept,
question}`, raise one question of the kind `harness` that blocks the task (`question.raised{id, task, kind: harness,
title, check, criteria, tests}`), and end the task `blocked`: no attempt is counted and no profile escalates
(L4-IMP-017). The unit goes to `awaiting_human` (exit 11; through `clarifying` when a clarifier runs, which never takes
a harness question), and a delivery plan waits on it without chaining a run (L4-YOLO-012). The answer is `accept` or
`retry` (L4-QMD-004). `accept` lets the next run, which replays the held step (L4-IMP-065: the harness saved the step's changes before it discarded
them, and no agent runs for the replay), count those criteria when the same
check is inconclusive again for criteria the question names (read from its `question.raised` event, whose `tests` the candidates of
the criterion must be among: an answer given about one test does not carry a later different test, which is why the step is replayed
and not written again; and from a `question.answered` event of
a person or, under `clarifier.answer_by_agents`, an agent, with the digest of the answer): the proof is `pre_satisfied` (run (b): `zero_value`)
with `via: human_override` (`agent_override` for an agent's answer, recorded `question.answered{by: agent}`), `question` and
`answer_sha256`, and `check.accepted{task, check, question, answer_sha256, by, criteria | tests}` and `criterion.pre_satisfied{via}` are recorded; a conclusive result always wins over
the answer, and an override is never an earlier red's evidence. `retry` runs the check again, and its note reaches the
agent as any answer does. A criterion that a run shows to be not discriminating still fails the attempt (L4-IMP-002).
The discrimination check of a test chore (`check: tests`) that cannot decide holds the chore the same way. [V: the halted unit above would have
waited here instead of spending nine attempts.]

**L4-IMP-064** The evidence of a variant run reaches the ledger and the console. `gate.finished` of a test gate that
failed with no report, no executed test or a collection error, and `task.attempt_failed`, SHALL carry `excerpt`: the `E`
lines and the deepest repository location of the failure, at most 600 characters, redacted by the run's redactor before it is cut (a cut
inside a secret would leave a prefix the redactor cannot see), never read into a prompt; `gate.finished` carries `collection_errors` whenever there is a report. The gate line of a run that
executed no test SHALL NOT say `(expected: zero values must fail)`, and the artefacts line SHALL say `not uploaded` when
`ci.upload_artifacts` is false in GitHub Actions, and SHALL say `(CI: job artifacts)` only in a CI job (`in_ci_job`, L4-CLI-004;
a local run names its agent and gate directories only; 0.4.44, change 101). [V: the same consumer sets `ci.upload_artifacts: false`, so no gate log
was kept, the ledger held only a log path (`excerpt_lines: 0`), and the console still printed `(CI: job artifacts)`.]

**L4-IMP-084** The zero-value run zeroes the stubs HEAD holds with red's own. When a red step has open criteria, its zero-value run
(run (b)) SHALL zero both the stubs red added and the modules the tests import that hold a `raise NotImplementedError`
stub at HEAD (an earlier task's leftover), and no longer the stubs of HEAD only when red added none.

**L4-IMP-085** A vacuous criterion whose tests only error is told what to stub. For a vacuous criterion all of whose tests errored
in the zero-value run, the red failure text SHALL name the error and the remedy instead of the generic sentence, by the
first rule that matches: a module the tests cannot import (`its tests cannot import <m>: create it in this red step with
signature-only stubs (a body that is only raise NotImplementedError), and the harness answers them with zero values`),
a `NotImplementedError` raised at a worktree file and line (`its tests stop with NotImplementedError at <path>:<line>:
that body is not a stub the zero-value run answers; make it one (only raise NotImplementedError) or stub what the tests
call in this red step`), or an `AttributeError` for a missing attribute (`its tests stop with AttributeError (<a>): add
<a> as a signature-only stub in this red step`). Other errors SHALL keep the current text.

**L4-IMP-086** The replay guard puts a base path back through the folder's descriptor. When the replay guard puts back a path
that is not part of the saved patch and that existed at the step base, it SHALL write the base entry through the folder's
file descriptor, as it writes the patch's paths: a regular file streamed from the base blob with its executable bit, a
link with the target the base blob holds. It SHALL set the index entry with an index-only command (`git update-index
--add --cacheinfo`). The guard MUST NOT run a git command that writes the work tree by path name (`checkout`, `restore`,
`reset --hard`, `stash`, `clean`). A base entry that is neither a regular file nor a link SHALL fail the step as an
attempt with `the replayed step could not be put back to its saved patch (<where>): <path> is a <kind> at the base`.

**L4-IMP-087** A silent implementer step is a limit of its profile, not a failed attempt. An implementer step that the idle
watchdog stops (L4-IMP-024) while its stream reader has seen no tool call, and while `roles.implementer` lists more than one
profile, SHALL be a *silent stop*: the run's status is `timeout`, the idle mark is set, a stream reader ran and counted 0 tool
calls. A silent stop SHALL be handled as a limit of kind `silent` (L4-AVL-006): `availability.limit{kind: silent}`, a
cool-down of the profile for `availability.default_cooldown` (L4-AVL-003), its cached hello cleared (L4-AVL-005),
`availability.fallback{reason: silent}`, the run's selected profile moved when the silent one was the run's, the step's
uncommitted work discarded (a red commit stays), and the task goes on on the next usable profile in a new session whose
previous-attempt note says the profile went silent (`no output for <implementer.idle_timeout>`); with no usable profile left
the unit waits for capacity (L4-AVL-007). It MUST NOT count: no `task.attempt_failed`, nothing toward
`implementer.escalate_after` or `implementer.max_task_attempts` (L4-IMP-017). A limit that the adapter itself found on the run
is kept as it is and the silent signal is made only when there is none. Token counts MUST NOT decide it: most adapters read
usage only from their final event, so any killed run reads 0 in and 0 out. A silent escalated profile cools, and the task
goes on on the next usable one. A fix task moves once, as for a limit; a second limit in the same fix task parks the unit and
the profile that hit it cools too (`Factory.cool_limited`, for any limit kind), so the next run does not select it again.
Judges and the delegate skip a cooling profile, as for any limit. A task's second silent stop (an earlier
`agent.idle{silent: true}` of the same task and fix unit in the task's window, whatever the profile and the run; the window is
the one that counts attempts, so a checkpoint of the task, a retry, a resume or a restart ends it) MUST count as a failed
attempt (`agent.idle{silent: false, reason: "silent: already once for this task"}`), so a chain whose profiles all go silent
halts on `max_task_attempts` (exit 13) and does not park run after run. An idle stop after at least one tool call, a step that
reaches its time limit, `implementer.idle_timeout: 0`, the deadline's cancel and every idle stop of a chain with a single
profile SHALL count as before. Risk (named, accepted): an agent whose first tool call runs, or which thinks, for longer than
`implementer.idle_timeout` with nothing printed reads as silent; OpenCode (1.x and 2.x share the stream reader) reports a tool
call only when the call ends, so a first call longer than `idle_timeout` reads as silent there, at the cost of one cool-down of
that profile and a move, at most once per task. [V, a consumer's run of 2026-10-29: seven implementer steps in a row on a
reachable free profile ended by the idle watchdog with no tool call, six with 0 tokens, each after 10 minutes, and every task
started on that profile again]

**L4-IMP-088** A baseline reuses the green gate run of the same tree. Within one job, the baseline of a task (the base report
of red check 4 and of green (b), L4-IMP-002) SHALL be the report of the run's last accepted green test gate, with neither
`gates.setup` nor the gate run again, when the gate's digest (sha256 of the command, the reports, the format, `gates.timeout`,
the per-test timeout, the network setting and the sandbox mode) is the same and the tree that green gate tested differs from
the base's tree only in the unit's ledger, its `tasks.md` and its files under `.l4/held/`; it SHALL record
`gate.reused{name: baseline, from: test, task, source_sha, tree}`. The tree is the worktree as git sees it before the gate (a
temporary index honouring the excluded config), not the green commit, because a gate can write tracked files. The harness MUST
keep the run only after an accepted green (the single step of a chore included) whose report exists and has no collection
error, and MUST NOT keep it when the gate ran with an extra environment (a fix unit's coverage run) or a `guard.violation`,
`env.rebuilt` or `held.replay_restored` was recorded between the mark and the keep. The keep is in memory: an agent step, a
discard and a rebuilt workbench (an escalation or a fall-back) end it, and a new job starts without one, so the first baseline
of a job is always measured. The step keys (L4-STA-003), `resume_red`, the static-gate baselines and the verifier's own base
measurement are unchanged. Residual risk (named, accepted): the tree compared is what git sees; ignored and excluded files and
git-derived state (a version taken from `git describe`, setuptools-scm or hatch-vcs, which differs because the green gate ran
with `HEAD` at the red commit) are outside it, so a test whose outcome depends on them may see a different result at the next
base than the reused report says. [V, a consumer's unit of 9 tasks, gate about 65 s: every baseline after the first ran right
after the previous green gate on the same code, 8 to 9 minutes per unit]

**L4-IMP-089 Red changes in place a named test of any language.** A backticked `path::name` in a task's reviewed text (the
block of L4-IMP-014 and its sources, as for L4-IMP-082), where `path` is a tracked regular file, not a symlink and not a
Python file, that matches `tdd.test_globs` and no support or ignore glob, SHALL name an existing test when the base report
has exactly one id that `test_locate.file_of_id` maps to `path` and whose test name equals `name` or ends with it after
` > ` (the text is split at the first `::`; a name may hold spaces and punctuation). A name that matches no test or more
than one, whose lines `test_locate.window()` cannot find (a test a `.each` generates), or whose id `file_of_id` does not map
(a Go id), SHALL name nothing: it is kept with a reason (`no test of that name in the base report`, `more than one test
matches`, `the lines of the test are not found`), recorded as `named_tests.kept{task, token, reason}` and listed in the red
prompt with the other names the text used that opened nothing; the red prompt lists the named tests and the kept names as
data blocks of one bounded line each. The cap of 5 named tests of L4-IMP-082 counts both kinds. Before the agent step of each
red attempt whose reviewed text names a test (of either kind), the harness SHALL record `named_tests.found{task, tests,
source}`, the tests as the red prompt lists them. `classify_red` SHALL excuse a named id that is still in the red report and
that red changed: its own lines (`window()`) differ between the base and red, or they are the same, the test fails at red,
and its file's shared lines differ (`test_locate.outside_tests`: the file's lines in no `window()` of the base report's tests
of that file at the base, of the red report's at red, blank lines dropped; a constant, fixture or helper of the file that
the test reads). Such a test MUST fail at red like a new red test, by an assertion or `NotImplementedError` (with the gate's
failure kinds on) and not by a hang or a time-out. One whose own lines changed and that passes at red, or one that fails
otherwise, fails the attempt (`a test the task names was changed but does not fail at red: <id>`); one whose own lines are
the same and that passes is not changed (nothing is excused, recorded or failed, so a red step that only adds tests or
imports to the file is not affected); and one that red deleted, renamed or that is gone from the report fails it as `red
broke existing tests`. A named test that fails at red while red changed neither its lines nor its file's shared lines is
`red broke existing tests`, and the reason adds `; the task names <id>, but red changed neither its lines nor the lines of
its file outside the tests: change the test, or a constant or helper of its own file that it reads`. A
changed named test does not count as a new test: the criteria still need one (`no new test: the test the task names does not
count as a new test: add the new test the criterion needs as well`), and a task whose red changed one SHALL NOT end as
already satisfied. The harness SHALL record `tests.superseded{task, tests, criteria: [], reason: "named_by_task", source,
language}` (the Python event has `language: "python"`) and the verifier SHALL treat the ids as L4-IMP-082 says. Green stays
closed: it SHALL NOT open a pre-existing test file in any language, a task text that names the file with no test opens
nothing, and the kept reasons of L4-IMP-014 are unchanged. Step 1 SHALL still run every other test of the file at its base
version and excuse only the ids that `tests.superseded` records; it folds a recorded id at `[` only for a Python id (an
event with no `language`, or `python`, whose name ends in a pytest parameter), and compares the ids of other languages,
whose names may hold brackets, exactly. Limits: a test whose expected value lives in another file (a shared fixture module)
is not changed by an edit of that file, so red must change the test or its own file; a shared-lines change is excused only
for the named test, while the file's other tests are protected by the regression check and by step 1 only (a Python test's
module definitions are read by L4-IMP-046's closure instead). [V, a consumer's later unit had to change an earlier unit's
merged TypeScript test: red could not, and green may not, so the task cost a question round and a run; from 0.4.47 the
shared lines count, because a later unit of the same consumer halted on `max_task_attempts` after five attempts that each
extended the module-level constant the reviewed task text named, outside the test's own lines]

**L4-IMP-090 A fix chore for a browser-test finding runs the build and the browser tests.** A fix chore (a `[chore]` task
of a fix unit, kind `fix`) whose task holds an *e2e finding* SHALL, when `gates.e2e` is configured and after the unit's
test gate passed, run `gates.build` (when it is configured; `gates.setup` ran before the step) and then the e2e gate
(`run_e2e`, name `e2e-chore`). An e2e finding is `e2e gate failed` (known from its title, whatever the stored verdict
says), or a `new tests failed` or `new tests errored` finding that names ids the parent round recorded under the e2e gate
(L4-VER-069; the round is the `verify_round` of the `fix.spawned` event of this fix unit in the parent's ledger, its
verdict read from the parent's folder). The attempt SHALL fail, naming the tests, unless: (a) for a task that holds `e2e
gate failed`, the e2e gate passes, judged whole as step 3 judges it (a gate that exits 1 for another reason, a collection
error, a missing report or a run of no test is a failure); (b) every id of the finding is in the report and passed (the ids
the round recorded; all of the round's failing e2e ids when the finding's list is cut or does not match whole); and (c) no
e2e test that passed in the parent round fails, errors or is missing from the report now (the parent's `tests`, with its
`e2e_tests` telling which are browser tests; a verdict without that key only checks the tests the report holds). A build
that fails is `gates.build failed before the e2e gate: …`. A server that is not ready SHALL fail the attempt with `the
e2e server was not ready (see <log name>)` and the last 2,000 characters of its log, redacted, as the excerpt, and SHALL
NOT be an error of the run. The ids of the finding's text are matched whole against the recorded ids (an id may hold a
comma), never split. A task with only a `new tests …` finding for which the round names no e2e failure runs no e2e gate.
The gate runs are not part of the chore: whatever they write into the tree (build output, `test-results/`, a snapshot
baseline, a lock file the build rewrote) is not committed. A path that is new since before the runs goes back to the base, a
path the step had edited gets the step's content back (files up to 1 MB are kept; a larger one is fingerprinted, not read),
and the test-path freeze runs once more; a symbolic link that a gate planted is removed first and recorded as a planted
link (L4-SEC-020, L4-SEC-021), which stops the unit like any other, and every write goes through `write_inside`. The test
gate's rules stay. [V, a consumer's second fix task changed correct product code (a status code the design fixes) to suit a
broken browser test, and nothing checked it against the browser tests; the unit's test gate cannot see them]

**L4-IMP-091 A repair step proposes an edit of the failing tests only, and only a person's accept applies it.** A candidate is a failing test of a round that (all of): sits in a file that matches `tdd.test_globs` and no
`tdd.test_support_globs` glob, is a Python file, is bound once in it, was first added by a harness commit that carries
`L4-TDD: red` of this unit (absent at the unit's base, `unit_base`, which for a fix unit is its parent's) and has not
been changed by a person's commit since (its facts and what it uses in the file, `tamper.facts_of`, are as the red
commit left them; a file taken out and added again is no candidate), failed with a kind other than `assertion` or
`not_implemented` (the round's `failures`), and was raised by the test itself: the round records every repository file
the traceback passes through (`frames`) and the deepest (`location`), and ALL of them SHALL match `tdd.test_globs` or
`tdd.test_support_globs`, so a production file anywhere in the traceback disqualifies it. A record that lacks them, or
whose traceback has a frame with an absolute path that is no library, is no candidate. No production file the unit
added or changed may mention `__tracebackhide__`. A browser test's message SHALL be a usage error (`TypeError`,
`ValueError`, `AttributeError`, `NameError`, "must be a ...", "unexpected keyword argument"); a timeout, a locator that
matched nothing or too much, or a failed connection is no candidate.
A finding SHALL become a `repair` chore only when every test id it fails on is a candidate; otherwise it stays a plain
fix chore. The task SHALL name each test, its kind and the first line of its message, carry the excerpt of the gate log
of the finding, and say that the test may be right and the code wrong. The step SHALL derive the candidates again from
git and the stored round; the marker is never the proof.

The repair step SHALL keep an edit only when the structural rules of a repair hold (the rules of the first design,
unchanged: every changed file is a candidate's file and UTF-8 before and after; the facts of every other name and the
module's statements that bind no name are equal; imports only added, in place, from `re`, `json`, `datetime`, `math`,
`decimal` or `fractions`, binding no name the file or the builtins bind; each repaired test keeps its decorators, its
signature and its number of top-level statements, at most 3 replaced in place with no new `try`, `if`, loop, `with` or
`match`; no check removed or moved into a nested scope or below `and`/`or`, a conditional expression or `:=`; a
replaced statement loads only the names the vocabulary rule allows and none of `os`, `sys`, `pathlib`, `open`,
`inspect`, `functools`, `operator`, `importlib`, `builtins`, `object`, `type`, `getattr`, `setattr`, `delattr`,
`globals`, `vars`, `environ`, `getenv` or a dunder, under any alias; in an `async def` a check counts only when awaited;
no `return`, `yield`, always-true `assert`, constant `and`/`or` operand, skip, `xfail`, `importorskip`, `SkipTest`,
`exit`, write outside its locals, `global`, `nonlocal`, `globals`, `vars`, `setattr`, `delattr`, `__import__`, `exec`,
`eval`, `compile` or `importlib`), the repaired tests pass in the gate they failed in under the test gate's
no-regression rule, and each is proved again (a unit-gate test fails by an assertion when the project's functions
answer their zero value; an e2e test fails by an assertion against the unit base's production code, built). A change
to any other file SHALL be put back and fail the attempt: product code is frozen in a repair. These rules are a filter
that keeps bad proposals from a person, not the boundary (design D1).

A step that passes them SHALL NOT be committed. Its edit SHALL be saved as a held step (L4-IMP-065: the patch and the
result under `<unit>/.l4/held/`, their digests in the raise) and the work tree put back, and one question of kind
`harness` with check `repair` SHALL block the task, with no attempt counted. The question SHALL show each repaired
test (id, kind and first line of the failure, the gate), the gate run that passed them, how each was proved, that the
structural rules held, the changed paths and the diff of each file, and offer `accept: apply this edit` and
`retry: <note>`. Its raise SHALL record `repair_blobs` (each changed path -> its blob before and after, from a
temporary index of the step base with the patch applied). A patch whose expected state cannot be computed, or that
changes a path outside the repaired tests' files or a link, SHALL NOT be offered: the attempt fails. Nor SHALL a patch
whose repaired files' text, before or after it, changes under the question's redaction or holds a character a view
does not show as it is (a C0 or C1 control other than tab, newline and a carriage return before a newline; U+2028,
U+2029; a bidirectional control; a zero-width character or U+FEFF; by Unicode class: what `str.isprintable()`
rejects except tab, newline, a carriage return before a newline and a leading byte order mark, and the
default-ignorable characters it accepts), or whose rendered question changes under the redaction as a whole or holds
a redaction mark, or whose saved patch's text changes under the redaction or has a line longer than a question shows
(the decision is made on the uncut text). Every line a held question shows SHALL spell such characters as escapes and
be cut once at most. The agent-field shape of the redactor SHALL NOT cross a line end, and a test's source view SHALL show the lines Python counts of the function its id names, inside the
class the id names.

An `accept` of a `repair` question SHALL count only when its `question.answered` record has `by: human`; an answer by
an agent (`clarifier.answer_by_agents`) or by the delegate never applies a repair. The delegate SHALL escalate such a
question without a model call ("a repair of a test is a person's decision"), and `l4 questions accept|answer` by an
agent SHALL refuse it, whatever `clarifier.answer_by_agents` says. A recorded accept that does not count SHALL replay
nothing and be recorded once (`held.accept_ignored`); the step runs again as an agent's and its proposal is held by a
question of its own. A person's accept SHALL make the next run replay the saved edit (no agent; the digests and the
stale rule of L4-IMP-065) and run the same checks on it again. Before the commit the replay SHALL compare the changed
test files with the raise's `repair_blobs` (the same paths; each one's blob at the step base and in the work tree are
the recorded pair); a difference fails the attempt. On pass the commit SHALL carry `L4-TDD: exempt` and the ledger
`task.repaired{task, base, files, tests, ids, proved, sha10, question, patch_sha256}`, staged with no line-ending
conversion and with no `notes_for_verifier` or `suppressions` of the saved result, where `proved` maps each test id
to how it was proved and `sha10` ties the proof to the content of its file. A replay that fails a check fails the
attempt and uses the accept up. `retry` drops the saved step and the next step is an agent's, with the note. When the
attempts are used up the task SHALL escalate as a fix chore does, with a note that the test may be right and the
product code wrong.

**Amendment of ci-evidence D11 (a fix chore may not change a test).** A fix chore SHALL NOT change a test file, with one exception: a `repair` chore (L4-IMP-091) may commit the definitions of
the unit's own new failing tests as a person accepted them, under the structural check, and nothing else. [V, a consumer's unit had a new browser test that raised an error of its own before any check (0.4.43); its fix chores either failed their attempts or changed correct product code to suit the broken test, and nothing could mend the test itself. The edit is a person's decision because the checks above are a filter, not a boundary: the digests from the saved patch to the commit to the verifier tie the commit to the exact bytes a person read.]

**L4-IMP-065** A held step is kept, and an `accept` takes effect only by replaying it. A replayed step meets the same guards as an agent step after the agent returns (scratch dropped, protected paths and runner configuration put back, environment checked), and the replay guard's expected state follows what the test-path freeze and the test-chore review put back. A step that the pre-existing-test check refuses is refused before any hold is taken. When a step is held with a harness question
(`check`: `pre_satisfied`, `vacuity`, `at_red` or `tests`, L4-IMP-063), the harness SHALL, before it discards the step's changes,
save them, whatever their size, as `git diff --binary --unified=3` of the step against its start, with the agent's result
beside it, at `<unit folder>/.l4/held/<task key>-<check>.patch` and `.json`, and commit both with the questions commit.
`question.raised` records `saved: true`, `patch_sha256`, `result_sha256`, the test ids, `source_sha256` (for audit only) and
`carries` (the question whose replay produced this step, if any). Only a question WITHOUT a `saved` field (raised by 0.4.16)
keeps the old rule by test id. The question's Context SHALL list every path the patch changes (added, modified, deleted), show
the source of each named test (at most 10) and the diff of the changed paths (at most 100), each redacted by the run's redactor
before it is cut to 40 lines of at most 400 characters; a cut SHALL say that the cut lines are replayed too and name the patch
path, and the accept line SHALL say that `accept` replays exactly the saved change of N files (the whole patch being in that
path). The file of a named test SHALL be found among the work tree's files (tracked and untracked, without what the
harness's excludes leave out) from the id's head, in this order: the head as a path; the one file whose path with dots
for slashes is the head; the dotted Python module; the one file whose path with dots for slashes ends with `.` and the
head. When several files match at the second or fourth step, the one file that the step changed is used, and no file is
found when that does not decide. The source of a test in a file that is not Python SHALL be the test's own lines, from the
test call that names the test to the line that closes it, taken after the file is redacted whole; when no file or no such
line is found, the source is `(the source of this test was not found)`. The whole Context is at most 48 KB, and less as `questions.md` fills (never below 4 KB, and the writer keeps the file under
three quarters of its 2 MB limit): over the bound, the question lists the paths (capped) and the patch path instead of the
diffs, so `questions.md` stays loadable however many large questions it holds. When the run reaches the step of that task and the newest harness
question of the task and check is answered `accept` by the rules of L4-IMP-063 (a person's answer, or an agent's where
`clarifier.answer_by_agents` allows it, with its digest in the ledger), has `saved: true`, has not been replayed
(`held.replayed{question}`) and no `unit.restarted` or `tasks.reopened` of the task follows it, the harness SHALL start no agent:
it reads both files as regular files, checks both digests (both are required), checks that the patch applies (`git apply
--check`) and applies the verified bytes (from standard input; the operator's git settings that change a patch's shape, such
as `diff.context`, colour or prefixes, do not matter). A global `core.autocrlf=true` is not defended against: the harness
forces `core.autocrlf=false` for its own capture and apply, but a checkout that git wrote with CRLF line ends can make the patch
not apply, which is a refused replay (a new question), never a pass. It then does what it does after an agent returns (the
environment setup runs again, protected paths are put back with `guard.violation`, the run ledger is restored, the secret scan
fails the step as an agent's would) and hands the saved result to the code that follows the step, so the scope guards, tamper
checks, gates and checks are the ones an agent step's changes get. The replayed step SHALL commit exactly the step base plus the saved patch. The expected state is not read from the work tree
(setup may run code of the patch, such as a build hook, before the first gate): it is taken from a temporary index
(`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `read-tree` of the step base, `apply --cached` of the verified patch bytes, `ls-files -s -z`), as the mode,
blob id and size of every path the patch changes and an absence for every path it deletes, never from text a file name can
forge. After every gate run, including the discrimination runs of a tests chore, the harness puts every non-ignored path (outside
its own outputs: the run ledger, the unit folder's `.l4/`, `tasks.md`, `questions.md`) back to that state: a path of the patch to
the patch's blob (streamed in with `git cat-file blob`, never held in memory) with its executable bit or link target, and every
other path that differs from the step base (a tracked file that setup or a gate changed, a new file) to the base, and records
`held.replay_restored{paths}`. A tracked file that setup modifies is therefore put back to the base (or to the base plus the patch)
and the step still passes; ignored files (a setup's environment, caches) are left alone. A file is compared by size first and then
by the git blob hash computed in chunks, and only where the expected blob has the file's size, so no file is read whole; at any
other path nothing is read. A path that cannot be put back fails the step as an attempt. The guard never follows a link: it
reaches the folder of each path from the work tree one component at a time with `O_NOFOLLOW` and acts only through that folder's
file descriptor (unlink, rmdir, mkdir, symlink, and file creation with `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`; an entry is removed by its own type,
so a FIFO is unlinked and never opened), checking again right before acting on each path. A patch whose paths hold a line break is
refused (a retry-only question). A link is trusted as the pair (path, target): the target comes from the patch's blob in that
index, a link at a patch path with another target (setup code re-pointed it) or any other link in the tree when the guard is armed
is planted, and a patch link is always restored to the patch's target. The work tree folder is opened once when the guard is armed
and every walk starts from that descriptor; before every restore and every git call it is checked to be still the same folder
(else `held.replay_unsafe`). The guard lists the paths that differ from the base by the base's ignore rules and by the work tree's
(a `.gitignore` of the patch can show a file the base hides), and the commit of a replayed step stages only the paths of the
expected state (deletions included) and the harness's own outputs (the ledger, `tasks.md`, the removal of the held files), never
`git add -A`. A path the guard cannot read (a gate removed a folder's permissions) fails the step cleanly, never as an exception. A cache
mount (`sandbox.caches`) at or above `<cache>/worktrees` is refused, so a writable mount never covers a work tree. Any other link in the snapshot (planted by the
setup), or a folder a gate replaced by a link above a path of the step, is never followed: the link itself is removed,
`held.replay_unsafe` is recorded and the step fails with its own message. Only the harness's own outputs are exempt (the
run ledger, the unit folder's `.l4/`, `tasks.md`, `questions.md`), not every path with a `.l4` component. This relies on
`O_NOFOLLOW`, `O_DIRECTORY` and `dir_fd`, available on Linux and macOS alike. For a harness question
whose step was not saved, `l4 questions show` and the `Next:` line of `l4 status` offer only `retry`. The sidecar holds nothing that grows with the step (`files_changed` and `tests_added` are
recomputed from the patch at replay), so a large step replays. It records
`held.replayed{question, task, check, patch_sha256, tests, sources}` after applying; the override covers the tests of the patch
during that step. The accept of a saved step takes effect ONLY through that replay (no content or digest rule widens it): once
the replay is used up (it failed a gate, or the check refuted a criterion; a failed replay counts as an attempt, so
`max_task_attempts` bounds the cycle), the accept covers nothing, and a later agent step that meets the same inconclusive check
is held again with a NEW question that saves the new step. The one exception is a step that a replay produced and that held
again for another check: its question records `carries`, says that it is the replay of the earlier accepted step (the same
paths, with the content its own gates rewrote) and the accept of the carried question applies to it again when this question is
accepted. A `tasks.reopened` of the task drops every accept raised before it, with or without a saved step. A missing or
unusable file, a digest that differs, a missing result digest or a patch that does not apply SHALL give no override, no agent
step and a new harness question with `saved: false` that offers ONLY `retry` and never says that a claim is taken; an `accept`
answer to it gives no override, and the run says so (`held.accept_ignored`) and runs the step again. `retry` (or `dismissed`)
SHALL delete both files in a commit before the agent step, whose prompt carries the note; a replay deletes them in the step's
own commit; a restarted unit or a reopened task drops them. An agent step of a task whose replay was used up carries the data
block `accepted tests` with the notice that the earlier accept was for the earlier step only and a new step needs a new answer
(for a question of 0.4.16 it lists the accepted tests and the rule to keep them unchanged). `<unit folder>/.l4/held/` is a
harness-owned path (`**/.l4/**`, L4-SEC-004): an agent's write to it is put back. [V: a consumer repository, a version-pin test
held on one criterion: the accepted question named a test that checks the installed version, the next agent wrote the test
again under another name, the accept did not cover it, and a second question was raised for the same criterion.]

**L4-IMP-066** The soft deadline counts from the job's start. The soft deadline SHALL count from the start of the CI
job. That start is `L4_JOB_STARTED_AT` when set, else GitLab's `CI_JOB_STARTED_AT`, else the start of the run, and a
value that does not parse is skipped. Both GitHub workflow templates SHALL have, as their first step, a step named `job
start` that writes `L4_JOB_STARTED_AT` (UTC, ISO 8601) to `$GITHUB_ENV`. When a budget is known and the job's start is
not, `l4 run` MUST say once, as a WARNING, that it counts from the run's start and that `l4 upgrade` adds the step.
`run.started` SHALL record `job_timeout_s` (the budget before the margin), `job_budget_source` (L4-IMP-078) and
`job_started_at` when they are known.

**L4-IMP-067** A step that does not fit is not started. When the deadline is known, `l4 run` SHALL compare the time left
to the soft deadline with the step's estimate before each implementer step (red, green, a single-phase chore, also of a
fix unit) and before each verification round. For a task, the first check SHALL be made when the task starts, before a
committed red is resumed (its setup and baseline belong to the green step), and again after a fall-back to another
profile. The estimate SHALL be the longest step of the same phase measured in this run or among the unit's last 10
recorded `step.timed` and stopped steps of that phase, or, with no measure of that phase, the longest of any phase. It
SHALL be at least 10 minutes, and at most a cap per phase: the agent's time limit plus `gates.timeout` for red, green
and single, and four times `gates.timeout` for a verification round. A step whose estimate exceeds the time left MUST
NOT start, and the step is handed back (L4-IMP-069). The first step of a run MUST start whenever any time is left. A
step that was stopped at the last deadline (L4-IMP-071) starts only as the first step of a run. Every step that starts
SHALL record `step.timed{phase, task, attempt, seconds}` (a round: `round` in place of `task` and `attempt`). With no
known budget, no step is checked.

**L4-IMP-068** A step still running at the soft deadline is stopped. When the soft deadline is reached, the harness
SHALL send SIGINT (never SIGTERM) to the process group of every agent, CLI judge and gate that the unit's run has
running, and SIGKILL to the group 5 seconds later if it has not exited. A process started after the deadline MUST be
stopped at once. A process stopped by the deadline MUST be reported as stopped by the deadline even when its idle limit
or its time limit fired too, so that it never counts as a failed attempt. The stopped step MUST be handed back
(L4-IMP-069) after the cleanup it already does (protected paths, gate and runner configuration and the ledger put back,
scratch dropped, `agent.finished` and the reported cost recorded). The agent's `step.finished` SHALL record `status:
deadline`. A stop inside the verifier MUST NOT become a failed verification step. A CLI judge or clarifier stopped this way MUST record the cost it metered (`budget.cost` with `usd` or `credits`) before the stop is handed back. A probe of an agent (and each of its steps) is not stopped once it runs, so none is started after the deadline has fired (the stop is `deadline.reached{when: before}`), and `soft_deadline_margin` counts a probe among the calls that cannot be stopped.

**L4-IMP-069** A step handed back at the soft deadline is resumed by the next run. A step handed back (not started under
L4-IMP-067, or stopped under L4-IMP-068) MUST NOT count as an attempt and MUST NOT change the unit's phase. The run
SHALL record `deadline.reached` filled from the step that was current when the deadline stopped it (phase, task, attempt
or round, `left_at_start_s`, `estimate_s`, `ran_s`, `first`). A stop with no current step (a clarifier call, work before
the unit's first check) SHALL record the unit's phase and `first: false`. The run SHALL end the unit with exit 10 and
the exit reason `soft deadline: …`, commit only its ledger file, push the unit branch, and record
`run.finished{exit_code: 10, reason}`. No unit after it in the same run SHALL start; each is listed as `not started:
soft deadline (…)`. The next run MUST continue from the last pushed step: a red that was committed is not done again,
and a replayed held step that was stopped is replayed again from its saved patch, with no agent, because a
`held.replayed` followed by a stop of the same task, phase and attempt, with no commit of that task between them, MUST NOT count
as a replay.

**L4-IMP-070** Exactly one continuation follows the soft deadline. A run in CI with `ci.continuation: dispatch` SHALL
dispatch exactly one continuation on the base when a unit was handed back or left at the soft deadline and the run's
exit code is a designed stop (10, 11, 12 or 13). On GitHub it is a `workflow_dispatch` of `l4.yml`, and none is sent
when a run is already queued; the check for a waiting run MUST NOT count the dispatching run itself, which is in
progress. On GitLab it is a pipeline on the base (`POST /pipeline`), and none is started when a pipeline of the base is
already created, waiting for a resource, preparing, pending or scheduled. When the continuation was dispatched or one is
already waiting, the plan's next-run start (L4-YOLO-012) of the same run MUST NOT be sent. When a unit was handed back and no step started in the run (the run's first check deferred its step), no continuation and no plan next-run start SHALL be sent, and a warning MUST say that no step fitted, print the time left at that first check, and name the fix for the budget's source (L4-IMP-078) or splitting the task; it starts with `continuation: not requested:` only when the run is in CI with `ci.continuation: dispatch`. A stop during a call that is not a step does not make the run one in which no step started.

**L4-IMP-071** A step stopped at the deadline twice halts the unit. A stop (L4-IMP-068) SHALL count toward
`deadline_repeated` when the step was the first step of its run, or when it started with at least its estimate left
(`left_at_start_s >= estimate_s`). The count of a task and phase SHALL start after the last `task.red_committed`,
`task.green_committed` or `task.done` of that task, and the count of a verification round after the last
`verify.verdict`; a `unit.retried`, `unit.resumed` or `unit.restarted` starts both again. After a stop, the same task
and phase (or round) SHALL start only as the first step of a run while the newest event of that task and phase in the
window is that stop; a `step.timed` of a later attempt that ran ends it. When the count reaches 2, the unit SHALL halt
with `breaker.tripped{reason: deadline_repeated, task, phase, stops: 2}`. The halt reason MUST say that the step does
not fit in one job, MUST name first the fix for the budget's source (L4-IMP-078), splitting the task, and
`l4 retry --unit <U> --reason TEXT`, and then show for both stops the time left at its start against its estimate.
The text SHALL be kept whole up to 600 characters in the halt's detail and the unit's exit reason. No continuation is
dispatched for a halted unit. A step that was not started and a stop with no current step MUST NOT count. `deadline.reached` of a stop
SHALL record `ran_s` (the seconds the step ran), `left_at_start_s`, `estimate_s` and `first`.

**L4-IMP-072** A run on a stale copy of the workflow relays to the base. In GitHub Actions, on any ref other than the base branch (`GITHUB_REF_NAME` differs from the base), `l4 doctor --ci`,
`l4 plan --sweep`, `l4 run` and `l4 status` SHALL check the pin (L4-ADO-005) before they load the configuration. The
check reads only the job environment (`GITHUB_*`, `L4_BASE_BRANCH`), the checked-out `.github/workflows/l4.yml`, and a
few keys of `.l4/config.yaml` read without the schema, with the strict loader's YAML 1.2 rules (`harness.delivery`,
`harness.repository`, `forge.type`, `forge.base_branch`, `forge.branch_prefix`, `forge.token_env`, `spec.openspec.root`,
`spec.kiro.root`; a scalar is read as a string, anything else is ignored). So a configuration key that the running
harness does not know cannot stop it. When `harness.delivery` cannot be read, a setup-action pin in the checked-out
workflow means `action`. On a mismatch, every one of these commands prints the existing warning, does no work and exits
0 before the configuration is loaded, and the first of `l4 doctor --ci`, `l4 plan --sweep` and `l4 run` in the job
relays: it dispatches one `workflow_dispatch` of `l4.yml` on the base and prints one line that says what it did. A later
command in the same job MUST NOT dispatch again; it trusts the job's marker only when the marker's run id, run attempt
and job equal the current ones. `l4 status` never relays. On the base branch itself nothing moves before the
configuration: a schema error stays exit 2, and a mismatch is reported as today. The relay MUST NOT dispatch when any of
these holds:
- a run of `l4.yml` other than this one is `queued`, `pending`, `waiting`, `requested` or `in_progress` on the base;
- the base has no possible work.
The base has possible work, read with git only, when a delivery plan ref is `active` or `waiting`, when a plan ref
cannot be read or folded, when a branch under the unit prefix exists on origin, when the checked-out base holds a unit
folder (a `tasks.md` under the OpenSpec changes, not in their archive, or under the Kiro specs), or when reading any of
these fails. A token that may not dispatch (no token, 401, 403, 404) MUST be a line that names `gh workflow run l4.yml
--ref <base>`, never a failure. `outcome.json` of `l4 run` SHALL record `relay` with the job's answer. Outside GitHub
Actions nothing changes: GitLab's `l4 sweep` schedule targets the base, and the pin guard does not apply there.

**L4-IMP-073** l4 yolo status names a run that ended without a record. For a plan that is `active`, `waiting` or `stopped`, `l4 yolo status` SHALL call the current unit's open run
(L4-OPS-020,
L4-YOLO-030) "ended without a record" when either of these holds:
- its `run.started` has a `ci_url` and its age exceeds its job's timeout plus 5 minutes. The timeout is
  `run.started.job_timeout_s`; for an older event it is `ci.time_budget` when that is not `auto`, else 180 minutes,
  and the text then says `assumed`. An open run without a `ci_url` (a local run) gets no age rule.
- the forge says the CI run of its `ci_url` has completed. For a re-run, the attempt of the URL is the one read
  (`/actions/runs/<id>/attempts/<n>` on GitHub). This is asked only when a token is available and the age rule does not
  hold, with a timeout of at most 10 seconds. Any failure to ask leaves the rule unused.
A CI run that the forge reports as held for approval (GitHub `conclusion: action_required`) has not ended: the open-run
line then ends `: the CI run waits for approval` before its link, `open_run.waiting_for_approval` is true in `--json`,
and for an `active` plan the `Next:` line says that the CI run (its URL) waits for approval and to open it and approve
the run; it never gives the command that starts a run on the base.
The open-run line MUST keep its words and add `: it ended without a record (<why>)`. `--json` SHALL carry
`open_run.ended_without_record` and, when it is true, `open_run.why`. For an `active` plan, the one `Next:` line (and
`next` in `--json`) SHALL give the command that starts a run on the base (`gh workflow run l4.yml --ref <base>` on
GitHub, the new-pipeline page of the project on GitLab) when its open run ended without a record (the line says so and
that the unit continues from its last pushed step), and when all of these hold: it has no open run that may still be
running; the forge says that no run of the harness's CI is queued, pending, waiting or in progress on the base; and the
plan is idle or no schedule can advance it. The plan is idle when the newest plan or unit event is older than twice the
period of `ci.schedule` (60 minutes when the cron's period cannot be read); no schedule can advance it when
`ci.schedule` is null, or when the default branch is not the base and its copy of `.github/workflows/l4.yml` is missing
or pins another harness (L4-IMP-074). The line SHALL say how long the plan has been idle, or why no schedule advances
it. It MUST NOT then say `nothing: CI advances the plan`. When the forge cannot be asked, today's line stays. A
`waiting` or `stopped` plan keeps
its own `Next:`.

**L4-IMP-074** The base's run names a default-branch copy that is behind. In GitHub Actions with `harness.delivery: action`, a run of `l4 run` on the base branch SHALL read the default
branch's name from the event payload (`repository.default_branch`). When it is not the base, it SHALL read
`origin/<default>:.github/workflows/l4.yml`. When that file is missing, it SHALL print one `::warning::` saying that no
scheduled run starts from the default branch, with the copy step. When its pin differs from the base's, it SHALL print
one `::warning::` that names the default branch, both short shas, the release of that copy when its `uses:` line has a
`# vX.Y.Z` comment (a comment that is not a version is ignored), and the step: copy `.github/workflows/l4.yml` to the
default branch once, or promote the base. Versions MUST be compared as numbers (0.4.9 is older than 0.4.19). With a
release older than 0.4.19, the warning MUST say that the default branch's scheduled runs cannot relay to the base; with
