no release known, it MUST say so conditionally (`if that copy is older than 0.4.19, its scheduled runs cannot relay`).
With the same pin, an unknown default branch, the default branch as base, or another delivery, nothing is printed.

**L4-IMP-075** Failed attempts of a task count across runs. When a task starts, the run SHALL count the task's
`task.attempt_failed` events of each phase and profile (of the same fix unit, or of none) in its window, as if they had
failed in this run. The window starts after the last `task.red_committed`, `task.green_committed` or `task.done` of that
task, `unit.retried`, `unit.resumed` or `unit.restarted`. So `implementer.max_task_attempts` and
`implementer.escalate_after` MUST hold across runs. A run that hands back and continues MUST NOT give a task fresh
attempts. The next attempt number SHALL continue after the highest attempt of that phase in the window (its failures and
its stops). A profile that already reached `escalate_after` for the task's phase in the window, with a later profile in
`roles.implementer`, SHALL be escalated before the task's first attempt in this run, and again while the profile it
moves to has also reached `escalate_after` and has a later profile (each move is recorded as `implementer.escalated`).

**L4-IMP-076** A usable budget below one step is refused before any unit. When `ci.time_budget` is a duration (not
`auto`) and `ci.time_budget` minus `ci.soft_deadline_margin` is less than the smallest step estimate
(`l4.deadline.FLOOR_S`, 600 s), the configuration SHALL be reported as an error with its cause and its fix, in these
words: `ci.time_budget <budget> minus soft_deadline_margin <margin> leaves <N> min, less than one step (10 min): set
ci.time_budget: auto (the job timeout) or raise it`, where `<budget>` and `<margin>` are the configured values and `<N>`
the whole minutes left, rounded down (`leaves no time` when nothing is left). Doctor `CFG-012` (scopes `ci`, `local`,
`config`) SHALL fail with this text as an error, so `l4 doctor` exits 3. `l4 run` SHALL refuse with this text and exit 2
after the configuration and the run's preflight are read and before the follow-ups, the plan step and any unit, so no
lease, worktree, ledger write, plan record or forge call happens. The configuration MUST still load: `l4 status`, `l4
upgrade` and every other command run on it. `l4 run --dry-run`, `l4 verify` and the budget read between units are not
changed. A budget equal to the floor after the margin is not an error. (Before 0.4.19 such a budget meant one unit per
run; since the deadline is checked inside a unit, the first step of each run starts with less than a minute and is
stopped, and the second stop halts the unit with `deadline_repeated`.)

**L4-IMP-077** A time budget that shortens the job is named. When `ci.time_budget` is a duration and the job's own
timeout is known, and the job's timeout minus `ci.time_budget` is more than `ci.soft_deadline_margin`, a warning SHALL
say so: `ci.time_budget <budget> is shorter than the job's timeout (<T> min, <source>) by more than
soft_deadline_margin <margin>: the soft deadline comes at minute <D>, not at minute <J>; set ci.time_budget: auto (the
job timeout) unless the job must stop early`, where `<D>` is the budget minus the margin and `<J>` the job's timeout
minus the margin, in whole minutes. The job's timeout SHALL be read from GitLab's `CI_JOB_TIMEOUT` (seconds), else
`L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, else the first `timeout-minutes: <integer>` of the checked-out `.github/workflows/l4.yml` (a
regular file of at most 1 MB, not a link; the source is then `.github/workflows/l4.yml timeout-minutes`); when none
gives it, no warning is given. Doctor `CFG-012` SHALL fail with this text as a warning (its result's severity is
`warn`; doctor's exit code is not changed by it). When the error of L4-IMP-076 applies too, `CFG-012` SHALL be an error
whose message is both texts joined by `; `. `l4 run` SHALL log the warning once, as a WARNING, at the point where it
checks L4-IMP-076, and go on; when L4-IMP-076 refuses, only the refusal's text is printed.

**L4-IMP-078** The deadline texts name the budget's source. The budget's source SHALL be `ci.time_budget` when that is
a duration, else `CI_JOB_TIMEOUT`, else `L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, the same order in which the budget is read. The fix
that the `deadline_repeated` halt reason (L4-IMP-071) and the "no step fitted" warning (L4-IMP-070) name SHALL be the
source's: `raise ci.time_budget (or set it to auto)` for `ci.time_budget`, `raise the job's timeout (CI_JOB_TIMEOUT)`
for `CI_JOB_TIMEOUT`, and `raise timeout-minutes and L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` for `L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` or an unknown
source. The halt reason SHALL read `<step> does not fit in one job: <fix> or split the task, then l4 retry --unit
<U> --reason TEXT (stopped twice: …)`, unchanged for `L4_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`. The warning SHALL read `no step fitted
before the soft deadline (<N> s left at the first step); <fix>, or split the task`, with the `continuation: not
requested: ` prefix of L4-IMP-070, and MUST NOT name another source's fix. `run.started` SHALL record
`job_budget_source` with the source, beside `job_timeout_s`, when a budget is known.

**L4-IMP-079** l4 upgrade names a budget problem. `l4 upgrade` (also with `--dry-run`, for every delivery: vendored,
fetched and action) SHALL print, after the files it changes, the text of L4-IMP-076 as `error: <text>; until it is
fixed, l4 run exits 2 and doctor CFG-012 fails` when it applies, and the text of L4-IMP-077 as `warning: <text>` when it
applies. For L4-IMP-077 the job's timeout SHALL be the `timeout-minutes` of the `.github/workflows/l4.yml` that the
upgrade writes when it writes one, else of the file on disk; the job's variables of the environment that runs `l4
upgrade` are not read. These lines MUST be printed whether or not a file changes, MUST NOT change any file, and MUST NOT
change the exit code (0).

**L4-IMP-080** The implementer is told what the gates see in CI. When the gates of the step receive variables of
L4-SEC-040, the gate section of the red, green and single prompts SHALL name them (`` `CI=true`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`
``), say that the step's own shell does not have them, tell how to reproduce a failure that only the CI shows (run the
gate command as `CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true <gate command>`), say that tools such as typer and rich may colour their
output under them, and that a test of a command's help or output must not depend on colour (strip the ANSI codes before
comparing, or turn the command's colour off in the test). When there is none, the prompt SHALL be byte-identical to
today's. No template file or template version changes.

**L4-IMP-081** A CI fix task is told what the gates may not show, and asks no one to unfreeze a file. When a `[chore]`
of a fix unit answers a `repository CI failed: <job>` finding of the last `repository_ci_failed` edge, the prompt of its
step SHALL carry one more line (built in code; no template file or version changes): the task answers that CI job, the
gates here may not show its failure, and when they do not the agent is to say so in `notes_for_verifier` and name the
file and the change a person must make, instead of guessing a change the gates cannot check. A chore that changes
nothing is committed as before. A fix step's change to a test file or a test-support file (`conftest.py`, fixtures, also
a new one) is put back (`guard.test_tamper` for a test path, `guard.violation` for a support file); the note for the next attempt and the harness note on a technical question that the step raises SHALL say that a person must commit that change on
the unit branch (step 1 of the verifier reads that commit, L4-VER-038: a person's last commit to the file) and that an
answer cannot unfreeze a file in a fix task, and MUST NOT offer an unfreeze. `l4 questions
show` and `accept` with `--unit <fix unit>` SHALL find the fix unit's questions, which live on its parent unit's branch
under the fix unit's own folder; `--unit <parent>` shows the parent's own questions.

## 8. Agent and model factory

### 8.1 Interfaces

**L4-FAC-001** Agent adapters MUST implement an ACP-shaped interface (sessions, prompts, stop reasons, streamed
updates, permission decisions), so that native-CLI and ACP transports are interchangeable:

```python
class AgentAdapter(Protocol):
    name: str                                       # "claude-code" | "codex" | "opencode" | "kiro-cli" | "copilot-cli" | "command" | "acp" | "fake"
    def capabilities(self) -> AgentCaps: ...        # schema_mode (native|prompt_contract), resume, preset_session_id,
                                                    # max_turns, budget_cap, mcp_injection, quota_query, worktree_cwd
    def probe(self, profile: Profile, step: ProbeStep, ctx: ProbeCtx) -> ProbeResult: ...
    def run(self, req: RunRequest) -> RunResult: ...  # blocking, streams events to the event sink

@dataclass
class RunRequest:
    profile: Profile; role: str; cwd: Path; prompt: str
    result_schema: dict | None; result_path: Path
    resume_session_id: str | None; preset_session_id: str | None
    mcp_servers: list[McpServer]; permission_policy: PermissionPolicy
    env: dict[str, str]                              # allowlisted; forge tokens are never passed (§18)
    timeout_s: int; max_turns: int | None; max_budget_usd: float | None
    stall_timeout_s: float | None = None             # SIGINT, then SIGKILL after 5 s, for a run with no stdout line for this long and no open tool call; None: only timeout_s (L4-IMP-024)
    watch: ActivityWatch | None = None               # the step's liveness record: heartbeat and tool-call state; None for a judge or a probe (L4-IMP-023, L4-FAC-012)
    interrupt: threading.Event                       # set at soft deadline → SIGINT / session/cancel

@dataclass
class RunResult:
    status: Literal["ok", "max_turns", "budget", "permission_blocked", "auth", "quota",
                    "rate_limited", "error", "timeout", "cancelled"]
    final_text: str | None; structured: dict | None
    last_message: str | None                          # the agent's text after its last tool call (L4-FAC-010)
    result_problem: Literal["missing", "not_json", "not_object", "invalid"] | None   # why a finished run gave no usable result (L4-FAC-010)
    session_id: str | None; exit_code: int | None
    usage: Usage                                      # tokens in/out/cached, cost_usd | None, context_peak_tokens | None, context_peak_percent | None (L4-FAC-011)
    limit: LimitSignal | None                          # §8.4
    model_resolved: str | None; raw_events_path: Path
    permission_denials: list[dict]                     # claude-code `permission_denials[]`; empty elsewhere
    tool_rejections: list[dict]                        # codex stderr `Rejected(…)` lines: {tool, reason}; empty elsewhere
```

**L4-FAC-002** `RunResult.status` MUST be derived from the event stream **and** the exit code, never the exit code
alone (OpenCode exits 0 even when stopped by a permission rejection; Claude returns `result: null` on max-turns [V,
research/02]). Claude status comes from `is_error` + `api_error_status`, never `subtype`: a bad model returns
`subtype:"success"`, `is_error:true`, `api_error_status:404` [V, spikes/01, `hello_bad_model.stream.jsonl`]. Per
adapter [spikes/00-summary §3.6]:

| `RunResult.status` | claude-code | codex | opencode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ok` | result event, `is_error:false`, and `structured_output` present when a schema was requested | exit 0, `turn.completed`, `-o` file parses | exit 0, last `step_finish.part.reason == "stop"` [V] |
| `permission_blocked` | (denials are recoverable; record `permission_denials[]`) | stderr `Rejected(…)` → `agent.tool_rejected` event only | exit 0, last reason ≠ `stop`, `tool_use` error containing "rejected permission" [V]; exit 0 with last reason `tool-calls` but without that error → `error` |
| `quota` / `rate_limited` | `rate_limit_event.status == "rejected"` + `resetsAt`; `api_retry{error: rate_limit}` → interrupt [V] | `turn.failed` with the usage-limit shape [U: not reproduced] | `error.data.statusCode` 429 (reset only in body text "retry in 9h9m42s") [V] |
| `quota` with `LimitSignal.kind: credits` [I: kind → status mapping] | — | — | `statusCode` 402, `isRetryable:false`, `limit_source:"openrouter_credits"` [V] |
| `auth` | `api_error_status` 401/403 [I] | `-32600` from the app-server quota call, not from a `codex exec` stream [V] | "Token refresh failed: 401" [V] |
| `error` (config, not retryable) | `is_error:true`, `api_error_status:404` (bad model) [V] | `turn.failed` 400 `invalid_json_schema` or "model is not supported" [V] | — |
| `error` (retryable) | — | — | "[503]" / "overloaded" [V] |
| `max_turns` / `budget` | `subtype` `error_max_turns` / `error_max_budget_usd`, `result: null` [V] | — | — |
| `timeout` | harness clock: the step's limit, or `implementer.idle_timeout` (L4-IMP-024) | harness clock: the same | harness clock: the same; silent gaps of 30–183 s are normal while it retries [V] |

OpenCode v2 (`options.cli_major: 2`, L4-OCV-007). The first rule that applies decides (the order is L4-OCV-007's); no row reads a final `step_finish` as a requirement:

| `RunResult.status` | opencode, `cli_major: 2` |
|---|---|
| `ok` | exit code 0, no `error` event, fewer `step_start` events than the step bound, `session export` `info.outcome == "succeeded"` and the result attaches [V for `succeeded`]; with no export, the last `step_finish` reason `stop` ([U] `export_decides`) |
| `permission_blocked` | a run at its step bound that recorded a denial ([U] `not_ok_named`); with no export and no final stop, any denial: a `tool_use` in error whose text starts with `Permission denied:` or contains `cannot ask the user for permission` [V] |
| `quota` / `rate_limited` | `error.status` 429 is `rate_limited` with a `rate_limit` limit and no reset; 402 is `quota` with kind `credits`; source `opencode2.status` for both, and the body, headers and message are never read ([U] `status_only`: no v2 402 or 429 was recorded) |
| `auth` | `error.status` 401 or 403, `error.type == "provider.auth"`, or v1's auth wording; both recorded free-tier 403s (denied tools; a flagged network) [V]; the OAuth refresh failure text is [U] (`auth_by_status`) |
| `error` | exit code other than 0 (`unsupported_version:` when stderr rejects a v1 flag, else `opencode2 exited with code <n>`); an `error` event of another type or status (`opencode2 reported an error (<type>, status <n>)`, with `, retryable` from status 500); a run at its bound with no denial (`step_bound: opencode2 stopped at agents.build.steps <N>`); another export outcome (`opencode2 session outcome <value>`, [U] `not_ok_named`); no export and no final stop (`opencode2 session export failed (<why>) and the stream has no final stop`) |
| `timeout` | harness clock: the step's limit; an interrupt is `cancelled` by the harness's own flag, never by the exit code ([U] `harness_interrupt`) |

**L4-FAC-010** A finished run reports its final message and why its result is not usable.

`RunResult` SHALL have the fields `last_message` and `result_problem`.

`last_message` SHALL be the agent's text after its last tool call, or `None` when the adapter cannot tell:
- opencode: the `text` parts after the last `tool_use` event, joined;
- kiro-cli: the `agent_message_chunk` text after the last `tool_call` update, joined (`runFinished.finalText` holds the
  text of the whole run);
- codex: the last `agent_message`;
- claude-code: the `result` of the final result event;
- command: `None`.
`final_text` MUST keep its meaning (the opencode judge reads it).

`result_problem` SHALL be set when the run finished but its result channel gave no usable object, and `None`
otherwise:
- `attach_file_result` (opencode, kiro-cli, copilot-cli, command): `missing` when there is no file, `not_json` when the file is not
  JSON, `not_object` when the JSON is not an object, and, for a request with a schema, `invalid` with the object in
  `rejected` when the object breaks the schema; with no schema in the request a missing file keeps the status `ok`,
  and every other problem keeps `error`;
- codex `_attach_result`: `missing`, `not_json` or `invalid`; claude-code `_attach_structured`: `missing` or
  `invalid`; both keep the status `error` and set `rejected` for an invalid object, as the judge path needs.
The status and the detail that an adapter reports today MUST NOT change.

**L4-FAC-011** agent.finished records the peak per-call context where the stream shows it.

`Usage` SHALL have the fields `context_peak_tokens` and `context_peak_percent`, and `agent.finished` SHALL record each
one when it is set:
- opencode: `context_peak_tokens`, the largest `tokens.input + tokens.cache.read + tokens.cache.write` of the run's
  `step_finish` events;
- claude-code: `context_peak_tokens`, the largest `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens +
  cache_creation_input_tokens` of the `message.usage` of the run's `assistant` events;
- kiro-cli: `context_peak_percent`, the largest `metadata.contextUsagePercentage`.
codex, command, copilot-cli and the fake adapter MUST NOT report a peak: codex reports one usage total for the whole turn, and
copilot-cli reports tokens and AI credits per model for the whole run (L4-FAC-019).
`input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `cached_input_tokens` MUST keep their meaning. The `agent.finished` progress line
SHALL end with `, context peak <n>k tokens` or `, context peak <p>%` when the event has the field, and SHALL stay as
before without it.

**L4-FAC-012** Each adapter reads its own stream for tool calls, and keeps no text.

The adapters `opencode`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `kiro-cli` and `copilot-cli` SHALL each have a stream reader: a pure function that
reads one stdout line of the agent and returns the tool-call signals in it, `start(id)`, `end(id)` or `call` (a call
that ended with no start seen):
- opencode: `call` for each `tool_use` event (the stream shows a call only when it ends);
- claude-code: `start` for each `tool_use` block of an `assistant` event (its `id`), `end` for each `tool_result`
  block of a `user` event (its `tool_use_id`);
- codex: `start` for `item.started` and `end` for `item.completed` of an item of type `command_execution`,
  `file_change`, `mcp_tool_call` or `web_search` (its `item.id`); no other item type is a tool call;
- kiro-cli: `start` for a `sessionUpdate` `tool_call` and `end` for a `tool_call_update` with `status` `completed` or
  `failed` (its `toolCallId`);
- copilot-cli: `start` for a `tool.execution_start` event and `end` for a `tool.execution_complete` event (its
  `toolCallId`); any other event is no signal.
The `command` adapter SHALL have no reader. A reader MUST return no signal, and MUST NOT raise, for a line that is not
JSON, not an object or of an unknown shape. A reader MUST NOT keep or return any text of the line.

Every adapter SHALL pass the request's activity watch and its reader to the process runner. The watch SHALL count
each stdout line as activity, count `start` and `call` signals as tool calls (and an `end` with an unknown id), and
keep the open calls by id. A request without a watch (a judge, a probe) SHALL run as before.

**L4-FAC-003** LLM backends (no tools) MUST implement:

```python
class LLMBackend(Protocol):
    def complete_structured(self, system: str, messages: list[Msg], json_schema: dict, *,
                            effort: str | None, max_tokens: int, timeout_s: int) -> StructuredResult: ...
# StructuredResult.status ∈ ok | refusal | truncated | schema_invalid | error ; parsed ; model_resolved ; usage
```

Implementations: `openai-chat` (base_url switch: OpenRouter — always send `provider.require_parameters: true`
[V]; OpenAI; Ollama `…:11434/v1`; LiteLLM proxy), `anthropic-messages` (native structured output; **not** the
OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which silently ignores `response_format` [V, research/04]), `fake`. Client-side JSON
Schema validation is mandatory; refusal/truncated/invalid map to "inconclusive", never "pass". When the response
reports a served model different from the requested one, the event `availability.model_mismatch` MUST be logged; a
judge verdict from a mismatched model is discarded (fail closed) and the next judge is tried; for implementers the
served model's vendor is the one recorded for independence.

OpenCode run mode does not report the served model [V, spikes/01, spikes/02]: log `availability.model_unverified` and
use the profile's declared `vendor`. A profile whose model is an undisclosed alias (OpenCode Zen `opencode/big-pickle`,
`*-free`) has vendor `unknown`, which is never independent of anything (L4-VER-001).

**CLI judge.** A `judges` or `clarifier` profile MAY name an agent adapter instead of a backend when that adapter
supports native schema with tools disabled. It is run tool-less (`claude-code`: the judge argv of §8.3.1; `codex`:
`exec -s read-only --output-schema` [U, not run as a judge]) and normalised to `StructuredResult`. An adapter without
native schema (`opencode`, `kiro-cli`, `copilot-cli`) is run on the prompt contract: the prompt carries the schema and the one-JSON-object
instruction, and the reply text, sliced from its first `{` to its last `}`, is parsed and validated (`opencode`: its
last text part; `kiro-cli`: `runFinished.finalText`, L4-KJD-003; `copilot-cli`: the content of the last non-blank `assistant.message`, L4-FAC-014); a missing or invalid object takes the deterministic
repair and at most one repair call (L4-VER-015). `kiro-cli` runs a tool-less harness agent with the prompt on stdin
(§8.3, L4-KJD-001..003) and also serves the clarifier, the plan-readiness review and the `s1_judge` stand-in
(L4-KJD-008). `copilot-cli` runs a tool-less call (`--available-tools=l4_no_tools`) with the prompt on stdin (§8.3.3,
L4-FAC-014) and serves the same roles. Reason: the only
verified independent pairing available on the reference runner today is a Codex implementer with a `claude -p` judge
[V on macOS, spikes/03; both logins exist on the runner, V, runner]: the OpenRouter account used by the spikes had a
negative balance (every call 402) [V, spikes/05], no API key is configured on the runner yet [V, runner], and OpenCode
Zen models have vendor `unknown` [V, spikes/02].

**L4-FAC-004** The System-One backend MUST speak the TypeSafe wire protocol (`POST /v1/systemone`, body
`{state, model, questions: {<id>: {type: noul|choice|score, instructions, criteria?}}}` [V, docs.typesafe.ai/api]).
`engine: laya-local` starts `laya-serve` (pinned `laya[serve]`) on a free localhost port for the duration of the
verify step and stops it afterwards; `engine: jev` uses the hosted API; `engine: ollama` uses Ollama's System One API
(`POST /v1/systemone` on a keyless host of the local network: same question types, `score` criteria sent as an array,
`choice` criteria as an object, a request over 64 KiB refused before it is sent [V, docs.ollama.com/api/systemone]).
Request/response pairs are logged for calibration (§10.8).

**L4-FAC-005** No backend or adapter may rely on sampling temperature for determinism; Claude Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 /
Fable 5.1 reject temperature/top-p and forced tool choice [V, research/03/04].

### 8.2 Profiles and the factory

**L4-FAC-006** `Factory.for_role(role, unit) -> Selected` MUST walk the role's chain in order, apply the
independence constraint (§10.1) and availability (§8.4), and return the first usable profile plus the list of skipped
profiles with reasons. The selection MUST be logged as `availability.selected`.

### 8.3 Adapter specifications (v1)

All adapters run with the harness-created worktree as `cwd`; none uses its CLI's own worktree flag (they differ in
location and resume semantics [V, research/02]). All adapters MUST isolate user/repo configuration in CI. Every
adapter spawn uses `stdin` = the prompt followed by EOF, or `DEVNULL`, plus a wall-clock timeout: an open stdin hangs
`opencode run` with no output [V 3/3, spikes/02]. Every spawn also runs in its own process group, and its environment
is built by `build_env` from the L4-SEC-001 allow-list (complete, never inherited); "credential var" below means the
profile's own variable.

**Custom OpenAI-compatible provider (`opencode`; magnitude, [V live] 2026-10-06).** A profile may declare
`options.provider {id, base_url, api_key_env, models{<id>: {context, output}}}`, `options.tools` and
`options.reasoning`; `model` is `<provider.id>/<model id>`, `vendor` is declared (the served model is not reported), and
the options are checked at load (an unknown nested key, a URL carrying credentials or a query, or a model without a
`models` entry is a config error that never echoes the value). The generated `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` gains
`provider.<id> = {npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", options: {baseURL, apiKey: "{file:<path>}"}, models: {<m>: {tool_call,
limit, options: {reasoningEffort}}}}`. **The key never enters the sandbox environment or the config text**: `--setenv`
values land in bwrap's argv (L4-SEC-001) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` is an environment value too, so the adapter reads
`api_key_env` from the harness's own environment (`RunRequest.host_env`, a field `build_agent_env` never copies),
writes it to a new 0600 file in the step's private `opencode-config` directory, and removes it when the run ends,
whatever the outcome; a file left by a killed run is removed when the unit's next workbench is built (L4-PRV-041). The redactor already knows the variable (every `*_env` key of the config). Implement mode
sends only `options.tools` (`tools: {"*": false, <t>: true}`) because the server compiles tool JSON schemas into a
constrained-decoding grammar and refuses a large set (HTTP 400 `grammar binding failed`, intermittent; 82 tools made
prefill take minutes [V]); judge mode sends none. `reasoning: none` is the working switch (`reasoning_effort: "none"`
top level; `reasoning:{effort}`, `thinking` and `enable_thinking` are ignored by this server [V]). Probe: `auth` is the
presence of the variable (no `opencode auth list`), `quota` is skipped, `hello` first does an unauthenticated
`GET <base_url>/models` (3 s; any HTTP answer, a 401 too, means the host is up) and treats a silent host (a sleeping
laptop) as **unavailable**, so the role chain falls back, then runs the tool-less hello through the provider (about 33 s
cold: raise `availability.probe_timeout` accordingly). A mid-run `grammar binding failed` or connection error ends the
step as `error` with the detail `provider_unavailable ... retryable`. Doctor `PRV-001` appends `<profile> provider
<host:port> reachable|unreachable` (host and port only; an unreachable provider is a note, not a failure). The sandbox
network is shared for agents; the host must be reachable from the runner [V from the runner, not from inside bwrap].

#### 8.3.1 Confirmed invocations (M1 spikes, 2026-10-03)

The env lists are the **complete** child environment. Bracketed parts are optional. Labels as in
`spikes/00-summary.md` §3.

A bracketed credential variable reaches only its own profile's agent process (L4-PRV-024).
1. The adapter writes the value to a new 0600 file in the step's private directory (0700, visible only in the step's own
   agent sandbox, L4-PRV-040).
2. A `/bin/sh` loader inside the sandbox reads the file, deletes it, exports the variable and execs the CLI.
3. The value is never in any argv. bwrap's `--setenv` list is excluded too, because it is readable by any local user.

[V for `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` on GitHub-hosted runners, docs/spikes/06 finding 10.]

**L4-PRV-028** OpenCode's own providers take their key from OPENCODE_API_KEY. An `opencode` profile with `auth: api_key`, a model of OpenCode's own providers (`opencode/…` or `opencode-go/…`) and
no custom provider in its options SHALL have `OPENCODE_API_KEY` as its credential variable (L4-PRV-024), as design D16
says:
- the generated GitHub job names it;
- the probe's auth step passes on its presence and fails with `OPENCODE_API_KEY is not set` when it is unset, before
  any model call;
- the probe's hello and the agent run receive it, the run through the credential loader (never in the sandbox
  environment or in an argv);
- it is redacted by default.

A free model without `auth: api_key`, a subscription profile and a profile with a custom provider MUST be unchanged.

**L4-PRV-040** The OpenCode provider key file (L4-PRV-028, the custom-provider key) and the credential-loader file
(L4-PRV-024) SHALL be written only in the step's private directory, created with mode 0700, as new 0600 files, and removed
when the step ends, whatever its outcome. That directory lies under the hidden runner cache (L4-SEC-031) and is bound only
into its own step's agent sandbox, so no gate or agent sandbox of another step, unit or project can read the files
(sandbox-security-4).

**L4-PRV-041** When a workbench is built, the harness SHALL remove a provider key file and a credential-loader file left
in the unit's private directory by a run that was killed (a SIGKILL skips every `finally`), before any agent or gate runs.
The probe's `hello` SHALL keep its key in a new 0700 temporary directory under its working directory, which is the runner
cache in a run (hidden, L4-SEC-031) and a system temp directory in doctor (hidden by the sandbox's own `/tmp`).

On the reference runner the OpenCode user config defines a local provider `magnitude`; `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` isolation
drops it, so a profile that uses it must re-supply `provider.magnitude` in `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` [I]. The same
isolation drops the user config's `npx …@latest` MCP servers, which is intended [V, runner].

**L4-FAC-008** Profiles declare `auth: api_key | subscription`. Subscription-authenticated profiles share one stored
login per runner. A refreshable OAuth store (claude-code, codex and kiro-cli unless `auth: api_key`; opencode with
`auth: subscription`) is refreshed by whichever process finds the token expired, and two processes refreshing with the
same single-use refresh token make the loser clear the stored credentials (runner incident 2026-10-07: the login was
wiped 3 s after a CI job started, while a free-model measurement and an `l4 eval` judge shared `~/.claude`) [V]. So the
harness MUST allow **exactly one** process at a time to drive such a login, whatever `max_concurrency` says (a higher
value applies only to an `api_key` login and to adapters with no refresh token); API-key profiles default to unlimited.
The rule is enforced by one lock mechanism (`l4.agents.gate`): (1) the lock key is the **resolved credential
directory** of the CLI the harness spawns (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, Kiro's data store, under `$HOME`; symlinks
followed), never the profile name, the model or `$L4_CACHE`; every spawn environment is built from `HOME` and never
carries `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `$CODEX_HOME`, so those variables in the host environment change neither the store the
CLI drives nor the key; (2) the lock files live in one directory per OS user,
`~/.cache/l4/locks` of the user the process runs as (`$L4_LOCK_DIR` replaces it in tests), created 0700 with 0600 files,
outside the checkout and outside everything an agent sandbox can write, so a CI job, an `l4 eval`, `l4 doctor --live`,
`l4 probe` and a hand-run `l4` of the same user take the same lock; (3) every place that spawns an agent CLI against the
stored login holds the lock for the spawn: each adapter run, the whole probe ladder of a profile (selection,
`l4 probe`, `doctor --live`) and the readiness probe of `doctor`; `--version` reads no login and is exempt; (4) the
wait is bounded by `availability.login_lock_wait` (default 20m); a login still taken then is `unavailable: another
process holds the <adapter> login`: a probe skips the profile as busy, a run returns `rate_limited` with a two-minute
reset, so the next profile of the chain is selected and the busy login is not retried at once; (5) every wait is
printed (`[l4] login: waited …s for another process to finish with the <adapter> login`) and ledgered
(`availability.login_wait {tool, slots, waited_s, outcome}`); (6) a process holds at most one login lock (a second
blocking request raises, it never waits on itself); (7) lock descriptors are close-on-exec and every spawn helper
passes `close_fds`, so a detached child cannot keep a lock after its parent lets go, and a crash leaks none (flock).
The converse is not covered [I]: every spawn starts its own session, so when the holding process is killed (SIGKILL,
or SIGTERM, which `l4` does not trap) its lock is freed at once while the CLI it started may still run. A sandboxed agent
run dies with it (`bwrap --die-with-parent`, one PID namespace); an unsandboxed probe step (`auth status`, `hello`,
`codex app-server`) can outlive it by at most its probe timeout, and a `sandbox.mode: none` run by its run timeout. The
lock only serialises processes that run a harness with it: a consumer repository runs the harness its `.l4` pins, so
every repository a runner user drives (and every out-of-CI driver that calls its `.l4/bin/l4`) needs `l4 upgrade`.
`doctor` ENV-014 warns when a profile's stored login looks wiped (claude: `refreshToken` empty or `expiresAt` 0; codex:
`refresh_token` empty; kiro: an empty `refresh_token` in the data store [I]) and prints the re-login command for the runner
user. The `quota` probe step applies to subscription auth and to OpenRouter-backed `api_key` profiles (zero-cost
`/api/v1/credits` + `/api/v1/key`, L4-AVL-001); other API-key profiles rely on HTTP 429 signals and cost budgets. With `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` the plan is unknown (`subscriptionType` is absent [V, spikes/05]). For
codex `api_key` the quota step is skipped (app-server returns `-32600` [V, spikes/05]). Logins made by a human as
another user are moved, not copied, to the runner user (`scripts/runner/prereqs.sh` PRQ-17), because two copies of one
OAuth refresh token race on refresh and one stops working [I].

**L4-FAC-007** Adapter-specific facts marked [U] above MUST be pinned by contract tests that replay recorded raw
outputs of the named CLI version, and re-checked by `doctor --live` (`LIVE-*`). Recordings live in
`tests/fixtures/recorded/<tool>/<version>/`. A runner CLI whose version differs from the recorded one only in the patch
component runs with doctor `LIVE-005` warning `unrecorded version` (both versions named), and the ledger records
`availability.unrecorded_version {role, profile, adapter, version, recorded}` at selection; it is not refused [I, decision]. A CLI whose major version differs from the adapter's supported major is refused at the
`binary` step with a named reason (L4-OCG-002); only a patch drift within the supported major runs with the
`unrecorded version` warning. Recorded versions are compared within one major (L4-OCV-012).
The packaged `recorded_versions.json` is generated from the fixture tree (`python -m l4.recordedversions --write`) and a
unit test fails when it drifts. (The reference
runner has OpenCode 1.18.34 against 1.18.33 recordings [V, runner].)

**L4-OCG-001 The major version is read from every opencode --version.** The harness SHALL derive the major version of
an agent CLI from the first version in its `--version` output with one shared function that accepts both `1.18.34` and
`opencode v2.0.32` [V]. The supported major of the `opencode` adapter SHALL be the major of the pinned
`OPENCODE_VERSION` (1). The probe `binary` step, doctor ENV-004, doctor LIVE-005, `l4 doctor --fix` and
`scripts/runner/prereqs.sh` PRQ-11 SHALL compare that major whenever they read an `opencode --version`, whether or not
the profile sets `min_version`. Output that holds no version SHALL stay the existing "did not report a version"
failure.

**L4-OCG-002 An unsupported major fails closed with a named reason.** When the major of the `opencode` binary differs
from the supported major, the probe `binary` step SHALL fail with the reason `opencode <version> is OpenCode v<major>;
this profile runs v1 (opencode-ai 1.x): install opencode-ai@<pin> (l4 doctor --fix installs it user-locally) or set options.cli_major: 2 to run OpenCode 2 (experimental)`, and the `auth`, `quota` and `hello` steps SHALL NOT run. The failure SHALL never
be a warning and never `transient`; like every free-step failure it is not cached. A passing `binary` step's detail
SHALL carry `major`. Doctor ENV-004 SHALL report the profile as failing with the same reason, with the existing chain
severity of a failing CLI. Doctor LIVE-005 SHALL report it as a failure with severity `error` before, and instead of,
the recorded-version comparison. `l4 doctor --live` (LIVE-001) SHALL report the same reason through the probe. The major SHALL be read from the first `N.N.N` that the callers count as the reported version, whatever precedes it (`x1.2.3`, `opencode_2.0.32`), and ENV-004 SHALL fail a gated CLI whose output holds no version.

**L4-OCG-003 A run or hello rejected for a v1 flag is unsupported_version.** `FailureClass` SHALL gain
`unsupported_version`. A hello whose exit code is not 0 and whose stderr matches `Unrecognized flag: --(pure|dir)\b`
[V] SHALL fail with the class `unsupported_version` and a reason beginning `unsupported_version:`. That class SHALL
NOT be remembered in the probe cache: only `other` and `auth` are, so installing v1 takes effect at the next probe. A
run SHALL read the tail (the last 8 KiB) of its stderr file. A run whose exit code is not 0, that has no `error`
event, and whose stderr matches the same pattern SHALL end with status `error` and a detail beginning
`unsupported_version:`. It SHALL never be marked retryable.

**L4-OCG-004 Provisioning replaces a wrong major with the pinned v1.** `l4 doctor --fix` SHALL treat an `opencode`
whose major differs from the supported major as not satisfied. It SHALL plan the pinned install with the reason `found
<version> (OpenCode v<major>), need opencode-ai 1.x (pinned <pin>)`, install into the harness's npm prefix, and link
`~/.local/bin/opencode`. The agent link step of a gated adapter SHALL NOT replace an existing path that is not a
symlink: the action fails and names the path and the manual command. The other links the harness makes (Node,
`laya-serve`, other agents) SHALL keep their current behaviour. After the install, the major of the `opencode` the harness
path resolves SHALL be checked, and a wrong one fails the action naming the resolved path. `scripts/runner/prereqs.sh`
PRQ-11 SHALL pass only an `opencode` of major 1 at least the pin. A v2 still first on the runner's login PATH after
the apply SHALL be reported FAILED with its path. PRQ-15 SHALL run `opencode models` only when PRQ-11's check passes.

**L4-OCG-005 A kiro-cli of another major than 2 is refused with a named reason.** The supported major of the `kiro-cli`
adapter SHALL be the major of the pinned `KIRO_VERSION` (2), in `SUPPORTED_MAJORS` beside `opencode`. Every caller of
L4-OCG-001 and L4-OCG-002 SHALL apply it to `kiro-cli --version` whether or not the profile sets `min_version`: the
probe `binary` step SHALL fail without running `auth`, `quota` or `hello`; doctor ENV-004 SHALL report the profile as
failing with the chain severity of a failing CLI, and SHALL fail closed on a `kiro-cli` whose `--version` holds no
version with `kiro-cli reports no version, so its Kiro CLI major cannot be checked`; doctor LIVE-005 SHALL report it
with severity `error` before, and instead of, the recorded-version comparison. The reason SHALL be `kiro-cli <version>
is Kiro CLI <major>; L4 runs Kiro CLI 2: install kiro-cli <pin> (in CI l4 doctor --ci --fix installs it; l4 doctor
prints the command for this machine); Kiro CLI 3 support comes in a later L4 release`, with the effective pin
(L4-PRV-045). The wording of every OpenCode text SHALL stay unchanged. Under `l4 doctor --ci --fix` a `kiro-cli` of
another major SHALL be `planned` with `found <version> (Kiro CLI <major>), need kiro-cli 2.x (pinned <pin>)` and
replaced by the pin (L4-PRV-042); without `--ci` it SHALL be `manual` with the same reason and the command, and its
files SHALL stay unchanged. After an install, a `kiro-cli` that still reports another major SHALL fail the action naming
the resolved path. `scripts/runner/prereqs.sh` PRQ-12 SHALL report a `kiro-cli` of another major as not satisfied,
naming `Kiro CLI <major>; L4 runs Kiro CLI 2` and the pin. [D: Kiro's CLI 3.0 makes V3 the default engine and, in V3,
`KIRO_HOME` also holds the sign-ins; V: the judge refuses a stream on any engine but v2; nothing of 3.x is recorded.]

**L4-OCG-006 A copilot of another major than 1 is refused with a named reason.** The supported major of the `copilot-cli` adapter SHALL be the major of the pinned `COPILOT_VERSION` (1), in
`SUPPORTED_MAJORS`. Every caller of L4-OCG-001 and L4-OCG-002 SHALL apply it to `copilot --version` whether or not the
profile sets `min_version`: the probe `binary` step SHALL fail without running `auth`, `quota` or `hello`; doctor
ENV-004 and LIVE-005 SHALL report it; `l4 doctor --ci --fix` SHALL replace it with the pin and a person's `l4 doctor
--fix` SHALL leave it as a `manual` action; PRQ-22 SHALL not accept it. The reason SHALL be `copilot <version> is
Copilot CLI <major>; L4 runs Copilot CLI 1: install copilot <pin> (in CI l4 doctor --ci --fix installs it; l4 doctor
prints the command for this machine); Copilot CLI <major> support comes in a later L4 release`, with the effective pin.
The OpenCode and Kiro texts SHALL stay unchanged.

**L4-OCV-001 A profile opts in to OpenCode v2 with options.cli_major.** An `opencode` profile SHALL select its CLI major
with `options.cli_major`, `1` or `2`, default `1`; the value SHALL be the integer 1 or 2, and any other value SHALL be a
configuration error. The harness SHALL NOT switch majors automatically, because the two majors differ in success
detection, in `ask` handling and in the error schema, and a silent switch would change what `ok` means in the middle of
a plan [V, `docs/plan/opencode-v2.md` rows 10, 13, 14]. A `cli_major: 1` profile runs `opencode` and requires major 1
(L4-OCG-002, whose reason ends `or set options.cli_major: 2 to run OpenCode 2 (experimental)`). A `cli_major: 2` profile
runs `opencode2` and requires major 2: its `binary` step SHALL fail otherwise with `opencode2 <version> is OpenCode
v<major>; this profile runs v2 (options.cli_major: 2, @opencode/cli 2.x): install @opencode/cli@<pin> (l4 doctor --fix
installs it user-locally) or remove options.cli_major`, and the `auth`, `quota` and `hello` steps SHALL NOT run. At load,
a `cli_major: 2` profile SHALL be refused when it sets `options.provider` ([U] the custom provider's `{file:}` key form
on v2 is not recorded; fallback `provider_refused`), when its model's provider is `azure-cognitive-services` or
`google-vertex-anthropic` (v2 renamed them to `azure` and `google-vertex` [D]; the message names the new id), or when
`options.tools` names `list` (v2 has no such permission action [D]). A profile without `cli_major: 2` SHALL be refused
when it sets `options.steps`. A message SHALL never repeat a configured value. The v2 adapter SHALL be experimental, so
the ledger records `agent.experimental` once per profile. Version 0.4.28 ships it experimental and not checked against a
live run (L4-OCV-013).

**L4-OCV-002 OpenCode v2 is installed in its own prefix as opencode2.** The harness SHALL pin `@opencode/cli` at
`OPENCODE2_VERSION` (`2.0.32`). Installing `@opencode/cli` into the v1 prefix silently takes `.bin/opencode` [V], so the
harness SHALL install it only when a `cli_major: 2` profile is in a role chain, into `$L4_HOME/npm-opencode2`, and SHALL
link only that prefix's `opencode2` as `~/.local/bin/opencode2`, never over a regular file. That prefix's `.bin` SHALL NOT
be on the harness path, because it holds an `opencode` (v2) that must never be found as `opencode`. `catalog_pins` SHALL
include `agent:opencode2` and `npm:opencode2`, and the agent-CLI cache key's `clis` list SHALL include `opencode2` when a
`cli_major: 2` profile needs it. `ci.cli_versions` SHALL accept the key `opencode2` with a version of major 2 only
(L4-OCG-001), and the exact pin and doctor ENV-015 SHALL apply to `opencode2` as to every agent CLI (L4-PRV-045).
`scripts/runner/prereqs.sh` SHALL pin `OPENCODE2_VERSION` in its top block and install it in PRQ-20, behind
`--with-opencode2`. The sandbox binds `$L4_HOME` read-only already, so the package is visible to the agent.

**L4-OCV-003 Every OpenCode v2 call is standalone with a private state directory.** Every `opencode2` invocation the
harness starts (run, hello, `auth list`, `session export`) SHALL carry `--standalone` and SHALL get an empty
`XDG_STATE_HOME` of its own. Without `--standalone` the first client's per-user daemon serves later clients with its own
environment and configuration [V, reproduced twice]. One argv builder SHALL build every v2 argv, SHALL put
`--standalone` right after the subcommand words and SHALL refuse a subcommand outside `run`, `auth list` and `session
export`. The harness SHALL NOT start `opencode2 debug config`, `serve`, `service`, `api`, `pair` or `models`.
`XDG_DATA_HOME` SHALL NOT be redirected, because it holds the credentials and `opencode.db`, which the export reads.
A directory the harness makes for a call SHALL be made empty and 0700 even when the agent planted an entry at its path:
a symlink or a file there SHALL be unlinked (a link is never followed) and a directory removed with its content, and
making it SHALL NOT raise.

**L4-OCV-004 The v2 run has no v1-only flags and keeps the v1 isolation.** A v2 run SHALL be `opencode2 run --standalone
--format json -m <provider/model> --title "l4 <role> <stem>"`, with the worktree (implement) or the empty judge directory
(judge) as cwd and the prompt on stdin, followed by EOF. A v2 hello SHALL be the same with `--title "l4 hello"` and the
hello prompt as the last argument, in an empty scratch directory with stdin closed. The `auth list` step and the export
SHALL also run with stdin closed: OpenCode 2 waits without output while stdin stays open, even with the prompt as an
argument [V, 2.0.32 and 2.1.4], so every v2 call SHALL see EOF. No v2 argv SHALL carry `--pure` or `--dir`, which v2
rejects [V]. The environment SHALL add to the allow-list an empty per-step `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, the private
`XDG_STATE_HOME`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS`,
`OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS` (v2 ignores it [V, binary strings]; it is harmless), `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`
(each `1`) and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`. Because `~/.config/opencode` is writable by every sandboxed agent run
(`CREDENTIAL_PATHS`) and so is the step's result directory, no harness call SHALL read a configuration the agent could
have written: the `auth list` step, which runs on the host outside the sandbox, SHALL run in its scratch directory with an
empty 0700 `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, the empty state directory, the disable switches and the hello's `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`
(`XDG_DATA_HOME` stays untouched), and the export SHALL run with a config directory of its own, created after the run
(`<step dir>/opencode2-export-config`), not the run's. [U] Whether the repository's guidance files (`AGENTS.md`, `.agents/skills`,
`.claude/skills`, `.opencode/skills`) reach a real prompt under these switches was not seen with a key; fallback
`deny_skill_and_mask`: the switches, a `skill` rule at the refuse value, the empty judge directory and the L4-SEC-005
masks.

**L4-OCV-005 The v2 configuration is native and keeps today's effective rules.** For a v2 profile,
`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` SHALL be the native v2 shape: `$schema`, `snapshots: false`, `share: "disabled"`, `update:
"disable"`, an ordered `permissions` array (the last matching rule wins, so the broad rules come first) and
`agents.build.steps`. It SHALL NOT contain `permission`, `tools`, `snapshot`, `autoupdate`, or a `list` or `doom_loop`
rule. v2 normalises today's v1 configuration without a warning [V, all six L4 shapes], but its normalisation of
`options.tools` allows `shell` again after the tools map's deny-all [V], so native is the form that keeps the intent. The
refuse value is `ask` for an `opencode/` model and `deny` otherwise (a removed tool gets a 403 from the free tier [V for
`read` and `shell`, I for `skill` and `subagent`]). The rules SHALL be:
- judge mode: `*:* deny`; for an `opencode/` model also `read:* ask` and `shell:* ask` (a full deny gets a 403 on v2 [V]);
- implement mode: `edit`, `read`, `glob`, `grep` and `shell` allowed; `shell` denied for `git commit*`, `git push*`,
  `git reset*` and `git checkout*`; `external_directory:* deny` before the allows for the private result directory;
  `webfetch`, `websearch` and `question` denied; `skill` and `subagent` (two v2 actions that v1 never named) at the refuse
  value [I];
- `options.tools`: `*:* deny` first, then the listed tools' v2 actions allowed (`bash` is `shell`; `edit`, `write` and
  `patch` are `edit`), then the git denies when `shell` is allowed and the rules above. [U] Whether a v2 deny drops the
  tool's schema from the request is not recorded; fallback `tools_by_permission` (a deny-all plus allows, no v1 `tools`
  map).
A read-only request SHALL raise `AdapterError` (L4-OCV-014). v1's configuration SHALL stay byte-identical.

**L4-OCV-006 Each v2 role has a step bound and a bounded run is never ok.** The v2 configuration SHALL set
`agents.build.steps` to `options.steps.judge` (default 3, allowed 2 to 20) for every judge-mode call and the hello, and
to `options.steps.implement` (default 200, allowed 10 to 2000) for an implementer step. Three is one answering step, one
tolerated rejected attempt and v2's forced tool-less summary step [D, V with `steps: 3`]; 200 is about ten times the
largest tool-call count recorded (19) and about fourteen times the largest step count (14), both from small spike
repositories, so the value is per profile and the wall-clock timeout stays the primary bound. [U] With `steps: 1` the
only step may be the forced summary; fallback: the judge floor is 2. A run whose count of `step_start` events reaches
the bound [V: one per step] SHALL NOT be `ok`: it SHALL be `permission_blocked` when it recorded a denial, else `error`
with a detail beginning `step_bound:`, whatever the export says. [U] The `outcome` of a bounded run is not recorded;
fallback `not_ok_named`. A v1 profile SHALL get no bound.

**L4-OCV-007 v2 status comes from the exit code, the error event, the bound and the exported outcome.** The first rule
that applies SHALL decide: a timed-out run is `timeout`, and an interrupted one `cancelled` ([U] SIGINT's exit code is not
recorded; fallback `harness_interrupt`: the harness's own flag decides, not the exit code); an `error` event is
classified by L4-OCV-009; an exit code other than 0 is `error`, with a detail beginning `unsupported_version:` when the stderr
tail matches the rule of L4-OCG-003, else `opencode2 exited with code <n>`; a run at its bound is decided by L4-OCV-006. Otherwise the run SHALL be `ok`
only when `opencode2 session export --standalone <id>` (stdin closed, 60 s, the run's wrap and environment with a state
directory and a config directory of its own, no credential loader) reports `info.outcome` `succeeded` and the result attaches: the judge's JSON
reply, sliced from the text after the last tool call with the one shared slicer (a v2 judge may write prose around a
rejected attempt), or the implementer's result file. A final `step_finish` SHALL NOT be required, because only 3 of 16
recorded finished runs emit it [V; cause I]. Any other `outcome` SHALL be `error` `opencode2 session outcome <value>`
([U] the other values are not recorded; fallback `not_ok_named`), and so SHALL an `info.outcome` that is present and not a
string (the value as JSON, cut to 80 characters); only a missing `outcome` leaves the export unavailable (below). The export is saved beside the raw events as
`<stem>.export.json` and is published redacted with the stream (L4-OBS-002); a session id outside
`[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` is never exported. When the export is unavailable (no session id, exit other than 0, timeout,
not JSON, no `info.outcome`), the v1 rule SHALL decide: a last `step_finish` reason `stop` attaches the result, denials
give `permission_blocked`, else `error` `opencode2 session export failed (<why>) and the stream has no final stop`. [U]
How often `step_finish` is missing on long runs is not recorded; fallback `export_decides`. A run that a v1 flag
rejected SHALL keep L4-OCG-003.

**L4-OCV-008 v2 usage comes from the export.** For a v2 run with an export that holds an assistant message, input,
output and cache-read tokens SHALL be the sums over the export's assistant messages, cost SHALL be `info.cost` (else the
messages' sum), and `context_peak_tokens` SHALL be the largest `input + cache.read + cache.write` of one assistant
message. Without an export, or with an export that holds no assistant message, the stream's `step_finish` parts SHALL be
summed as in v1, which may be partial. When both exist, each field SHALL be the larger of the two (cost and context peak:
the larger of the values that are not null, null only when both are): the export may raise usage over the stream's
sums, never lower it, because the agent can write the `opencode.db` the export reads. [U] The recorded export has one assistant message; whether a multi-step run exports
one message per step is not recorded; fallback `sum_messages` (the sum above, which equals `info.tokens` for one message).

**L4-OCV-009 v2 errors, limits and denials are read from the v2 shapes only.** A v2 `error` event is `{type, message,
status, response.body}` [V]. It SHALL be classified as: `auth` for `status` 401 or 403, `type` `provider.auth`, or the
existing auth wording (both recorded free-tier 403s, for denied tools and for a flagged network, are `auth` [V]; [U] the
OAuth refresh failure text is not recorded, fallback `auth_by_status`); a `credits` limit for `status` 402 (source
`opencode2.status`); a `rate_limit` limit with no reset for `status` 429 (source `opencode2.status`); `error` with `,
retryable` for `status` of 500 or more; otherwise `error` `opencode2 reported an error (<type>, status <n>)`. [U] The 402
and 429 shapes and where `retry-after` lives are not recorded; fallback `status_only`: the body, the headers and the
message are never read for a reset, and no text fallback runs for a v2 payload, so a 429 gets the default cool-down. A
denial SHALL be a `tool_use` in error whose text starts with `Permission denied:` or contains `cannot ask the user for
permission` [V]; each gives `{tool_name, tool_input}`.

**L4-OCV-010 v2 auth presence comes from auth list in JSON.** For a provider that `OPENCODE_API_KEY` does not decide
(L4-PRV-028) and that is not free, the v2 auth step SHALL run `opencode2 auth list --standalone --format json`, whose
answer is `[{id, name, connections: [{type, name, status?}]}]` [V]. The provider SHALL count as present when an entry's
`id` equals the model's provider and it has a connection whose status is not `needs_auth`. A `needs_auth` connection
SHALL fail the step with `opencode2 reports <provider> needs auth (<message>)`. Unparsable output SHALL fail the step as
an unrecognised answer. The call SHALL be isolated like the hello (L4-OCV-004). Presence only, as in v1: the hello stays
the authoritative check.

**L4-OCV-011 A v2 reply's leaked leading reasoning is stripped.** On v2 only, a text part that holds `</think>` before any
`<think>` SHALL lose everything up to and including the first `</think>`, and SHALL then be trimmed, before the hello
compares its reply and before the judge reply is sliced. A text with an opening `<think>` first, or with no tag, SHALL be
left alone, and a reply that is only reasoning still fails. One of six recorded v2 hellos was `…</think>L4-OK` [V once;
cause I]. [U] The cause, and whether the leak recurs, are not recorded; fallback `strip_leading_think`.

**L4-OCV-012 The probe, the doctor and the recorded versions follow the profile's major.** The probe, doctor ENV-004
and doctor LIVE-005 SHALL check the profile's own binary and major (`opencode2` and 2 for a v2 profile). The probe's
`hello` SHALL map errors as L4-OCV-009 does, SHALL need no export and SHALL pass on exit code 0, no `error` event and the
reply `L4-OK`. LIVE-005 SHALL compare a version only with the recorded versions of the same major
(`tests/fixtures/recorded/opencode/2.0.32/` holds the v2 recordings).

**L4-OCV-013 Each unverified v2 fact sits on a named fallback until a live run records it.** Each [U] fact of the v2
adapter SHALL ship with its named fallback, a unit test that pins that fallback by name, and the [U] marker in this
specification. No parser for a [U] shape SHALL be written before its fixture is recorded. The adapter SHALL stay
experimental until a live CI run on the owner's dummy repository, with a real `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, has recorded a fixture
or a LIVE check for every row; a fallback SHALL be replaced only by behaviour pinned by such a recording. The rows:

| # | [U] fact | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | the 402 and 429 shapes, and where `retry-after` lives | `status_only` (L4-OCV-009) |
| U2 | whether a v2 deny drops the tool's schema | `tools_by_permission` (L4-OCV-005) |
| U3 | the custom provider's `{file:}` key | `provider_refused` (L4-OCV-001) |
| U4 | the OAuth refresh failure text | `auth_by_status` (L4-OCV-009) |
| U5 | how often `step_finish` is missing on long runs | `export_decides` (L4-OCV-007) |
| U6 | guidance isolation in a real prompt | `deny_skill_and_mask` (L4-OCV-004, L4-SEC-005) |
| U7 | `outcome` values other than `succeeded`, and a bounded run's outcome | `not_ok_named` (L4-OCV-006, L4-OCV-007) |
| U8 | v1 and v2 sharing one `opencode.db` over time | `live_coexistence` (no code: try v2 only on a runner user no v1 profile shares) |
| U9 | the `</think>` cause, and whether `steps: 1` makes step 1 the summary | `strip_leading_think` (L4-OCV-011) and the judge floor 2 (L4-OCV-006) |
| U10 | SIGINT's exit code | `harness_interrupt` (L4-OCV-007) |
| U11 | a multi-step export's message layout | `sum_messages` (L4-OCV-008) |

Version 0.4.28 ships the adapter experimental, before that live run (design E8); every row above is open. The next
release that runs it replaces a fallback with a parser only for a row whose fixture the run recorded, and changes that
row's [U] to [V] here.

**L4-OCV-014 An OpenCode v2 profile does not serve the delegate in this release.** The read-only mode
(`PermissionPolicy("read_only")`) exists only for the delegate (L4-DLG-015, L4-DLG-016), and nothing of it is recorded on
v2: the read tools' rules, `lsp`, the Zen `bash` sentinel and the masked instruction files. A `cli_major: 2` profile in
`roles.delegate` SHALL be a configuration error at load, whose message names the profile, `roles.delegate` and
L4-DLG-016, and says to remove the profile from the role or to use a `cli_major: 1` profile. The v2 adapter SHALL refuse a
read-only request with `AdapterError` before it starts anything. A `cli_major: 2` profile in the other roles SHALL be
unaffected.

**L4-FAC-009 Strict schema for OpenAI-strict backends.** For native schema mode on Codex, and on any OpenAI-strict
backend [I for `openai-chat`], the adapter MUST send a strictified copy of the canonical schema:
`additionalProperties:false` on every object, every property in `required`, optional properties nullable, `$id`
removed. It MUST map `null` back to absent before validating against the canonical schema. A rejection with
`invalid_json_schema` is `RunResult.status=error` (configuration), never quota and never retried. [V, spikes/03: the
verbatim schema failed with `turn.failed` `invalid_json_schema`, exit 1; the strictified copy
`tests/fixtures/recorded/codex/0.160.0/implementer-result.strict.schema.json` gave 12/12 valid results]

#### 8.3.2 Kiro as a judge, a clarifier and a readiness reviewer (KJD)

kiro-cli answers as a judge, a clarifier and a readiness reviewer: tool-less, with the prompt on stdin and a validated
JSON reply, its credits recorded, its vendor taken from its model, and its failures read for what they are. By default it
runs Kiro's `auto` model, whose possible vendors are the makers of the models Kiro may route it to. The facts behind the
requirements were measured on kiro-cli 2.32.0 with no model call (`openspec/changes/kiro-judge/design.md` §2.2, R1 to
R22) and are labelled in §8.3 (**[V]** observed, **[D]** Kiro's documentation, **[I]** inferred, **[U]** not checked).
The delegate does not take a kiro-cli profile in this change.

**L4-KJD-001 A Kiro judge runs a tool-less harness agent with no trust flag.** In judge mode (`PermissionPolicy("judge")`) the kiro-cli adapter SHALL write, before each call, a fresh `KIRO_HOME` at
`<step private dir>/kiro-home` that holds only `agents/l4-judge-<12 hex>.json` and `settings/cli.json`. The agent file
SHALL have `tools: []`, `allowedTools: []`, `toolAliases: {}`, `mcpServers: {}`, `includeMcpJson: false`,
`resources: []`, `hooks: {}`, `toolsSettings: {}`, `prompt: null` and `model` equal to the profile's model, or `auto`
when the profile has none (L4-KJD-012). The settings file SHALL be `{"chat.disableInheritingDefaultResources": true,
"chat.agentEngine": "v2", "chat.enableAutoAgentUpgrade": false, "app.disableAutoupdates": true}`. The argv SHALL be
exactly `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive --v2 --agent <name> --model <model> --output-format stream-json`, where
`<model>` is the agent file's `model`: it SHALL NOT carry `--trust-tools` with any value, `--trust-all-tools` or the
prompt. The judge SHALL run this agent whatever `options.agent` says, in the empty `judge-cwd`, with `KIRO_HOME` set and
`KIRO_LOG_LEVEL` unset. No permission-policy table SHALL hold a trust list for the judge.

**L4-KJD-002 A Kiro judge gets its prompt on stdin.** A judge-mode kiro-cli call SHALL pass the whole prompt on standard input followed by EOF, with no positional argument,
and SHALL NOT apply the one-argument size limit to it. An empty prompt SHALL be refused before the spawn. The
implementer and read-only modes SHALL keep their argv transport.

**L4-KJD-003 A Kiro judge's reply is a validated JSON object from the stream.** For a judge-mode run that exits 0 with `runFinished.status` `success`, the adapter SHALL take the reply text from
`runFinished.finalText`, or from the joined `agent_message_chunk` text when `finalTextTruncated` is true, slice it from
the first `{` to the last `}`, parse and validate it against the request's schema with the helper the opencode judge
uses. A valid object SHALL be the run's `structured` result with status `ok`. A missing or invalid object SHALL give a
detail that starts with the structured-output marker (with the rejected object kept for the repair), so that the judge
takes its deterministic repair and then at most one repair call; a stop reason other than `end_turn` SHALL be named in
that detail. A judge run that holds a `tool_call` update, that has a `runStarted` whose engine is not `v2` (every
`runStarted` counts, and one that names no engine is not `v2`), that holds a `runError`, or whose served model
contradicts a pinned model (L4-KJD-015) SHALL end as `error` and SHALL NOT give a verdict.

**L4-KJD-004 The credits of a Kiro judge or clarifier call are recorded, never as dollars.** When a judge call's usage carries credits, the verifier SHALL add `credits` to its `verify.judge` event and SHALL write
`budget.cost{credits, credits_source: "kiro.stream", profile, role: "judge"}`; the clarifier SHALL write the same event
with `role: "clarifier"`. Credits SHALL NOT be added to any dollar total.

**L4-KJD-005 A kiro-cli profile's vendor is its model's family.** The vendor of a kiro-cli profile with a pinned model SHALL be the vendor of its model's family (`claude-` anthropic,
`gpt-` and `o<digit>` openai, `gemini-` google, `deepseek-` deepseek, `glm-` zhipu, `minimax-` minimax, `qwen`
alibaba, `kimi-` moonshot), with provenance `declared`; a model of no known family SHALL keep the declared vendor. A
kiro-cli profile with no model or `auto` SHALL be routed (L4-KJD-014): its vendors SHALL be the possible vendors of
L4-KJD-013 with provenance `routed`, and a `vendor:` on it SHALL be ignored (it loads, and doctor notes that it is
ignored). A kiro-cli profile whose `vendor:` contradicts its pinned model's family SHALL fail to load, naming the
family's vendor; `vendor: unknown` (in any letter case) makes no claim, so it SHALL load and the family's vendor SHALL
count. Under `verifier.independence: different_model`, models SHALL be compared after normalisation that
also folds a `.` between digits to `-`.

**L4-KJD-006 Kiro authentication, configuration and quota failures are classified.** A kiro-cli run SHALL end with status `auth` when a `runError` message says the bearer token is invalid, the token is
invalid or expired, access is denied, or the user is not logged in, or when it exits 1 with no stream event and its
output says that it needs authentication or `kiro-cli login`. An exit 4 or a `runError` at stage `init` or `input`
SHALL be `error` with the stage in the detail. Throttling and used-up credits SHALL keep their rules and come first. A
`/usage` answer that says the usage could not be retrieved for an authentication reason SHALL fail the quota step as an
auth failure, not as an unrecognised text.

**L4-KJD-007 The hello of a kiro-cli profile runs the judge invocation.** The hello probe of every kiro-cli profile SHALL run the tool-less harness agent of L4-KJD-001 from a private
`KIRO_HOME` in a temporary directory, with the argv of L4-KJD-001 followed by the hello prompt as its last argument
and an empty working directory, and SHALL read the reply text of L4-KJD-003. A profile with no model SHALL run it with
`model: auto` in the agent file and `--model auto`. Its failures SHALL be classified by L4-KJD-006. A hello whose
stream holds a `runError` SHALL fail with the reason `kiro-cli reported runError (<stage>): <message>`, the message
redacted (no e-mail, ARN, account, profile, request or session id, no path, no token shape; whitespace folded) and cut
to 200 characters, so that the next run shows why; a `runError` with no message keeps the stage alone. Observed on
kiro-cli 2.32.0: a pinned model id the account does not have fails the prompt with a `runError` at stage `prompt`, and
the profile is skipped like any failed hello.

**L4-KJD-008 kiro-cli serves the roles that use the tool-less judge contract.** kiro-cli SHALL be one of the adapters that serve `roles.judges` (step 9 and the plan-readiness review),
`roles.clarifier`, the `s1_judge` stand-in, the escalation keeper and the step-9 preflight: it SHALL be in `JUDGE_ADAPTERS` (`l4/config/roles.py`), so that the load check of L4-CFG-006 passes a kiro-cli profile in `roles.judges`, `roles.verifier_agent`, `roles.clarifier` and `roles.s1_judge`.

**L4-KJD-009 Doctor checks Kiro judge profiles.** Doctor CFG-011 SHALL check the kiro-cli profiles of `roles.judges` and `roles.clarifier`. A profile with no model or
`model: auto` SHALL NOT fail the check: its line SHALL name `auto`, its possible vendors and their source (the latest
recorded model listing with its date, or the built-in set; the built-in set of a profile that has no probe recorded
yet, as on a fresh runner where doctor runs before any probe, reads `built-in (no listing recorded yet)`, and one whose
listing failed reads `built-in`), and SHALL say that a pinned model makes the served model checkable. A pinned profile's line SHALL name its model and vendor. Every line SHALL say that the profile runs a
tool-less harness agent with the prompt on stdin and no trust flag. CFG-011 SHALL warn for such a profile that sets
`options.agent`, or whose `min_version` is unset or below `2.32.0`. For every kiro-cli profile that a role names, a
`vendor:` on a profile with no model or `auto` SHALL be noted in the message as ignored, without failing the check.

**L4-KJD-010 Kiro judge behaviour is pinned by recorded fixtures and a replay scenario.** The harness SHALL keep the kiro-cli 2.32.0 shapes of this change under `tests/fixtures/recorded/kiro-cli/2.32.0/`,
with a README that says how each was made and which one is synthetic or reconstructed until the live run replaces it.
The simulation SHALL be able to replay a judge's stream through the real kiro-cli adapter, and the scenario
`happy-kiro-judge` SHALL pass.

**L4-KJD-011 A Kiro judge is proven live on the owner's dummy repository.** The change SHALL be proven in CI on the owner's dummy repository, never on a consumer, with a non-Anthropic implementer
(an opencode-go DeepSeek profile that declares `vendor: deepseek`) in two legs: a kiro-cli judge with no model (`auto`,
the default) and a kiro-cli judge pinned to `claude-sonnet-5.5`. Each leg SHALL reach a verdict from the kiro-cli
judge. The evidence under `docs/live/kiro-judge/` SHALL hold, per leg, the redacted judge stream, the `verify.judge`
and `budget.cost` events, the independence line, the CLI version, the `model_id` of the run's session file, any
fallback notice and any standard-error warning about the model, and the answers to the open kiro-cli questions of the
change's design, among them whether `chat --list-models --format json` carries a status field. The CI job SHALL NOT run
`kiro-cli whoami` and SHALL NOT print account data. The recorded judge stream SHALL replace the synthetic fixture, and
the recorded listing the reconstructed one.

**L4-KJD-012 A kiro-cli profile with no model runs auto.** A kiro-cli profile with no `model` SHALL run Kiro's `auto` model, passed explicitly as `--model auto`, in every mode:
judge, clarifier, readiness review, hello, implementer and read-only. A `model` that is `auto` in any letter case SHALL
be passed as `auto`. A pinned model SHALL be passed as it is. An implementer step that runs a configured
`options.agent` SHALL also get `--model auto` when its profile has no model.

**L4-KJD-013 The possible vendors of auto come from Kiro's model list.** For a kiro-cli profile on `auto`, the probe's `auth` step SHALL, after the login check passes (also when a credential
variable decides it), list the models once with `kiro-cli chat --list-models --format json` in the profile's probe
environment with a private `KIRO_HOME` (the login stays in the CLI data store) and within the step timeout, and SHALL
record in that step's result, cached with the other probe results, the possible vendors, the
Active model ids and the source `listed`. The possible vendors and the model ids SHALL be the union of the listing's
and the built-in set's, so that a vendor Kiro removed from the Active list, or a restricted listing, never shrinks the
set. Only the listing's `models` list SHALL be read: a top-level key beside it (kiro-cli 2.32.0 adds
`"default_model": "auto"`) SHALL change nothing. A listed model SHALL be Experimental when its `description` contains
`experimental`, `preview` or `excluded model` in any letter case; `auto` SHALL be skipped; every other listed model,
one with no description included, SHALL be Active. The possible vendors SHALL be the makers of the Active models by the
family table of L4-KJD-005; an Active model of no known family SHALL add `unknown`. When the listing fails (a non-zero
exit, a timeout, no JSON object with a `models` list, or no Active model), the `auth` step SHALL still pass and SHALL
record the built-in set (vendors `anthropic`, `minimax` and `zhipu` and the Active ids of the kiro-cli 2.32.0 listing
of 2026-10-19) with the source `built-in` and the reason; `l4 probe` and doctor SHALL say which source counts. A
pinned profile SHALL NOT be listed. The probe SHALL keep nothing of `whoami` but whether a login is present: never the
account e-mail.

**L4-KJD-014 An auto profile is independent only of vendors Kiro cannot route it to.** A kiro-cli profile on `auto` that reports no served model (L4-KJD-015) SHALL have provenance `routed`, and its vendors
SHALL be its possible vendors: those recorded by that profile's latest probe, whatever their age, else the built-in
set. Wherever the independence rule applies (the step-9 judges, `roles.verifier_agent`, the escalation keeper and the
step-9 preflight), a profile that is not routed SHALL have its one vendor, and:
- under `different_vendor`, a judge SHALL be vetoed for a unit when its vendors and any implementer's vendors share a
  vendor, or either holds `unknown`;
- under `different_model`, when the judge or an implementer is routed, the judge SHALL be vetoed when the other
  party's model, normalised and taken after its last `/`, is among the routed party's normalised Active ids, when the
  other party's vendor is unknown, or when both are routed;
- after `select_judge` selects a routed judge, it SHALL check that judge again against the set its own probe recorded,
  and SHALL skip it and select the next judge when that set vetoes it.
When the judge is independent and any party is routed, the independence status SHALL be `routed (unverified)`; with no
routed party, `declared (unverified)` and `verified` keep their meaning. A routed party SHALL read `<profile> routed:
<vendors, sorted, comma-separated> (auto)` in the independence line and SHALL carry its possible vendors in the
independence record. The clarifier, the readiness review and the `s1_judge` stand-in have no implementer to be
independent of and SHALL serve an `auto` profile as any other.

**L4-KJD-015 The served model of a Kiro judge run.** The kiro-cli adapter SHALL report the served model
(`model_resolved`) of a judge-mode run on `auto` when the run's session file `<KIRO_HOME>/sessions/cli/<sessionId>.json`
(a regular file of at most 1 MiB) names a concrete model id in `session_state.rts_model_state.model_info.model_id`, that
is one that is neither empty nor `auto`; a fallback notice that names the model that continued SHALL count the same once
its shape is recorded. For a profile on `auto`, a reported model SHALL make the judge's provenance `served` and its
vendor the served model's family; a served model whose vendor is an implementer's, or unknown, SHALL drop the verdict as
`model_mismatch`, and the next independent judge SHALL be asked, as for any judge that reports its served model. For a
pinned model, a session file or notice that names another model (after normalisation), or a standard-error warning that
Kiro could not set the requested model, SHALL end the run as `error` with a detail that starts with `model_mismatch:`
and no verdict, and the judge SHALL record it as `model_mismatch`: the profile SHALL be skipped for the round and cooled
as for any model mismatch, and the next independent judge SHALL be asked. A pinned run with no session file and no such
warning SHALL block nothing. Observed on kiro-cli 2.32.0 (live run): a pinned id the account does not have fails the first prompt with a
`runError` at stage `prompt` and no standard-error warning, which is a failed hello (L4-KJD-007) that skips the profile
like any other; the standard-error check stays as a second guard, its pattern still provisional. For a pinned model the session file SHALL only detect a mismatch: one that names the pinned
model (after normalisation) SHALL report no served model, and the judge's provenance SHALL stay `declared` (the session
file is the CLI's own selection, an echo of the configuration, not a server report). A session file that is missing,
unreadable, larger than 1 MiB or names no concrete model SHALL report no served model.

#### 8.3.3 GitHub Copilot CLI (FAC, PRV, OCG)

GitHub Copilot CLI is an experimental fifth agent CLI, `copilot-cli` (binary `copilot`): an implementer, a tool-less judge,
clarifier and readiness reviewer, and a read-only delegate. It runs from a private `COPILOT_HOME` with one credential,
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, at a pinned version installed from a digest-checked tarball (L4-PRV-047), never waits for a limit,
never loops on denials without bound, and records its tokens and AI credits, never as dollars. No default role chain and
no `l4 init` output names it, and it is not released before one GitHub-routed recording (L4-FAC-022). The facts behind
the requirements are labelled as in §8.3 (`openspec/changes/copilot-cli/design.md` §2.2): **[V]** verified by the spike of
2026-10-22 or by a task, **[V-BYOK]** verified with the CLI driving a local model (no GitHub account), **[V help]** read in
the CLI's own help, **[V here]** verified while the design was written, **[I]** inferred, **[G]** guessed, **[U]** not known
until a task records it. The install, credential and major-gate requirements are L4-PRV-047 to L4-PRV-050 (after
L4-PRV-046) and L4-OCG-006 (after L4-OCG-005).

- Version and input: `copilot --version` prints `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102.` [V]; piped stdin with no `-p` runs one prompt and
  exits [V-BYOK].
- Stream: `--output-format json` writes JSONL events (`user.message`, `assistant.message {model, content, toolRequests}`,
  `tool.execution_start {toolCallId, toolName}`, `tool.execution_complete {toolCallId, error{code}}`, `session.info`,
  `session.error {errorType, message, statusCode}`, `assistant.turn_retry {reason}`, `model.call_failure {statusCode}`) and a
  final `result {sessionId, exitCode, usage}` event; a run killed from outside has no `result` event [V-BYOK].
  `--session-id` presets the session id; no resume flag was observed [V-BYOK].
- Usage: `--usage-output-file` writes `totalNanoAiu` and `modelMetrics.<model>.usage` [V-BYOK]; `totalNanoAiu` is AI credits
  × 10^9 [G]; a Copilot Free account runs headless and reports `totalNanoAiu` [V]; `totalNanoAiu` follows a run's
  tokens, each user request costs one premium request (`totalPremiumRequestCost`), and `aiCreditsStatus` is `complete` [V].
- Errors: a fatal model error is a `session.error` and exit 1 with an empty standard error (401 `authentication` after 3
  tries, 402 with no retry, 500 after 5 retries) [V-BYOK]; with no credential: exit 1, empty stdout, `Error: No authentication
  information found.` [V]; a rejected token, GitHub-routed: exit 1, empty stdout, `Authentication token found but could not
  be validated.` and `Failed to fetch PAT user login (401)` [V]; a pinned model that the account does not offer: exit 1,
  empty stdout, `Error: Model "<id>" from --model flag is not available.`, nothing billed [V]; the GitHub-routed wording
  of 402, 429 and of a session or weekly limit [G].
- Rate limit: the CLI retries a 429 by itself; `model.call_failure {statusCode: 429}` comes at once and `assistant.turn_retry
  {reason: "rate_limit"}` comes only after the `Retry-After` wait (32.7 s in the recorded run) [V-BYOK]. There is no
  max-turns flag, and a denied-call loop printed more than 10,000 lines in 6 minutes [V-BYOK].
- Credential: `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` is read before `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`, then a stored login and `gh`; a user-owned
  fine-grained PAT with "Copilot Requests" works and classic `ghp_` tokens are refused [V]. The CLI removes its own token from
  its shell tool's environment [V-BYOK].
- Tools: `--available-tools` decides what the model sees, and an EMPTY list means every tool [V help, V-BYOK]; an unknown
  name gives the model no tool (recorded with `l4_none` and `l4_no_such_tool` [V-BYOK], and with `l4_no_tools` on the
  GitHub-routed path [V]); `--available-tools=view,grep,glob` gave exactly those, and an OpenAI-served model got `rg` for
  `grep` and `apply_patch` for `create` and `edit` [V-BYOK]. `--allow-tool` and `--deny-tool` decide approval and deny beats
