  allow [V help]. Prompt mode never asks: a call outside the policy ends `error.code: "denied"` and the run goes on, exit 0
  [V-BYOK]; reads inside the working directory and read-only shell commands run with no rule, writes and other commands are
  denied [V-BYOK]; `--allow-tool=write` with a shell rule and `--add-dir <step>` let an implementer write the worktree and
  its result file [V-BYOK]. A shell rule matches a command's first word [V-BYOK]. On the GitHub-routed path
  `--allow-tool=write` approves the `apply_patch` of an OpenAI-served model, the `--additional-mcp-config` file
  `{"mcpServers": {<name>: {command, args, env}}}` loads, the server's tools are named `<name>-<tool>`, and
  `--allow-tool=<name>` approves them (recorded with Serena) [V].
- Isolation: `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=true` also trusts the working directory [V help]; `COPILOT_HOME` moves config and state and
  `settings.json` is read [V, V help]; auto-update is off with `--no-auto-update`, `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` or `autoUpdate:
  false`, and also when `CI` is set [V help]; `--no-custom-instructions` stops repository instructions, and whether a nested
  instruction file still loads is [U]; built-in MCP servers load unless `--disable-builtin-mcps` [V help]. An L4-like bwrap run
  answered [V-BYOK].
- Install: release `v1.0.102` has a `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and each of the six tarballs holds one member `copilot`, a regular file
  of mode 0755 [V]; the binary embeds Node [V]. The CLI extracts a package of about 220 MB to
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/copilot/pkg/<platform>/<version>/` on its first run, `copilot --version` alone does it, an unwritable cache
  fails the run, and a warm cache mounted read-only (also through a symbolic link at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/copilot/pkg`) works
  and is not written [V]. On macOS `XDG_CACHE_HOME` has no effect: the package lands under `$HOME/Library/Caches` [V]. Linux
  x64 ran `--version` under emulation [V] and runs natively on a GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` runner (glibc 2.39) [V]; the
  minimum glibc of the gnu builds is not known [G].
- Models: `--model auto` exists, and 1.0.102's `copilot help config` lists models of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI,
  Moonshot and Microsoft [V]. `assistant.message.model` named the BYOK model [V-BYOK]; under `auto` the stream holds
  `session.auto_mode_resolved {chosenModel, candidateModels, availableModels}` before the reply and
  `assistant.message.model` is the chosen id [V]; a Copilot Free account was offered `gpt-6-luna` only, and refused
  `--model gpt-6-luna` before any billed call, so only `auto` runs there [V]. Under a pinned model on the GitHub-routed
  path, whether `assistant.message.model` can differ from the request is [I] (not recordable on that account).

**L4-FAC-013 copilot-cli runs every mode from a private home with one common invocation.** The harness SHALL register the adapter `copilot-cli` (binary `copilot`) in the factory, in `HARNESS_ADAPTERS`, in
`JUDGE_ADAPTERS` and in the adapters that serve the delegate, and SHALL announce each of its runs as experimental. No
default role chain and no `l4 init` output SHALL name it. Every run SHALL start `copilot --output-format json
--no-ask-user --no-auto-update --no-custom-instructions --disable-builtin-mcps --disable-client-telemetry
--disallow-temp-dir --session-id <id> --usage-output-file <step>/copilot-usage.json --model <model>` followed by the
flags of its mode, where `<id>` is the preset session id or a new uuid4 and `<model>` is the profile's model, or
`auto` when the profile has none or names `auto` in any letter case. The prompt SHALL go on standard input followed
by EOF, never into the argv; an empty prompt SHALL be refused before the spawn. Each run SHALL set `COPILOT_HOME` to a
fresh `<step private dir>/copilot-home` that holds only `settings.json` = `{"autoUpdate": false, "disableAllHooks":
true, "memory": false, "includeCoAuthoredBy": false}`, SHALL set `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` to
a fresh per-run directory `<step private dir>/xdg-cache` whose only entry is `copilot/pkg`, a link to the harness's
Copilot package cache (L4-PRV-048), and SHALL NOT pass `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL`, `CI`, `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No argv entry SHALL be `--available-tools` or `--available-tools=`, or start with `--allow-all`,
`--yolo`, `--deny-tool` or `--sandbox`.

**L4-FAC-014 A Copilot judge offers the model no tool and fails closed on a tool call.** In judge mode (the judges, the clarifier, the readiness review and the `s1_judge` stand-in) the adapter SHALL add
exactly `--available-tools=l4_no_tools` and no allow flag, and SHALL run in the empty `judge-cwd`. The reply SHALL be
the content of the last `assistant.message` whose content is not blank, sliced and validated by the shared
prompt-contract helper, so a missing or invalid object takes the judge's repair path. A judge run whose stream holds
any `tool.execution_start` SHALL end as `error` with the detail `copilot-cli judge called a tool (<toolName>)` and no
structured result.

**L4-FAC-015 A Copilot delegate offers only the read tools and fails closed on any other tool.** In read-only mode the adapter SHALL add exactly `--available-tools=view,grep,glob` and no allow flag, and SHALL run in
the delegate's detached worktree, built with the instruction files removed as for opencode. A run that started any
tool whose name is not `view`, `grep`, `rg` or `glob` SHALL end as `error` with the detail `copilot-cli delegate
called a tool outside the read set (<sorted names>)` and no structured result. Otherwise the reply SHALL be the
assistant text after the last tool call, else the last assistant text, read by the shared read-only helper.

**L4-FAC-016 A Copilot implementer edits the worktree, runs only the gate binary and writes its result.** In implement mode the adapter SHALL add, in this order, `--allow-tool=write`, `--allow-tool=shell(<first word of the
gate prefix>:*)` when the policy has a gate prefix, and `--add-dir <step private dir>`, and SHALL run in the worktree.
With MCP servers in the request it SHALL write `<step>/copilot-mcp.json` = `{"mcpServers": {<name>: <server
entry>}}` and add `--additional-mcp-config @<that path>` and one `--allow-tool=<name>` per server. With
`memory.serena` on, the Serena server of a copilot-cli implementer SHALL start with `--context copilot-cli`, a context
that Serena 1.7.0 ships [V]. The result SHALL be
the prompt contract: the file that `$L4_RESULT_PATH` names, validated against the request's schema. Each
`tool.execution_complete` whose `error.code` is `denied` SHALL be recorded as a permission denial with the tool name
of its start event, and SHALL NOT by itself fail the run.

**L4-FAC-017 A Copilot run's status comes from its stream, its exit code and its standard error.** The adapter SHALL take the session id from the final `result` event, the served model from the last
`assistant.message.model`, and the HTTP status from `session.error.statusCode`. Unless L4-FAC-018 decides it, a run
SHALL end, first match wins: `timeout` when it timed out or stalled; `cancelled` when the caller interrupted it;
`auth` with `copilot-cli found no credential (set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN)` when it exited non-zero with no JSON event
and its standard error says `No authentication information found`; `auth` with `copilot-cli could not authenticate
(COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, expired or rejected)` and a limit from `copilot.stderr` when it exited non-zero
with no JSON event and its standard error says `Authentication token found but could not be validated` with a 401
or 403, and a retryable `error` with `copilot-cli could not validate COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN (no 401 or 403: the
network?)` when that text comes without either status; `error` with `model_mismatch: copilot-cli could not set
<id> (the account does not offer it: pin a model it offers, or use auto)`, with no limit and not retryable, when
it exited non-zero with no JSON event and its standard error says `Model "<id>" from --model flag is not
available`; from the last `session.error`: `auth` with
`copilot-cli could not authenticate (COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN is missing, expired or rejected)` for `errorType`
`authentication` or status 401 or 403, `rate_limited` with `copilot-cli reported a rate limit (session.error 429)`
for 429, `quota` with a `credits` limit and `copilot-cli reported that the AI credits are used up (session.error
402)` for 402, else `error` with `copilot-cli reported an error (<errorType or unknown>, status <statusCode or
none>)`, retryable when the status is a server-side overload or at least 500; `error` with `copilot-cli could not
extract its bundled package (the L4 package cache is cold or not writable): run l4 doctor --fix` when it exited
non-zero and its output says `Failed to extract bundled package`; `error` with `copilot-cli exited with code <n>` for
any other non-zero exit; else its mode decides. Every limit from a `session.error` SHALL name the source `copilot.session_error`. Under `auto`, when no
`assistant.message.model` came, the served model SHALL be `session.auto_mode_resolved.chosenModel`.

**L4-FAC-018 A Copilot run is stopped on its first rate limit and on a loop of denied calls.** Every run SHALL pass a line watcher to the process runner as its stop hook. The watcher SHALL stop the run on the first
`model.call_failure` whose `statusCode` is 429 (or the first `assistant.turn_retry` whose `reason` is `rate_limit`, if
that comes first), and when 20 `tool.execution_complete` events in a row have
`error.code` `denied` (any other completion SHALL set the count back to zero). It SHALL keep no text of a line and
SHALL NOT raise. A run the watcher stopped for a rate limit SHALL end as `rate_limited` with the detail `copilot-cli
hit a rate limit (HTTP 429); the harness stopped the run (it never waits for a limit)` and a `rate_limit` limit from
`copilot.model_call_failure` (or `copilot.turn_retry`) with no reset time, so the profile cools for `availability.default_cooldown` and the next profile
takes the step. A run it stopped for denials SHALL end as `permission_blocked` with the detail `copilot-cli was
stopped after 20 denied tool calls in a row: its permission rules refuse what it tries`. A run that timed out or
stalled with no `result` event, whose stream holds a `rate_limit` retry or a `model.call_failure` with status 429,
SHALL end as `rate_limited` with the detail `copilot-cli was waiting out a rate limit when the run timed out`. The
decision SHALL come from the watcher's own record and the stream, not only from the runner's abort flag.

**L4-FAC-019 Copilot usage counts tokens and AI credits, never dollars, and its reader counts tool calls.** The adapter SHALL read `<step>/copilot-usage.json` after the run as a regular file of at most 1 MiB. Input, output and
cached input tokens SHALL be the sums of `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` and `cacheReadTokens` over `modelMetrics`.
`totalNanoAiu / 1e9`, when it is a number above 0, SHALL be the run's credits with the source `copilot.usage_file`;
`cost_usd` SHALL stay None, and credits SHALL NOT be added to any dollar total. A missing, linked, oversized or
unreadable document SHALL be zero usage. No context peak SHALL be reported. The stream reader `copilot_signals` SHALL
return `start(toolCallId)` for `tool.execution_start` and `end(toolCallId)` for `tool.execution_complete`, and no
signal, without raising, for any other line; it SHALL keep no text.

**L4-FAC-020 A Copilot profile's vendor is its model's family, auto is routed, and the served model is checked.** The vendor of a `copilot-cli` profile with a pinned model SHALL be its model family's vendor with provenance
`declared` (`MODEL_FAMILIES`, which SHALL also map `grok-` to `xai` and `mai-` to `microsoft`), and a `vendor:` that
contradicts that family SHALL fail to load as for `kiro-cli`. A `copilot-cli` profile with no model, a blank model or
`auto` SHALL be routed: its possible vendors and models SHALL be the built-in set of Copilot CLI 1.0.102's model list,
whatever `vendor:` says. The adapter SHALL report `served_model`. Under `auto`, a concrete served model (neither empty
nor `auto`) SHALL be the judge's served model and SHALL be checked against the implementers' vendors as for every
adapter that reports one. For a pinned model, a served model that differs under model normalisation SHALL be
`model_mismatch`, and one that is the same SHALL report nothing, so the judge stays `declared`.

**L4-FAC-021 The Copilot probe ladder proves the binary, the token and one tool-less reply.** The `binary` step SHALL read `copilot --version` with `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME` = the package
cache, and SHALL apply the major gate (L4-OCG-006) and `min_version`. The `auth` step SHALL pass when
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set and SHALL fail with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN is not set` when it is not, whatever `auth:`
says; it SHALL read no stored login. The `quota` step SHALL be skipped with the reason `copilot-cli has no headless
quota query`. The `hello` step SHALL run the common argv with `--available-tools=l4_no_tools` and `-p <hello prompt>`
from an empty directory and a private `COPILOT_HOME` in a temporary directory, with the credential, and SHALL pass on
the reply `L4-OK`. A hello that started a tool SHALL fail with `copilot-cli hello called a tool (<toolName>)`. A hello
whose output holds a `rate_limit` retry or a 429 `model.call_failure` SHALL fail as a rate limit with `copilot-cli was
retrying a rate limit (hello)`, also when it timed out.

**L4-FAC-022 BYOK streams are no contract recording, and a GitHub-routed recording gates the release.** The BYOK streams SHALL live in `tests/fixtures/recorded/copilot-cli/1.0.102-byok/` and the outputs recorded without a
token in `tests/fixtures/recorded/copilot-cli/1.0.102-notoken/`; `recorded_versions.json` SHALL NOT list
`copilot-cli` for either. The change SHALL NOT be released before one GitHub-routed recording session with a real
token, on the owner's dummy repository and never a consumer, has added `tests/fixtures/recorded/copilot-cli/1.0.102/`,
regenerated `recorded_versions.json` and corrected every mapping that the recording disproves. No test SHALL need a
token.

### 8.4 Availability: probes, limits, cool-downs, fallback

**L4-AVL-001** Probe ladder steps (configurable per profile, cheapest first; the ladder stops at the first failure):

| Step | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `binary` | executable on PATH, version ≥ profile `min_version` It runs within `availability.probe_step_timeout` (L4-AVL-012). | `codex --version`, `claude --version` |
| `auth` | credentials present; records **only** `logged_in`, `auth_method`, `plan` — never e-mail or tokens. Env-credential auth proves presence, not validity: `hello` is the authoritative auth check [V, spikes/05: a dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` still yields `loggedIn:true`] It runs within `availability.probe_step_timeout` (L4-AVL-012). | claude `auth status` (keep `loggedIn`, `authMethod`, `subscriptionType`; drop `email`, `orgId`, `orgName`, `projectsDirectory`, `configDirectory`); codex app-server `account/read` (keep `type`, `planType`), or for `api_key` the presence of `CODEX_API_KEY` (`codex login status` writes stderr only and ignores `CODEX_API_KEY` [V]); opencode `auth list` (presence only; strip ANSI, map display names to ids, accept the `Environment` section; it runs in a scratch directory with an empty private `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and the disable switches, because `~/.config/opencode` is writable by agent runs and the call is outside the sandbox); gemini credential env or settings (exit 41 = not configured); `kiro-cli whoami --format json` (exit 0 and a flat object with a non-empty `accountType`, 2.27.1 and 2.28.0 [V]; logged out is exit 1 with `{"account": null}`; the e-mail is never kept). For a kiro-cli profile on `auto` (no model, or `auto`), once the login check passes (also when the credential variable decides it), the step runs `kiro-cli chat --list-models --format json` once in the probe environment, with a private `KIRO_HOME`, and records under `routed` the possible vendors and Active model ids (sorted; the union of the listing's and the built-in set's), with the source `listed`, or, when the listing fails, the built-in set with the source `built-in` and the reason; the step passes either way and `l4 probe` says which source counts (L4-KJD-013); a pinned profile is never listed. With the profile's own credential variable set (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `KIRO_API_KEY`, or `OPENCODE_API_KEY` for an opencode `api_key` profile with an `opencode/` or `opencode-go/` model, L4-PRV-024, L4-PRV-028) auth passes on its presence (`auth_method: env`) with no status command; unset on an `api_key` profile, auth fails with `<VARIABLE> is not set` |
| `quota` | remaining usage in every window ≥ `min_remaining_percent` (L4-AVL-009), or for OpenRouter-backed profiles a remaining balance and key limit ≥ `availability.min_remaining_usd`; skipped when no zero-cost query exists It runs within `availability.probe_step_timeout` (L4-AVL-012; the Kiro `/usage` call has a floor of 90 s, capped by `probe_timeout`). | codex app-server `account/rateLimits/read` (both windows of the model's bucket, plus `ordinaryUsageAllowed`, `rateLimitReachedType` and `spendControlReached`; never redeem reset credits); claude `TZ=UTC claude -p --safe-mode --no-session-persistence --output-format json "/usage"` (the only source of the per-model weekly window), or the latest `rate_limit_event`; OpenRouter-backed profiles: `GET /api/v1/credits` + `/api/v1/key` against `availability.min_remaining_usd` (default 0.50); Kiro `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive "/usage"` (no model call; `Credits (X of Y covered in plan)` and `resets on YYYY-MM-DD`, parsed into one `credits` window [V, 2.28.0 PRO]; the free-tier text is not recorded; a text that says the usage could not be retrieved for an authentication reason fails the step as `auth` with `kiro-cli usage: authentication failed`, L4-KJD-006; any other unknown text is `quota_unrecognised`) |
| `hello` | minimal prompt must return `L4-OK` within `probe_timeout`, single turn, on the profile's own model (limits are per model, and a warm Sonnet hello costs the same as Haiku [V, spikes/05]); anything else fails | on the profile's own model; the reply is accepted after: trim; remove one wrapping layer (a whole ``` fence with an optional language tag, or a matching `` ` ``/`"`/`'` pair); trim; equals `L4-OK`. Costs: Claude $0.0008 warm to $0.011 cold, about 3 s; Codex about 5 s and about 19k input tokens (run only on a cold cache entry, after the zero-token `model/list`); OpenCode isolated $0.0005, about 3 s, with `--title` [V, spikes/05]. On the reference runner: claude (haiku) 2.6 s, codex 5.4 s, opencode `big-pickle` 6.1 s [V, runner]. A kiro-cli profile, implementers included, runs the hello through the judge invocation of L4-KJD-001 (the tool-less harness agent, a private `KIRO_HOME`, an empty directory, `--model auto` when the profile has no model) with the hello prompt as its last argument, one tool-less turn, and its failures are classified by L4-KJD-006 (L4-KJD-007) |
| `mcp` | configured MCP servers start | Kiro `--require-mcp-startup` exit 3; Claude/Codex init events |
| `custom` | user command; exit 0 = OK | GPU present, VPN up |

**L4-AVL-002** Every limit signal (probe or real run) MUST be normalised to
`LimitSignal{tool, model?, kind: usage_limit|rate_limit|spend_limit|credits, resets_at?, source, raw_excerpt}`.
Structured sources take precedence (Codex `resetsAt`, Claude `rate_limit_event.resetsAt`, OpenCode `retry-after`,
Kiro month boundary); localized text ("Try again at 3:45 PM", "resets 6pm (Europe/Bucharest)") is a last resort.
Structured sources also include OpenCode `error.data.statusCode` (402 → `credits`, 429 → `rate_limit`) with
`responseBody.error.metadata.limit_source`, and Claude `rate_limit_event.status == "rejected"`. Google 429 resets are
parsed from the body text `Please retry in <h>h<m>m<s>s` (`retry-after` is absent [V]). OpenCode 1.x writes the status of an upstream error only into the message, as `[NNN] …` with no `statusCode`: an integer `statusCode` (or v2's `error.status`) wins, else the `[NNN]` of the message that no word character precedes (`messages[503]` is no status) is read as the structured status, and a `[429]` or "too many requests" in the message is a rate limit in v1 and in v2 (0.4.40, change 89). Not limits: Claude
`api_error_status:404`, Codex `turn.failed` 400 (configuration), OpenCode `Token refresh failed: 401` and Gemini
exit 41 (`auth`). [V, spikes/02, spikes/05]

**L4-AVL-003** The cool-down registry MUST record `{profile, until, kind, source, recorded_by_run}` in the runner
cache (`$L4_CACHE/availability.json`) and as a ledger event, and selection MUST skip a cooling profile without
spending a request. Without a reset time, `availability.default_cooldown` applies. `kind: credits` has no reset time:
it uses `availability.credits_cooldown` (default 24h) and a doctor warning (ENV-011). `kind: silent` (L4-IMP-087) has no reset
time either and uses `availability.default_cooldown`. For a binding OpenRouter key
limit, `resets_at` is the next `limit_reset` boundary [boundary semantics U].

**L4-AVL-004** Model-family limits (e.g. a Claude "Opus limit" or a Gemini Pro quota) affect one model, not the
tool [V, research/02; V, spikes/05: a Google free-tier 429 hit one model while sibling models still answered]; chains
SHOULD list another model on the same tool before switching tools, and the registry key MUST include the model.

**L4-AVL-005** Probe results are cached per `(profile, auth identity hash)` for `availability.cache_ttl`; a real run
failure, and a silent stop (L4-IMP-087), invalidates the cache entry immediately. A failed `hello` has a class, and the class decides how long it is
remembered: `limit` (a usage or rate limit) is never cached, the cool-down registry owns it; `auth` (HTTP 401 or 403, or
authentication wording: the account, the organisation or the key refused the call) is cached for
`availability.auth_failure_ttl` (default 2m), because a person fixes it; `transient` (a timeout, a 5xx, no result) is not
cached; `other` (the model answered, wrongly) is cached for `cache_ttl`. An OpenCode error event is classed by its integer status when it has one (401 and 403 `auth`, 5xx `transient`, any other status `other`; a `limit` class that no limit signal backs is `other`), and with no status only by server-side words ("unavailable", "overloaded", a timeout, a connection reset, refused or closed): `transient` for them, else `other`, with no auth wording looked for again, so a 503 that OpenCode names only in its message is not cached (0.4.40, change 89). A failure of a free step (binary, auth, quota)
is never cached. A profile skipped on a cached failure says so: the line ends `(cached Nm ago; l4 probe --no-cache
re-probes)`, and the `availability.selected`, `availability.unavailable` and `l4 probe --json` records carry `cached` and
`age_s`. A required role that finds nothing else usable has each profile it skipped on a cached `auth` failure re-probed
once before it parks (L4-AVL-007): at most one `hello` per such profile per selection, and never again while the
entry that the re-probe itself wrote stands (`auth_failure_ttl`), so repeated selections of a parked role cannot probe in a loop.

**L4-AVL-006** Mid-run limit: the adapter MUST fail fast (no waiting), the harness records the cool-down, keeps the
task's committed progress, re-selects via the chain and starts a fresh session on the next profile with the
"previous attempt" context. The switch is logged as `availability.fallback` with `from`, `to`, `reason`, `resets_at`.
An implementer step that the idle watchdog stopped with no tool call, with a later profile in the chain, is a limit of kind
`silent` (L4-IMP-087): the profile cools for `availability.default_cooldown`, its cached hello is cleared, `reason` is
`silent`, and nothing counts as a failed attempt; a second limit in one fix task also cools its profile before the unit parks.
A transient server error (claude: `api_error_status` 529 or 503, or `overloaded_error`) is not a limit: judge, verifier-agent
and clarifier calls retry it in the run, 3 tries with waits of 20 s and 60 s (a wait the adapter reports replaces them,
capped at 60 s), one `availability.transient{role, profile, status, attempt, wait_s}` per retry, and after the third try
the role is unavailable as before; the `hello` probe of every adapter whose hello reads an error event (claude, OpenCode 1.x and 2.x) is tried once more after 20 s, only for an error event of the transient class, with the run deadline checked before and after the wait: a limit, an auth failure, a wrong answer, an unsupported version, a hello that timed out, an exit with no error event and an unreachable custom provider are not tried again, a second transient answer is final, and `availability.selected` carries `hello_retry_wait_s` next to `hello_ms`. OpenCode's run path (1.x and 2.x) marks an error of the transient class (a 5xx or server-side words, named in the message only or not) as transient, with the status in `availability.transient`, so judge, verifier-agent and clarifier calls retry it in the run (0.4.40, change 89). An implementer step is never retried
this way: it is not idempotent once it has edited the worktree. A chain also moves on repeated failures of one task phase (L4-IMP-017); that move is a selection, not a limit: nothing cools down.

**L4-AVL-007** If no profile in a required chain is usable (after the one re-probe of a remembered auth refusal that
L4-AVL-005 describes), the unit goes to `waiting_capacity`, the run exits 12,
and `outcome.json` carries `retry_after` = the earliest known reset; the sweeper resumes it after that time. When no
profile of the chain is cooling (every failure was a missing binary, a missing login, a `hello` that was refused or
answered wrongly, a constraint or `serves`), nothing but a fix ends it and the next run probes again, so `retry_after`
is the time of the park (the unit is due on the next run, any pipeline); only a limit or credit exhaustion gives a later
reset, and a transient failure bounds the wait as L4-AVL-013 says. `outcome.json` also
carries `exit_reason` (`waiting_capacity: <reason>`), and the MR's sticky note gets a "Waiting for capacity" section
naming the unusable profiles, the human steps of a login (PRV-001) or the time capacity returns; the next
`capacity_restored` clears it (L4-ARC-002).

**L4-AVL-013** A transient failure in a chain bounds the capacity wait. When no profile of a required chain is usable
and at least one profile was skipped in that selection for a failure of the `transient` class with no limit (a probe
step that timed out, a `hello` that timed out or found its provider unreachable), `retry_after` SHALL be the earlier of
the earliest end of a cool-down in the chain and the time of the park plus `availability.default_cooldown` (30 m).
Without such a skip, `retry_after` SHALL stay as L4-AVL-007 says. A missing binary, a failed login, a `hello` that was
refused or answered wrongly, an unsupported version, a constraint and `serves` SHALL NOT shorten the wait: a person
fixes those, and the re-probe of L4-AVL-005 or `l4 retry` takes the fix. A transient failure records no cool-down and is
not remembered, so before this rule one cooling profile in the chain (credits used up, 24 hours) set the time for all of
it, and a unit whose other judges were back ten minutes after the park waited a day. A chain whose only failures are
transient waits `default_cooldown` too: its park is not fix-only (L4-YOLO-035), so an outage does not stop the plan with
`capacity_needs_fix`; a model that hangs at every hello is probed again at each trigger after the wait, up to the plan's
`max_runs`. The delegate is optional and keeps L4-DLG-013.

**L4-AVL-008** Logging: every selection MUST produce one human-readable line per considered profile and one
structured event (`availability.selected`; a selection that finds nothing usable writes `availability.unavailable{role,
required, skipped[], retry_after}` instead, also for an optional role, so a failed judge choice is as visible as a
successful one):

```
[l4] implementer: codex-sol skipped — quota: 5h window 100% used, 0% remaining (resets 2026-10-03T14:32Z); cool-down recorded
[l4] implementer: claude-sonnet ok (binary 2.1.288 · auth subscription · quota 49% used (session) · hello 2.1s) → selected, fallback #1
[l4] judges: judge-sol skipped — cooling until 2026-10-04T13:00Z (credits); no probe sent
```

`quota <N>% used (<window>)` names the most-used window. The event adds `quota_window`. The cooling line is
`[l4] <role>: <profile> skipped — cooling until <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ> (<kind>); no probe sent`.

```json
{"event": "availability.selected", "role": "implementer", "unit": "openspec:add-login",
 "selected": "claude-sonnet", "fallback_index": 1,
 "skipped": [{"profile": "codex-sol", "step": "quota", "reason": "usage window exhausted",
              "used_percent": 100, "window_minutes": 300, "resets_at": "2026-10-03T14:32:00Z"}],
 "probes": {"claude-sonnet": {"binary": "2.1.288", "auth": "subscription", "quota_used_percent": 49,
                               "quota_window": "session", "hello_ms": 2104}}}
```

> *Given* `roles.implementer: [codex-sol, claude-sonnet]` and Codex reports `primary.usedPercent: 100`
> *When* `l4 run` selects an implementer *Then* no request is sent to Codex, `claude-sonnet` is probed and used,
> the console shows both lines above, the ledger records `availability.selected` and a cool-down for `codex-sol`
> until its `resetsAt`, and the commit trailers include `L4-Fallback-From: codex-sol`.

**L4-AVL-009** A usage-limited profile is exhausted when **any** of its windows (Codex 5-hour and weekly; Claude
session, weekly and per-model weekly) has less than `min_remaining_percent` remaining; its cool-down ends at that
window's `resets_at`. Claude windows are `session`, `weekly (all models)` and `weekly (<model family>)`. Codex: every
window of the model's bucket. [V, spikes/05 on a Max plan; the runner's `pro` plan is U]

**L4-AVL-011** In-run wait. When a limit leaves no implementer to take the step (every profile of the chain
cooling) and the earliest cool-down ends within `availability.wait_in_run` (default 5m, `0` switches it off), the run
prints `[l4] waiting <N>s for <profile> (<kind>)`, sleeps until the cool-down ends, ledgers
`availability.wait_in_run{profile, waited_s, kind}` and selects again; the step goes on from its last checkpoint as after
a fallback and consumes no attempt. A run waits at most `availability.wait_in_run_max_total` (default 15m) in all, its
units together, never longer than the CI job's remaining time (`ci.time_budget` minus `soft_deadline_margin`, since
`CI_JOB_STARTED_AT` or the run's start; `auto` reads `CI_JOB_TIMEOUT`, and no known budget imposes no job bound). A longer cool-down (a 429 without
a reset time cools for `default_cooldown`, 30m) parks the unit as L4-AVL-007 says (exit 12).

**L4-AVL-012** Probe steps are bounded and a timeout is named. Every subprocess of an availability probe (the
`binary`, `auth`, `quota` and `hello` steps) SHALL run in its own process group. Its output SHALL be read until the
direct child has exited and both pipes are closed, or until a grace of 2 seconds after the child's exit, whichever
comes first. The read MUST NOT wait for a process that still holds a pipe after that grace, inside or outside the
group. A child that exited before the timeout MUST NOT be reported as timed out: its return code and the output read so far are returned, the grace ending at the timeout when that comes first. At the grace or the timeout, the harness MUST kill the whole group. The `binary`, `auth` and `quota` steps SHALL
use `availability.probe_step_timeout` (default `20s`), and the `hello` SHALL keep `availability.probe_timeout`. An
adapter MAY declare a longer floor for a slow call of its own: the `kiro-cli chat --no-interactive /usage` call of
the `quota` step and the `kiro-cli chat --list-models` call of the `auth` step declare 90 s (measured on a
GitHub-hosted runner: 23 to 30 s), and run for the longer of the step timeout and that floor, so that a default
kiro-cli profile passes without configuration; the `binary` step and `kiro-cli whoami` keep the step timeout. Every
step timeout, a floor included, is capped by `availability.probe_timeout` (default `60s`: under the defaults the
kiro-cli floor is 60 s, and it is 90 s once `probe_timeout` is 90 s or more). Every probe step SHALL record how long
it ran as `step_ms` in its result; a step of 1 s or more SHALL show that time in the `l4 probe` line
(`quota 44.3% used (credits) 27.1s`), in `probes.<profile>.step_ms` of `availability.selected` and in the `l4
doctor` LIVE-001 line, so that the next slow step is visible. A step that does not answer in time MUST fail as `transient` with the reason `<cli>
did not answer within <N> s (<step> step); <cause>: run l4 doctor`, where `<cause>` names an OpenCode v2 daemon or a
login prompt for `opencode`, and a login prompt or a helper process for any other CLI. An agent run (`ProcRunner`) MUST
end within a bounded time after its kill, even when a process outside its group holds its output.

**L4-AVL-010** Roles are *required* (`implementer`, `verifier_agent`, `judges`) or *optional* (`clarifier`,
`s1_judge`, an LLM `spec_writer`, `delegate`). No usable profile in a required chain → `waiting_capacity` (exit 12). No usable
profile in an optional chain → the role is skipped with its documented degradation: clarifier → questions go to humans
(L4-CLR-005); S1 → recorded `unavailable`, and every decision that needs S1 to be automatic (clarifier auto-accept)
takes the human path instead; delegate → the question is deferred or escalated to a person (L4-DLG-013), and the unit
stays in `awaiting_human`.

---

## 9. Clarifier

**L4-CLR-001** For each open question the clarifier MUST receive: the question section, the unit's spec documents,
relevant code (agentic profiles run read-only: Claude `--permission-mode plan` or a read-only tool allow-list; Codex
`-s read-only`), answered questions of the unit, and selected lessons. It MUST return `l4/clarifier-answer@2`:

```json
{"question_id": "Q-002", "answer": "…", "confidence": "high|medium|low",
 "kind": "technical|product|ambiguous",
 "citations": [{"ref": "design.md#L42", "quote": "…", "claim": "the one thing this citation is cited for"}],
 "rationale": "…"}
```

`claim` is required on every citation (a non-empty string, at most 400 characters): the single statement the cited
text is meant to show. S1 checks the citation against that statement (L4-CLR-003), because a whole answer rarely
follows from one passage and a check over the answer would reject true citations. `@1` documents (no `claim`) are
invalid and go through the one repair of L4-CLR-005.

**L4-CLR-002** Routing: a question is auto-answered (`answered-by-clarifier`) only if **all** hold:
1. the implementer's `kind` **and** the clarifier's `kind` are both in `clarifier.auto_accept_kinds` (default
   `[technical]`) — a question the implementer called `product` or `ambiguous` always goes to a human or, where it is in
   scope, the delegate;
2. the clarifier's `confidence ≥ clarifier.min_confidence`;
3. the S1 router gives `p(technical) ≥ verifier.s1.decisions.router.technical_min` (0.85), the mean over the two
   option orders of the `choice` question of L4-CLR-003; anything lower, including the middle band, goes to a human
   (banding per research/03 §1.6);
4. every citation resolves (file exists, quoted text found at the cited place) **and**, for **each** citation, the S1
   citation checks of L4-CLR-003 all hold: `shows ≥ decisions.citation.support_min` (0.9), `opposite ≤
   decisions.citation.opposite_max` (0.2), `establishes ≥ decisions.citation.establishes_min` (0.8) and `internal ≥
   decisions.router.internal_min` (0.8). One failing citation sends the question to a human. All thresholds are
   starting points for calibration (§3.2), not measured operating points;
5. S1 is available (L4-AVL-010): a System-One profile on the `s1_judge` chain, or — only when
   `clarifier.s1_standin: llm_boolean` (default `none`) and no System-One profile is usable — an LLM backend profile
   (L4-FAC-003; M1: `openai-chat`) on that chain that answers the two boolean stand-in questions of L4-CLR-003 with the schema `{"answer": boolean}`, mapped to
   p = 1.0 (yes) or 0.0 (no); the stand-in is gated by `verifier.s1.reject_threshold` (0.1) and
   `verifier.s1.accept_threshold` (0.9) as before, not by `decisions.*`. Without S1 nothing is auto-accepted; with `s1_standin: none` an LLM backend profile on the
   `s1_judge` chain does not count as S1. [I, decision of delivery change 7 `clarification-loop` (design D5): M1 has no Laya/Jev on the
   reference runner, and the stand-in is opt-in so the default stays this SPEC's rule]

Otherwise the question stays `open` with a *Clarifier suggestion* and the unit goes to `awaiting_human`. A `verdict`
question and a `harness` question (L4-IMP-063) are never routed to the clarifier: the first is the verifier's, the
second a check of the harness's own, and only a person, an agent where `clarifier.answer_by_agents` is true, or the
delegate where the unit is in its scope (L4-DLG-001) answers either. The delegate runs after the clarifier and takes
only the questions the clarifier left open.

**L4-CLR-003** S1 questions (Laya or Jev). The two yes/no questions first proposed ("is this a product decision?",
"does `cited_text` support `answer`?") did not separate the cases on Jev (technical questions scored 0.24 and 0.42
against a bound of 0.1; the supporting line itself peaked at 0.89 against a bound of 0.9), so nothing would ever be
auto-accepted. The shipped questions carry the project's policy in their option criteria and are versioned as the
question set `clarifier-s1@2`; a change to any question or criterion bumps it, because thresholds belong to a
version of the questions.
* **Router** — state: question title, context, options; instruction: "Who has to settle the question below: the
  project's own material (technical), the product owner (product), or is it too unclear to tell (ambiguous)?" One
  `choice` over `technical | product | ambiguous` (each option carries a criterion that states the project's policy),
  asked **in both option orders** in one request (the order of the options moves the split by 0.13 to 0.21); `p(technical)`
  is the mean of the two.
* **Citation checks** — asked **per citation**, on the state `{question, answer, claim, cited_text}`, where
  `cited_text` is a **window centred on the quoted lines** (never a prefix of the file) cut to the budget; the
  question, answer and claim are never cut. Four `noul` questions: `shows` ("Does `cited_text` state or show
  `claim`?"), `opposite` ("Does `cited_text` state or show the opposite of `claim`?"), `establishes` ("Does `claim`,
  as shown by `cited_text`, establish `answer` as the answer to `question`?", so that a true claim cannot vouch for a
  wrong answer) and `internal` ("Can the answer be derived from this project's own specification, code and
  documentation, without the owner's preferences and without facts about systems outside the project?"). `internal` is asked here and not on
  the router state because it needs the answer and the cited text: over the question alone, Jev rated every
  repo-answerable question 0.28 to 0.58.
* Each state is kept within the engine's state budget (§3.2), measured with the S1 model's tokenizer.
* Every raw `p`, the served model and the question-set id are recorded in the ledger (`clarifier.result`) for
  calibration; S1 only ever makes auto-accept stricter.
* The opt-in boolean stand-in (`clarifier.s1_standin: llm_boolean`) keeps the two original questions: "Does answering
  this require a product, business, UX or policy decision by the project owner (rather than a technical decision
  derivable from the spec and code)?" over the router state, and "Does `cited_text` support `answer`?" over the
  citation state.

**L4-CLR-004** On `awaiting_human` the forge MUST get label `l4:needs-answers`, a sticky comment listing open
question IDs and titles with a link to `questions.md` on the unit branch, and the configured mentions. The section
also names a harness question whose answer does not start with `accept` or `retry` (L4-QMD-004): `Q-NNN has an
answer that does not start with `accept` or `retry`: it was not read. Please answer again.` When the delegate
escalated an open question (L4-DLG-008), the forge MUST also get the label `l4:needs-person` and the sticky comment a
section `Needs a person (the delegate escalated)` that lists each such question with the delegate's reason; when the
delegate answered questions, the sticky comment SHALL list them under `Answered by the delegate` with the model and the
CLI. `l4:needs-person` SHALL be removed when no escalated question of the unit is open, and SHALL be in the label set
that setup creates (`managed_labels`). No doctor check reads the `l4:*` labels yet: the `FORGE-003` row lists the check
that is still to come.

**L4-CLR-005** If no clarifier profile is available or its output stays invalid after one repair, the questions stay
`open` without suggestion, the unit goes to `awaiting_human` (exit 11, not 12 — humans can always answer), and the
sticky comment says the clarifier was unavailable.

**L4-CLR-006** Answers are injected into implementer prompts inside
`<l4:data kind="answer" id="Q-002" by="human|agent|clarifier|delegate">…</l4:data>` blocks, which the harness contract
defines as information, never instructions; `by` is the actor of L4-QMD-009. Answer text is redacted (L4-OBS-002)
before rendering.

**L4-CLR-007** The clarifier reads signatures and keep-rules before it suggests an answer. The clarifier's system text SHALL tell
it to read a function's signature before suggesting a call (keyword arguments after a defaulted parameter, no assumed
positional order, say so when no excerpt shows the signature) and never to suggest deleting, skipping or renaming an item
the specification says is kept, not deleted or rewritten in place. Its excerpts SHALL include the definition line (up to
12 lines) of up to three functions the question calls (`name(` in its text), when found by `git grep` in a tracked source
file and not covered by an excerpt already; they count against the code budget. Its prompt version SHALL be 6.

### 9.1 Delegate

**L4-DLG-001 The delegate is off unless the base branch enables it, and acts only in scope.** The top-level `delegate:`
section (`enabled`, default `false`; `scope`, `yolo` or `all`; `kinds`; `independence`; `unfreeze`; limits; `timeout`)
and `roles.delegate` MUST be read from the base branch only. With `scope: yolo` a unit SHALL be in scope when it is the
current unit of an `active` or `waiting` plan, or its fix unit; `scope: all` SHALL add units that no plan file lists
while no plan is active. Held units, units of a stopped or cancelled plan and finished units MUST NOT be in scope.

**L4-DLG-002 The delegate is a profile chain that never asked or judged the question.** `roles.delegate` SHALL be a factory chain of `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `kiro-cli` and `copilot-cli` adapter profiles (a profile of another adapter, or a backend profile, MUST be skipped as one that does not serve the role, L4-DLG-015). `question.raised` SHALL record the asker (`profile`,
`model`; `judges` for a verdict question). With `delegate.independence: model` (default) the selection MUST veto an
asker's profile name or model, with `profile` only the name. For a verdict question the askers are the round's judges
AND the unit's implementer profiles (every implementer profile that ran a step of the unit, from its ledger; the
configured `roles.implementer` chain when the ledger names none, and every model those steps reported in `agent.finished`), so the model that wrote the code never overturns the
judge's dispute of it. A step's raise with no asker MUST count every implementer (and judge) profile of the unit; an intake raise has no asker. A profile with no `model`, and an asker whose model cannot be resolved, MUST veto under `model` (fail safe), also an asker whose model is the literal `auto` (a kiro-cli implementer or judge profile with `model: auto` vetoes every delegate profile, L4-DLG-018); the
model that served the call (`model_resolved`) MUST be checked against the askers too, and a reply served by an asker's
model MUST be discarded and escalated. No profile left MUST escalate (`no independent delegate`).

**L4-DLG-003 The delegate answers at the end of the run that parks the unit, and in a later run.** A run that leaves a
unit in scope in `awaiting_human` (or `fixing` with a waiting fix unit) SHALL run the delegate pass before it closes,
after the clarifier, under the unit's lease. The planner SHALL name the action `delegate` for such a unit whose open
question in `delegate.kinds` has no final delegate record for its current raise and no future deferral. The pass SHALL
ask once per question, oldest first, and MUST NOT ask a decided question again. A pass at the end of a run in which a
step of the unit ran SHALL ask at most `delegate.max_questions_per_run` questions (a batch of L4-DLG-028 counts each of its questions). A pass in a run in which no step of the unit
ran before it (the run exists for the delegate: no `agent.finished`, `gate.finished`, `delegate.asked` or
`budget.cost`, no clarifier call that was made, no phase change but into a wait phase; `is_idle_run` on the ledger as it
stands, read once before the pass writes anything, handed to the pass as `idle_run`) SHALL NOT be bound by
`delegate.max_questions_per_run`: it asks until no question is due, until the first deferral for lack of time (L4-DLG-013)
ends it (that deferral still asks for the next run; the questions after it get no record and are asked by that run, where
a capped pass defers each question it reaches), or until a cost limit escalates the rest (L4-DLG-009). The unit does not
continue in the same run, in either case. A pass with a question due appends `delegate.pass{bound,
delegate_only}` when its loop ends (data only, no change to the fold; none when nothing was due): `delegate_only` says
whether the cap was lifted, and `bound` is the first of `deadline` (a deferral for lack of time), `cost` (a refusal for the
unit's cost cap or the plan's share), `cap` (the loop broke on the cap), else `none_due`. A consumer's unit (2026-10-29/30)
raised 30 and 33 verdict questions in one verification round, and each run answered 5 in 3.3 minutes; the cost cap
(`delegate.max_cost_usd_per_unit`, the owner's setting, default $15; a call needs `max_cost_usd_per_answer`, $3, left) still stops the pass after about
12 calls, so the change saves about one run per flood of verdicts, not most of them (0.4.44, change 99). From 0.4.53
such a flood is asked in batches (L4-DLG-028): the cap still counts questions, and the cost cap counts the calls.

**L4-DLG-004 The delegate reads the repository read-only and gets its material as data.** The delegate SHALL run in the
adapters' `read_only` mode (Claude Code: `--permission-mode plan`, tools `Read,Grep,Glob`; Codex: `-s read-only`,
`--ephemeral`; opencode: L4-DLG-016; kiro-cli: L4-DLG-017) with no tool server and no forge or CI token, in a detached
worktree of the pushed unit head that the sandbox MUST mount read-only, only its private directory writable. Its prompt
`delegate@7` (a batch of L4-DLG-028: `delegate-batch@1`, the same rules for each of its questions; 0.4.22 amendment: the read tools named for any CLI, and the rules of L4-DLG-023 to L4-DLG-025; 0.4.34: the reference forms of L4-DLG-005 and the reason a previous reply was discarded; 0.4.35: which `.l4/` files are evidence; 0.4.39: a frozen test file opens only through `accept` of the clarifier suggestion; 0.4.44: a `quote` is at least 12 characters, copied word for word) SHALL hold the question and
its evidence inside `<l4:data>` blocks that the system text calls data, never instructions, redacted before any cut.

**L4-DLG-005 The delegate returns one strict result, and anything else escalates.** The delegate SHALL return
`l4/delegate-result@1` `{question, decision, text, reason, checked}` (for a batch of L4-DLG-028, `l4/delegate-batch@1`
holds one per question, and each is checked as one reply). A reply SHALL be kept only when the decision fits
the kind, every decision but `escalate` has `checked` entries that resolve at the unit head, `text` passes the text
checks of `l4 questions answer` and unfreezes nothing (L4-DLG-014), and a reject asks for `WHEN … THEN …` where the
question does. A `checked` entry MUST NOT cite a harness-written file: `questions.md` or `verification.md`, a path with a `.l4` part below the repository root (a unit folder's `.l4/`), a path under the repository's `.l4/vendor/`, `.l4/ci/` or `.l4/bin/`, or a path under `.l4-out/` (the harness's and the asker's own words); any other path under the repository's `.l4/` (`.l4/config.yaml`, `.l4/gates/`, `.l4/plans/`) is a repository file, checked like the others. The quote of a `path:line` or `spec:` entry MUST have at least 12 characters, whitespace folded (a `test:` entry has no quote: it MUST name a test id of the unit's verification evidence); a shorter quote MUST be refused as `checked <ref>: the quote of <ref> is shorter than 12 characters`, retryable like a reference that does not resolve (checked before resolution, so a short quote on a file that is missing is named as short), and the prompt MUST state the minimum (`quote` is at least 12 characters, copied word for word) (0.4.44; a consumer's unit lost 5 replies, about $5.40 of its $15, to a quote such as `c: {},`, which the old reason called `does not resolve`). A `path:line` entry resolves when its quote, whitespace folded, starts within three lines of the named line (its first occurrence from line `line - 3` on starts in those seven lines; it may run past them and keep or drop the file's line breaks). A `spec:<name>` entry names `<unit folder>/<name>`, else `<name>` when it starts with the unit folder's repository path, else, for a name without `/`, the one tracked file of the unit folder of that file name (two or more: it does not resolve). A reply with more than 20 `checked` entries, or an entry whose `ref` has more than 300 characters or whose `quote` or `claim` has more than 600, MUST be discarded, and an `escalate` reply records only the (redacted) refs of its entries. Any other reply MUST be recorded `delegate.result{status: discarded}` with its entries' `ref` and `quote`, redacted, and the question escalated, except that a reply discarded only because an entry does not resolve, with an attempt left under `delegate.max_attempts_per_question`, is recorded `delegate.result{status: deferred, discarded}` and asked again, and the next prompt (`delegate@5`) says why the previous reply was discarded. The prompt MUST state which files are no evidence and which `.l4/` files are evidence. The discard reason of such a reference MUST be `checked <ref> cites a harness-written file (questions.md, verification.md, the harness's .l4/ files): not evidence`, distinct from `checked <ref> does not resolve`; one such reference discards the whole reply (the harness MUST NOT drop it and keep the rest). A discarded reply MUST be recorded `delegate.result{status: discarded, decision, reason}` with the decision it would have made (never its text), and the `Escalated by:` line and the `l4:needs-person` note MUST say `the reply was discarded: <reason>`.

**L4-DLG-006 The delegate's answer takes the path and the commit of `l4 questions`.** A kept reply SHALL be written by
the edit core of `l4 questions` on the run's worktree, without `clarifier.answer_by_agents`, as `text`, `accept|reject
<text>` (verdict) or `accept:|retry: <text>` (harness), with the line `Answered by: the delegate (<model> via <cli>)`.
The run SHALL commit it with the `l4 questions` subject, `By: delegate (…)`, `Via: l4 delegate` and `[skip ci]`, push
it, and record `question.answered{by: delegate, profile, model, answer_sha256}`. A refused write MUST escalate.

**L4-DLG-007 After an answer the next run is started, in a plan and outside one.** After a pass that wrote an answer,
the run SHALL ask the forge once to start the next run on the base branch, as `l4 questions answer` does, also when the
plan step waited; a refused start or no token SHALL be a log line only. The next run SHALL read the answer as it reads a
person's. A delegate's verdict `accept` outside a plan MUST only move the unit on: the harness MUST NOT merge a unit
that is not the current unit of an active `merge: auto` plan.

**L4-DLG-008 An escalation leaves the question to a person.** An escalated question SHALL stay `open` with
`delegate.result{status: escalated, reason}`, the line `Escalated by: the delegate (<model> via <cli>): <reason>`
(redacted, at most 300 characters), the forge label `l4:needs-person` and a sticky section that lists it with its
reason. A plan SHALL wait with `unit_awaiting_human`, a detail naming the escalated questions and no chained run. The
label SHALL go when no escalated question of the unit is open.

**L4-DLG-009 The delegate's calls and cost are bounded.** The harness SHALL bound, from the base branch: attempts per
question (`max_attempts_per_question`, 2), answers per task or verdict target (`max_answers_per_task`, 3), questions per
run (5), cost per answer (3.0 USD), per unit (15.0 USD) and, in a plan with a cost limit, the delegate's share of it
(`plan_cost_share`, 0.25). A call SHALL need one answer's cost left in each cost limit (a batch of N questions, N answers' cost, L4-DLG-028), an unknown cost counting at that figure (also for a call that hit a limit before the next profile answered). A limit reached MUST escalate. The cost SHALL be unit cost.

**L4-DLG-010 Every delegate decision is audited and labelled.** A delegate's accept of a harness question SHALL give
proofs `via: delegate_override` with `question` and `answer_sha256`; a delegate's verdict SHALL be recorded
`human.verdict{by: delegate, profile, model}`. The judge's view, `verification.md` and `l4 yolo report` SHALL label each
`by the delegate (<model> via <cli>) through Q-NNN`. S1 calibration labels MUST be made only from verdicts recorded `by:
human`.

**L4-DLG-011 The status names the delegate's answers and escalations.** `l4 status` SHALL give a unit whose open
question the delegate escalated the REASON `Q-NNN needs a person (the delegate escalated)`. `l4 status --unit` SHALL
print a `Delegate:` line per decided question (answered with model, CLI and cost; escalated with the reason; deferred
with the time). `l4 yolo status` SHALL print, for the current unit, `delegate: <n> answered, <m> escalated` with the
first escalation, and the plan's delegate cost against its share. `--json` SHALL carry the same.

**L4-DLG-012 Doctor checks the delegate's configuration and availability.** With `delegate.enabled`, doctor `DLG-001`
(error) SHALL check that `roles.delegate` is not empty, names existing `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `kiro-cli` or `copilot-cli`
adapter profiles, that `delegate.kinds` and the limits are valid, that every kind of `delegate.kinds` has a profile of the
chain that may answer it and every `profiles.<p>.options.delegate_kinds` is valid (L4-DLG-019), that under `independence:
model` no profile it needs is routed (a model `auto`, or none, L4-DLG-018), and that every profile of `roles.implementer` and `roles.judges` has a
delegate profile that passes the independence rule, naming each that has none, and that, for each kind of `delegate.kinds`, one profile is both allowed that kind and independent of every asker of it (the judges and the implementers for a verdict question, the implementers for the others), naming the kind and the askers when none is (else every question of that kind escalates). `DLG-002` (warn) SHALL check that a
delegate profile is usable now (`hello` with `--live`), and under `independence: model` SHALL warn that a profile whose `model` is an alias (no digit, such as `opus`) may be served as another model (D3: the model a step reports is the asker's). `DLG-002` SHALL also warn, naming each profile of `roles.delegate` that would answer verdict questions (`delegate.kinds` and `options.delegate_kinds` leave `verdict` to it), and SHALL flag an `opencode` profile among them (a model L4 cannot rate, such as an `opencode-go/…` id or a local custom provider) as one that can overturn a judge's dispute and, under `merge: auto`, merge it. `DLG-001` also fails when `ci.time_budget` is known and `delegate.timeout` is not less than it minus
`ci.soft_deadline_margin` (no call would fit), and when a profile it needs has no `model` under
`independence: model`. Both MUST pass while the delegate is off, with no finding; DLG-001's line then names how to turn
it on (L4-DLG-022).

**L4-DLG-013 An unusable delegate defers or escalates, and never parks the unit.** With no usable delegate profile the pass SHALL defer the question (`delegate.result{status: deferred, retry_after}`)
when every profile is cooling with a known reset, or a call timed out or failed, and SHALL escalate when a profile is
unusable for a cause only a fix ends (binary, login, `hello`, constraint). Deferrals and calls SHALL be bounded by
`max_attempts_per_question`. A deferral for lack of time (`reason: soft_deadline`) made no call and MUST NOT count as an
attempt (as L4-IMP-070 does not charge a run that started no step), so that time-budget pressure never escalates a
question as `delegate attempts used`. A question deferred for lack of time three times in a row (its latest three
`delegate.result` records of the current raise are `deferred` with `reason: soft_deadline`) MUST stop asking for the
next run (L4-DLG-026): the delegate then waits for the next scheduled or pushed run, so that deferrals never chain runs
without bound outside a plan. The unit MUST stay in `awaiting_human`, never `waiting_capacity`.

**L4-DLG-014 The delegate unfreezes a file only where the base branch allows it.** `delegate.unfreeze` SHALL default to
`false`. With `false`, a question whose effective answer (the `text`, or the suggestion an `accept` takes) names a
frozen test or test-support file of a held task MUST be escalated with the path named. With `true`, the delegate MAY
accept the clarifier's suggestion that unfreezes a frozen test file under the rules of a person's accepted suggestion
(L4-IMP-015), recorded and shown as `delegate_override`. A free-text answer naming a frozen file MUST still escalate.
`delegate.unfreeze` MUST NOT cover a test-support file (a path `tdd.test_support_globs` matches, such as `conftest.py`),
which stays a person's change, nor anything in a fix task (0.4.22 amendment, L4-DLG-025). The same two rules hold when the grant is made: `unfrozen` keeps a `support` file
of the freeze manifest frozen and grants nothing in a fix task for an answer only the delegate recorded, whatever the
reply-time check said. The delegate's `accept` of a question that takes option 1 (L4-QMD-008) takes it and writes the
block through the same edit as `l4 questions accept`, under these rules, and the delegate's prompt says that a frozen
test file opens only through `accept` of the clarifier suggestion: an `answer` that names a frozen path is refused
(0.4.39, change 85).

**L4-DLG-015 Five adapters serve the delegate, and a prompt-contract adapter replies in its last message.** `claude-code`, `codex`, `opencode`, `kiro-cli` and `copilot-cli` adapter profiles SHALL serve `roles.delegate`; a profile of another
adapter (`command`) or a backend profile MUST be skipped as one that does not serve the role. On a prompt-contract
adapter (`opencode`, `kiro-cli`, `copilot-cli`) the read-only mode MUST offer only tools that read files (no write, no command, no
network fetch, no sub-agent), MUST NOT write or read a result file, and SHALL take the reply from the run's final
message: the LAST top-level JSON object of the text after its last tool call, else of the whole reply text. The object
SHALL be found by scanning the text with `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode` from each `{` (a scan resumes after an object it
decoded, so an object inside another is not top-level; a `{` that does not decode is skipped; code fences are ignored),
never as the text from the first `{` to the last `}`; the object is then validated as a judge's reply (L4-KJD-003). The
schema suffix of such a prompt SHALL tell the model to read the repository with its read-only tools and then reply with
the object, writing nothing after it, and MUST NOT say to call no tool; it stays outside `prompt_sha256` and the
published prompt. A run that called a tool outside its read set MUST give no reply (an adapter error that the pass
defers and, at the attempts limit, escalates, L4-DLG-013). One exception: a call that the adapter refused before it ran
(opencode's permission map) did nothing, so a run that goes on and finishes yields a reply when, and only when, that
reply is valid; a run that ended on a refused call with no valid reply yields none. An `opencode` profile with `options.cli_major: 2` does not serve the delegate and is refused in
`roles.delegate` at load (L4-OCV-014).

**L4-DLG-016 The opencode delegate reads the worktree and nothing else.** An `opencode` delegate SHALL run `opencode run --pure --format json -m <provider/model> --dir <the detached worktree>`
with the prompt on stdin and the isolation of every opencode run (an empty per-step `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, the
`OPENCODE_DISABLE_*` switches, `snapshot: false`, `autoupdate: false`). Its `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` SHALL deny by
default: `tools` `{"*": false}` then `read`, `glob`, `grep` true; `permission` `{"*": "deny"}` first, then `read`,
`glob`, `grep` `allow` and `external_directory` denied but for the step's private directory (`list` is not an opencode
1.18 tool and is not in the set). The `read` permission SHALL keep opencode's `*.env` and `*.env.*` denials after its
allow (the last matching rule wins), so a `.env` file stays unreadable. In this mode a profile's `options.tools` MUST be
ignored: it can never re-enable a tool (opencode turns a tools map into permission rules after `"*": "deny"`, which
would re-enable `bash` or `edit`). For an OpenCode Zen model (`opencode/…`) `bash` SHALL be sent in the request with the
permission `{"*": "deny", "<sentinel>": "ask"}` (a pattern no command matches), so every command is refused and the run
is not ended; a refused call yields a reply only as L4-DLG-015 says. Before an opencode delegate runs, the harness SHALL
remove the nested instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and every other file name the adapter knows
as an opencode instruction file) from the detached worktree's checkout, because opencode loads them from the directory
of any file it reads, upward, whatever `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG` says; the git tree (`HeadTree`) is untouched,
so the claim checks that resolve against it are unaffected. The configured model SHALL stand as the served model (run
mode reports none). The delegate SHALL run only on the pinned OpenCode major (1): a binary of another major fails its
probe as `unsupported_version`, which MUST escalate the question, not defer it.

**L4-DLG-017 The kiro-cli delegate runs a read-only harness agent.** A `kiro-cli` delegate SHALL run a harness agent `l4-delegate-<12 hex>` whose `tools` and `allowedTools` are `read`,
`glob` and `grep` (no MCP server, `includeMcpJson: false`, no resource, no hook, the profile's model), from a fresh
`KIRO_HOME` in the step's private directory that holds only that agent and the judge's `settings/cli.json`, as `kiro-cli
chat --no-interactive --v2 --agent l4-delegate-<hex> --model <M> --trust-all-tools --output-format stream-json`, with
the prompt on stdin, its working directory the detached worktree, no `--require-mcp-startup` and no `KIRO_LOG_LEVEL`.
The `--v2` flag is not load-bearing: engine v2 is the kiro-cli 2.x default and ran K3's tooled agent (recorded 2.28.0),
and the engine is pinned by `chat.agentEngine: v2` in the private settings and by the `runStarted` engine check. If the
live record shows that a tooled agent fails with the prompt on stdin, the specified fallback is the prompt as an
argument, with a prompt over `MAX_ARG_BYTES` escalated, taken as an amendment of this argv. The adapter SHALL keep every
tool name of a turn of the stream (not the first only) for the read-only check. A run that ran an engine other than v2,
reported a `runError`, or called a tool other than `read`, `glob` or `grep` (a tool the agent does not have included)
MUST give no reply: an adapter error and a deferral source (L4-DLG-013). The served model SHALL be the session file's
(L4-KJD-015); a pinned model it contradicts MUST escalate the question with both ids. Under `independence: model` a
profile on `auto` or with no model MUST NOT answer (L4-DLG-018). A call's credits SHALL be recorded as credits, never as
dollars (L4-DLG-020). The delegate SHALL run only on the pinned Kiro CLI major (2): another major MUST escalate the
question.

**L4-DLG-018 Models of every adapter are compared as one id.** Before the independence rule compares an asker's model with a delegate profile's (configured or served), each id SHALL
be lowercased and cut after its last `/`, then stripped, in this order, of a `[…]` context marker, a trailing `@…` (a
Vertex date), a trailing `:…` (`:free`, `:thinking`, a Bedrock `:0`), a leading `(<region>.)?anthropic.` (Bedrock; the
prefix shape of `MODEL_FAMILIES` in `l4.availability.vendor`, reused) and a trailing `-v\d+(:\d+)?` (a Bedrock version),
then of a date suffix, and a `.` between digits SHALL be folded to `-`. Two ids SHALL be the same model when they are
equal or when one is the other followed by `-` and more (fail safe). An id whose name after the last `/` is `auto`, and
a missing id, MUST veto under `independence: model`. The free-tier test of L4-DLG-019 reads the id as configured, before
this cut. The served model is the one the run reported (Claude Code, Codex, the kiro-cli session file), else the
configured one (opencode).

**L4-DLG-019 A weak model answers only what a later step checks.** A delegate profile SHALL answer the kinds of `delegate.kinds`, narrowed by `profiles.<p>.options.delegate_kinds` when
it is set. A free-tier model (an OpenCode Zen id `opencode/…`, or an id ending `:free`) MUST answer only `technical`
and `harness` questions, whatever its options say. The selection SHALL skip, per question, a profile that may not
answer its kind (reason `kinds: <p> answers <kinds> questions`), so that no fallback reaches it; a question no profile
of the chain may answer MUST escalate with `no delegate profile answers <kind> questions`.

**L4-DLG-020 The cost of every adapter is bounded, known or not.** A call's cost SHALL be the cost the CLI reported in dollars (Claude Code; opencode's `step_finish.cost`, where 0 is a
known cost), else unknown (Codex tokens without a `budgets.price_table` entry, kiro-cli credits, opencode with no
cost), and an unknown cost SHALL count at `max_cost_usd_per_answer` against the delegate's limits (L4-DLG-009). A
kiro-cli call SHALL record `budget.cost{credits, credits_source, profile, role: delegate, question}` and never add
credits to dollars. `delegate.timeout` SHALL bound a call of every adapter.

**L4-DLG-021 A unit that waits on questions names the delegate while it is off.** While `delegate.enabled` is false on the base branch (and the base configuration can be read: when it cannot, the delegate section falls back to its defaults and no hint is given), for a unit in `awaiting_human` (or `fixing` with a waiting fix
unit) with an open question of a kind in `delegate.kinds` that would be in scope were the delegate on, `l4 questions`,
`l4 status --unit` and `l4 yolo status` (its current unit) SHALL print after their `Next:` line exactly one line
`Hint: the delegate can answer these questions in CI: set delegate.enabled: true and roles.delegate in .l4/config.yaml
on <base> (docs/runbook.md 7.1, the delegate).`, `--json` SHALL carry it as `delegate_hint`, and the sticky note's
waiting section SHALL end with it. It MUST NOT be shown while the delegate is on, for a unit out of scope, or when no
open question is of a kind the delegate answers and could still take (one it escalated for its current raise is final).

**L4-DLG-022 The configuration and the doctor name the delegate.** `l4 init` SHALL write after the configuration a commented-out block that shows how to turn the delegate on: a model
pinned on each init profile the block references (the implementer's and the judge's, so that `independence: model` can
compare them), a third model as the delegate profile (`delegate-sonnet` on `claude-sonnet-5`, as SPEC 3.2), the
`roles.delegate` line and the `delegate:` section with `enabled: true` and `scope`; it says that every implementer and
judge profile needs a model under the default independence, and names docs/runbook.md 7.1. Every YAML line of the block
SHALL be a single-`#` comment placed inside the mapping it belongs to, at that mapping's indentation (`model:` under the
profile it pins, the delegate profile at the end of `profiles:`, `delegate: [delegate-sonnet]` at the end of `roles:`,
the `delegate:` section last), and every prose line SHALL begin with `##`, so that removing the leading `# ` of the
single-`#` lines yields valid YAML with no duplicate key (no second `delegate:`, `profiles:` or `roles:`) on which
doctor `DLG-001` passes. Doctor `DLG-001`'s line while the delegate is off SHALL be `the delegate is off
(delegate.enabled is false; docs/runbook.md 7.1 tells how to turn it on)`. No other doctor check is added.

**L4-DLG-023 A delegate's reject sets the check as a person's does.** The harness SHALL judge a delegate's composed reject with the parser the fix unit uses (its last `WHEN … THEN …`). A
reject MUST end with a `WHEN … THEN …` sentence when it rejects a hold other than a scope, coverage or judge-view hold,
or a judge-only finding that cites no criterion; a reject of a finding that cites a criterion, or of a criterion, MAY
end with one (L4-VER-059). The prompt SHALL say that the sentence states the behaviour the fix must give, is the last
sentence, and is never the judge's suggested fix. A reply that breaks the rule MUST be discarded and the question
escalated; there is no repair call.

**L4-DLG-024 The delegate answers the verifier's cap-only, split and judge-view questions by reading.** A cap-only criterion question (L4-VER-055) and a split-evidence question (L4-VER-058) SHALL be answerable. A delegate
`accept` of a cap-only question MUST cite, as `path:line`, the file of the candidate test its reason names; that file
SHALL be the path before `::` of the candidate test's pytest-style id (the test report has no file field), and when
the id has no such path the question MUST escalate without a call (the check cannot be made); its prompt SHALL hold that reason. The prompt of a split-evidence question SHALL
hold the criterion's `judge_split` record (the parts and the files not shown). A judge-view hold (L4-VER-044) MAY be
accepted with a `checked` entry in a file the hold names; a `reject` of it MUST be discarded and the question escalated.
A judge-view hold that names no file (`LEGACY_LENGTH_HOLD`, the 0.4.14 text) MUST escalate without a delegate call.

**L4-DLG-025 A CI failure and a test-support change stay a person's.** A unit escalated with `ci_not_fixed` MUST NOT get a delegate pass or the planner action `delegate`. `question.raised` of
a blocked fix chore SHALL carry `chore: true`; a fix unit's technical question raised before it counts as a chore's when
its context holds the harness's fix-task note. The delegate MAY answer such a question, but an effective answer that
names a path `tdd.test_globs` or `tdd.test_support_globs` matches MUST escalate it with `a fix task cannot change
<path>: a person commits that change on the unit branch, then answers`; an answer "names a path" by the `names_path`
rule of L4-IMP-015 (a path as written: "the conftest" alone names none). With `delegate.unfreeze: true` an answer that
would unfreeze a test-support file, or any file of a fix task, MUST escalate (L4-DLG-014).

**L4-DLG-026 A delegate answer starts one run even where the continuation rule starts none.** A run whose pass answered a question (or deferred one for the soft deadline, which is no attempt, L4-DLG-013) SHALL ask once for the next run on the
base branch, also when the plan's request was dropped because no step started (L4-IMP-070); when the run dispatched a
continuation or found one queued, it MUST NOT ask again (the continuation reads the answer). An escalation or a
deferral for a cool-down SHALL ask for nothing. A soft-deadline deferral that is the third in a row for its question
(L4-DLG-013) SHALL ask for nothing either.

**L4-DLG-027 The delegate's answers are named where people read them, and a decision is final for its raise.** `verification.md` SHALL title the verdict answers `## Answers to verdict questions`, each line naming its actor. The PR
body written at the hand-off SHALL hold one line `Answered by the delegate:` with each question the delegate answered
and its model and CLI. A question the delegate answered, escalated or whose reply it discarded MUST NOT be asked again
for its current raise, also after a harness upgrade or a configuration change; a person's answer ends it, and a new
`question.raised` of the id SHALL be a new question for the delegate.

**L4-DLG-028 The verdict questions of one round share a delegate call.** The pass SHALL ask the due verdict questions of
one target folder (the unit, or its open fix unit) that have the same askers in batches of up to `delegate.batch_size`
(default 5, which the default caps fit: $15 for the unit, $3 an answer; 1 asks one question per call), in the pass's order and within the questions a capped pass may still ask
(L4-DLG-003; with the defaults a capped pass asks one batch of five). A question whose blocking tasks or verdict target
meets a key of a question already in the batch, and a question whose latest result of its raise is a deferral from a
batch call that ended `timeout` or `error`, SHALL NOT join a batch: the first starts a later batch, the second is asked
alone. Each question SHALL first pass the checks of a single question, in their order: still open, `limit_reached`, a
question no call can settle (L4-DLG-024), the soft deadline (which also ends the batch). A batch SHALL be one call with
the prompt `delegate-batch@1` (the shared blocks once: the unit's specification, the conventions, the earlier answers
but the batch's questions, the latest failing gate; then each question with its previous-discard reason and its verdict
material; `max_turns` `40 + 20 × (N − 1)`, at most 140) and the result `l4/delegate-batch@1` (`{results:
[l4/delegate-result@1]}`, 1 to N items). A batch of N SHALL need N answers' cost left in the unit's cap and in the plan's
share and SHALL be shortened from its end to fit them, and to keep its user text within `BATCH_MAX_CHARS` (160,000);
the adapter's budget SHALL be N times `max_cost_usd_per_answer`. A `limit` SHALL move the whole batch to the next
profile; a timeout, an error or a reply that is not a batch document (a schema break included) SHALL give each question
the outcome of a single call that timed out or failed: a deferral while an attempt is left (then asked alone), else an
escalation; a served model that is an asker SHALL discard every result. Each result of a valid document SHALL
be checked, answered, deferred or escalated on its own, with its question's own inputs (L4-DLG-005); a question with no
result or two results SHALL be a failed attempt, `delegate.result{status: deferred, reason}` with an attempt left, else
escalated; a result for a question outside the batch SHALL be ignored. The call's cost SHALL be one
`budget.cost{role: delegate, questions, batch}`, and each `delegate.result` SHALL carry `batch`, `batch_size` and its
share of the cost (None when the call reported none, so an unpriced batch counts at N answers' cost, its budget).
`delegate.pass` SHALL record `calls`. A batch of one and a question of another kind SHALL be asked as before
(`delegate@7`, `l4/delegate-result@1`). A consumer's unit spent $43.83 of its $50 cap on 30 verdict questions of one
round, about $1.46 each, and escalated the other 21 on the cap; each call paid again for the same rules, specification
and reading of the same head.

---

## 10. Verifier

### 10.1 Independence

**L4-VER-001** The verifier MUST run in a fresh worktree checked out at the unit branch head, MUST NOT receive the
implementer's transcripts (only `notes_for_verifier`, labelled as unverified hints), and profile selection MUST honour
`verifier.independence` against **every** implementer profile that authored commits in the unit (including fix units
and fallbacks), using the vendor of the model actually served: `different_vendor` (default) excludes all those
vendors; `different_model` excludes those model ids. If no independent verifier agent or judge is available, the unit
goes to `waiting_capacity` (reason `no independent verifier`) — independence is never relaxed at run time, and
`CFG-003` guarantees the configuration can always satisfy it once capacity returns. Where the served model is not
reported (OpenCode run mode), the profile's declared `vendor` counts (L4-FAC-003). A profile with vendor `unknown` is
never independent. An implementer with vendor `unknown` makes every verifier non-independent, so the unit waits.
The judge's diff leaves out the `verification.md` of every unit of the family (the harness's own report of an earlier round), and its prompt lists, under *Owner changes*, the files only the project's people changed on the unit branch: the criteria are judged on the committed code, owner changes included, but no finding is raised about an owner change itself. It also lists, under *Written by the harness this round*, the audit tests accepted in this round (path, outcomes of the audit gate run, source): they are committed after its review, so they are not in the diff or in the gate report's list, and the judge takes them as evidence and raises no finding that they are missing. It also lists, as `<l4:data kind="answer">` blocks, the answered technical, product and ambiguous questions of the unit and its fix units, the question text marked as the implementer's and unverified (L4-VER-065).

**L4-VER-002a** The verifier agent MAY only change paths matching `tdd.test_globs`, MAY NOT modify pre-existing tests
or tests written by the implementer, and MAY only "heal" (selectors, waits) tests it generated itself in the current
round; every other change is reverted by the guard. The audit writer also finds the code by import only: a test with
`inspect`, `dir(...)`, `vars(...)`, `__dict__`, or `getattr`/`hasattr` with a computed name, or with a secret-shaped string
literal (a redactor token shape, or a run of 12 or more letters, digits, `_` and `-` holding an upper-case letter, a
lower-case letter and a digit; a hex digest is fine) is `invalid`, and the writer is asked once more with the reason.
M1.13 (wave C, W-C4) adds three rules of the same kind: a test that calls `hasattr` with constant names on one object
