more than once (a cascade that guesses a method) is `invalid`; an audit test that imports a name from a shown source file
(or reads one off an imported module) that the file does not bind is `invalid`, the reason naming what the file does bind
(a module that is not shown, a submodule, a dunder, a file with a star import or a module `__getattr__` is not checked);
and the writer is shown the unit's `design.md` and `proposal.md` (at most 8,000 characters) after the code, with the
rule never to snapshot or compare a folder, a log or an event stream that the criterion or the design lets change
(`testwriter/audit` v4).

Live wave D (W-D2) adds three static checks of the same kind, so that a weak verifier agent's broken audit test is
rejected before it reaches the judge or a question (`testwriter/audit` v5): a module attribute read or called off a shown
source file that the file does not bind is `invalid` through every way of importing it (`from pkg import demo`,
`import pkg.demo as demo`, `import demo`, `import pkg.demo`, `importlib.import_module` with a constant name) and through
`getattr` with a constant name and no default (a name the test rebinds is not checked; a name a function of the module
declares `global` counts as bound; a module that binds names at run time, through `globals()` or its own `sys.modules`
entry, is not checked, and neither is `from pkg import name` of a package, which may name a submodule that is not shown);
`python -m <module>` (an argv list or a command string) of a shown source file that neither has an `if` testing
`__name__` against `"__main__"` nor calls or raises anything at its top level is `invalid` (a package is allowed, as is a
module that is not shown: only the unit's changed files are known); and a name the test reads but never imports, assigns
or defines (`threading` without `import threading`) is `invalid` (the check is blind to scope, so it never flags a bound
name, a star import turns it off, and a name only in annotations is left to the collection retry). The writer is asked
once more with the reason. A file that passes these but cannot be collected (an `ImportError` when the audit gate run
collects it) is removed, and the writer is asked once more with the collection output of its own file and its own code;
a file that still cannot be collected, or a retry with no test, is a `minor` finding (`an audit test was rejected`),
never a held criterion or a human question. The writer also refuses (audit and e2e) code whose bytes as `write_test_file` would write them, the marker on line 1 and then the code, declare an encoding other than UTF-8 (a coding cookie lands on line 2, where Python honours it and `ast.parse` does not see it): the reply is `invalid` with the reason `the test declares the encoding <encoding>; write UTF-8 without a coding cookie`, and `write_test_file` raises (L4-SEC-042, SCN-SEC-117).

**Vendor of a kiro-cli profile and `auto`** (L4-KJD-005, L4-KJD-013 to L4-KJD-015.) The vendor of a kiro-cli
profile with a pinned model is the vendor of its model's family (`claude-` anthropic, `gpt-` and `o<digit>` openai,
`gemini-` google, `deepseek-` deepseek, `glm-` zhipu, `minimax-` minimax, `qwen` alibaba, `kimi-` moonshot, `grok-` xai, `mai-` microsoft; the model id
is matched lowercased after its last `/`), with provenance `declared`; a model of no known family keeps the declared
vendor. A kiro-cli or copilot-cli profile whose `vendor:` contradicts its model's family does not load (`vendor contradicts the model:
<model> is made by <vendor>`; `amazon` and `aws` are not a family), the claude-code and codex rule. Under
`different_model`, models are compared after normalisation that folds a `.` between digits to `-`
(`claude-sonnet-4.5` is `claude-sonnet-4-5` is `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`). The rule is not applied to opencode in this
change: it keeps its declared vendor.

A kiro-cli profile with no model or `auto` is **routed**: Kiro may serve it with any Active model of the account (never an
Experimental one), so it has no single vendor, and its `vendor:` is ignored (it loads; doctor CFG-011 notes it). Its
possible vendors are those its latest probe recorded (the `auth` step lists the models, L4-KJD-013), whatever their age,
else the built-in set `anthropic`, `minimax`, `zhipu`, and are the union of the listing's and the built-in set's. Each
party of the check has a set of vendors: a routed party its possible vendors, any other its one vendor (`unknown` when none
is known). Under `different_vendor` a judge is vetoed when its set meets an implementer's set or either holds `unknown`.
Under `different_model`, when the judge or an implementer is routed, the judge is vetoed when the other party's model
(normalised, after its last `/`) is among the routed party's Active ids, when the other party's vendor is unknown, or when
both are routed. Two `auto` profiles are therefore never independent: pin a model on one side. A judge selected on a set
older than its own probe is checked again against the set that probe recorded and skipped when that set vetoes it. The
rule applies to the step-9 judges, `roles.verifier_agent`, the escalation keeper and the step-9 preflight, not to the
clarifier, the plan-readiness review or the `s1_judge` stand-in, which have no implementer to be independent of.

**A copilot-cli profile and `auto`** (L4-FAC-020.) A copilot-cli profile with no model, a blank model or `auto` is routed
too, whatever `vendor:` says: its possible vendors and models are the built-in set of Copilot CLI 1.0.102's model list
(`anthropic`, `google`, `microsoft`, `moonshot`, `openai` and `xai`; no probe lists models). A copilot-cli judge on `auto` is
therefore never independent of a claude-code or codex implementer under `different_vendor`: pin a model. The adapter
reports the served model (`assistant.message.model`, under `auto` else `session.auto_mode_resolved.chosenModel`): under
`auto` a concrete served model is the judge's `served` model and is checked like any adapter's, so a served vendor that is an
implementer's or unknown drops the verdict as `model_mismatch`; for a pinned model a served model that differs after
normalisation is a `model_mismatch` and one that is the same reports nothing, so the judge stays `declared` (whether GitHub
routing reports another id for a pinned model is [I]).

The independence record (`verdict.json` `independence`, and the line `independence: <status>: <parties>` in
`verification.md`) names a routed party `<profile> routed: <vendors, sorted, comma-separated> (auto)` and carries its
`vendors`; the status is `not independent (<mode>)`, else `routed (unverified)` when any party is routed, else
`declared (unverified)` when any is declared, else `verified (<mode>)`. When the session file of the run names the model
that served an `auto` judge (L4-KJD-015), the judge is `served`: its vendor is that model's family, the line reads
`<profile> <vendor> (served <model>)`, and a served vendor that is an implementer's or unknown drops the verdict as
`model_mismatch` and asks the next independent judge. A pinned kiro-cli model that the session file or a standard-error
warning contradicts is a `model_mismatch` too. The served model of a Kiro run is the CLI's own record, not a server
report [I].

### 10.2 Ladder

**L4-VER-002** Steps run in order; a hard failure in steps 0–3 stops the ladder with `FAIL` (evidence collected so
far is still written). Each step is resumable (L4-VER-011).

| Step | Name | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | preconditions | done-gate passes; branch contains base head (else merge first, §12.3); unit validates strict |
| 1 | integrity | no outstanding `guard.violation`; no deleted/skipped/weakened pre-existing tests (diff analysis); **red→green freeze held** for every task (test files, test-support paths and runner-config sections identical at the red and green commits); **a test or support path changed by a green or fix-chore commit** of the harness (test path freeze, L4-IMP-006 (7); allowed: the paths of a `task.unfrozen` (listed with their source and counted `(+n opened by task text)`), the files of a `task.tests_added` for an exempt commit, and the commits of a `[test-infra]` task; a blocker); **content scan** of the unit's test-support and runner-config changes for result-manipulating constructs — pytest hooks `pytest_runtest_makereport`, `pytest_report_teststatus`, `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (deselect/skip), `pytest_runtest_call` wrappers; jest/vitest custom `reporters`, `testResultsProcessor`, `testPathIgnorePatterns` additions; Playwright reporter or `grepInvert` changes; Go `TestMain` exiting 0; equivalents per language — any hit is a blocker unless the task carries a human `[test-infra]` tag; **support files never replace the code under test**: test-support files may not monkeypatch, patch or assign the **symbols the unit added or changed** (functions, methods, classes from the stub list and the diff) — patching collaborators such as clocks, network clients or environment on those modules stays allowed — and may not make any patch conditional on files or environment variables the unit creates (AST rule for Python, per-language rules [U] from the change-0 fixtures); a hit is a blocker; the rule is checked for opened files (L4-IMP-016) and stays [U] for other support changes; test-only dependencies added in green are a major finding (red is where they belong); gate configuration unchanged (L4-IMP-006), and runner sections changed by no red commit without `[test-infra]` or an answer (L4-IMP-040), including the **script entries the gate commands resolve to** (`package.json` scripts, Makefile/tox/poe/just targets); **new inline suppressions** in the unit's diff (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `eslint-disable`, `//nolint`, `#nosec`/`nosec`, `gitleaks:allow`) must each be **declared** in the implementer result (`suppressions: [{file, line, rule, reason}]`): an undeclared suppression is a major finding (the fix unit removes it, and declares it only if it cannot be removed); a suppression or a result-manipulating support or runner-config change that only people's commits wrote (per commit, as for tests: the commits that raised the number of that comment in the file are all people's; `git blame` only tells two lines of one text apart when both kinds of author added it; the author rule of L4-SEC-004) is the owner's edit on the unit branch: listed in `verification.md` (`## Suppressions added by humans`, `## Support and runner-config changes made by humans`), never a finding (W-D6, "human edits are listed, not reverted"); declared ones are listed in the PR and reviewed by the judge panel (a judge objection is judge-only → human verdict, never an automatic FAIL); `gitleaks:allow` and `nosec` are never accepted without a human `[config]` tag; no bulk snapshot updates without a task that says so; secret scan clean on the diff, run with the **harness-owned** gitleaks config and ignore file (the repository's `.gitleaksignore` is ignored); scope check per `sdd.scope_check`; **TDD history** for each non-exempt, non-`pre_adoption` task: a red commit (or a verifier red commit, L4-VER-012) precedes its green commit, the red tests fail at the red commit, and the red tests as committed in the red commit pass at head; a frozen test that a human answer unfroze for green (`task.unfrozen`, L4-IMP-002) is not a freeze violation: it is listed in `verification.md` and in the step's note (`(+n unfrozen by human answers)`); **Python encoding** (L4-SEC-042): a `.py` or `.pyi` file that base..head adds or changes, whoever committed it, and that declares an encoding other than `utf-8`, `utf-8-sig` or `ascii` (or whose first two lines cannot be read within a 64 KiB prefix) is a blocker, and so is a Python-named link, touched by base..head, whose target does or that ends at no regular file (one blocker lists every file) |
| 1 | integrity | no outstanding `guard.violation`; no pre-existing test deleted, skipped, changed or bound again by a harness commit, and no test an earlier step of the unit wrote changed by a later red commit, compared per test on the AST by file and qualified name (L4-VER-030..032; people's changes and allowed ones are listed); and **every test that passed at the base still passes on the unit's code** when the gate runs at head with every test and support file the unit added or changed at its base version (L4-VER-038; any language with a JUnit report); **red→green freeze held** for every task (test files, test-support paths and runner-config sections identical at the red and green commits); **a test or support path changed by a green or fix-chore commit** of the harness (test path freeze, L4-IMP-006 (7); allowed: the paths of a `task.unfrozen` (listed with their source and counted `(+n opened by task text)`), the files of a `task.tests_added` for an exempt commit, and the commits of a `[test-infra]` task; a blocker); **content scan** of the unit's test-support and runner-config changes for result-manipulating constructs — pytest hooks `pytest_runtest_makereport`, `pytest_report_teststatus`, `pytest_collection_modifyitems` (deselect/skip), `pytest_runtest_call` wrappers; jest/vitest custom `reporters`, `testResultsProcessor`, `testPathIgnorePatterns` additions; Playwright reporter or `grepInvert` changes; Go `TestMain` exiting 0; equivalents per language — any hit is a blocker unless the task carries a human `[test-infra]` tag; **support files never replace the code under test**: test-support files may not monkeypatch, patch or assign the **symbols the unit added or changed** (functions, methods, classes from the stub list and the diff) — patching collaborators such as clocks, network clients or environment on those modules stays allowed — and may not make any patch conditional on files or environment variables the unit creates (AST rule for Python, per-language rules [U] from the change-0 fixtures); a hit is a blocker; the rule is checked for opened files (L4-IMP-016) and for every changed Python test-support file, a test-glob file with no test included (L4-VER-037, L4-VER-039: module-level code, an autouse fixture, a fixture one requests and a plain function that patch the unit's code block; a fixture a test requests by name is listed), and its list of result-manipulating constructs, which also covers the unit's production diff (a line naming `.l4-out`, a report path, `L4_*` or `PYTEST_*` is a blocker; a test for pytest is listed for the judge), gains `pytest_pyfunc_call`, a non-wrapper `pytest_runtest_call` or `pytest_runtest_setup`, and an assignment to `.obj` or `.runtest` (L4-VER-039); it stays [U] for other languages; test-only dependencies added in green are a major finding (red is where they belong); gate configuration unchanged (L4-IMP-006), including the **script entries the gate commands resolve to** (`package.json` scripts, Makefile/tox/poe/just targets); **new inline suppressions** in the unit's diff (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `eslint-disable`, `//nolint`, `#nosec`/`nosec`, `gitleaks:allow`) must each be **declared** in the implementer result (`suppressions: [{file, line, rule, reason}]`): an undeclared suppression is a major finding (the fix unit removes it, and declares it only if it cannot be removed); a suppression or a result-manipulating support or runner-config change that only people's commits wrote (per commit, as for tests: the commits that raised the number of that comment in the file are all people's; `git blame` only tells two lines of one text apart when both kinds of author added it; the author rule of L4-SEC-004) is the owner's edit on the unit branch: listed in `verification.md` (`## Suppressions added by humans`, `## Support and runner-config changes made by humans`), never a finding (W-D6, "human edits are listed, not reverted"); declared ones are listed in the PR and reviewed by the judge panel (a judge objection is judge-only → human verdict, never an automatic FAIL); `gitleaks:allow` and `nosec` are never accepted without a human `[config]` tag; no bulk snapshot updates without a task that says so; secret scan clean on the diff, run with the **harness-owned** gitleaks config and ignore file (the repository's `.gitleaksignore` is ignored); scope check per `sdd.scope_check`; **TDD history** for each non-exempt, non-`pre_adoption` task: a red commit (or a verifier red commit, L4-VER-012) precedes its green commit, the red tests fail at the red commit, and the red tests as committed in the red commit pass at head; a frozen test that a human answer unfroze for green (`task.unfrozen`, L4-IMP-002) is not a freeze violation: it is listed in `verification.md` and in the step's note (`(+n unfrozen by human answers)`); **Python encoding** (L4-SEC-042): a `.py` or `.pyi` file that base..head adds or changes, whoever committed it, and that declares an encoding other than `utf-8`, `utf-8-sig` or `ascii` (or whose first two lines cannot be read within a 64 KiB prefix) is a blocker, and so is a Python-named link, touched by base..head, whose target does or that ends at no regular file (one blocker lists every file) |
| 2 | build | `gates.setup`, `build`, `lint`, `typecheck` succeed, then each reproduced `repository-ci:<job>` step of the active window (L4-ARC-002; a failure is the finding `repository CI failed: <job>`) |
| 3 | tests | full `gates.test` (+ `e2e` when configured, with `gates.e2e.serve`) re-run by the verifier; non-vacuous (L4-GAT-002); every test added in the unit executed; each new test repeated `flaky_repeats` times — any flip = flaky finding |
| 4 | traceability | build `criterion → [tests] → status` from reports; apply L4-VER-009 (discriminating evidence) and `max_criteria_per_test`; criteria without discriminating passing evidence are *uncovered*; a proved, passing test over the cap is kept as a candidate that the judge can name for a criterion (L4-VER-054) |
| 4a | audit sampling | for `audit_sample_ratio` of the covered **new** criteria (at least 1, chosen by a seeded hash of unit id + round so the choice is reproducible), the verifier agent writes an independent test from the criterion text alone, in an **exported tree without `.git`** from which every test file and test-support file the unit added or changed has been removed (so it cannot read them, not even through git history); the audit test must be discriminating against the baseline of L4-VER-009 and pass on head — a failure on head goes to L4-VER-012. An accepted audit test is then linted in this step, on its own file: every `gates.lint` and `gates.typecheck` command runs on it (the lint gate of step 2 stays where it is, since it runs before the test exists and moving it behind 4a would fail the ladder on a test the verifier wrote); a failure goes back to the writer once with the lint output, and a test that still fails is rejected (`lint: <first line>`), not committed and not shown to the judge, and reported as a minor finding like any rejected audit test (the criterion is not held: the unit's own tests trace it), so a lint failure never reaches a hand-off head. The judge's per-test list holds the round's accepted audit tests, labelled `audit`, and `verification.md` lists the rejected ones with the reason. The zero-value run of an audit test is judged by L4-IMP-060 against the audit's head run: a run that could not run the test (no test executed, its module did not import) is recorded `inconclusive` (L4-VER-050), not rejected: no finding, the file is not committed, and `verification.md` lists it under `## Inconclusive audit runs`. Audit tests, and their zero-value run, run with every test and support file the unit added, changed or deleted at its base version (added data under `fixtures/`, `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `testdata/` excepted), collecting only the audit file when the gate is pytest (L4-VER-033); they never run with the unit's files in place; an audit test whose import fails in a production module, or that gives no readable result, holds its criterion, and one whose own import fails twice is rejected (L4-VER-034); each record says `support` (L4-VER-036) |
| 5 | test generation | for each uncovered criterion (when `generate_missing_tests`) the verifier agent writes a test tagged with the criterion ID — Playwright when the criterion is UI-facing (L4-VER-014), else the project's unit/integration framework. It must be **discriminating against the baseline of L4-VER-009** and **pass on head** (the head run with the e2e runner's own support files the unit changed at their base versions, never added app data; when it cannot run so or its server does not start, uncollectable and held, never run in place, L4-VER-035). Pass at the baseline → rejected as non-discriminating (one retry). Fail on head → L4-VER-012. "Generation impossible" = the agent returns `not_testable` with a reason, or two non-discriminating attempts, or the test cannot be collected. A UI criterion whose accept is in force is **waived**: the writer is not called, no hold is raised and `verify.generated` says `waived` (L4-VER-067). Generated and audit tests are kept in the round's evidence directory and committed **once, at the end of the round** (L4-VER-011) |
| 6 | quality (opt-in) | `gates.extra` entries such as diff coverage or mutation testing on changed files |
| 7 | contracts / security (opt-in) | `gates.extra` entries such as schemathesis, property tests, `semgrep --baseline-commit <base>` |
| 8 | S1 judge | per criterion one `noul` over a compact evidence state (criterion text, tracing tests with status, most relevant excerpt) kept within the engine's state budget (§3.2, measured with the S1 tokenizer): the true/false question "Does this evidence show that the criterion is satisfied?" (`p`) **and** a 4-way `choice` over `implemented | contradicted | not_implemented | unrelated` (the choice's probabilities are recorded under `evidence`). Both are **recorded only**: no `p` changes a verdict or a finding (`decisions.criterion.accept` is reserved for a later calibrated gate; nothing reads it today). The step is `unavailable` when the server is missing, down or answers unusably (for `engine: ollama` also: the host is older than 0.35.0, the model is not pulled, or the request would exceed the 64 KiB body limit: `unavailable: input too large`, never cut), and aggregation goes on (SCN-VER-24); it is `not_run` when `verifier.s1.enabled` is off, `roles.s1_judge` is empty, or it holds no `backend: system-one` profile (an adapter profile there serves only the clarifier's `llm_boolean` stand-in, L4-CLR-002) |
| 9 | LLM judge panel | per criterion: verdict + findings (§10.3) **and** an adequacy review of every tracing test ("does this test check the criterion's observable outcome?"); every evidence reference re-checked by code (file:line exists and contains the quote; test id exists in the report with the claimed status); an unverifiable citation downgrades that verdict to `insufficient_evidence`. The judge prompt contains the gate report (per-test outcome with criterion IDs) as well as the diff. Every criterion verdict `fail` MUST carry `counterexample: {call, expected, actual}`, which the harness executes in the gate sandbox on a scratch copy of head (never the unit worktree: the `call` is model-written code) before the verdict counts. A `fail` whose counterexample does not reproduce is downgraded to `insufficient_evidence`. The judge prompt asks for inputs that no scenario pins down, which are reported as `spec_gap` findings [spikes/01–03: 2/2 wrong `fail` verdicts without a report or counterexample, V; the Sonnet judge with the report found a real `spec_gap`, V; causality I, model and input are confounded]. A diff over 120000 characters is judged in parts (L4-VER-041) whose replies are merged (L4-VER-042), and what the judge cannot see is a `judge_view` hold (L4-VER-043, L4-VER-044). A criterion whose evidence the parts split is judged once more on all of its files in a follow-up call, and its reason says so (L4-VER-056 to L4-VER-058) |
| 9 | LLM judge panel | per criterion: verdict + findings (§10.3) **and** an adequacy review of every tracing test ("does this test check the criterion's observable outcome?"); every evidence reference re-checked by code (file:line exists and contains the quote; test id exists in the report with the claimed status); an unverifiable citation downgrades that verdict to `insufficient_evidence`. The judge prompt contains the gate report (per-test outcome with criterion IDs) as well as the diff. Every criterion verdict `fail` MUST carry `counterexample: {call, expected, actual}`, which the harness executes in the gate sandbox on a scratch copy of head (never the unit worktree: the `call` is model-written code) before the verdict counts. A `fail` whose counterexample does not reproduce is downgraded to `insufficient_evidence`. The judge prompt asks for inputs that no scenario pins down, which are reported as `spec_gap` findings A spec file that is over 262,144 bytes or not a regular file, or a requirements, bugfix or spec-delta file cut by `verifier.judge_context_budget_tokens`, is named to the judge and holds the round (L4-KSP-014); each done task's whole block is checked against the diff. [spikes/01–03: 2/2 wrong `fail` verdicts without a report or counterexample, V; the Sonnet judge with the report found a real `spec_gap`, V; causality I, model and input are confounded] |
| 10 | aggregation | §10.4 |

**Rows that read nothing say so (L4-VER-002).** A row of the ladder or of the Evidence section never reports success for
a check that looked at no file. (1) *Step 6, diff coverage* measures the languages of `verifier.evidence.diff_coverage.languages`
(`python`). A change that touches no code at all (documentation, spec and harness paths, deleted files) keeps `100.0`.
A change whose code (source files by extension, not tests and not the exempt paths of the files table) is all outside
the measured languages is `not_applicable`: the row and the Evidence section say `not measured: diff coverage measures
python only; changed code outside it: <files>` (at most five files, then `and N more`), no percentage is given, and it
raises no hold under `warn` or `fail` and no "Needs attention" line. A mixed change measures its Python as before and
names the other files in a `Not measured:` line. (2) *Step 1, content scan and suppressions* read Python files. When the
diff holds changed files they cannot read (test-support and runner-config files for the scan, source and test files for
suppressions) and found nothing in the files they read, the row is `skipped` with `not checked: python only; changed
files outside it: <files>`; a `skipped` row blocks nothing. (3) *Step 4a, audit sampling* writes pytest tests: when the
unit changed files outside the exempt paths and none is a `.py` file the step is `not_run` with `audit sampling writes
pytest tests only; changed code is not python`: no writer call, no finding, no file.

### 10.3 Judge verdict schema

```json
{
  "$id": "l4/judge-verdict@1",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["criteria", "test_adequacy", "findings", "riskiest_assumptions"],
  "properties": {
    "criteria": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["id", "verdict", "evidence"],
      "properties": {
        "id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^C-[0-9a-f]{8}$"},
        "verdict": {"enum": ["pass", "fail", "insufficient_evidence", "not_verifiable"]},
        "confidence": {"enum": ["high", "medium", "low"]},
        "evidence": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "required": ["kind", "ref"],
          "properties": {"kind": {"enum": ["file", "test", "log", "trace"]},
                         "ref": {"type": "string"}, "quote": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 300}}}},
        "reasoning": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 1200},
        "counterexample": {"type": "object", "required": ["call", "expected", "actual"],
          "description": "required when verdict is fail; executed by the harness before the verdict counts (L4-VER-002 step 9)",
          "properties": {"call": {"type": "string"}, "expected": {"type": "string"}, "actual": {"type": "string"}}}}}},
    "test_adequacy": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["test", "criterion", "adequate"],
      "properties": {"test": {"type": "string"}, "criterion": {"type": "string"},
                     "adequate": {"type": "boolean"}, "reason": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 600},
                     "generated_test_misreads_criterion": {"type": "boolean"}}}},
    "findings": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["severity", "title", "detail", "evidence"],
      "properties": {
        "severity": {"enum": ["blocker", "major", "minor"]},
        "criterion": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
        "title": {"type": "string"}, "detail": {"type": "string"},
        "evidence": {"type": "array"}, "suggested_fix": {"type": "string"},
        "spec_gap": {"type": "boolean", "description": "behaviour not covered by any criterion"}}}},
    "riskiest_assumptions": {"type": "array", "minItems": 3, "maxItems": 3, "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "feedback": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["id", "addressed", "evidence"],
      "properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^FB-[0-9]{3,}$"},
                     "addressed": {"type": "boolean"}, "evidence": {"type": "string"}}}},
    "accepted": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["id", "addressed", "evidence"],
      "properties": {"id": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^F-[0-9a-f]{6}$"},
                     "addressed": {"type": "boolean"}, "evidence": {"type": "string"}}}},
    "satisfied": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object",
      "required": ["task", "holds", "evidence"],
      "properties": {"task": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 40},
                     "holds": {"type": "boolean"}, "evidence": {"type": "string"}}}}
  }
}
```

`riskiest_assumptions` is mandatory so that a judge that "finds nothing" still has to name what could make its
verdict wrong (a reviewer reporting zero findings on a large diff is treated as suspicious, per the maintainer's
operating rules). `counterexample` is optional in the schema (a `pass` has none) and required by L4-VER-002 step 9
for every `fail`; a `fail` without one, or with one that does not reproduce, counts as `insufficient_evidence`.

`feedback` is optional. When the prompt holds a `<l4:data kind="feedback">` block (L4-FBK-007), the reply answers once per
listed item: `addressed` says whether the change does what the item asks, and `evidence` cites `file:line` of the diff. A
reply without the array, or without an item, counts as `addressed: false` with the evidence "not answered". The harness
decides from the answers (every judge asked must say `true`; a `config` item also needs its variable in the changed
non-test code); the judge's answer alone closes nothing.

`satisfied` is optional. When the prompt holds a `<l4:data kind="satisfied">` block (L4-VER-018), the reply answers once
per listed task: `holds` says whether the code and documents at head do what the task's text says, and `evidence`
cites `file:line` or a test id. A task left out is asked for once more (L4-VER-017) and then counts as
`holds: false` with the evidence "not answered", which is a minor finding; a `holds: false` answer is a major one.

**Weak judges (live wave D, W-D1).** A reply that breaks the schema only trivially is repaired by the harness
before it counts as invalid: a string over its `maxLength` is cut there and ends in `…`, a free-text field (`suggested_fix`,
`reasoning`, `reason`, `detail`, `title`, `quote`, `expected`, `actual`) that is a list is joined by newlines and one that is
an object or a number becomes its JSON or its text, a key the schema does not list is dropped, a `null` in an optional
field that does not allow one is dropped, and a list of free text (`riskiest_assumptions`) longer than its `maxItems`
keeps its first items and joins the rest, by newlines, into its last allowed item (L4-VER-074). Nothing else is touched:
an enum is never guessed, a missing field is never invented, a short list is never filled, a list of objects is never
shortened, and a repair that would change the id or the verdict of any criterion, or that leaves the reply invalid, is not
applied, so a reply is never repaired into a `pass` it did not state. A repaired reply is kept, costs no second call and is
recorded as `judge.reply_repaired{round, profile, fields}` (schema paths, never values). A reply that is still invalid is
asked for once more with the violated paths (at most 800 characters, never values) and its own rejected reply; a second
break discards the judge, and the next independent judge is asked (L4-VER-015, L4-VER-075). Every `verify.judge` event carries `reply`, one of `valid`, `repaired` (the repair
alone), `retried` (a second call answered a schema break, or a reply that left out an asked accepted, feedback or satisfied id, L4-VER-017) or `discarded`, and `verification.md` and `verdict.json` count the
four per judge profile over the unit's ledger (`judge_replies`) beside the round's own (`judge_reply`).

### 10.4 Aggregation (deterministic)

**L4-VER-003** Per criterion (evidence = discriminating tracing tests per L4-VER-009 whose adequacy the panel did not
reject):

| Deterministic evidence | Judge panel | S1 `p` | Criterion result |
|---|---|---|---|
| ≥ 1 adequate discriminating test passes (incl. accepted generated/audit tests) | pass | any | **pass** |
| ≥ 1 adequate discriminating test passes | fail with validated evidence and a reproducing counterexample | any | **disputed** → tie-breaker judge if configured, else **needs_human** |
| a tracing or audit test fails on head (and is not a misreading per L4-VER-012) | any | any | **fail** |
| uncovered | any | any | **needs_human** when `sdd.require_traceability: true` (default) |
| uncovered | pass with validated evidence | ≥ accept_threshold | **pass (judgment)** — only when `sdd.require_traceability: false`; flagged in the report |
| uncovered | pass with validated evidence | < accept_threshold | **needs_human** (traceability off) |
| any | `not_verifiable` | any | **needs_human** |
| any | error / refusal / truncated / schema-invalid after repair / served-model mismatch | any | **needs_human** (fail closed) |

Unit verdict: **FAIL** if any of steps 0–3 failed, any criterion is `fail` (which always rests on a failing
deterministic check: a gate, a tracing/audit/generated test, or an integrity check), or any **deterministic**
`blocker`/`major` finding exists (e.g. flaky test, undeclared suppression, test-only dependency added in green, scope
violation with `scope_check: fail`); else **NEEDS_HUMAN** if any
criterion is `disputed`/`needs_human`, or a judge raised a `blocker`/`major` finding with validated citations that no
deterministic check confirms (the human decides; `reject` turns it into a fix-unit finding, L4-VER-013); else
**PASS**. LLM judgments alone never FAIL a unit (P7).
`minor` findings never block; they are listed in the PR and (if `fix_minor_findings`) become a fix unit after PASS.
S1 never decides a criterion on its own: it only participates in the traceability-off judgment row and is otherwise
recorded for calibration.

**L4-VER-009 Discriminating evidence.** A passing tracing test counts as evidence for a criterion only if it traces
at most `verifier.max_criteria_per_test` criteria (or the judge named it for that criterion, L4-VER-054), the panel
did not mark it inadequate, and it is discriminating
against the unit's single **synthetic baseline**: the unit's *base tree* — the merge-base for a parent unit, the
parent's head at fix-unit creation for a fix unit — **plus all red-phase stubs of the unit** (and their zero-value
variants, L4-IMP-002). Stubs make new modules and symbols exist at the baseline, so compiled languages build and every
test reports individually. A test is discriminating when it fails at the synthetic baseline, and a criterion's
evidence is discriminating when **at least one** of its tracing tests also fails **by assertion** against the
zero-value stubs (tests whose correct answer is the zero value count together with such a sibling, never alone):
* **implementer tests** — proven during the red phase (both runs, L4-IMP-002) and re-checked by the TDD-history step;
  a criterion recorded `not applicable` or accepted by a person after an inconclusive check is labelled for the judge
  (L4-VER-051);
* **verifier-written tests** (steps 4a and 5) — run by the verifier at the synthetic baseline and with zero-value stubs;
* **existing criteria** (text unchanged from the base specs, e.g. an untouched scenario inside a MODIFIED
  requirement): pass-to-pass is accepted. The base specs are read from git at the baseline commit (`git show
  <base>:openspec/specs/…`), never from the worktree, which is at the unit's head (HB-3);
* units without red stubs (`pre_adoption`): a collection or import error at the baseline does not count; such
  criteria go to step 5 and, failing that, to a human verdict.
* **tests people or a test chore wrote** (M1.11): a test that carries a criterion and has no proof above, and whose file
  only people's commits touched since the base (`human`) or that a test chore added (`chore`, `task.tests_added`), is run
  by the verifier in step 4: first with the project's functions answering their zero value (it must fail by assertion), and
  if it still passes, with the unit's changed production files swapped to the base's (it must fail by assertion there too:
  an error, which is what a test meets that only reaches the unit's new code, a module that does not import at the base, a
  skipped id and a missing report are no proof). At most two gate runs per round, none
  without such a test. An accepted test is recorded (`verify.extra_proof{round, criterion, tests, source, via, files}`) and
  counts with the proof `human` or `chore` while its file has the content that was run; a rejected one stays a finding.
A non-discriminating or inadequate tracing test is ignored as evidence and recorded as a `minor` finding.

**L4-VER-010** Internal verifier errors (exceptions, infrastructure failures) MUST leave the unit in `verifying` with
no verdict and exit 1; after 3 consecutive internal errors on the same unit it goes to `escalated`. Each such error
(an exception out of the verifier hook; not a missing role, exit 12, a secret in a push, exit 13, or an `L4Exit`, which
have their own codes) is recorded as `verify.error {error, message}` in the unit's ledger before the run ends. The
count is the `verify.error` events at the end of the committed ledger since the last `verify.verdict` or phase
change; the third one ends the run in `escalated`, exit 13, `exit_reason` `escalated: 3 consecutive internal verifier
errors`, and a later run of the unit does not call the verifier again.

**L4-VER-061 The excerpt of a red GitHub job is the failing step's.** When the sweep reads a red GitHub Actions job,
the forge SHALL read the job's steps (`GET actions/jobs/:id`, one short try) besides its log and SHALL build the excerpt
from the failing step's section of the log. The log's lines SHALL lose the byte-order mark and the runner's timestamp
prefix. The failing step of the API is its first step with the conclusion `failure`, else `timed_out` or `cancelled`.
The anchor is the first line that starts with `##[error]`, counting only lines not before that step's `started_at` when
it is known and such a line exists (a `continue-on-error` step prints `##[error]` and does not fail the job). A section
starts at a line that starts with `##[group]Run ` (a step's header, also a step inside a composite action), at `Post job
cleanup.` and at `Cleaning up orphan processes`; the lines before the first header are the set-up section. The excerpt
SHALL be the anchor's section to its end, not to the anchor line (a tool's `::error::` annotation is a `##[error]` line
in the middle of a step): its `Run …` header line, then the output of L4-VER-063, never the header's group (the script,
`shell:`, `env:`, `with:`). `##[error]`, `##[warning]` and `##[notice]` SHALL read `Error: `, `Warning: ` and `Notice: `,
as on GitHub's page. `ci.failed.jobs[].failed_step` SHALL record the API's failing step's name, else the section's
header, redacted and at most 300 characters. A log with no `##[error]` line SHALL give its last 40 lines as before,
without the timestamps; no log (expired, not an Actions job) SHALL give an empty excerpt as before, and the steps are
then not read. A failed read of the steps MUST NOT lose the log. `l4 ci watch --tail N` prints the last N lines of this
excerpt.

**L4-VER-062 The excerpt of a red GitLab job ends with the job's script.** When the trace of a red GitLab job has a
`step_script` (or `build_script`) section, the excerpt SHALL be that section's lines (L4-VER-063) followed by the
trace's closing line when it starts with `ERROR: Job failed`; `after_script`, the cache upload and the artifact upload,
which the runner writes after a failed script, MUST NOT be in it. A trace without such a section SHALL give the last 40
lines of the cleaned trace as before, and the cleaning also drops the runner's sections `archive_cache` and
`archive_cache_on_failure`. The recorded `step` (the last `$ ` command of the script) is unchanged.

**L4-VER-063 The excerpt keeps the failure's summary lines within the budgets.** The excerpt of L4-VER-061 and
L4-VER-062 SHALL be, in this order: the header line (GitHub), the summary lines of the section that come before its
last 40 lines, one `...` line when lines were left out, the last 40 lines, and the closing line (GitLab). A summary
line is one of: pytest's `FAILED` and `ERROR` lines (its short test summary), its first six `E` lines, a count of
failures or errors above zero (`1 failed, 2277 passed`, `Found 2 errors`), a jest, vitest or go `FAIL` line, and a
GitHub `Error:` annotation other than `Process completed with exit code`; at most 12 lines and 1,200 characters, in log
order, without repeats. Every line SHALL be cut to 500 characters. The excerpt SHALL be at most 3,000 characters: the
tail's first lines go first, down to five, then the summary's last lines. Redaction SHALL stay in the sweep, after the
forge: the `tail`, the `step` and the `failed_step` are redacted with the run's redactor before they are recorded.

**L4-VER-064 The blocker's detail names the failing step and leads with the failure.** The detail of a `repository CI
failed: <job>` blocker (step 0) SHALL read ``job `<job>` (stage <stage>) failed in step `<failed_step>` on the hand-off
commit <H10> (<url>)`` when the job's `failed_step` is recorded and no command was derived, and as before otherwise.
When summary lines (L4-VER-063) of the recorded tail are not in the end of the log that the detail quotes (`Log ends:`,
up to 300 characters), the detail SHALL add `Failed: <those lines, joined with " | ">` after that part, the lines that name a failing test first (pytest `FAILED` and `ERROR`, jest and vitest `FAIL`, go `--- FAIL`), then the counts, then pytest's `E` lines, then annotations, at most 240 characters, and quote a shorter end (at least 80 characters), so that both fit the first 600 characters, which every fix spec keeps (the window is the one shown after the `again:` sentence of L4-OPS-023, when there is one); when there is none, the detail SHALL be byte-identical to the detail of 0.4.20. The `Failed:` part SHALL open only when a line that names a failing test, or a count line, is not in the first window; its lines SHALL be chosen against the smallest window that part can leave (`max(80, min(300, 600 - len(where) - 250 - 19))` or the like), so that no failing test falls out of both parts, and a detail whose only missing lines are `E` lines or annotations SHALL have no `Failed:` part. Step 0 SHALL record a
GitHub job's `ci.step` as `skipped`, with `step` its `failed_step` and the reason `a GitHub Actions step is named, not
re-run: no command is derived from a workflow file`; it MUST NOT read `.gitlab-ci.yml` for it or take a `$ ` line of
its output as a step.

**L4-VER-065 Every judge prompt carries the family's answered questions.** Every judge prompt of a round (the whole
diff, each part and each follow-up) SHALL carry one `<l4:data kind="answer" id="<id>" by="<actor>">` block per answered
question of the unit's family whose kind is `technical`, `product`, `ambiguous` or unknown. `verdict` and `harness`
questions, and dismissed, superseded and open questions, SHALL be left out. `<id>` SHALL be `<fix unit>/Q-NNN` for a fix
unit's question, and `<actor>` the answer's actor (L4-QMD-009). A block SHALL hold the question's title and options,
marked as the implementer's unverified text, and the effective answer, each redacted before it is cut (title 300,
options 2,000, answer 3,000 characters). The blocks together SHALL be at most 12,000 characters, and the questions past
that SHALL be named. The block's length SHALL be charged to the judge's context budget before the spec text. An
unreadable questions file SHALL be named in the block and SHALL NOT stop the round.

**L4-VER-066 The judge judges a criterion as an answer narrowed it.** The judge's rules SHALL say that an answer block is
the project's decision and its question text the implementer's, that a criterion an answer settles or narrows is judged
as the answer reads it with the answer's id in its reason, that an answer never makes a criterion pass without evidence,
never outweighs a failing gate and adds no criterion, and that an input an answer settles is not a `spec_gap`. The
judge prompt version SHALL be `judge@13`. The round's `verify.judge` event SHALL list the answers shown as
`answers: [[<id>, <answer_sha256>], ...]`, and `[]` when the prompt held none.

**L4-VER-067 An accepted UI criterion is not held again.** The text of a UI hold SHALL be ``UI criterion C-… has no end-to-end
test; see the generated UI tests table`` and name no status, so its id (`H-` and eight hex digits of the text) is the same in
every round; the status and the writer's reason stay in the generated UI tests table and in `verify.generated`, and the
hold's question (not hashed) and the delegate's material give them and say that an accept lasts until the criterion's text or
its tracing tests change. An accept of a UI hold SHALL be bound to a hash of the hold's text, `text_sha256` of the criterion
and the head blobs of the files of the criterion's tracing tests (step 4's trace; a test id is mapped to its file by
`file_of_test`, else by `test_locate.file_of_id` over the work tree, so a test of any language counts; the audit and generated
tests are left out, a round writes them after the accept), as an accept of a `judge view:` hold is (L4-VER-046); an accept of
the criterion itself is bound to its text only (L4-VER-013). Before step 5 calls the writer, a UI criterion with a gap SHALL
be *waived* when an accept of the criterion is in force, or the latest accept of any UI hold of the criterion is in force;
the hold's criterion is found by `question.raised{criterion, criterion_sha256}` and, for a ledger written before this change,
by the title ``Hold H-…: UI criterion C-… has no end-to-end test``. A waived criterion SHALL record
`verify.generated{criterion, status: waived, by: <the answered question>, attempts: 0}`, call no writer and raise no hold;
its minor gap finding stays and says `waived by …`, no fix unit is made for it (a waived gap is closed), and when every gap of
the round is waived nothing is checked out. A waiver ends when the criterion's text changes or, for an accept of a hold, a
file of its tracing tests changes; on a `human.void`; and on a later reject of the criterion or of any of its holds, also one
a fix unit consumed. A criterion whose own verdict in force is a reject SHALL NOT be waived by the accept of a hold. A
failing tracing test of the criterion suspends the waiver for that round only (no `human.void` is written for a hold's
accept); the criterion is waived again once the test passes. An accept of a hold written before this change carries no
binding: it survives a change of the criterion's text or tracing files and ends only by a reject, a void or a failing tracing
test. Only `accept` waives; a rejected hold keeps the path of L4-VER-013, and a delegate's accept waives as any accept does.
Residual risk (named, accepted): an accept given on `fails_at_head` survives later UI rework that does not touch the tracing
tests. [V, a consumer's unit raised the UI hold of one criterion three times in five rounds, once per generator status, and
each was a question for a person and a run]

**L4-VER-068 The judge is told which named tests red changed.** The judge's prompt SHALL have a data block `## Named tests changed
in place`, beside the owner changes and in the user text only (`judge@13` and its system text do not change), that lists once
per id, at most 40 lines, each test of a `tests.superseded{reason: named_by_task}` event (L4-IMP-082, L4-IMP-089) with its
source and the words that the reviewed task names it, red changed it and green made it pass. For a test of another language
the block SHALL also give its lines at the base and at head (each cut at 1500 characters; the diff shows a Python test) and
ask the judge to check that the new version still asserts all the old one did except what the task changes. When those
lines are found and the same at both (red changed the test through its file's shared lines, L4-IMP-089), the block SHALL give
instead the words `its own lines are the same at the base and at head; red changed it through its file (shared constants,
fixtures or helpers):` and the file's unified diff between the base and head (3 lines of context, cut at 1500 characters).

**L4-VER-069 Step 3 records why each test failed, and in which gate.** The verdict of a round (`verdict.json`) SHALL hold,
beside the `tests` map (id to status, unchanged), a `failures` map: for each test id that failed or errored in step 3,
`{gate, kind, message}`. `gate` is `test` (the unit's test gate) or `e2e` (the browser gate; an id both reports hold is the
e2e one). `kind` is the failure kind the JUnit reader gives (`assertion`, `not_implemented`, `error`, `other`, …), and
where the reader gives none `error` for an errored test and `other` for a failed one. `message` is the first line of the
failure message, redacted and at most 200 characters. A module that a report could not collect has a record of its own,
kind `collection`, with the first line of its collection detail (else the module's name): it is not a test id, so it is
left out of the ids a fix chore must see passing (L4-IMP-090) and of the grouping of L4-VER-006. The `test` side holds at
most 200 records (the first ids in order) and `failures_dropped` counts the rest; the `e2e` side is whole, because a fix
chore asks for those tests. The verdict also holds `e2e_tests`, the ids of the e2e report, which tells a browser test from a
unit test in `tests`. `restore_round` keeps the three keys of a reused round. Readers that do not know the keys keep
working, and a verdict written before them has none (no id is known then, and a fix chore relies on the finding's title
alone, L4-IMP-090). [V, a consumer's end-to-end test raised an error before any check; nothing in the round said which gate
a failing test came from or whether it failed by assertion or by error, so a broken test and broken code looked the same]

**L4-VER-015 Failure precedence.** One rule decides what a failing verifier dependency means:
| Situation | Outcome |
|---|---|
| a required role (verifier agent, judges) has no usable profile — quota, 429, cool-down, independence | `waiting_capacity`, exit 12 (L4-AVL-010) |
| exception or infrastructure failure inside the harness | stays `verifying`, exit 1 (L4-VER-010) |
| a judge answered but the answer is refused, truncated, schema-invalid after repair, or from a mismatched model | that judge's verdicts are discarded; the next independent judge is tried; if none remains, affected criteria are `needs_human` |
| a judge call fails mid-request with a limit signal | treated as "no usable profile" for that judge (first row) |
| a judge call times out (no answer within the backend timeout) | retried once, or split (L4-VER-071); a timeout left after that holds the round, and the next judge is not asked (L4-VER-075) |

**L4-VER-016 A feedback-only fix unit consumes the rejects its round could not convert.** A `reject` ends when the fix
unit that took it is spawned (`fix.spawned.consumed`). A round whose only fix tasks are feedback tasks (`feedback_only`)
takes no reject, because the planner lists a human reject that has no criterion and no `WHEN … THEN …` as not
converted. `effective_verdicts` SHALL drop a `reject` whose `human.verdict` event is before (in ledger order) a
`fix.spawned` event with `feedback_only: true` and no `lists_unconverted: true`, the event as 0.4.5 and older wrote it.
A spawn that has `lists_unconverted: true` consumes only the questions of its `consumed` list. A `reject` recorded
after that event stays in force. A `fix.spawned` without `feedback_only: true` keeps the rule that only the questions of
its `consumed` list are consumed, and an `accept` is not changed. When the fix loop spawns a feedback-only fix unit, the
`consumed` list of its `fix.spawned` event SHALL also hold the questions of the rejects in force that the round listed as
not converted. A hold that is raised again in a later round has then no verdict in force: it is asked as a new hold
question (the earlier question is consumed), so a person or an allowed agent decides on the fixed code, and the round
does not fail on the old reject. Why this is right: a feedback-only plan exists only when no finding was convertible, so
every reject in force was a non-convertible human one; the documented way out of that escalation is the feedback
(L4-OPS-022); the feedback is the concrete form of the rejection, and `feedback.judged` checks that it was addressed.

**L4-VER-017 The judge's evidence answers survive a resumed round and a reply that leaves one out.** When a round
resumes at aggregation (D4), the ladder SHALL record each `review.accepted_judged` row of the reused round again, with
the new round's number and `reused_from` set to the reused round; a reused round with no such row carries none. The
merge guard of L4-YOLO-028 reads the rows of the PASS round only, so a PASS that a person's accepted hold gave keeps
the judge's answers of the round it reuses. When the judge prompt has an accepted block or a feedback block and a
valid reply leaves out an id of a block, the judge run SHALL make one more call, within its at most two calls: the
first prompt, the judge's own reply (redacted and cut as for a schema repair) and a message that names each missing
id. A valid second reply SHALL be the verdict (`reply: retried`). A second reply that is not valid, a second call that
times out or errs, and a second call served by another model SHALL keep the first verdict: a valid verdict is never
dropped over an evidence answer. An id that no kept reply answers is recorded as not answered, as before.

**L4-VER-050 The audit tells an inconclusive run from a rejection.** Step 4a SHALL judge the zero-value run of its audit
tests by L4-IMP-060 against the audit's head run: confirmed is accepted, not applicable (L4-IMP-062) is accepted with
the label `not applicable: no project code`, refuted is rejected (a minor finding), and inconclusive is recorded
`inconclusive` with its reason: no finding, not committed, listed in `verification.md`. The two runs for tests that
people or a test chore wrote (L4-VER-009) are judged the same way: at most two gate runs per round, plus at most two keep
reruns of the zero-value run (L4-IMP-061), none without such a test; a test whose runs were inconclusive is no proof,
and its minor finding says `inconclusive: <reason>`, not that it passes against the zero values and on the base. A test
chore whose added tests are all inconclusive SHALL be held with a harness question (L4-IMP-063, `check: tests`), not accepted.
Both runs vary Python files only. When neither can be made (the tests import no Python module of the project and the
unit changed no Python production file, as in a TypeScript project), every such test SHALL be inconclusive with that
reason and no gate run, not rejected as a test that passes both runs: a test chore of such tests is held, its
question's `Runs:` line saying `none`. Step 4 takes only a test whose file is a Python file (`file_of_test`): such a
Python test's minor finding says `inconclusive: neither run could be made: …`, and a test in a file of another language
is no candidate and keeps its `no proof (no red, audit or generated record)` finding.

Both runs vary Python files only, so a test in a file of another language does not load what they vary. A test that no
run accepted, whose file is found among the repository's files and has the extension of another language (`.ts`, `.js`,
`.go`, `.java`, `.swift` and the others in `OTHER_LANGUAGES`), SHALL be inconclusive with `the zero-value run and the
base run vary Python files only, and <file> is not a Python file`, and SHALL NOT be rejected, also when the unit changed
a Python production file and both runs were made. A run that makes such a test fail by assertion still accepts it. A test
that failed by an error on the base, or in the zero-value run, was reached by a run, so it stays rejected. A reason that a
run already gave is kept. A test file of another kind, such as a Markdown file with a pytest doctest, is decided by the
runs. When no run could be made because no file of the zero-value scope could be varied and the unit changed no Python
production file, every test not accepted SHALL be inconclusive with `no run could be made: no file of the zero-value scope
could be varied, and the unit changed no Python production file`. The check SHALL record the names of the runs it made
(`test-extra-zero`, `test-extra-base`), and the question's `Runs:` line SHALL name those runs only. When the added tests
of a chore are partly rejected and partly inconclusive, the attempt SHALL fail, and its reason names the runs made, lists
only the rejected tests as passing them, and lists each inconclusive test apart with its reason.

**L4-VER-051 The judge sees evidence the harness did not prove.** A tracing test whose red proof has `via:
not_applicable`, `via: human_override`, `via: agent_override` or `via: delegate_override` SHALL count as evidence and
SHALL be labelled in the judge's per-test list, in the satisfied block of L4-VER-018 and in `verification.md`: `not
applicable: no project code`, `accepted by Q-NNN: the check was inconclusive`, `accepted by an agent through Q-NNN: the
check was inconclusive`, or `accepted by the delegate (<model> via <cli>) through Q-NNN: the check was inconclusive`. A
verdict recorded `by: agent` or `by: delegate` SHALL be named so in `verification.md` and in the judge's view of the
round that follows. Such a criterion is pre-satisfied, so step 4a samples it before the others, but the audit takes at
most `MAX_AUDIT_PER_ROUND` criteria per round and is off without a verifier agent or with `audit_sample_ratio` 0: the
label for the judge is the guarantee, not the audit.

**L4-VER-052 The per-test cap is stated and checked when a test is written.** The implementer's harness contract SHALL
state the cap with its configured value next to the tagging rule, in every role's prompt: `A test that traces more than
<N> of this unit's criteria counts for none of them (verifier.max_criteria_per_test), and the harness rejects a red step
or test chore that writes one: give each test one behaviour and at most <N> ids, tag a test only with the criteria whose
outcome it asserts, put a criterion that many tests touch (a precondition, or a list of commands) only on the tests that
assert it directly, and write another test rather than add an id to a test that has <N>.`, where `<N>` is
`verifier.max_criteria_per_test`. The red phase SHALL say that a `_Requirements:_` line that names K criteria needs at
least ⌈K/<N>⌉ tests, and that a test may carry a zero-answer criterion as well only when it then carries at most `<N>`
ids. A red step SHALL fail its attempt, before the pre-satisfied, base and zero-value runs, when one of its new tests
traces more than `<N>` of the unit's criteria (the criteria the verifier traces for the unit; other ids do not count),
with this text: `too many criteria on one test: <test> traces <n> of this unit's criteria (<ids>), more than
verifier.max_criteria_per_test (<N>), so the verifier counts it for none of them: split it into tests that each assert
one behaviour and carry at most <N> ids, and tag a test only with the criteria whose outcome it asserts`, naming at most
three tests (then `(+k more)`). A test chore SHALL fail its attempt with the same text when one of its added tests does,
before its discrimination runs. Tests that existed before the step MUST NOT be checked. The contract's template version
SHALL be 13 and the red template's 12.

**L4-VER-053 The red remedies respect the cap.** The red phase's zero-answer remedy (a criterion whose tests pass or
error against the zero-value stubs, L4-IMP-002) SHALL propose tagging the criterion on a test of the attempt that
failed on the zero values only when that test traces fewer than `verifier.max_criteria_per_test` of the unit's criteria
and not the criterion itself. The example SHALL show that test's whole list of the unit's ids plus the criterion, in
the gate's own form (`@pytest.mark.l4("<id>", …)` for a pytest gate, `it("<id> <id>: …")` otherwise). When no such
test has room, the remedy SHALL say instead `, or write a new test that asserts a real answer and tag it with
<criterion> alone (every test that failed on the zero values already carries <N> ids)`. No retry text of the harness MAY
advise adding an id that puts a test over the cap.

**L4-VER-054 A proved test over the cap counts when the judge named it for the criterion.** Step 4 SHALL keep, for each
criterion, every test over the cap that has a proof for it under L4-VER-009 (the cap aside) and passed, as a candidate
with the number of the unit's criteria it traces; such a test SHALL stay ignored with its reason and its minor finding.
A test with no proof, or skipped, MUST NOT be a candidate. The judge's traceability lines SHALL list a criterion's
candidates as `over the per-test cap: <test> (traces <n> criteria)` (at most five, then `(+k more)`), and its system
text SHALL say that such a test counts for that criterion only when the judge passes the criterion and gives a
`test_adequacy` entry for that test and that criterion with `adequate: true`, and ask for one entry, true or false, per
candidate it read, and say that the evidence of its pass alone does not count; the judge prompt version SHALL be 12.
After the judge's reply, where its `test_adequacy` is applied, a candidate SHALL become a tracing test of the criterion,
keeping its proof, when all hold: the judge's verdict for the criterion is `pass`; the judge named the test for it, by a
`test_adequacy` entry with `adequate: true` for that test and that criterion, whose reason does not start with `not in
this part` (a part of a diff judged in parts that never saw the test cannot name it); a `test` evidence item of the
criterion's pass is not enough on its own; no `test_adequacy` entry with `adequate: false` names that test with that
criterion or with no criterion; and the test traces at most `min(M // 2, 3 × N)` of the unit's criteria (M the unit's
criteria, N the cap; the 3 is not configurable). An `uncovered` criterion is then `covered` (a `fail` stays `fail`), the
test leaves its ignored list, and `verification.md` labels it `over the per-test cap: traces <n> criteria, named by the
judge`. No other candidate SHALL count. `verdict.json` SHALL record the candidates and the label in the round's trace,
and a round resumed at aggregation SHALL read them back, with the labels of L4-VER-051; a record without them SHALL load
with no candidates. Why the cap still holds: one test that fails on the zero values proves every criterion it traces, so
the tag alone or the judge's pass alone is never enough; the judge must name this test for this criterion, its own doubt
wins, and a test that traces more than `min(M // 2, 3 × N)` of the unit (a catch-all) is never counted, so in a unit of
up to twice the cap nothing over the cap is. The rescue depends on the judge following its system text; when it does
not, the criterion stays a question for a person, which is the safe direction.

**L4-VER-055 A criterion that only the cap left uncovered says so.** When a criterion has no usable tracing test and no
passing test within the cap, the judge's verdict for it is `pass`, and it has a candidate of L4-VER-054 that was not counted, its outcome reason SHALL be
`uncovered: the judge passed it, and only the per-test cap left it uncovered: <test> traces <n> criteria, more than
verifier.max_criteria_per_test (<N>)<why>`, with `<why>` `; it traces more than <C> of the unit's <M> criteria, the most
the judge can make count` when it does (<C> is `min(M // 2, 3 × N)`), else `; the judge did not confirm it for this
criterion` (not named, or named inadequate), for the candidate with the fewest criteria (then by id), followed by `(+k
more)` when there are more. Its verdict question SHALL show that reason and, before the answer line, `Fix: answer accept
if <test> checks this criterion as its scenario says; or reject: give it its own test of at most <N> ids (a reject fails
the criterion and spends a fix round).` A criterion the judge did not pass, one with no candidate, or one that a passing test within the cap traces (the judge called that test inadequate, so the cap is not why it is uncovered) SHALL keep today's reason and question.

**L4-VER-018 The judge checks each task ticked as already satisfied.** A task the harness ticked `already satisfied`
(L4-IMP-003) has no change of its own, and its criteria passing does not show that its own text is done: a README line
that a task asks for is no criterion's. The judge prompt SHALL hold a satisfied block when the unit has such tasks: the
unit's own tasks (not a fix unit's) whose last `task.done` outside any fix-unit context has `tdd: already-satisfied`.
Per task it lists the key, the text from `tasks.md`, and the criteria of its last `task.red_ok` with their
`discriminating` tests. The system text asks for `satisfied: [{task, holds, evidence}]`, one entry per listed task.
`holds` is true only when the diff or the gate report shows that the code and documents at head do what the task's
text says. `evidence` is the file:line or test id that shows it, or what is still missing. A prompt with no such task
has no block, and the reply leaves `satisfied` out. Each answer is recorded as
`verify.satisfied_judged{task, round, holds, evidence, profile}`. `holds: false` adds the major judge finding `task
<key> is ticked as already satisfied, but its text is not done` with the evidence as its detail. It is judge-only, so it
goes to a person (L4-VER-013): only a person can tell a task whose work sits in base code the diff does not show. A
listed task the reply leaves out is asked for in L4-VER-017's second call (`satisfied <key>`). A task still not answered
adds the minor finding `the judge did not say whether task <key> is done` and is recorded with `holds: false` and
evidence `not answered`, so a missing answer never fails a round. The prompt template was `judge@9`; it is `judge@13` (`judge@10` since
L4-VER-041, `judge@11` since L4-KSP-014, `judge@12` since L4-VER-056, `judge@13` since L4-VER-065).

**L4-VER-040 The judge's diff leaves out the harness's bookkeeping, named once.** The diffs the judge and the S1 step read, and the length the judge step compares with the cap, SHALL leave out the
harness's bookkeeping, given by one list (`bookkeeping_pathspecs`): every path under a `.l4/` directory,
`.serena/memories/harness/**`, and `verification.md`, `questions.md` and `feedback.md` in each unit folder of the
family. The file names SHALL come from the unit folder's channel list in `l4.state.review`. A file of those names
outside the family's folders SHALL stay in the diff.

**L4-VER-041 A diff longer than one prompt is judged in parts.** A diff (L4-VER-040) over 120000 characters SHALL be judged in parts, not cut: whole files, a test next to the code it
is named after or imports, at most 8 parts of at most 120000 characters (a longer file alone, cut). Each part SHALL be
one judge call: the round's prompt with the part's diff, `part K of N`, a capped file list, and the rule that a
criterion whose code the part does not show is `insufficient_evidence`, not `fail`, and, since `judge@12`, that a part
showing only some of a criterion's code cites the files of the part that hold it when it answers `insufficient_evidence`
(L4-VER-056). A diff within the cap keeps one prompt.

**L4-VER-042 The parts' replies are merged into one verdict.** The replies of the parts SHALL be merged into one verdict before anything reads it: per criterion a `fail` of any
part, else a `pass`, else a `not_verifiable`, else `insufficient_evidence`; a test is inadequate when a part that sees
it says so; the findings of all parts without repeats; a feedback, accepted or satisfied item is true when a part says
true and no part says false with evidence other than `not in this part`. A part whose reply is discarded SHALL discard
the round's judge verdict. A criterion that the merge leaves `insufficient_evidence` and whose files lie in two or more
parts is then judged once more (L4-VER-056, L4-VER-057).

**L4-VER-043 What the judge could not see is a hold of the kind judge_view.** A file cut to one part SHALL raise the hold ``judge view: the diff of `<path>` is longer than one part (120000
characters): the judge saw only its start``, and files in no judged part a `judge view:` hold naming them. These and
the 0.4.14 hold `the diff is longer than 120000 characters: the judge saw only the start` and the holds about a spec
file the judge did not see or saw only in part (`the spec file <path> …: the judge saw only …` or `… did not see it`,
L4-KSP-014) SHALL be of the kind `judge_view`, whose question SHALL say that `accept` means a person checked those files and that no fix unit can
shrink the diff, and ask for no `WHEN … THEN …`.

**L4-VER-044 A rejected judge_view hold never becomes a fix unit.** A rejected `judge_view` hold SHALL be a human major finding (`Rejected hold: the judge could not see all of the diff`)
that no fix task is derived from, whatever its reason. A failed round with nothing else to fix SHALL escalate the unit
with `judge_view_rejected`; `l4 status --unit`, the refusal of `l4 run --unit` and the sticky note SHALL name its way
out (split the change, then `l4 restart`; or `accept` by `--replace`, then `l4 retry`), never `l4 feedback add`.

**L4-VER-045 A lock file is one line for the judge, never a diff.** A file whose old and new base names are both lock files (`uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`,
`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `go.sum`, `Cargo.lock`, `composer.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`) SHALL be
shown as one line, never diffed, and never cause a hold: path (and the old path of a rename), old and new size, lines
added and removed, how many changed lines touch a source, registry, remote, tarball, resolution or integrity field, and the hosts of every URL in the changed lines.

**L4-VER-046 An accept of a hold on the judge's view is bound to what the judge did not see.** The hash an accept of a `judge view:` hold is bound to SHALL cover the hold's text, the head blob id of every file the
hold covers and the full list of files the judge did not see; the hold's id stays the hash of its text. The accept is
void when that content changes, and the hold is asked again. The question SHALL list every unseen file (at most 100,
then a pointer to `verdict.json`, which lists them all); it covers the file mode too.

**L4-VER-047 The file list of a part prompt is bounded and the content is read once.** The file list of every part prompt SHALL hold at most 200 files and then `+K more files: see verification.md`, which
lists all of them; the room the list takes SHALL come out of the part's characters. The diff content of all files SHALL
come from one `git diff` split at its `diff --git` lines, and the text of files that land in no part SHALL not be kept.

**L4-VER-056 A criterion whose evidence the parts split is found from the harness's records.** After the replies of a
diff judged in parts are merged (L4-VER-042), a criterion SHALL be *split* when the round judged two or more parts, its
merged verdict is `insufficient_evidence` (no part answered `fail`, `pass` or `not_verifiable`), no person has given a
verdict for it, its trace is `covered` and not held once the parts' test adequacy is applied to it (a criterion whose only passing
tracing tests the parts called inadequate is not covered; a criterion whose only passing tests are over the per-test
cap, the candidates of L4-VER-054 that the judge may still name and have counted, has a passing tracing test for this
decision, so the cap rescue can happen for it), and its files lie in two or more judged parts (a
part cut to the cap counts as the part it is). Its files SHALL be the paths of the diff named, in this order and without
repeats, by: the evidence references (`file` or `test`) of each part's verdict for it, in part order (a reference names
the longest diff path it equals or that it starts with followed by `:`); the file of each of its tracing test ids, and of each such candidate, as `file_of_test` resolves it, when it is a path
of the diff (a pytest id is `classname::name` with a dotted classname, as
`packages.api.tests.test_x::test_y`, never a path); the non-test entries whose name key is a module those test files'
added lines import (the packing rule of L4-VER-041); and the files that the harness commits `base..head` changed of the
tasks whose `task.red_ok` proof for the criterion lists tests (`task.red_ok.criteria`; `L4-Task` one of those tasks,
`L4-Unit` a unit of the family). A path outside the diff, and a path that `file_kind` classifies as exempt (a harness,
spec or unit-folder path, the rule by which `_changed_code` leaves such files out), MUST NOT be a file of a criterion, so a task's tick of `tasks.md` never makes a criterion split. A file of the tasks'
commits counts toward "two or more judged parts" only when `file_kind` classifies it as code or a test: any other (a
lock file or a README at the root of the repository) is a file of the criterion that a follow-up may show as context
when room remains, but it never makes a criterion split. The files SHALL be computed only when a criterion meets
the first four conditions, so a round without one runs no extra git command. A criterion whose files lie in one part, or
in no judged part, MUST NOT be split: its `insufficient_evidence` stands and its reason is unchanged. Each part prompt
SHALL hold the rule `A criterion whose code this part shows only in part: judge it when what is shown is enough;
otherwise answer insufficient_evidence and cite in its evidence each file of this part that holds some of its code.`,
and the judge template SHALL be `judge@12`, the number that the change `verifier-cap` also gives the template in the
same release (0.4.21); the template lock is regenerated after each of the two changes. The user text of a diff that fits
in one prompt is unchanged by this change.

**L4-VER-057 A split criterion is judged once more on all of its files, never making a round worse.** The judge step
SHALL make follow-up calls for the split criteria (L4-VER-056) after the merge and before anything reads the verdict. A follow-up SHALL hold whole entries in at most the characters of a part (120000 less the room of the file list), and
the diff it shows and the `shown:` lines of its file list SHALL together stay within the characters of a part less the
line that counts the files the list leaves out: each file taken is charged its characters and its `shown:` line, at most
200 files are shown (the cap of L4-VER-047 applies to the whole list, the shown files first), and the other lines of the
list take only the room that remains, so the diff and the file list never exceed 120000 characters together. For each
split criterion, its files SHALL be taken in their order while they fit, a file that does not fit skipped; a file of a
part cut to the cap and a file in no judged part MUST NOT be shown. A criterion whose taken files lie in one part SHALL get no follow-up, and neither SHALL a group whose files shown for
its criteria (those that count for the split) all lie in one part once the room is filled: its criteria are recorded
`no_fit`, and the calls that are made are numbered without a gap. The split criteria SHALL be grouped in the unit's criteria order on the files of the first three
sources of L4-VER-056 (cited, tracing tests, imported code), each joining the first group whose files together with its
own still fit, else starting a new one; the room that remains in each group SHALL then be filled with the files of the
tasks' commits, in the same order, each while it fits; a group's files SHALL be shown in the order the parts hold them;
a round SHALL make at most as many follow-up calls as it judged parts. A follow-up prompt SHALL be the round's prompt
with only the group's criteria, no feedback, accepted, satisfied or done-tasks block, and a diff section headed `## Diff
(base...head), follow-up K of M` with the rules of a follow-up (judge each listed criterion on what is shown; a file
marked not shown never makes a `fail`, and is a reason for `insufficient_evidence` when what is shown is not enough; a
`fail` cites code shown; a test not shown is left out of `test_adequacy`) and a file list of every file of the diff,
each marked `shown: <path> (part K, <chars> characters)` or `not shown: <path> (part K, <chars> characters)` (`(no part,
…)` for a file in no judged part). The wording of the follow-up prompt MUST NOT say or suggest that it shows the whole
change. A follow-up SHALL be asked through the same judge chain as a part. Its verdict for a criterion of its group
SHALL replace the merged verdict; a verdict for another id MUST be ignored; a group criterion it leaves out keeps the
merged verdict. A follow-up changes only its own group: of its `test_adequacy` entries and findings only those whose `criterion` is in the group count (an entry with an empty
criterion is dropped), and an entry counts only for a test whose file the follow-up was shown (an entry for a test it
was not shown, or whose file the diff does not resolve, is dropped), and they are merged as a part's (L4-VER-042). A criterion that any part answered `fail`, `pass` or `not_verifiable`, or that has a person's verdict,
MUST NOT be re-judged. A follow-up `fail` SHALL go through the counterexample rule like any judge `fail`, so it never
fails the unit alone. A follow-up that gives no valid verdict (schema break after the repair or retry, timeout, model
mismatch, error, usage limit with no next judge, or no judge available) SHALL keep the merged verdict of its criteria
and MUST NOT discard the round's judge verdict, raise a hold or stop the round. A usage limit SHALL be recorded with
status `limit` and the groups after it SHALL NOT be asked (each is recorded `no_answer` with status `limit`, no call
