made); a judge that is not available for any other reason SHALL be recorded with status `unavailable` and does not stop
the later groups.

**L4-VER-058 The verdict and the question say that the evidence was split and what was done.** For each split criterion,
the round SHALL record in `verdict.json` `judge_split` its parts, its outcome (`answered`, `not_answered`, `no_answer`,
`no_fit` or `no_call_left`), its follow-up, the number of files shown, the files not shown (as `[path, part, characters]`, part 0 for a file in no judged part), the follow-up's answer and the status of a follow-up with no answer (a schema or timeout status, `model_mismatch`,
`error`, `limit` or `unavailable`). The reason of its outcome, when the outcome rests on the judge's verdict or is the cap-only reason (L4-VER-055),
SHALL end with `; ` and a note that starts `its evidence was split over parts <parts> of the diff: ` (`<parts>` as `1
and 2` or `1, 2 and 4`) and then says what was done: `follow-up call <K> judged its <n> files of those parts together
and answered <verdict>` (with ` (<m> not shown: …)` naming at most three paths when files were not shown), `follow-up
call <K> judged its files of those parts together but gave no verdict for it, so the parts' verdict stands`, `follow-up
call <K> gave no usable answer (<status>), so the parts' verdict stands`, `no follow-up call was made, because its files
of those parts do not fit in one part together`, or `no follow-up call was made, because the round's <N> follow-up calls
were used`. That reason SHALL be the verdict question's `Why:` line and the reason in the criteria table of
`verification.md`. `verification.md` SHALL say `judged in <N> parts and <M> follow-up` (`follow-ups` for more than one)
and list each follow-up call (`follow-up K: <ids>; files of parts <parts>: <n> file(s), <c> characters, profile <p>,
reply <reply>`). `verdict.json` SHALL list `judge_followups`, one row per call. A follow-up's `verify.judge` SHALL carry
`followup`, `followups` and `criteria`. The round's `prompt_sha256` SHALL hash the part prompts' hashes and then the hashes of the follow-up prompts that were
sent; `judge_calls` and the cost SHALL count the follow-up calls; `judge_reply` SHALL stay the
worst reply of the parts, and `judge_replies` SHALL count the replies of the round's judge profile, that of the parts, follow-ups of that judge included. `verdict.json`
`judge_verdict` SHALL be the verdict after the follow-ups. The round's `judge_profile`, `judge_model` and `independence`
SHALL stay those of the judge of the parts; the profile of a follow-up is in its `judge_followups` row and its
`verify.judge` event. A resumed round MUST make no follow-up call and SHALL keep the records, the notes and the
follow-ups' verdicts of the round it reuses.

**L4-VER-071 A judge whose reply does not fit its output limit or its time is asked again with fewer criteria.** When a
step-9 judge's reply to a prompt of two or more criteria stops at the model's output limit, or its call ends `timeout`
(from 0.4.49), the harness SHALL ask the same judge again with the prompt's criteria split in two halves (the first has `ceil(n/2)`, in the criteria's order), and SHALL split
a half whose reply stops at the limit or times out again while its depth is below `verifier.judge_length_splits` (default 2, 0 to 4;
0 turns the split off), so a part has at most 4 batches and 7 calls of one judge with the default. An agent run marks such
a stop with `length_stop` (its status stays `error`): the opencode adapters (v1 and v2) set it when the stream's last
reason is `length` and the run gave no result; Claude Code, Codex, Kiro and Copilot report no such stop that the harness
reads. Each batch call SHALL get the bookkeeping of a whole prompt's call (the served-model independence check of
L4-VER-001, the calls, the cost, `verify.judge`). The batch prompt SHALL begin its criteria section with `This call judges
<k> of the unit's <n> criteria, listed below; the unit's other criteria are judged in other calls with the same diff.
Answer only these criteria, and give test adequacy only for them.`; only the first batch SHALL carry the feedback,
accepted, satisfied and done-task blocks, and every batch the answers block. When every batch has a verdict, the batch
verdicts SHALL be merged (as parts are, L4-VER-041) into one reply for the prompt, whose outcome is the worst of the
batches, so a diff in parts keeps one reply per part for the follow-ups (L4-VER-056, L4-VER-057). A batch that ends
`error` or `model_mismatch` (a length stop that cannot be split again too) SHALL discard the judge for the round, with
`availability.judge_error` naming the batch's size and depth, and the next judge SHALL be given the whole prompt; a batch
that ends `schema_invalid` SHALL be handled as a whole prompt's schema break is (from 0.4.51 the next judge is given the
whole prompt, L4-VER-075), and one that ends `timeout` SHALL hold the round as a whole prompt that times out does; a usage limit in a
batch SHALL move to the next judge with the whole prompt. While a prompt can still be split, its timeout SHALL NOT be retried with the same prompt (`run_judge(retry_timeout=False)`:
the split is the retry); a batch that cannot be split again SHALL keep the one retry of a timeout, and its timeout SHALL
hold the round as before, so a part whose every call times out costs at most 4 timeouts with the default (2 before).
Follow-up calls SHALL NOT be split. The round SHALL record
`judge.length_split{round, profile, criteria, into, depth, cause, part, parts}` (`cause`: `length` or `timeout`), `verify.judge.batch_criteria` and `batch_depth`
for a batch call, `judge_batches` in `verdict.json` (`{part, depth, criteria, profile, calls, reply, prompt_sha256}`, part
0 for a diff in one prompt, one row per batch call, a batch that stopped again included with an empty `reply`; restored
with the round) and `batches` in each `judge_parts` row; the round's
`prompt_sha256` covers the batch prompts. A reasoning model whose thinking alone fills its limit is not helped by fewer
criteria: it is discarded after its batches, and the remedy is a reasoning cap (`options.provider`) or a judge with a
larger output limit. [V, 0.4.47: a consumer's unit of 29 criteria lost both working judges on part 1 of 4 (32,000 output
tokens each, last reason `length`), each part asking for every criterion, and waited for capacity.]

**L4-VER-072 A round whose judge gave no verdict keeps the earlier judge's pass of an unchanged criterion.** At step 10 of
a fresh round whose step 9 ran and failed (a part's reply was discarded, so the round has no judge verdict), the harness
SHALL give a criterion C the `pass` of the newest earlier stored round R whose `judge_verdict` has criteria, only when
all of these hold: (1) R's judge verdict for C is `pass`; (2) C's source file has the same blob at R's head and at this
head; (3) every path of `git diff --name-only <R head> <head>` is in a directory of the unit family (the spec,
`questions.md`, the evidence, fix-unit directories) or the harness's own memory (`.serena/memories/harness/`), or matches `tdd.test_globs` and no `tdd.test_support_globs`, or
else no criterion is carried; (4) no changed path is the file of a test that traces C, or of a candidate over the cap,
in R's trace or in this round's (a test whose file is not found keeps C from being carried); (5) the tests that trace C
now are among those of R's trace, and each passes now. R's test-adequacy rows for C SHALL be applied to the trace as the
judge's own are (`apply_adequacy`, then `count_named`), and C's reason SHALL read `the judge of round <R> passed it at
<head10>, and only tests that do not trace it changed since (carried)`. A human verdict in force and a failing tracing
test SHALL still come first. The round SHALL record `verify.carried{round, criterion, from_round, from_head}` for each
carried criterion, or once `verify.not_carried{round, from_round, reason, paths}` when none is, and SHALL store
`judge_carried` (`{criterion: {round, head, verdict, adequacy}}`) in `verdict.json`, so that a resumed round keeps the
carried passes with no git call and no read of R. The round SHALL keep the hold of the discarded reply (it cannot PASS
until that hold is answered), SHALL NOT carry findings or any verdict but `pass`, and SHALL NOT carry anything when its
judge answered or its step 9 did not run; `run.judged` and the stored `judge_verdict` stay the round's own, so S1
calibration never reads a carried verdict. A failure to read R or the diff SHALL carry nothing. Limit: any edit to a
criterion's source file stops carrying every criterion in it (a Kiro unit has one `requirements.md`). [V, 0.4.48: a
consumer's round 3 whose judge timed out on part 3 of 4 asked all 29 criteria, which round 1 had passed on the same
production code; only one test file changed between the two heads.]

**L4-VER-073 The verifier accepts only the edit a person accepted, re-checks it, and the judge sees it.** `check_test_paths` and the check that red's tests are unchanged after red SHALL accept, for an `L4-TDD: exempt` commit,
the files a `task.repaired` of the same unit and task names, and nothing else, and only when, per file: the event names
a `question` and a `patch_sha256`; the unit's ledger has a `question.raised{kind: harness, check: repair}` of that
question and task with the same `patch_sha256` and `repair_blobs` naming the file; a `question.answered` of it with
`by: human` follows the raise; a `held.replayed` of it with the same `patch_sha256` follows that answer; and the
commit's parent blob and
blob of the file are the `repair_blobs` pair. A file that fails any of these SHALL be a blocker "a repaired test differs
from the edit a person accepted" that names the file, the task, the commit and the first condition that failed. For each
accepted file the structural rules of a repair (the encoding rule included) SHALL run again on the file before and after
the commit, with the tests the event names; a file that breaks them, was added or deleted by the commit, or is named
with no test, is a blocker. A test a `task.repaired` lists SHALL keep no red proof by its id: its proof is the one the
event records (`proved`), valid only while the file still has the content `sha10` names. The judge's material for the
next round SHALL show each repaired test's lines before and after the repair (as for a named test that red changed,
L4-VER-068).

**L4-VER-074 An over-long list of free text in a judge's reply is folded, not discarded.** The deterministic repair of a
judge's reply (W-D1, 10.3) SHALL fold a list in a field of `judge_repair.FOLDED_LISTS` (`riskiest_assumptions`) that has
more items than its `maxItems` N and only string items: the first N − 1 items SHALL stay as they are, the remaining items
SHALL be joined by newlines into the N-th, and the field's path SHALL be recorded in `judge.reply_repaired`. A list in
another field, a list with an item that is not a string and a list with fewer items than its `minItems` SHALL NOT be
changed. The other rules of the repair hold: a reply that is still invalid, or whose criteria's ids or verdicts would
change, is not repaired. The field cannot change a verdict, so its length never costs the round its judge. [V, 0.4.49: a
consumer's judge listed more than three riskiest assumptions in both calls on part 1 of 2; the reply was discarded and
the round's 25 criteria became verdict questions.]

**L4-VER-075 A judge whose reply still breaks the schema gives way to the next independent judge.** When the reply to a
step-9 prompt or part is `schema_invalid` after the repair and the retry, `ladder._ask_judges` SHALL discard it and ask
the next independent judge the same prompt (`next_judge("schema_invalid")`), as after a `model_mismatch` or an `error`
(L4-VER-015); the discarded judge SHALL be skipped for the rest of the round and SHALL NOT be cooled down, and its
`verify.judge` row (`status: schema_invalid`, `reply: discarded`) stays in the ledger before the next judge's.
When no independent judge remains, the round SHALL hold the discarded reply (`the judge's reply was discarded
(…schema_invalid: …)`), its criteria SHALL be `needs_human`, and the unit SHALL NOT wait for capacity: every judge asked
answered. A batch of L4-VER-071 that ends `schema_invalid` SHALL give the next judge the whole prompt. A follow-up
(L4-VER-057) SHALL NOT be moved to another judge. A timeout left after the splits of L4-VER-071 SHALL still hold the
round without asking the next judge, which would spend its own timeouts on the same prompt within the same job. [V, the
same round as L4-VER-074: part 2 was never asked and no other judge of the chain was, while the precedence table of
L4-VER-015 said the next independent judge is tried.]

**L4-VER-030** Step 1 SHALL compare every test that exists at the base in each changed test file with head (L4-IMP-045..047). A test
changed, rebound or unparsable SHALL be the blocker `a pre-existing test was changed` and a deleted test that did not
move the blocker `a pre-existing test was deleted`, each naming `<path>::<name>` and why, when a harness commit
introduced it and no allowance of L4-VER-031 holds. A test that the skip check blocks SHALL not be reported again.

**L4-VER-031** Step 1 SHALL list, never block, a change of L4-VER-030 that only people's commits introduced (`Test changes made by
humans`), that a `tests.superseded` event records, or whose every harness commit belongs to a `[test-infra]` task or
changes a path that a `task.unfrozen` of the same unit and task names (`Pre-existing tests changed with an allowance`).
A harness commit without an `L4-Task`, or one no allowance covers, SHALL keep the blocker.

**L4-VER-032** For each harness commit with `L4-TDD: red` or `already-satisfied` of a task without `[test-infra]`, step 1 SHALL compare
the test files it changed with its first parent (L4-IMP-045..047). A test that existed at the parent, not at the base,
that the commit changed, rebound or deleted, and that no `tests.superseded` event names, SHALL be the blocker `a red step
changed a test that an earlier step wrote`, naming the test, the task and the commit.

**L4-VER-033** Step 4a SHALL run each audit test and its zero-value run with every test and support file the unit added, changed or
deleted at its base version (an added one set aside; added data under `fixtures/`, `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `testdata/`
kept), collecting only the audit file, written next to the unit's own test files (else where a `--collect-only` run
shows the test command collects it, else `tests`). Each file SHALL be restored byte for byte after.

**L4-VER-034** An audit test SHALL never run with the unit's test or support files in place. One whose collection fails in a
production module, whose cause the log does not show, or that leaves no report SHALL hold its criterion (L4-VER-012). One
whose own import fails SHALL get the writer's one retry and be a minor rejection when it fails again; so SHALL one the
test command never collects (the reason names the command). Every record SHALL carry `support` `base` or `unchanged`.

**L4-VER-035** Step 5 SHALL run a generated UI test at head with the e2e runner's own support files the unit changed at their base
versions (a test-glob file with no test included), never added app data, collecting only the generated file. One that
does not run so, or whose server does not start, SHALL be `uncollectable` and held, naming the files; no run SHALL
have the unit's files in place. `verify.generated` SHALL carry `support`; for a waived criterion it carries `status: waived` and `by`
(L4-VER-067).

**L4-VER-036** `verify.audit` SHALL carry `support` and `support_files`, and verification.md's Audit table a `Support` column.
`verify.base_tests` SHALL carry the counts, the base source and the reverted files of L4-VER-038, shown in the row
`pre-existing tests still pass`. verification.md SHALL list the changes L4-VER-031 allowed and the fixtures of
L4-VER-037 that patch the unit's code on request.

**L4-VER-037** Step 1 SHALL check every changed Python test-support file, not only an opened one, for a new patch or assignment of a
symbol of a production module the unit changed (L4-IMP-016 rule 3). One that runs for every test, or whose use is
unknown, SHALL be a content-scan blocker; one inside a fixture that a test requests by name SHALL be listed. A person's
commit and a `[test-infra]` task SHALL be handled as for every other content-scan hit.

**L4-VER-038** Step 1 SHALL run the test gate at head with every test and support file the unit added or changed at its base version
and SHALL require each test that passed at the base to pass. One that fails twice, does not run or no longer collects
SHALL be a blocker, unless `tests.superseded` names it, a `task.unfrozen` of the unit frees its file, a `[test-infra]`
task's commit changed its file, or the last commit of `base..head` that changed its file is a person's (not the
harness's under the author rule). The first three are listed as allowed; the fourth is a person's line that names every
commit that changed the file, the harness's included, and a harness commit after the person's keeps the blocker. A
test's file SHALL be found from its id: a pytest id from its dotted module (`tests.test_x.TestY::test_z` is
`tests/test_x.py`), a Go id (`<import path>::<name>`) as the one `*_test.go` file directly in the package's directory
that declares `func <name up to the first />(`, the directory found from the `module` line of the `go.mod` whose module
path is the longest prefix of the import path, at head and then at the base; a test with no file, or with more than
one, has none of the three allowances that read a file. A test or support file that only people changed, that a
`[test-infra]` task changed or that a `task.unfrozen` frees, and a test module whose last change in `base..head` is a
person's commit, SHALL stay at head for the run, listed; the last kind as a person's line that names every commit that
changed it, the harness's included. A harness commit after the person's puts the file back, and so does being support
(step 5's rule: one of `tdd.test_support_globs`, a `.py` file that defines no test, another language's file whose name
does not look like a test module).

**L4-VER-039** Step 1's content scan SHALL flag in support files call/setup hooks that replace tests, `atexit.register`, `os._exit` and
session-end file writers. In test, support and production files it SHALL flag the names `l4_trace`, `_OUTCOME_FD`,
`L4_OUTCOME_FILE`, `config.option.xmlpath`, `sys.modules` lookups of `l4` and assignments to `.exitstatus`/`.xmlpath`,
and a production read of `L4_*`/`PYTEST_*`; `verifier.test_awareness_allow` lists instead of blocking.

**L4-VER-011 Resumable ladder.** Each completed step is recorded (`verify.step{round, step, subject_sha, evidence_hash,
status}`), where `subject_sha` is the **last commit not authored by the verifier**. Verifier-generated tests live in the
round's evidence directory and in the verifier worktree until the round ends, then are committed in one commit
`test(<unit>): verifier round <n>` (`L4-Phase: verifying`). A continuation resumes at the first incomplete step when
`subject_sha` is unchanged; if a non-verifier commit arrived (human push, base merge in step 0), the round restarts at
step 0. A merge commit (two or more parents) is never skipped for its `L4-Phase`; the base merge of step 0 is
`chore(<unit>): merge <base>@<sha> into the unit branch [skip ci]` with `L4-Phase: verifying`. Its first-parent diff
(what the merge brought into the unit branch) decides: a merge that brings a path other than the unit's harness-owned
files (`questions.md`, `verification.md`, `.l4/**`) and `.serena/memories/harness/**` is a new subject; one that brings
nothing else is not. Long steps honour the soft deadline like agent phases (L4-IMP-012).

**L4-VER-012 Failing generated or audit tests are reviewed before they fail the unit.** When a verifier-written test
fails on head, the panel reviews the test against the criterion text (`generated_test_misreads_criterion`). If any
available independent judge says it misreads the criterion, the test is discarded and the criterion is
`needs_human`; otherwise it is a `fail` and the test becomes the fix unit's red test. Order: the spec writer creates
the fix unit **first** (L4-VER-006), then the round's verifier commit is made carrying `L4-TDD: red` and
`L4-Task: <fix-unit task id>`; that fix task starts directly at **green**, and the TDD-history check for it considers
only the tests tagged to that task (other tests in the same verifier commit pass and are not part of its red). An implementer working on that fix unit that believes the test is wrong reports `blocked` with a
`technical` question instead of editing it.

**L4-VER-013 Human verdicts.** On NEEDS_HUMAN the verifier writes one question per affected criterion into
`questions.md` with `Kind: verdict` ("Criterion C-… (alias) is disputed: accept as satisfied?"), plus the evidence
summary. The human answers with a first word `accept` or `reject` and a reason, and sets Status `answered`. The
harness records `human.verdict{criterion, decision, by, reason}`; aggregation then uses the human verdict for that
criterion in this and later rounds, so a dispute cannot loop. A human `accept` is void as soon as the criterion text
changes **or** any deterministic check tracing the criterion fails later (a regression always wins). `reject` turns
the criterion into a `fail` finding (→ fix unit). Judge-only findings (unit verdict rule above) are asked the same way.
A `reject` of a finding stands until a fix unit consumes it, also in a round judged afresh (a round that cannot reuse
the last one, such as a record from an older harness or a subject the human moved by merging the base): a finding's id
hashes its title and criterion, so the fresh judge can raise the same finding under another id (tied to a criterion),
rename it or not raise it. The reject then applies to that round's judge finding of the same title that has no verdict
of its own, else the finding the question asked about comes back from its round's `verdict.json` as the human's; either
way the round fails into a fix unit (L4-VER-006) and the question is not asked again.

**Holds are decisions too (M1.6 holds: scope under `sdd.scope_check: warn`, diff coverage under `warn`).** A hold is
asked like a finding (`Kind: verdict`, target `H-` and eight hex digits of its text), and its answer is a human
decision that is never asked again, whichever way it went. `accept` waives the hold. The text of a UI hold names no status, so a
new status is not a new hold; its accept is bound to the hold, the criterion's text and the head blobs of the criterion's tracing-test
files, and an accept of the criterion itself stays bound to its text only (L4-VER-067). `reject` turns it into a finding
that carries the human's text: the round is a **FAIL** and the M1.3 fix-unit path runs, with the human's decision first
in the fix proposal (as for a rejected finding). A hold of the two kinds a task can be derived from, rejected with a
reason, becomes a **deterministic** major finding with the hold's id (the reject applies by hand the `fail` policy of the
check that raised it, whose finding it equals in kind): a rejected **scope** hold ("scope: `path` changes module …")
gives a chore task to remove the change from this unit or relocate it to its own change; a rejected **coverage** hold
(`diff coverage: changed code not run by any test: …`) gives a chore task to add tests that run the functions it names.
(A chore runs without a red step, D8: a test of code that already exists cannot be red.) A reject with no text, or of any
other hold (not measured, unsafe path name, no scope declared, a UI criterion without an e2e test, a discarded judge
reply, a diff over the judge's limit), has nothing to act on unless its reason ends with a `WHEN … THEN …` sentence:
then the hold becomes a **deterministic** major behaviour finding, and its fix task carries the reason and the scenario
exactly as a rejected judge finding with no criterion does (the question of such a hold says "end the reason with a
sentence WHEN … THEN … so that a fix unit can be made", and promises a fix unit only for scope and coverage holds).
Without the scenario this is the unusable-answer path of a rejected finding with no criterion and no
`WHEN … THEN …`. The finding is the human's, the fix planner lists it as not converted, no fix unit is written and the
round ends in `verify_fail_exhausted` (exit 13); nothing is asked or spawned on a later run. The question of the hold is
consumed by the fix unit (`fix.spawned{consumed}`); a hold that is still true in a later round after its fix unit is
judged afresh and asked again, as a rejected finding is. A reject that no task could be derived from is consumed by a feedback-only fix unit that comes after it (L4-VER-016).

**One question per subject.** A blocking judge-only finding whose title, detail or suggested fix names a subject of a
hold is *about the hold*: it is not asked on its own. A scope hold's subject is its file; a coverage hold's subjects are
its functions, each named by its name (a whole word of at least four characters), and the file of its module-level code
(`path::<module>`, which has no name). A file is named as a whole path (`app.py` is not named by `webapp.py`; a
leading `./` is allowed). Another function of a file whose function a coverage hold names is another subject. The hold's
question quotes the finding (title, detail, suggested fix), says that one answer settles both, and records the quoted
finding ids on its `question.raised{kind: verdict, covers}`. The match is textual and deterministic; no model decides
it. When the hold is answered, a finding its question quoted is settled with it (minor, noted with the hold id and the
human's reason, never a blocker), unless it has an answer of its own, which wins. **An answer settles only what its
question showed:** a finding that names the hold's subject but that the answered question did not quote (a later round,
judged afresh after a new commit, raised it, while the `accept` of a hold with the same text stays in force) is not
settled and is asked on its own, as is a finding that a hold's still-waiting question did not quote. A rejected hold's
finding quotes the judge findings its question quoted, so the fix unit has one task for the subject, not two. [V, live
M1.6: jobs 5541 and 5543 asked four questions where two held, and asked a rejected hold again as Q-006.]

A unit that an older harness version left `awaiting_human` on a NEEDS_HUMAN round that has no verdict question (the
ledger holds no `question.raised{kind: verdict}` for that round's number and `questions.md` has no waiting verdict
question) MUST NOT stay stuck, since nobody can answer a question that was never asked. `l4 plan` offers such a unit as
`verify` ("legacy round N"), and the next run, `l4 run` with or without `--unit` or `l4 verify`, raises the verdict
questions from the round's stored record (`.l4/evidence/round-<n>/verdict.json`) by the rules above, with the same
format, the next free `Q-NNN` ids and the same `question.raised{kind: verdict, round}` events. It commits them as a
normal question commit (`docs(<unit>): verdict questions [skip ci]`), sets the merge request labels as a fresh
NEEDS_HUMAN does (`l4:awaiting_human`, `l4:needs-answers`) and exits 11, with no implementer step and no judge call. A
second run raises nothing. The legacy path also applies when the round's verdict questions are **stale** (L4-VER-070): no `question.raised{kind: verdict}` of the unit's current ledgers names them, because `l4 restart` carried them over or a person wrote them. A stale question is not waiting, so the unit is not stuck on it; the next run raises the round's questions from its stored record, with no judge call, and `l4 plan` says `legacy round N: NEEDS_HUMAN, and its verdict questions were raised by an earlier attempt (Q-001, ...), the run raises them again`. The legacy check is that no verdict question of the unit is open, ready or invalid, which is stricter than "every question that names the round's targets is stale" in one case: a live question for target A with stale ones for B and C (rounds run on 0.4.45 left them) keeps the unit waiting for A, and B and C are asked one round later, once A is answered and consumed. The unit is never stuck. When the stored round holds nothing to ask about (a judge that failed without findings, no
`verdict.json`, or one that is a symlink or that the current harness cannot read, such as a finding without a known
severity), it raises one hold question, "re-verify the unit?", and never fails the run: its answer, `accept` or
`reject`, is consumed like any verdict and returns the unit to `verifying` for a fresh round.

**L4-VER-070 A verdict question counts only in the attempt that raised it.** A verdict question in `questions.md` SHALL count as open, ready, invalid or dismissed, and as waiting for its target, only when a `question.raised{kind: verdict}` event of the unit's current ledgers (the branch's and the lock ref's pending files) names its id. A verdict question that no such event names SHALL be `stale`: it SHALL NOT make a run take `VERDICTS_ANSWERED`, SHALL NOT be consumed, SHALL NOT keep `raise_verdict_questions` or the legacy path of L4-VER-013 from asking its target, SHALL NOT be offered to the delegate and SHALL NOT appear in the sticky note as waiting. Every reader of verdict questions SHALL apply this rule, the one `consume_verdicts` applies: `verdict_status` takes the raised ids (`UnitState.verdicts_raised`, from the fold) as a required argument, and its callers in the orchestrator, the planner, the delegate, the sticky note and the legacy check pass them. A superseded question is history, not stale. `l4 questions list` SHALL list a stale verdict question, whatever its Status (an answered one too), as `<unit> Q-NNN stale <blocking> <title>` with the line `stale: raised by an earlier attempt; the next round asks again` under it, `l4 questions show` SHALL say `Q-NNN is stale: raised by an earlier attempt; the next round asks again`, `--json` SHALL carry `status`, `stale` and, for a stale question, `note`, and `l4 questions answer` on a stale question SHALL print one info line, `Q-NNN is stale: raised by an earlier attempt; the next round asks its criterion again`. A ledger that cannot be read marks no question stale (its warning is shown instead), and a fix unit's folder is never marked. When a round asks a target that a stale question names, the harness SHALL set that stale question to `superseded by Q-NNN` (the new question; its answer stays as history, and no `question.superseded` event is written), so that it is not listed as asked again once it was; a stale question of another target stays stale, and a waiting live question changes nothing. The `question.raised` of a round's questions SHALL reach origin with the round's `questions.md`: the evidence commit of the round holds the run's ledger, or the question would read as stale on another machine. A unit whose runs already loop on a carried-over answer stops at its next run on a harness with this rule, with no edit by a person. [V, a consumer unit after `l4 restart` verified again on every run, at about $0.72 of judge per round, on three carried-over answered verdict questions that it never consumed; three rounds ran before a person noticed]

**L4-VER-060 A verdict question says how a person sets the fix's check.** The verdict question of a judge-only finding
SHALL say that a rejected finding is fixed by a fix unit and that the reason comes first in it; when the finding cites a
criterion, that ending the reason with one sentence `WHEN <the situation> THEN <the behaviour you expect>` (WHEN and
THEN in capitals) makes it a scenario of the fix unit, and that without one the fix is checked against that criterion
as it is written (L4-VER-059); when it cites none, that the sentence is needed or no fix can be made from the reject.
For a spec gap whose suggested fix ends with a `WHEN … THEN …` sentence it SHALL also say that the suggested fix
describes what the code does now, that a reject does not use it, and that ending the reason with it pins that
behaviour; a suggested fix of another kind (such as advice to clarify the spec) gets no such sentence. The verdict
question of a criterion SHALL say the same of `the scenario above`, in place of the advice to answer with a scenario
only when the code is right. Both SHALL offer the options `accept` and `reject: <reason>, then WHEN ... THEN ... to set
the check`. Hold questions are unchanged. `l4 questions answer` SHALL refuse (exit 2) a `reject` with no reason on the
verdict question of a spec-gap finding, naming what to add (`a spec gap's reject needs a reason or a WHEN ... THEN ...`,
with the command that adds it); it knows the question is a spec gap's from the sentence the question writer puts in the first paragraph of its context (a sentence in the judge's own text further down does not count). When that paragraph names no criterion the refusal says `a spec gap that cites no criterion needs a WHEN ... THEN ...`, since a reason alone would be refused again at conversion. A bare `reject` of any other verdict question is unchanged.

**L4-VER-014 UI-facing criteria.** A criterion is UI-facing when the unit's changed or declared paths match
`verifier.playwright.ui_paths`, or the S1 choice question "Is this criterion about user-visible UI behaviour?" gives
p ≥ `accept_threshold`. UI-facing criteria get Playwright tests when Playwright is enabled; the app is started with
`gates.e2e.serve` separately for the merge-base and the head worktree, and stopped afterwards. A UI criterion is
*covered* for step 5 only by a **proved** end-to-end test: one that traces it by id in the e2e report **and** is among the
tests step 4 accepted as evidence for it (a red proof, an audit or generated record of an earlier round, or the
criterion's text being unchanged from the base specs). An e2e test the implementer wrote is not proved, since the red
gate runs `gates.test` only and nothing showed that it fails without the change; it stays in the report as "not
evidence" and does **not** suppress generation: the criterion is a gap, its deterministic minor finding says that the
named test was never proved, and step 5 generates one that fails at the merge base and passes at head. The generator
never overwrites a file it did not write (L4-VER-002a): when the implementer's test sits at the harness's own path
`e2e/test_l4_c_<hex>.py`, generation ends `writer_failed` with that reason, the criterion becomes a hold, and a human
decides (`accept` when the unit test is enough). A UI criterion, or a UI hold of it, that a person accepted is not generated for
or held again while the accept is in force (L4-VER-067). [V, live M1.5 P3, job 5528: step 5 generated nothing for a criterion
whose only browser test had no proof.]

### 10.5 Panel

**L4-VER-004** The panel runs the first `verifier.panel.size` (≥ 1) profiles in `roles.judges` that are available and
independent. With ≥ 2 judges, a criterion `pass` requires all judges to agree; a split is `disputed`.
`pass_k > 1` repeats each judge k times and requires all runs to pass (pass^k). The tie-breaker is the next
available independent judge in the chain.

### 10.6 Outputs

**L4-VER-005** The verifier MUST write `<unit>/verification.md` (overwritten per round, previous rounds kept in
`.l4/evidence/round-<n>/verification.md`) containing: verdict and round; the base SHA and head SHA the evidence refers
to; profiles used (with fallbacks); ladder table with status and timings; the traceability matrix (alias, ID, tests,
discriminating?, adequacy, S1 p, judge verdicts, human verdicts); findings with evidence; TDD exemptions and
`pre_adoption` tasks; guard events; links to CI artifacts (logs, traces, screenshots, reports); cost. The machine
version goes to `.l4/evidence/round-<n>/verdict.json`, which also records the judge prompt `template` (`judge@<version>`)
and the `harness_commit` that wrote it (null for a checkout or an installed wheel). The prompt of every judge and audit-writer call (redacted,
L4-OBS-002) MUST be published next to the agent's events as `.l4-out/agent/<run>/<stem>-<n>.prompt.md`; the SHA-256
of the prompt document (system text, a blank line, the user text) recorded as `prompt_sha256` in `verdict.json` MUST
equal the hash of the first such file (a prompt-contract adapter appends its schema instruction after that document).

### 10.7 Fix units

**L4-VER-006** On FAIL, while fewer than `verifier.max_fix_rounds` fix units exist for the parent, the spec writer
MUST create one fix unit for the round's blocker/major findings (§4.4/§4.5): one TDD task per finding (or per group of
findings on the same criterion); a `new tests failed` or `new tests errored` finding whose test ids are all among the failing ids that the round's `failures` map (L4-VER-069) holds for the gate of a `test gate failed` or `e2e gate failed` finding of the same round (a finding with no criterion) joins that finding's task, which then names both: one failure, one task (a list the finding cut with `and <n> more`, ids of two gates, a verdict without the map, and a finding that names no id leave it a task of its own; verdicts, finding ids and `same_failure` do not change); tasks cite finding and criterion IDs. The fix unit's proposal lists each task's
findings with the human's decisions first ("Decided by human in Q-NNN: <reason>"), so a length cut on a long finding
never drops a decision and leaves the implementer an open question it must not decide. A decision is kept whole up to 1,200 characters (the finding's own detail is what is cut). A test chore (a rejected coverage hold) whose task begins with a decision that calls the code wrong must add tests that assert the decision: a failing test is not kept and is reported `blocked` with a technical question naming the test and the decision, and tests that all pass against that code get one retry reason naming the decision (attempt 1 only). A finding with `spec_gap: true` produces, before
its task, an **ADDED** regression requirement with a scenario when L4-VER-059 gives it one (OpenSpec: `## ADDED Requirements` →
`### Requirement: <parent requirement> — regression <n>`; Kiro: a new `2.n` acceptance criterion in `bugfix.md`, or a `3.n` when the scenario says `SHALL CONTINUE TO`). The parent requirement is the cited criterion's, else the parent's only one. When a person rejected a finding that cites no criterion with a `WHEN … THEN …` and the parent has several requirements, the scenario SHALL go under an ADDED requirement of its own, `<finding title> — finding <id>`, in the parent's first capability by name, as a feedback item's does (L4-FBK-004): the person's scenario is never dropped. A judge's spec-gap suggestion that no person asked for gets no such requirement. Fix units
never use MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED deltas (the parent's requirements are not in the base specs until the parent is
archived, L4-OSP-006). The task of a rejected **coverage** hold is a test chore (`test_chores` in `.l4/fix.json`): its prompt
says to add tests that run the changed code the hold names; its step may add test files and append new tests to the unit's
own test files (kept only when every earlier top-level statement of the file is unchanged, no added definition rebinds a
name the file binds or a fixture its tests request, and what is added only defines tests, test classes, imports and
constants: no fixture, module mark, xunit setup, pytest hook or call made at import, which would reach the file's existing
tests), any other change to a test file and any new or changed test-support file is put back, a change to a
non-test file fails the attempt, at least one new test must pass, and `task.tests_added{task, files, tests}` records it. A finding about the tests of a criterion the round found satisfied (M1.13, W-C1) is a test chore as well, and the task keeps the criterion: it is a judge's or a human's finding (a gate's is not), its title speaks of tests, it cites a criterion whose round result is `pass` (judged, or accepted by a human), and no regression scenario is to be pinned; when any of these fails, or when one finding of the criterion's task is of another kind, the task stays red/green (the code is not assumed right). The code of such a task is right, so no honest red test can fail and the red step, which needs a new failing test, would halt the unit; instead the step must add at least one test that fails by assertion when the project's functions answer their zero value or on the unit base's code (the verifier's `discriminate_extra`, run in the step for a chore that cites a criterion, recorded as `task.tests_added.discriminating`). A fix unit with no ADDED requirement sets `skip_specs: true` (a spec gap that L4-VER-059 gives no scenario adds none). The fix unit is validated strict before
commit. Parent → `fixing`; when the fix unit's tasks are done, the **parent** is re-verified as a whole (round + 1),
covering parent and fix criteria.

A finding with `source: "feedback"` (a taken item of `feedback.md`, L4-FBK-004, or an item the judge found not addressed,
L4-FBK-007) is one task of its own: it is never grouped with another finding and never dropped for lacking a criterion or a
scenario. The proposal (OpenSpec) or `bugfix.md` (Kiro) puts the request first, before every other finding and decision:
`Requested by <By> in FB-NNN (<kind>, <places>): <text>`, the text kept whole up to 1,200 characters, followed by the quoted
code. The task is by the item's kind:
* `refactor` and `duplication`: a chore listed under `refactors` in `.l4/fix.json`, run with no red step (it cites no
  requirement; the implementer's `run_single` runs it as `kind=refactor`). After the agent's step every
  path matching `tdd.test_globs` or `tdd.test_support_globs` that it changed is put back (a new one is removed) as
  `guard.restored{task, paths, reason: "feedback_refactor"}`, the attempt fails with `nothing changed` when no other file
  changed, and every gate must pass: the unchanged, passing tests are the proof that behaviour did not change.
* `tests`: the test chore above (`test_chores`).
* `config` and `behaviour`: an **ADDED** requirement (OpenSpec: `### Requirement: <item title> — feedback FB-NNN` in the
  parent's one capability, else the first by name; Kiro: `2.n`/`3.n` items of `bugfix.md`) and the task goes red, then green.
  Its scenarios are, for `behaviour`, the item's `WHEN <when>` / `THEN <then>`; for `config`, `WHEN the environment variable
  NAME is set THEN the system SHALL use its value instead of the value written at <first place>` (the item's own When/Then
  replaces this one when given) and `WHEN NAME is not set THEN the system SHALL CONTINUE TO behave as before this change`.

The retake rule for both chores: when every feedback item a chore task carries is a *retake* (the finding is listed under
`retakes` in `.l4/fix.json`: the item had a `feedback.taken` before this fix unit and its content is the one taken), a step
that leaves "nothing changed" (refactor) or adds "no tests" (test chore) does not fail the attempt. The change may have
been made already, with the judge leaving the item out of its reply. The task is ticked in a commit that changes no file
of the project, with `L4-TDD: already-done`, and recorded as `task.done{tdd: "already-done", reason: "retaken FB-NNN:
nothing left to change"}` without `task.tdd_exempt`; the integrity check of the TDD history accepts that value as it does
`exempt`, and the test-path check still applies to its commit. The parent is then re-verified and the judge looks at the
item again; an item that is still not addressed is taken again until `feedback.max_rounds`. A first take keeps failing as
before. A `config` or `behaviour` item is red/green and needs no rule of its own: when the tests its retake writes pass
already, the `already_satisfied` exemption of L4-IMP-002 applies.

A fix unit holds at most `MAX_FIX_TASKS` (5) tasks. Feedback items past that cap are not converted: they stay takeable,
are recorded as `feedback.waiting{ids, reason: "fix_unit_full"}`, and the sticky note says they wait for the next round.

**L4-VER-059 A person's reject decides a fix task's check.** The verdicts of a finding in a fix task SHALL be the
`reject` of the finding and the `reject` of its cited criterion, in that order, each when present. Every verdict of
every finding of a task SHALL be quoted in the task's decisions (`Decided by <by> in Q-NNN: <reason>; Q-MMM:
<reason>.`, together within the characters L4-VER-006 keeps for decisions), whichever of them gave a scenario, and both questions are
consumed. The task's regression scenarios SHALL come from these verdicts only: the `WHEN … THEN …` of each reason that
has one, the finding's first, each text pinned once. The judge's `suggested_fix` SHALL be a scenario only of a spec-gap
finding that has no verdict (a minor on a PASS with `verifier.fix_minor_findings`); it MUST NOT become a scenario of a
finding that has a verdict, whether the reason is empty, says nothing of it, or agrees with it, and no model or text
match decides agreement: the judge prompt asks for a spec gap's suggestion as the behaviour the committed code shows, so
after a reject it is the behaviour in dispute. A finding that has a verdict and no scenario from it SHALL keep its cited
criterion and add no regression requirement, so the fix is checked against that criterion's own scenarios (OpenSpec:
`skip_specs: true` when no other task adds a scenario; Kiro: only the restated criterion as `2.n`). Without a cited
criterion such a finding SHALL NOT be converted: it is listed `rejected with no criterion and no WHEN ... THEN ...:
answer again with a scenario`, and its question is not consumed. A spec-gap finding all of whose verdicts have an empty
reason (a bare `reject` that reached the file by another route than `l4 questions answer`, such as an edit by hand)
SHALL NOT be converted either: it is listed `rejected with no reason: answer again with a reason or a scenario` (when it cites no criterion, the rule above applies first and it is listed as that one says: answer again with a scenario), and its questions are not consumed. The `WHEN … THEN …` of a reason is its last one, so a reason may quote the criterion's
`WHEN … THEN …` and then give its own; a reason with one is read as before. [V, 0.4.20: a reject of a spec gap whose reason had
no `WHEN … THEN …` pinned the judge's "exits 2" beside the criterion's "exits 1"; a reproduction of a consumer's
finding.] The reason is the one `human.verdict` records (`verdicts.bounded_reason`): at most 4,000 characters; a longer
reason that has a `WHEN … THEN …` keeps that sentence whole, from its last `WHEN`, after the first characters of the text
before it and ` … `, while a longer one without a sentence, or whose sentence alone exceeds 3,800 characters, keeps its
first 4,000 characters; the answer's digest is of the whole answer. [V, 0.4.45: the reason was cut at 1,000 characters,
and a consumer's delegate ended two rejects of 1,207 and 1,264 characters with the sentence the question asks for, so the
fix unit's scenarios read `THEN a` and `THEN a test asserts that [...DEFAULT_ROLES].sort() deep-equals [`.]

**L4-VER-007** On FAIL when `max_fix_rounds` fix units already exist (i.e. at most `max_fix_rounds + 1` verification
rounds), or after 3 consecutive internal errors, the unit goes to `escalated`, label `l4:escalated`, sticky comment
with the verdict summary, exit 13.

A fix unit all of whose consumed blocking findings have `source: "feedback"` is a *feedback fix unit* (recorded as
`fix.spawned{…, feedback_only: true}`). It is not counted against `verifier.max_fix_rounds`; it is counted against
`feedback.max_rounds` (§3.2; default 5, 0 turns taking off), raised by `budget.extended{feedback_rounds}` (L4-IMP-013).
On a FAIL whose fix unit would be a feedback fix unit and whose feedback limit is used up, the unit goes to `escalated`
(exit 13, label `l4:escalated`) with `phase.changed{reason: "feedback_rounds_exhausted"}` and the note `feedback round
limit reached (N)` in the sticky comment; `l4 resume --extend-feedback-rounds N` or the resume label continues it, and the
comment's resume line says so (`--extend-feedback-rounds N`, "one more feedback round per label event"), not the fix-round
wording of a fix-limit escalation. A fix
unit that also consumes a non-feedback finding (a red repository CI job, a gate failure) is a normal fix round, counted
by `max_fix_rounds`, and its feedback items are still marked taken.

### 10.8 System-One calibration data

**L4-VER-008** Each S1 judgment MUST be appended to `$L4_CACHE/s1-calibration.jsonl` (runner, L4-CFG-005) and
summarised in the evidence (`state` hash, question, `p`, deterministic outcome, judge outcome, later human outcome if any).
Each row also carries what is needed to compare rows across servers: the **served model** (as the reply names it:
Laya answers `laya-rl-agent` whatever it loaded, Jev answers `jev-1.13.0` to `jev-latest`), the configured
**checkpoint** (`model`), the Laya package version, or `ollama <version>` for an Ollama host (`server_version`), the **question-set id** (`criterion-s1@1` for
step 8, `clarifier-s1@2` for the clarifier), the engine, the state size (`state_tokens`) and whether the server cut the
state (`server_truncated`), and the choice probabilities (`evidence`). Rows are written after step 9, so the `judge`
column holds the judge's word, and they are still written when step 9 fails; the `verify.s1` event carries the
checkpoint beside the served model.
`l4 lessons`-adjacent tooling (v1.1) exports a labelled set for `laya-evals run … --min-accuracy --max-ece` gating
[V, Laya README] and fine-tuning.

## 11. Archive, PR/MR and the merge gate

**L4-ARC-008 Hand-off invariant.** At PASS the harness makes exactly **one hand-off commit H** on the unit branch (it
contains `verification.md`, the round's evidence index and the folded ledger; no `[skip ci]`) and marks the PR ready.
It records the sha of H as `pr.ready{head}` on the unit's lock ref (L4-STA-004), and that record is H from then on
(`UnitState.ready_head`). The verdict, the evidence, the approval and the repository's required checks all bind to H. While the PR is ready
(`in_review`, `archived`), the only harness pushes to the unit branch are, each as **one push**: (a) on approval —
an optional base-merge commit plus the archive commit (L4-ARC-001); (b) on a base move — archive revert, base merge and
re-archive (L4-ARC-006); and (c) when the unit leaves review — the archive revert, pushed after the PR was set back to
draft (from then on the normal checkpoint rules apply). After every push of type (a) or (b) the PR head MUST be a
harness commit **without** `[skip ci]` (the archive commit), so required checks run on the head a human merges. Ledger
events produced after H (`phase.changed`, costs, approvals) are written to the unit's lock-ref commits (off-branch,
never a PR head; L4-STA-004) and folded into the next unit-branch commit. Any commit after the recorded H that the harness did not make **voids the approval**. With
`archive.mode: post_merge_pr`, where the harness pushes nothing to the unit branch while the PR is ready (L4-ARC-007),
that is every commit after the recorded H, whatever its author, committer or trailers, and a recorded H that is not an
ancestor of the branch head is rewritten history. Only a unit with no recorded H keeps the identity rule: a commit is
the harness's only when its author **and** its committer are the harness bot identity **and** it carries an `L4-Run`
trailer, so an amended, rebased or cherry-picked H is a person's. H is read from the pending files of the unit's lock ref
only, never from events in the branch tree. Anyone who can push the lock ref can forge `pr.ready{head}`: that residual
is accepted, and closing it needs signed harness commits or a ref only the harness can write. A voided approval removes
`archive.approval_label` and sends the unit back (answers or spec
edits → `implementing`; anything else → `verifying` for a new round). Before the harness itself rewrites the PR content
after H (archive revert), it MUST set the PR back to draft and the `l4/<unit>` status to `pending`.

**L4-ARC-001 Archive on approval (opt-in `archive.mode: on_approval`).** After PASS and H the unit is `in_review`.
Approval = `archive.approval_label` set by a member, or (with `accept_forge_approval`) a PR review approval / MR approval,
**given for head H** (approvals on an older head are ignored). Then the harness MUST: merge the current base into the
unit branch if it moved (§12.3) and re-run verification steps 0–3 when it did (a failure → `verifying`); run the
provider `done_gate()`; re-validate strict; archive the **parent first, then its fix units in round order** (OpenSpec
`archive --yes` with `TZ=UTC`; Kiro per §4.5) in a single commit `chore(<unit>): archive` with `L4-Phase: archived`
(a hand-off commit: no `[skip ci]`); push it; and create an annotated tag `l4/<fw>/<name>/verified-<round>-<short-sha>`.
On any archive error the worktree is restored, nothing is pushed, and the unit goes to `escalated`. The approval label
is removed whenever the unit leaves `in_review`/`archived` for any phase other than `merged`.

**L4-ARC-002** PR/MR lifecycle: opened as **draft** on the first push of the unit branch; title
`[l4] <name>: <first line of proposal Why / requirements intro>` (a proposal heading that only repeats the unit name is not a title: the Why line is used, else the title is `[l4] <name>`); body regenerated from `state.json` on every phase
change (phase, task progress, questions, last verdict summary, the base SHA and H the evidence refers to, evidence
links, cost, profiles, "approve with `l4:approve` to archive"); labels `l4:<phase>` (one at a time) plus
`l4:needs-answers` / `l4:escalated` when applicable; commit status `l4/<unit>` with state `pending|success|failed`. If
the repository's own CI fails on H or on the archive commit, the unit returns to `verifying` with a deterministic finding
`repository CI failed: <job>` — counted only for jobs that are green on the base head (jobs already red on the base are
reported as pre-existing and do not consume fix rounds). A base head with no pipeline, or none that has the job, counts
the job as new (a unit should not hand off red; the cost is at most one fix round per H, bounded by
`max_fix_rounds`), and a job red on H that has no finished attempt on the base head defers the decision (an earlier
finished attempt there counts, so the base pipeline the sweep itself runs in does not hide it).
The failing step of such a job (the last `$` command of its `step_script`, recorded by the sweep as `ci.failed.jobs[].step`)
is re-derived from the project's CI files at H, never trusted from the log: it must be one whole entry of the job's
`before_script` + `script`, runnable without a shell (a shell given a command string, `sh -c '…'`, is refused) and
outside a denylist (containers, deployment, installs, the network). When it can be derived safely and reproduces the CI failure at the fix's base, it is re-run in the gate
sandbox as `repository-ci:<job>`: it must pass after the `[chore]` fix, and it runs as a step-2 gate of the rounds that
follow, until a PASS verdict or another review edge. Otherwise the fix is checked by the judge alone, and the reason is
recorded (`ci.step{status: skipped, reason}`). A GitHub job's step is named (`ci.failed.jobs[].failed_step`), never
re-run (L4-VER-064). The finding's detail carries the failing step's excerpt (L4-VER-061 to L4-VER-063). A CI job
that fails again on a hand-off after no commit changed a project file does not get another fix unit: the unit escalates with
`ci_not_fixed` (L4-OPS-023).
A forge POST that creates something (the MR or pull request, the sticky note or comment, a label) MUST be retried
blindly only when it cannot have landed: a connect error or HTTP 429. After a lost response (a read timeout, a dropped
connection) or an HTTP 5xx the forge MUST first read the effect back (the open MR of the branch, the note carrying the
sticky marker by the bot, the label by name) and POST again only when the read finds nothing; a second lost response is
an error. A lost response therefore never yields a second note, MR or label.
The sticky note carries a *Your feedback* section while the unit's `feedback.md` has any item, with one line per item
(`FB-NNN <kind> <first place> — <state>`: draft, submitted, taken into `<fix unit>`, waiting for the next round with its
reason, addressed in round N at `<sha>`, not addressed in round N with the evidence, invalid with the problem, or
withdrawn), and the note of a unit in `in_review` ends with the line `To ask for changes: l4 feedback add --kind
refactor|duplication|tests|config|behaviour --at FILE:LINE --text "…", then commit and push (docs/feedback.md).`
(L4-FBK-011). The hand-off writes the note even when nothing else is waiting. `verification.md` has a `## Feedback`
section for the items taken or judged in the round, and `l4 status` counts the items per state.

**L4-ARC-003** With `merge_policy: human` the harness MUST NOT merge. The PR body MUST say that any merge method works: the harness detects a
merge from the merge request and the tree, a merge commit keeps the commits' L4 trailers in the history and a squash
drops them (the history of truth is in the files either way). The body is static and also says who merges: a person,
unless the unit is in an active delivery plan with `merge: auto`, where the harness merges it (L4-YOLO-008). A merged PR is detected by the
sweeper → `merged`; the lock ref moves to `refs/l4/archived/…` after the archive merge (nothing pushes the WIP branch: it is a local ref). Whether the merged result is archived is decided from the
**tree at the merge commit** (is the unit's change folder still under `openspec/changes/` / is the Kiro unit's ledger
phase `archived`), never from the presence of an archive commit in history; a merged but unarchived unit gets the
post-merge archive PR of L4-ARC-007.

**L4-ARC-004** Answers or spec edits pushed by a human after H, in `in_review` or `archived`, void the approval
(L4-ARC-008); the harness first reverts its archive commit if one exists (a new `revert` commit; pushed history is
never rewritten), then the unit goes to `implementing`; the PR returns to draft. Re-archiving later starts from the
restored change folders, so no delta is applied twice. Any other foreign commit after H sends the unit to `verifying`.

**L4-ARC-005** A PR/MR closed without merging MUST move the unit to `abandoned` (terminal: no runs, lock released, WIP
branch kept for 30 days); reopening it restores the phase recorded before `abandoned`.

**L4-ARC-006 Base moves after archiving.** If the base branch moves while a unit is `archived` (approved, not yet
merged) and the PR is no longer mergeable or the base changed any file under the unit's capability specs, the sweeper
MUST set the PR to draft and the status to `pending` (L4-ARC-008), revert the archive commit, merge the base, re-run
steps 0–3 and re-archive, then mark the PR ready again (the approval stays valid because the approved evidence is
re-checked deterministically on the same H content plus the base). Otherwise it leaves the PR alone.

**L4-ARC-007 Post-merge archive (default `archive.mode: post_merge_pr`).** Verified units go to `in_review` without
archiving and need no approval label; the human merge of H is the sign-off. After the merge the sweeper opens one
harness PR on the base branch that contains only that unit's archive changes (serialised across units; a later unit's
archive PR is rebuilt on the latest base, so parallel units never conflict), for a human to merge — or merges it itself
when `archive.auto_merge_archive_pr: true`. The unit is `archived` when that PR merges. This mode has no revert,
re-archive or approval paths, and while the code PR is ready the harness pushes nothing to the unit branch.

**L4-RACE-001** Concurrent human pushes: every harness push of the unit branch MUST be a fast-forward under a lease on
the head the run last saw (the remote-tracking ref, else what this run pushed last), never a force push. A refused lease
SHALL be classified with `git ls-remote <remote> refs/heads/<branch>` against the lease value: no such branch is **gone**
(W-D2: it is never recreated; exit 1, and `l4 restart` is a person's decision), a remote head that contains the lease
value is **moved** forward, any other head is **rewritten** (exit 1, the harness never forces, and `l4 restart` is a
person's decision). A refusal while the remote still holds the lease value, or when the remote cannot be asked, stays
unclassified (L4-LCK-001). For a moved branch the harness fetches the remote head to a private ref
(`refs/l4/tmp/<pid>/<branch>`, removed after use) and reads, commit by commit, what the new commits change. When every
commit only adds or modifies, and leaves a regular file, the `questions.md` of this unit's folder or of one of its
fix-unit folders (`<unit>-fix-<n>/`) that the branch holds, the harness SHALL **merge** the remote head into its HEAD,
never rebase it (pushed history is never rewritten): `merge --no-ff`, a strict harness commit
`chore(<name>): merge <n> answer commit(s) from the forge` with the harness identity and the run's trailers; a
`questions.md` conflict is settled per question, a person's answer beating the delegate's (§12.3); then it scans the
outgoing commits again (L4-SEC-007), moves the lease to the merged head and pushes. It makes at most 3 pushes in all, 5 s
and then 15 s apart, and each try classifies the branch again from the new remote head; after the third the run exits 1
`the unit branch keeps moving on the forge` (a person's answers arrive faster than the run can merge them): the answers
stay on the forge and the next run takes them. Each merge records `push.merged{remote, commits, paths}` (data only; the
fold ignores it). The judgement is per commit: a code commit that a later commit reverts, a deleted, mode-changed or
linked `questions.md` is not an answer, and a person's merge commit of answers is. The harness SHALL NOT merge into a
hand-off: while HEAD is the unit's hand-off commit H, the push of H fails as a moved branch and the next run hands off
again on the answers. A commit that changes any other path is never merged (a person's code on the second parent would
pass for the harness's own in the walkers that follow the first parent): the run exits 1 with `a person pushed <n>
commits to <branch> during this run that change <first five paths>; the harness merges only answers to this unit's
`questions.md`, and never into a hand-off, so this run's work since its last push is not pushed. The next run starts
from the forge's branch`, without `l4 restart` advice; a merge that cannot be settled (a conflict outside
`questions.md`, a dirty worktree) ends the same way with its own message. Only a gone and a rewritten branch name
`l4 restart`. After a merge the next step reads `questions.md` from the worktree (level-triggered, P2), and the delegate
pass reads each question from the worktree again before it asks and skips one that is no longer open (no call, no
event). A push that failed ends the run with L4-RACE-002.

**L4-RACE-002** A run whose push of the unit branch fails still ends on the forge. When the push of the unit branch
failed during a run, or the final push in `close()` fails, the run SHALL publish a reduced copy of its ledger file to the
lock ref's pending ledger (kept on disk for the next run when that publish fails too), so that the run has its
`run.finished`, its costs count and no reader takes it for a run that is open for ever. The copy holds the lines of the
run's file that the unit branch has (the file at `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` as of the last successful push; none if
the run never pushed), unchanged and with their sequence numbers; every `budget.cost` and `lock.released`; and
`run.finished` with `reason: "the push of the unit branch failed: <why>"`, cut to 400 characters and with the forge's host
scrubbed (L4-OBS-002; git names it). It SHALL NOT hold any other event written after the last push: those describe
commits that never reached the branch, and a reader must not take them for facts (a `delegate.result{answered}` would
make `due_questions` drop a question that is still open on the branch, a `task.done` or a `phase.changed` would move the
fold ahead of the branch). The fold, `due_questions`, `delegate_cost`, unfreeze and held read the branch's state plus the
money spent and the run's end; none of them looks a commit up. The run's commits stay on the runner. One risk is named:
a delegate call that reported no cost (an unpriced profile) is no longer counted at `max_cost_usd_per_answer` by
`delegate_cost` after such a failure, because its `delegate.result` is not published.

---

## 12. State, ledger, locks

### 12.0 Lifecycle (normative)

States: `intake`, `rejected`, `ready`, `implementing`, `clarifying`, `awaiting_human`, `waiting_capacity`,
`implemented`, `verifying`, `fixing`, `verified`, `in_review`, `archived`, `merged`, `abandoned`, `halted`,
`escalated`. The orchestrator is the only component that changes the phase; every change is a `phase.changed` ledger
event. Internal steps (merge-conflict resolution, base merge, the archive re-check of L4-ARC-006) do not change the
phase; the archive on approval is the `in_review → archived` transition.

| From | Condition / event | To | Run exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | unit discovered with pending non-optional tasks | `intake` | — |
| — | unit discovered with all tasks `[x]` and no PASS record (L4-ODD-003) | `implemented` | — |
| `intake` | any ODD/SDD check fails (incl. missing oracle → bootstrap unit created, L4-ODD-002) | `rejected` | 14 |
| `rejected` | spec/config/oracle changed and intake re-run passes | `ready` | — |
| `intake` | all checks pass | `ready` | — |
| `ready` | lease acquired and implementer selected | `implementing` | — |
| `ready`, `implementing`, `implemented`, `verifying`, `fixing`, `clarifying` | a **required** role has no usable profile (L4-AVL-010, L4-VER-015) | `waiting_capacity` (previous phase remembered) | 12 |
| `waiting_capacity` | `retry_after` passed and selection succeeds, or `l4 retry` / `l4:retry` (L4-OPS-001) | previous phase | — |
| `implementing` | blocking questions raised and clarifier available | `clarifying` | — |
| `implementing` | blocking questions raised, clarifier unavailable/disabled, or no eligible task remains while questions are open | `awaiting_human` | 11 |
| `clarifying` | every blocking question answered | `implementing` | — |
| `clarifying` | some question needs a human | `awaiting_human` | 11 |
| `awaiting_human` | answers submitted (explicit Status) unblock ≥ 1 eligible task | `implementing` | — |
| `awaiting_human` | all verdict questions answered (L4-VER-013; a stale one does not count, L4-VER-070) | `verifying` | — |
| `implementing` | all non-optional leaves `[x]` | `implemented` | — |
| `implementing`, `fixing`, `verifying`, `verified` | breaker or budget (L4-IMP-008/009); a secret in the outgoing commits halts in any of these (L4-OPS-009) | `halted` | 13 |
| `implemented` | — | `verifying` | — |
| `verifying` | PASS | `verified` | — |
| `verifying` | FAIL and fewer than `max_fix_rounds` (+ extensions) fix units (feedback fix units are not counted, L4-FBK-006) | `fixing` (fix unit created) | 10 or 0 |
| `verifying` | NEEDS_HUMAN | `awaiting_human` (verdict questions) | 11 |
| `verifying` | FAIL with all allowed fix units used (for a feedback-only fix unit: the `feedback.max_rounds` rounds, L4-FBK-006), or 3 consecutive internal errors | `escalated` | 13 |
| `fixing` | the fix unit's tasks are all done | `verifying` (round + 1) | — |
| `fixing` | the fix unit needs answers | stays `fixing`; outcome reports the child's `awaiting_human` | 11 |
| `verified`, `in_review`, `archived` | a consumed answer was overridden (L4-QMD-006) | `fixing` (clarification-apply unit) | — |
| `verified` | minor findings and `fix_minor_findings: true` | `fixing` | — |
| `verified` | done-gate fails (a human added an unchecked task) | `implementing` | — |
| `verified` | hand-off commit H pushed, PR marked ready (L4-ARC-008) | `in_review` | 0 |
| `in_review`, `archived` | the repository's own CI fails on H or on the archive commit (jobs green on base only) | `verifying` (finding) | — |
| `in_review` | approval for H (`on_approval` mode), re-check passes, archive succeeds | `archived` | 0 |
| `in_review` | approval for H, but the base-merge re-check of steps 0–3 fails | `verifying` | — |
| `in_review` | approval for H, but archive fails | `escalated` | 13 |
| `in_review` | `l4 retry` or the label `retry` (`retry_requested`, L4-OPS-001) | `verifying` | — |
| `in_review`, `archived` | human pushes answers or spec edits after H (approval voided, archive reverted) | `implementing` | — |
| `in_review`, `archived` | any other commit after H not made by the harness (approval voided, archive reverted) | `verifying` | — |
| `archived` | base moved and re-check required (L4-ARC-006) | stays `archived` (draft → revert → merge → steps 0–3 → re-archive → ready); on failure `verifying` | — |
| `in_review`, `archived` | PR merged (archived-ness decided from the merge tree, L4-ARC-003) | `merged` | 0 |
| any phase but `merged`, `abandoned` and `archived` | PR closed unmerged (`pr_closed`, L4-OPS-009) | `abandoned` | — |
| `abandoned` | PR reopened before any restart (`pr_reopened`) | phase before `abandoned` | — |
| `halted`, `escalated` | `l4 resume` or `l4 retry` by a member, or the label `retry` / `resume` (with the needed budget extension, L4-IMP-013, L4-OPS-001) | phase before halting | — |
| `halted`, `escalated` | `l4 retry` finds a person's change of the unit folder since the stop (`spec_edit_since_stop`, L4-OPS-003) | `implementing` | — |
| `intake`, `ready`, `implemented`, `verifying`, `verified`, `awaiting_human`, `clarifying`, `halted`, `escalated` | a person's push changed the unit folder (`spec_edited`, L4-OPS-014) | `implementing` | — |
| any non-terminal | the unit's spec no longer validates | `rejected` | 14 |

`merged` and `abandoned` are terminal (until reopened). With the default `archive.mode: post_merge_pr`,
`in_review → merged` happens without `archived`; the archive PR is tracked as a unit field (`archive_pr`, its state) and
the unit's ledger records `archive.done` when it merges. The rows mentioning approval and `archived` apply to the
opt-in `on_approval` mode only. No other transitions exist; the simulation
suite asserts that every edge above is exercised and that no other edge occurs.

*Planner actions.* `l4 plan` names one next action per unit: `implement`, `clarify`, `verify`, `hand_off`, `follow_up`
or `none`. `follow_up` is for a `merged` unit whose `feedback.md` on the base branch has takeable items and no open
follow-up (L4-FBK-010); it creates the unit `<name>-followup-<n>` and changes no phase of the parent.

*M1 form of the review rows (M1.9).* `archived` is a source only in `on_approval`, and leaving it needs the archive
revert of L4-ARC-004, which is not built: the built rows have `in_review` as their only source, and the approval half
(voided approval, archive revert) is N/A in `post_merge_pr`. The three edges carry no run exit: `commit_after_handoff` →
`verifying` (a commit after H that the harness did not make: the harness's have the bot identity as author **and**
committer and an `L4-Run` trailer), `spec_edit_after_handoff` → `implementing` (the net diff after H changes the unit
folder outside `verification.md` and `.l4/`: answers or spec edits) and `repository_ci_failed` → `verifying` (the
sweep recorded `ci.failed` for H, and the branch head is still H). Foreign commits come first; a branch that lost its H
(an amended or rebased H is no longer H) counts as one. The orchestrator takes the
edge at the start of the run, sets the MR back to draft before its first push (L4-ARC-008 (c)), and the verifier's
step 0 turns the recorded CI result into one `repository CI failed: <job>` blocker per red job, in that round only. The
harness never re-triggers itself: its own commits are the bot's with `L4-Run`, H2 carries `L4-Run` too (so it starts no
`l4` job), and the sweep acts once per H.

### 12.1 Ledger

**L4-STA-001** Each run appends JSONL events to `<unit>/.l4/ledger/<run-id>.jsonl` (one file per run → merge
conflicts impossible). Every event has `{ts, run_id, unit, seq, type, …}`. Event types (minimum set):
`run.started` (harness version and commit, base/head SHA, iteration, `runner {id, description}` from `CI_RUNNER_ID` and `CI_RUNNER_DESCRIPTION` when set, `tools {python, git, bwrap}` versions, each left out when the tool is missing; the selected agent CLI's version is `availability.selected.probes.<profile>.binary`), `intake.passed|unit.rejected`, `phase.changed`,
`availability.selected|availability.unavailable|availability.fallback|availability.cooldown|availability.model_unverified|availability.unrecorded_version|availability.login_wait|availability.wait_in_run`,
`step.started|step.finished` (idempotency key; `step.finished.status` is the agent's own `RunResult.status`: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth`, `error`, ...; a step cut short by an exception is `error`), `agent.finished` (status, exit code, tokens, `permission_denials` count and `denied_tools`, never a tool input), `agent.session` (adapter, session id), `agent.tool_rejected` (`{task, phase, tool, reason}`, one per `RunResult.tool_rejections` entry),
`task.started|task.red_ok|task.done|task.failed|task.tdd_exempt|task.unfrozen` (`task.unfrozen{task, paths, reason, source, question, answer_sha256, red_sha, kept}`: the frozen test and support files that a human answer (`reason: "human_answer"`, also read when `reason` is absent; `question` and `answer_sha256` set) or the task's own reviewed text (`reason: "named_by_task"`; `source` is `plan:<plan id>@<digest>` or `base:<sha>`) freed for green; `kept` lists each named path that stays frozen, with its reason), `criterion.pre_satisfied`, `stub.scope_leak`,
`named_tests.found` (`{task, tests, source}`: before the agent step of a red attempt, the existing tests the task's reviewed text names, as the red prompt lists them, with the text's source, L4-IMP-089),
`named_tests.kept` (`{task, token, reason}`: a name the task's reviewed text used, a backticked `path::name`, that opened no test to change in place, with why, L4-IMP-089),
`judge.length_split` (`{round, profile, criteria, into, depth, cause, part, parts}`: a step-9 judge's reply stopped at its output limit or its call timed out (`cause`), and the prompt's criteria were split in two for the same judge, L4-VER-071),
`verify.carried` (`{round, criterion, from_round, from_head}`: a round whose judge gave no verdict kept an earlier round's pass of an unchanged criterion, L4-VER-072), `verify.not_carried` (`{round, from_round, reason, paths}`: once, when no criterion could be carried),
`gate.result`, `gate.reused` (`{name: "baseline", from: "test", task, source_sha, tree}`: a task's baseline that took the report of the green gate run of `source_sha` instead of running the gate, because the tree tested is the same up to the unit's ledger, `tasks.md` and held files, L4-IMP-088), `guard.violation|guard.test_tamper|guard.agent_commit|guard.secret` (`guard.test_tamper{phase: "red", rule: "pre-existing test", action: "rejected", tests, why}` when a red attempt changed a test that existed before it, L4-IMP-048), `verify.base_tests{round, base_sha, base_source, reverted, passed_at_base, still_passing, failing, not_run, collection_errors, flaky, allowed}` (step 1's run of the base's tests, L4-VER-038), `question.raised|question.answered|
question.status_inferred|question.override` (`question.raised` carries the question's `title`), `clarifier.result`, `verify.step|verify.verdict|verify.error`, `verify.generated` (step 5's record of a UI criterion; `status: waived` with `by`, the answered question, `attempts: 0` and no writer call, when an accept of the criterion or of its UI hold is in force, L4-VER-067), `base.merged|base.conflict` (verifier step 0: the base merged into the unit
branch `{base, base_sha, merge_sha, behind, resolved, frozen_touched}`, or a source conflict `{base, base_sha, files, resolved}`),
`fix.spawned` (`feedback_only: true` for a feedback fix unit, L4-VER-007),
`feedback.taken` (`{id, kind, sha256, round, fix_unit}`) | `feedback.addressed` (`{id, round, sha, evidence}`) |
`feedback.not_addressed` (`{id, round, evidence}`) | `feedback.changed` (`{id, previous_sha256, sha256}`) |
`feedback.judged` (`{id, round, evidence}`: the judge's yes, closed only by a PASS round) |
`feedback.withdrawn` (`{id}`) | `feedback.invalid` (`{id, problem}`, and `duplicate: true` for a copy of a heading; the problems are the rule that the item breaks, `duplicate id FB-NNN` and `no Status line`) | `feedback.waiting` (`{ids, reason}`, `fix_unit_full` or `follow_up_open`),
all L4-FBK-004..007, `guard.restored` (`{task, paths, reason}`; `feedback_refactor` for the frozen tests of a refactor chore,
L4-VER-006),
`archive.done` (`{via: "done_gate", base}` for a Kiro unit), `pr.updated`, `pr.ready` (`{url, number, head}`: `head` is the sha of H, read from the lock ref's pending files as `ready_head`, never from the branch tree, L4-ARC-008), `ci.failed` (`{head, pipeline,
jobs: [{name, stage, url, tail, step}], preexisting: [name]}`: the project's own CI is red on H; on GitHub a job is named `<workflow file> / <job>` (L4-CI-011); `tail` is the end of the job's
log, redacted; `step` the last `$` command of its `step_script`, redacted, at most 300 characters; `failed_step` the name of a GitHub job's failing step, redacted, at most 300 characters, L4-VER-061) and `ci.step` (`{job, head, step,
command, status: derived|skipped|reproduced, reason, source}`: what step 0 or a `[chore]` decided about a red job's failing
step; the last event per `(head, job)` wins) and `ci.preexisting` (`{head, pipeline, jobs: [name]}`: red on H and on the base head, so no fix round),
`lock.acquired|lock.released|lock.stolen`, `budget.cost` (`{usd, profile, task}`; kiro-cli meters plan credits, not dollars: `{credits, credits_source: "kiro.stream", profile, task}`, the sum of the stream's `meteringUsage` values, never added to `usd` or to the unit's cost; a Kiro judge or clarifier call writes the same event with `role: "judge"` or `role: "clarifier"` instead of a task, and `verify.judge` carries the judge's `credits` summed over its calls, L4-KJD-004; a follow-up judge call's `verify.judge` carries `followup`, `followups` and `criteria`, L4-VER-058; `verify.verdict` and `verdict.json` carry the `independence` record, whose routed party has `vendors`, §10.1; the quota probe's `/usage` reading rides on `availability.selected.probes.<profile>` as `credits_used`, `credits_included` and `credits_source: "kiro.usage"`, because the two disagree on the FREE plan [V, 10.72 metered against 5.42 of `/usage`]), `breaker.tripped`,
`availability.transient` (`{role, profile, status, attempt, wait_s}`), `unit.resumed` (`{reason, by, signal, note_task, note_fix_unit}`; the two note fields only when the command gives a note, L4-OPS-018), `resume.refused`
(`{signal, why}`), `resume.hint` (`{head}`), `task.tests_added` (`{task, files, tests}`), `verify.extra_proof`
