**L4-YOLO-031** A person can waive an accepted finding, audited. `l4 yolo waive PLAN FINDING --reason TEXT [--withdraw]
[--yes] [--no-run]` SHALL record `plan.finding_waived{finding, subject, reason, by, actor, marker}` in the plan ledger,
pushed with the lease, then start the harness's CI on the base branch unless `--no-run`. It MUST be refused, with
nothing recorded, for a plan that is not `active`, `waiting` or `stopped` (before the activation the command is
`l4 yolo accept`), for an id that is not a finding of the activation's accepted items, for an empty reason, and for an
agent unless `yolo.review.accept_by_agents` is true at `origin/<base>` and `--yes` is given. A person MUST type the
plan id after the finding and its acceptance are shown, or pass `--yes` (L4-YOLO-063). `--withdraw` SHALL record `plan.waiver_withdrawn{finding,
reason, by, actor}` for a waived id. A new activation clears the waivers. With `merge: auto`, the merge guard of
L4-YOLO-028 SHALL count a waived finding as answered, so the harness merges the unit through its guarded merge. The
report SHALL show `waived by <by> (<actor>): <reason>` for a waived finding the verifier did not answer
`addressed: true`, and `l4 yolo status` SHALL list the waivers. For a plan waiting with `accepted_finding_open`, the
`Next:` line SHALL name `l4 retry --unit U` (the verifier gave no answer), `l4 feedback add --unit U` (the code must
change) and `l4 yolo waive` (the finding needs no handling).

**L4-YOLO-032** The plan merges a unit by squash unless configured to fast-forward. The configuration has
`yolo.merge.method` (`squash` or `fast-forward`, default `squash`). With `squash`, after every precondition of
L4-YOLO-008 and `unit.merge_requested`, the plan step SHALL merge the unit's PR through the forge's merge call with the
squash method, pinned to the recorded hand-off commit H (L4-YOLO-040), never a branch tip it read, with a message the harness writes: the PR title without `[skip ci]` and with
` (#<pr>)`, and the trailers `L4-Unit`, `L4-Verified-Head` and `L4-Run`. A forge answer that the head moved SHALL be
`not_ready`; any other refusal SHALL stop the plan with `merge_refused` and the forge's message. After the merge the
harness SHALL compare the landed commit's parent with the target tip it read and its tree with H's tree, and
SHALL record `unit.merged{head, merge_commit, method, raced, ci, ci_jobs}` (`head` is H, or the head a person merged the PR at) with `raced: true` when either differs. The post-merge
check SHALL run on the landed commit. With `fast-forward` the merge SHALL stay the push of L4-YOLO-008, recorded with
`merge_commit` equal to the head.

**L4-YOLO-033** Merged branches are deleted unless configured to stay. The configuration has
`yolo.merge.delete_branches` (default `true`). When it is true, after the forge reports a plan unit's PR merged, the
harness SHALL push `refs/l4/merged/<framework>/<name>` at the verified head and then delete the unit branch with a lease
on that head; after `archive.merged` it SHALL delete the archive branch with a lease on the archive head. A lease that
fails SHALL keep the branch and record `unit.branch_kept{branch, reason}`; a deleted branch SHALL be recorded as
`unit.branch_deleted{branch, head}`. Neither SHALL stop the plan. A plan step SHALL also delete, at most five per step,
the unit and archive branches of the plan's integrated units whose PR is merged and whose tip is still the recorded
head. The lock ref SHALL NOT be deleted at merge time. A branch of a PR the forge does not show merged SHALL NOT be
deleted. The evidence link in the PR body names the unit head commit, so it opens after the branch is gone.
**L4-YOLO-034** A plan is checked in the working tree before the push. `l4 yolo check PLAN --worktree` SHALL read the
plan files and the units from the working tree and run the admission of `l4 yolo check` on them, and SHALL also report,
across all plan files of the working tree, `uncovered` (a unit no plan lists as planned or excluded, except a derived
unit whose parent is listed, and except a unit `yolo.hold` matches) and `covered_twice` (a unit two plan files plan).
It SHALL print every finding, then the order of the units and the budget warnings, write nothing, and exit 0 when the
plan is admitted and nothing is uncovered or covered twice, else 2. A plan file that is not in the working tree SHALL be
exit 2 naming the path. For the same tree, its coverage findings SHALL be the ones `scripts/validate_plan.py` prints.
`l4 yolo draft` and the worktree review SHALL name this command in their hints.

**L4-YOLO-035** A capacity wait never chains runs, and a wait only a fix can end stops the plan. A plan step that
dispatches its current unit while the unit is `waiting_capacity` SHALL NOT start the next run; the next schedule, push
or person's command probes again. When the current unit parks in `waiting_capacity` with no profile of the chain
cooling (every failure a missing binary, a failed login, a `hello` that was refused or answered wrongly, a constraint
or `serves`; the unit's `availability.unavailable` has no `cooling`, `quota` or `concurrency` skip and its `retry_after`
is not in the future, which a transient failure's wait is, L4-AVL-013),
for the same set of unusable profiles as its previous park, with no `task.done`, `task.red_ok`, `task.green_committed`
or successful `step.finished` of the unit between them, and both parks after the plan was last activated or resumed, the
plan SHALL stop with `capacity_needs_fix`. The stop SHALL name each profile, its failure and the fix (renew the secret
the profile reads, for example `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, or install the binary). `l4 yolo resume` SHALL be allowed after that
stop; the next run probes. A park with a profile cooling (a limit or credit with a reset) keeps the plan waiting until
`retry_after` (L4-AVL-007, L4-YOLO-013).

### 12.6 L4 as an MCP server (MCP)

Any MCP client (an IDE, an agent) manages delivery plans and debugs units through typed tools, under the same rules as the
CLI. The decisions are in `openspec/changes/mcp-server/design.md` (D1..D5).

**L4-MCP-001** `l4 mcp serve` is an MCP server over stdio. It SHALL speak newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0: `initialize` (answering the client's protocol revision when the server knows it, else its pinned one, with `capabilities.tools` and `serverInfo {name: l4, version}`), `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` and `notifications/initialized`.
- An unknown method SHALL answer -32601, a line that is not JSON -32700, an invalid request -32600; the server keeps serving.
- Only protocol messages SHALL go to stdout; logs go to stderr.
- The harness SHALL add no runtime dependency for it (the official `mcp` package is a dev dependency of the interop test only).
- The streams SHALL be read and written as UTF-8 bytes whatever the locale; bytes that are not UTF-8 give a parse error on that line, never a crash.
- A `progress` value of a progress notification SHALL be greater than that of the notification before it for the same token, and none SHALL follow the response of its call.
- `initialize` and `tools/list` SHALL name the repositories the instance serves (`serverInfo.title`, `instructions`, each tool's description), so a client with several instances can tell them apart.

**L4-MCP-005** An instance serves the repositories it was started for. `l4 mcp serve` SHALL take `--repo PATH`, repeatable; each PATH SHALL resolve to the root of a git repository with `.l4/config.yaml`, else the server SHALL exit 2 before it serves.
- One `--repo`: every tool runs there, and a tool's `repo` argument, when given, SHALL name it (folder name or path), else the call is refused.
- Several: every tool SHALL take a required `repo` argument naming one of them (folder name, or path compared after resolving symlinks); any other value SHALL be refused, never resolved. Two repositories with the same folder name SHALL be refused at start.
- No `--repo`: the working directory serves when it is such a repository; otherwise every tool call SHALL answer an error that names `--repo`.
- Every tool result SHALL name the repository it ran in. A tool SHALL NOT run in a repository the server was not started for.

**L4-MCP-002** Every tool runs the `l4` command it names, as an agent. A tool SHALL run `python -P -m l4 <command>` as a subprocess in the repository (`-P`, on this child only, keeps the repository's own files, such as a `yaml.py`, off `sys.path`), with the caller's environment plus `AI_AGENT=l4-mcp` and no terminal on stdin, so that every rule the CLI applies to an agent caller holds (`clarifier.answer_by_agents` and the others). The server SHALL make no write of its own, and SHALL NOT pass the global `--repo` or `--config` options.
- A value reaches the command as `--option=value` or after `--`, so it cannot be read as an option.
- A result SHALL carry the exit code, the output redacted again and cut at 64 KiB with the cut said, the parsed JSON when the command printed JSON, and `isError` for a non-zero exit, a timeout or a cancel.
- A timeout or a cancel SHALL stop the command's whole process group: SIGTERM, then a grace period counted in wall-clock time from the signal, also after the command itself exited (a descendant may clean up), then SIGKILL to what remains, so a descendant that ignores SIGTERM does not keep running.
- A `number` argument SHALL be finite; NaN and infinity are refused as a bad argument, and `--extend-cost` of `l4 resume` and `l4 yolo resume` refuses them too (exit 2).

**L4-MCP-003** The tools manage plans and debug units.
- Read: `l4_status`, `l4_doctor`, `l4_plan_status`, `l4_plan_check` (`worktree`: `l4 yolo check --worktree`), `l4_plan_findings`, `l4_plan_report`, `l4_questions`, `l4_question`, `l4_unit_events` (`l4 status --unit U --events`), `l4_verification` (`l4 status --unit U --verification`).
- Write: `l4_plan_draft`, `l4_plan_review` (`worktree`), `l4_plan_go` (L4-YOLO-090), `l4_question_answer`, `l4_retry`, `l4_plan_resume`. A write tool's description SHALL say what it writes, whether it pushes to origin, and that CI may be running; `l4_plan_review`'s and `l4_plan_go`'s SHALL say that they cost judge tokens and take minutes.
- Not offered: `l4 yolo activate`, `l4 yolo cancel`, `l4 run`, anything that starts an agent CLI. The descriptions name the command a person runs.
- The read-only command `l4 status --unit U --events|--verification` SHALL exist for them and SHALL write nothing to a ref, the index or a tracked file; `l4_plan_check` with `worktree` runs `l4 yolo check PLAN --worktree` (L4-YOLO-034).

**L4-MCP-004** `l4 mcp install` configures a client in one command. `l4 mcp install --client <name> [--project] [--repo PATH] [--name NAME] [--dry-run]` SHALL write the client's documented MCP configuration with the command `l4 mcp serve --repo <absolute path>` (user scope) or `l4 mcp serve` with no path (`--project`: the file is committed, so each clone and worktree serves its own folder: `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` when it names an L4 repository, else the working directory's) under the entry NAME (default `l4` with `--project`, `l4-<repository folder>` otherwise), merging into an existing file, keeping every other server and the keys of the entry the user added, atomically.
- It SHALL refuse a file it cannot parse (exit 2, naming the file, nothing written) and print what it wrote.
- It SHALL refuse (exit 2, nothing written) an entry of that name that serves another repository, naming both paths and `--name`, and, for `--project`, a symlink on the file or on a folder above it inside the repository.
- Only clients whose path and format were checked against the vendor's documentation are offered: Claude Code (project `.mcp.json`; user scope prints `claude mcp add --scope user`), Cursor, VS Code (project only), Kiro, Codex (TOML, only the `[mcp_servers.NAME]` table is replaced), OpenCode. The vendor URLs are in `src/l4/mcp/install.py`.
- A project entry depends on where the client starts the server. Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (from v2.1.139), VS Code starts it in the workspace folder, OpenCode and Codex in the session's directory: their entries hold `l4 mcp serve` with no path. Cursor documents no working directory, so its project entry holds `--repo ${workspaceFolder}` (the folder that contains `.cursor/mcp.json`; https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp). Kiro documents neither, so `--project` for Kiro SHALL be refused (exit 2, nothing written) with the hint to use the user scope.
- Codex starts a server with an allowlisted environment: its entry SHALL also carry `env_vars` naming `forge.token_env` of the repository's `.l4/config.yaml` (the schema default when it does not), keeping the variables the user listed.
- Claude Code desktop worktree sessions read `.mcp.json` of the main checkout and set `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to it (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees): a project file serves a worktree only for a session started inside it; to serve a worktree otherwise, use a user-scope entry with `--repo <worktree path>`.

**L4-YOLO-040** The plan merges the recorded hand-off commit H and nothing after it. The guarded merge SHALL take H from `UnitState.ready_head`. It SHALL be `not_ready` when no H is recorded, naming `l4 retry --unit <id>`, and when the snapshot's hand-off commit or branch head is not H, naming both shas. Every sha the merge uses SHALL be H: the `ls-remote` and PR-head checks, the squash `sha`, the fast-forward push, the keep ref and the leased branch delete.

**L4-YOLO-041** A review edge comes before the merge. When the plan's current unit is in review with a PASS and the planner gives it work (a commit after H, a spec edit, rewritten history, or red repository CI recorded on H), the plan step SHALL dispatch the unit and SHALL NOT call the guarded merge. The guarded merge SHALL itself be `not_ready` when the unit's recorded `ci.failed` is for H.

**L4-YOLO-042** The merge waits for the repository's CI on H. Before `unit.merge_requested` the guarded merge SHALL read the repository's CI on H as the sweep does (L4-CI-012). `running`, `failed`, `blocked` (a cancelled or held job), an unreported required check and a read error SHALL be `not_ready` whatever `yolo.merge.require_ci` says, naming H and the jobs or the check. `green` and `preexisting` SHALL go on, and `not_run` too unless `yolo.merge.require_ci` is true (L4-YOLO-043). `unit.merged` SHALL record `ci`, and `ci_jobs` for `preexisting`.

**L4-YOLO-043** Whether a hand-off commit that no CI ran on is merged is configured. The configuration SHALL have `yolo.merge.require_ci` (default `false`): whether a `not_run` CI on H blocks the merge. Running, red (new on H) and unreadable CI SHALL block whatever its value. With `false`, `not_run` SHALL NOT block: the plan step SHALL merge, record `unit.merged{ci: not_run}` and warn in the plan report and on the merged PR or MR. With `true`, it SHALL be `not_ready`, naming `yolo.merge.require_ci: false`.

---

**L4-YOLO-050 A limit of an active plan is raised without waiting for the stop.** `l4 yolo resume PLAN --reason TEXT --extend-…` on an `active` plan SHALL record `plan.extended{by, actor, marker,
agent_key, reason, extend, limits_before, limits_after}` and nothing else: no resume, no run. The limits in force
(L4-YOLO-014) SHALL include it. No `--extend-…`, one that changes no limit and a cost that is not finite SHALL be
refused (exit 2). `l4 yolo
status` SHALL list the extensions and name the option in an active plan's `Next:` line.

**L4-YOLO-051 Raising a plan's limit is a person's decision.** Every `--extend-…` of `l4 yolo resume`, on an active, waiting or stopped plan, SHALL be refused (exit 2, nothing
written) for an agent (`l4.actor.actor`), unless `yolo.extend_by_agents` is `true` in `.l4/config.yaml` at the plan's own
target branch (default `false`), and only if the configuration's base branch is that target and the plan file there is
the one the plan recorded. The refusal names the command a person runs and the key; the event records `actor`, `marker`
and `agent_key`.

**L4-YOLO-052 After an answer is pushed, the resume does not refuse it.** The plan step, `l4 yolo resume` and `l4 yolo status` SHALL decide by one predicate (`l4.yolo.cycle.still_waits`)
whether the current `awaiting_human` or `clarifying` unit of a waiting plan still waits. When its answers are pushed
and no run has read them, `l4 yolo resume` SHALL resume the plan and start the run that reads them. While a question is
open, the refusal SHALL say that the plan continues by itself at the run that reads the answer, so no resume is needed.

**L4-YOLO-053 After an answer, the status says what happens next.** For a waiting plan whose current unit is `awaiting_human`, the `Next:` line of `l4 yolo status` SHALL say: with a
question open, how to answer it (`l4 questions --unit U`, then `l4 questions answer Q-NNN --unit U --text TEXT`, which
pushes the answer and starts a run) and that the plan continues by itself, naming no `l4 yolo resume`; with the answers
pushed, that the next run reads them and how to start that run now (`l4 yolo resume PLAN --reason TEXT`, or the forge's
start command).

**L4-YOLO-054 After an answer, the wait line shows the live reason.** With the answers of the current unit pushed (the planner's own reason: an answer that unblocks a task, or verdict
answers not consumed), the wait detail that `l4 yolo status` prints (text and `--json`) SHALL be
the live reason (the answer is recorded and the next run reads it), not the detail recorded when the plan began to wait.

**L4-YOLO-055 A plan stopped on a unit with its own way out names that way first.** For a plan stopped with `unit_escalated` on a unit whose escalation has its own way out (`l4.state.next_step.way_out`:
`judge_view_rejected`, `no_convertible_finding`, `ci_not_fixed`), the `Next:` line of `l4 yolo status` and the refusal of
`l4 yolo resume` SHALL name that way out, not `l4 retry --unit U` first. Any other cause keeps its text.

**L4-YOLO-056 The next line of a waiting plan follows the unit's answer step.** For a waiting plan whose current unit is `awaiting_human` with an answer that is invalid, dismissed or only a draft, the
`Next:` line of `l4 yolo status` SHALL give the step `l4 status --unit` gives (fix the answer, answer the question) and
how to replace a recorded answer (`l4 questions answer Q-NNN --unit U --text "accept ..." --replace`).

**L4-YOLO-057 A person can force-accept every subject of a plan without a review.** `l4 yolo accept PLAN --all --force --reason TEXT [--yes]` SHALL accept every unit of the plan and every batch with more than one unit as it stands, whatever the review says or lacks: no review, a review for other inputs, BLOCKED, a blocking finding, a material finding and fewer than `yolo.review.accept_after_rounds` judged versions are all overridden. It MUST NOT call a model. It SHALL print each subject with what it overrides, then take the person's confirmation (L4-YOLO-063), then append in one leased write `plan.admitted` (unless the plan is already admitted or reviewed at this digest with this order) and `plan.force_accepted{plan_digest, subjects, reason, by, actor: person, marker: null, confirmed}`, where each subject has its digest (a batch: its units' digests), `skipped` (`no_review`, `stale_review`, `blocked`, `blocking`, `material`, `rounds`, `not_ready`, or none), `review_at`, `verdict` and `material`. `--force` without `--all`, `--all` without `--force`, `--all` with a SUBJECT, and neither a SUBJECT nor `--all` MUST exit 2 before anything is read.

**L4-YOLO-058 Only a person in a terminal force-accepts.** `l4 yolo accept --all --force` SHALL be refused (exit 2, before the plan is fetched, nothing written) for every caller that `l4.actor.actor` does not name a person: an agent marker is set, or stdin is not a terminal. It MUST be refused for an agent even when `yolo.review.accept_by_agents` is true, and for every MCP caller (the server runs the CLI with `AI_AGENT=l4-mcp` and no terminal); the MCP server MUST offer no tool that runs `l4 yolo accept`. The refusal SHALL say that it is a person's decision, why the caller is not one, and the command a person runs.

**L4-YOLO-059 What a force acceptance never overrides.** `l4 yolo accept --all --force` SHALL keep, with their own refusal and nothing recorded: a missing plan file or one that is not a plan; the plan status rule of L4-YOLO-027 (before the activation, or stopped with `inputs_changed` or `unit_rejected`); every finding of the admission that `l4 yolo activate` runs (among them `unknown_unit` for a unit folder that does not exist on the target, `cycle`, `unknown_dependency`, `intake`, `open_questions`); and a unit whose current digest is missing (`unit_missing`).

**L4-YOLO-060 A force acceptance is bound to the text it accepted.** A force acceptance SHALL hold for a subject while the plan file's digest is the one it recorded and the subject's current unit digest (a batch: each of its units') is the one it recorded, by the digest rule of the activation and of `inputs_changed`. A change of the plan file MUST void it for every subject; a change of a unit's spec MUST void it for that unit and every batch that holds the unit. A later `plan.force_accepted` SHALL replace the earlier one. The plan fold MUST ignore a `plan.force_accepted` whose `actor` is not `person` (the command never writes one for an agent). `l4 yolo accept PLAN --all --force --withdraw --reason TEXT` SHALL record `plan.force_acceptance_withdrawn{reason, by, actor, marker}`; it MUST NOT be refused for who runs it, and is refused after the activation and when no force acceptance is recorded.

**L4-YOLO-061 Activation of a force-accepted plan.** `l4 yolo activate` SHALL NOT require a review when a force acceptance holds for every subject of the plan (a missing or stale review is not a refusal; the findings of a current review on a subject the acceptance did not override still are); every other refusal of L4-YOLO-005 stays. Otherwise the review rules of L4-YOLO-005 apply, and a subject that a holding force acceptance overrode (its recorded `skipped` is not empty) MUST count as cleared whatever a current review says of it. `plan.activated{accepted}` SHALL hold each such subject as `{findings: [], reason, by, actor: person, force: true}` and the event SHALL record `review: force_accepted` when it holds one. A refusal while a force acceptance is recorded MUST name the subjects it no longer holds for.

**L4-YOLO-062 A force acceptance is shown wherever the plan and its units are.** `l4 yolo status` and `l4 yolo findings` (text and `--json`) SHALL show each overriding subject of a recorded force acceptance as `<subject>: force-accepted without review by <by> (<reason>)`, with `; no longer holds: its spec or the plan file changed` when it does not hold, and `l4 yolo status` SHALL name `l4 yolo activate` in its `Next:` line when it covers the plan. After the activation the status, the plan report and each force-accepted unit's PR body SHALL name it, and the unit's implementer prompt SHALL carry the reason with the rule that no model reviewed the specification.

**L4-YOLO-063 A person's --yes replaces the typed plan id.** For a person, `--yes` SHALL replace the typed plan id in `l4 yolo accept PLAN SUBJECT`, in `l4 yolo accept PLAN --all --force` and in `l4 yolo waive`; the command MUST still print what it prints today before recording (the findings, the waived finding and its acceptance, the force summary). `plan.accepted`, `plan.finding_waived` and `plan.force_accepted` SHALL record `confirmed: typed` or `confirmed: --yes`. For an agent, `--yes` SHALL keep its rule: `l4 yolo accept PLAN SUBJECT` and `l4 yolo waive` only with `yolo.review.accept_by_agents` true at `origin/<base>`; `--force` never.

**L4-YOLO-064 No confirmation prompt waits unseen.** `l4 yolo accept` and `l4 yolo waive` SHALL prompt only when stdin is a terminal; without one and without `--yes` they MUST exit 2 at once with a message that names `--yes`, and MUST NOT read stdin. Every prompt SHALL be written to stderr and flushed before stdin is read, so that a pipe or a wrapper on stdout cannot hide it.

**L4-YOLO-065 A reuse keeps the judgement a person accepted.** When a review reuses a recorded judgement of a material (the CI step, `l4 yolo review --local`, `l4 yolo review --worktree` with or without `--record`) and an acceptance of the plan is bound to that material, the review SHALL reuse the newest recorded judgement of that material whose findings have the acceptance's `findings_sha`, when the ledger holds one, and otherwise the newest judgement of the material. The binding of L4-YOLO-027 MUST NOT change: an acceptance holds only on the same material and the same findings.

**L4-YOLO-066 An acceptance says whether it holds, and why not.** Where the verdict of an accepted subject is printed (`l4 yolo findings`, `l4 yolo review --worktree`, `l4 yolo review --local`, the CI review log line) an acceptance that holds SHALL be said on that line, and a reused entry SHALL show when it was judged. An acceptance that does not hold SHALL be explained in one line in `l4 yolo status`, `l4 yolo findings` (text and `--json`) and the activation refusal: `other material` or `other findings of the same material`, the accepted material and findings (8 characters each) and when they were judged, the latest review's material and findings, when they were judged and whether they were `reused` or `new`, and for other material whether the subject's own spec changed.

**L4-YOLO-067 Documentation of the force path and of the confirmation.** `docs/yolo-mode.md` SHALL have a section "When the reviewer is unavailable" with the force path, who may run it, what it never overrides, the risk that specifications no model reviewed get built, and the alternative of reviewing in CI with `l4 yolo review <plan>` without `--local`. The runbook SHALL give the procedure. The skill's `plan.md` and `operate.md` MUST tell an agent never to run `--force` and to give the person the exact command. The CHANGELOG's 0.4.18 section and the SPEC SHALL name the force path, a person's `--yes` and the acceptance binding fix.
**L4-YOLO-068 A stale review names what differs and the next command.** When the latest review of a plan is not for what `origin/<base>` holds, `l4 yolo activate` SHALL refuse with exit 2, `l4 yolo status` SHALL show it (text, and `--json` `review.stale`) and `l4 yolo review` SHALL print it before it asks CI, each with one line per cause: a review prompt change (both versions); the plan file (its digest at the review and now, with the short sha of `origin/<base>`); each unit whose spec digest changed (both digests, the ref it is read on now, `origin/<base>` or its branch, with its short sha, and the files whose content changed when the review recorded its revisions); each subject the review did not judge; and, when the local HEAD is ahead of `origin/<base>` and they differ in the plan file or a unit folder, both short shas, the commit counts and those paths, with "push, then review". The refusal MUST end with a `Fix:` line that holds the exact command. Every `plan.reviewed` event SHALL record `target_rev` (the sha of `origin/<base>` the review read) and `unit_revs` (per unit, the sha of the revision its folder was read on); a review without them MUST still give every line except the changed files. A refusal for a plan file that is not on `origin/<base>` MUST name the sha and, when HEAD or the working tree holds the file, how to push it. A plan stopped with `inputs_changed` MUST record in its stop detail the frozen and the current digest, where the unit is read, and the changed files when known. Commit shas MUST be shown as 7 characters and digests as 8.

**L4-YOLO-069 `--record` records only a review of `origin/<base>`.** `l4 yolo review PLAN --worktree --record` SHALL fetch `origin/<base>` and, before any judge call, MUST refuse with exit 2 and record nothing when HEAD is not `origin/<base>`. The refusal MUST name both short shas, the number of commits HEAD is ahead and behind, the plan paths that differ, and "push, then review" (or the pull), and its `Fix:` line MUST hold the exact commands. When the two shas differ and git cannot count the commits between them, it MUST refuse the same way, naming both short shas and a `Fix:` that fetches and makes HEAD the same commit. It MUST also refuse when CI reads a unit of the plan on its branch on origin and that branch holds another spec digest than HEAD, naming the unit, the branch, both digests and the changed files. When HEAD is `origin/<base>`, it SHALL record the review with `target_rev` equal to HEAD. Its last line SHALL be `Next: a person runs l4 yolo activate <plan> --reason TEXT` when every subject is READY or accepted, else `Next: l4 yolo findings <plan>`. The dry run (`--worktree` without `--record`) SHALL keep reading the working tree whatever HEAD is.

**L4-YOLO-070 The CI review warns about unpushed plan commits.** `l4 yolo review PLAN`, without `--worktree` and with or without `--local`, SHALL print one warning before anything else it prints when HEAD is ahead of `origin/<base>` and HEAD and `origin/<base>` differ in the plan file or a unit folder of the plan. The warning names both short shas, the count and the paths, and says that the review reads `origin/<base>`, not the local commits: push, then review. It MUST NOT change the exit code. There MUST be no warning when the unpushed commits change none of these paths, or when HEAD is only behind.

**L4-YOLO-080 One command runs the plan's steps in order.** `l4 yolo go PLAN --reason TEXT [--accept-findings | --force] [--yes] [--json] [--no-push] [--local] [--wait DURATION]` SHALL run the steps preflight, push, check, review, findings, accept and activate in that order. Before each step it SHALL read whether the step already holds and SHALL NOT repeat a step that holds. Every write it causes MUST be made by the existing command that makes it today (`l4 yolo review --local`, `l4 yolo accept`, `l4 yolo activate`) with that command's rules, event and lease; it MUST NOT record an event of its own. `--reason` SHALL be the reason of every acceptance and of the activation it causes. These usage errors MUST exit 2 before anything is read or fetched: a plan id that is not one, an empty `--reason` or one over 1,000 characters, `--accept-findings` with `--force`, `--force` with `--local`, and a `--wait` that is neither `0` nor a duration.

**L4-YOLO-081 Preflight checks the working tree as the skill's script does.** The preflight step SHALL run, with no network and before anything is fetched, the checks of the skill's `scripts/yolo_preflight.py`: no tracked file differs from HEAD (`dirty`), the plan file exists in the working tree (`plan_missing`; when `origin/<base>` has it the fix is `git pull --ff-only origin <base>`) and is JSON (`plan_not_json`), the plan file is not untracked (`plan_uncommitted`), and no file under the folder of a unit the plan lists is untracked (`unit_uncommitted`). An untracked file elsewhere MUST NOT stop it. The checks SHALL have one implementation in the harness (`l4.yolo.preflight`); the script MUST NOT be changed to call the harness, and a test SHALL keep the two in agreement. A problem, a repository with no `origin`, or a base branch that is not on `origin` SHALL stop the run with exit 20, every problem, and the first one's fix as the next command.

**L4-YOLO-082 The push is a fast-forward of the base branch and never a surprise.** When HEAD is ahead of `origin/<base>`, the push step SHALL push the branch `<base>` to `origin` without `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, after the working-tree admission of `l4 yolo check PLAN --worktree` passed, and fetch it again. It MUST NOT push and SHALL stop with exit 21 and the command that clears the cause when: HEAD and `origin/<base>` have diverged (`git pull --rebase origin <base>`); HEAD is not the branch `<base>` (`git switch <base>`); a plan on `origin` that is active or waiting (this one, or another) has its plan file or one of its unit folders changed by a commit ahead, a rename counting at its old and its new path, which would stop it with `inputs_changed` (`l4 yolo status PLAN`); `--no-push` is given (`git push origin <base>`); git refuses the push (its reason: the repository's own `pre-push` hooks run, so a hook that fails refuses the push). A working-tree admission finding (`uncovered` among them) MUST stop it with exit 22 before the push. For an agent caller, a commit ahead that touches any path (a rename's old path too) other than `.l4/plans/PLAN.json` and the folders of the plan's units MUST make the push a person's step (exit 27, `next_by` person), with `--no-push` too (the `l4_plan_go` tool always has it): `--no-push` gives an agent `git push origin <base>` as its own command (exit 21) only when the commits ahead hold nothing but the plan file and its unit folders. With nothing ahead the step SHALL be `ok` and push nothing.

**L4-YOLO-083 The check step admits the plan at the target and reads its state.** The check step SHALL read the plan's ledger and admit the plan file at `origin/<base>` as `l4 yolo check PLAN` does. An active or waiting plan SHALL end the run with exit 0 and its state, before admission, with nothing written; a completed plan likewise, with `l4 yolo report PLAN` as the next command. A cancelled plan, a plan stopped for a reason other than `inputs_changed` or `unit_rejected`, and a plan stopped with `unit_rejected` whose rejected unit's spec has not changed MUST stop the run with exit 23, the status's own next step in the detail and `l4 yolo status PLAN` as the next command. A missing plan file, a file that is not a plan and every admission finding MUST stop the run with exit 22, each finding, and `l4 yolo check PLAN --worktree` as the next command.

**L4-YOLO-084 The review is reused when current, else made in CI with a bounded wait or here.** The review step SHALL reuse a review at the current plan and unit digests and prompt version, with no dispatch and no judge, and SHALL be skipped when a force acceptance holds for every subject and no review is current (a current review is said to be there, with a note that its problems stop at findings when they do). Otherwise, with `--local` it SHALL review here as `l4 yolo review PLAN --local` does; with `--force` it MUST NOT review or ask for a review. Else CI reviews it: when this run pushed the base branch, the push starts the run; otherwise `go` SHALL ask the forge to start one, and when the forge cannot, it MUST stop at once with exit 24 and the command that starts a run by hand. It SHALL then poll the plan ledger at most every 15 seconds until the review at the current digests is recorded, a refusal newer than the ask is recorded (exit 22) or `--wait` (default 30m; `0`: no wait) ends (exit 24, `pending`, the go command as the next command). A judge that cannot run with `--local` MUST stop the run with exit 25 and the go command without `--local`.

**L4-YOLO-085 Findings stop the run unless they are accepted by the accept rules.** A subject that is not READY, has no acceptance that holds and is not cleared by a force acceptance SHALL stop the run at the findings step with exit 26, one line per such subject (its verdict and most severe finding), and as the next command the go command with `--accept-findings` when this caller may accept every such subject, else `l4 yolo findings PLAN`. With `--accept-findings`, `go` SHALL accept each such subject by running `l4 yolo accept` for it with the reason and the caller's `--yes`, so that every rule of L4-YOLO-027 and L4-YOLO-063 applies; when one subject cannot be accepted by this caller it MUST record nothing and stop (exit 27 when only a person may accept them, else exit 26 with each refusal). An agent without `--yes` MUST stop with exit 29. With `--force` a person's run SHALL force-accept the plan by running `l4 yolo accept PLAN --all --force` (L4-YOLO-057), and an agent's run MUST stop with exit 27 before anything is read. A person who does not type the plan id MUST stop the run with exit 29.

**L4-YOLO-086 Activation is a person's step.** When every subject is READY, accepted with an acceptance that holds, or cleared by a force acceptance, a person's run SHALL activate the plan by running `l4 yolo activate PLAN --reason TEXT`, with that command's rules, output and run start, after the person has typed the plan id (`Type the plan id (PLAN) to activate PLAN`, a prompt on stderr, on a terminal only; `--yes` skips it; a wrong answer or no terminal without `--yes` MUST stop with exit 29 and the go command, recording nothing). An agent's run MUST NOT activate: it SHALL check the refusals of the activation that remain after the review (the target on `origin`, no other plan active, waiting or stopped on the target); a refusal MUST stop it with exit 28 and that refusal, otherwise it SHALL stop with exit 27 and `a person runs: l4 yolo go PLAN --reason TEXT`. When the refusal is another plan holding the target, the next command SHALL be `l4 yolo cancel OTHER --reason TEXT`, which for an agent is printed as a person's step (`a person runs:`, cancelling a plan is a person's decision). Nothing is recorded by an agent's stop.

**L4-YOLO-087 Each stop has its own exit code and exactly one next command.** `l4 yolo go` SHALL end with one of: 0 `active` (the plan is active, waiting or completed, now or before), 20 `preflight`, 21 `push`, 22 `not_admitted`, 23 `plan_state`, 24 `review_pending`, 25 `review_failed`, 26 `findings`, 27 `person` (the next step is a person's), 28 `refused` (a called command or an activation check refused, or the plan lease was lost three times), 29 `not_confirmed`; 1, 2 and 16 keep the meaning of L4-CLI-001. These stop codes MUST NOT be members of the harness's `ExitCode` and MUST NOT change `SEVERITY_ORDER`, `CI_ALLOWED` or `l4 ci map-exit`. In text mode it SHALL print one line per step reached, `<step>: <status>: <detail>`, with the output of a command it ran indented under it and without that command's own `Next:` lines, and SHALL print exactly one `Next:` line, last: `Next: <command>`, or `Next: a person runs: <command>` for exit 27. The next command of a refusal SHALL be the command of the refusal's `Fix:` line when it has one, else the go command again. A reason in a next command MUST be quoted for the shell.

**L4-YOLO-088 --json prints one document and nothing else.** With `--json`, stdout SHALL hold exactly one JSON document, printed when the run ends: `{schema: "l4/yolo-go@1", plan, step_reached, steps, next_command, next_by, exit}`, where `steps` lists the seven steps `preflight`, `push`, `check`, `review`, `findings`, `accept`, `activate` in that order, each `{name, status, detail}` with `status` one of `ok`, `done`, `skipped`, `pending`, `stopped`, `person`, `not_reached`, `step_reached` is the last step whose status is not `not_reached`, `next_command` is the command alone, `next_by` is `person` when that command is a person's step (exit 27, and exit 28 when the cancel command is handed to an agent) and `caller` otherwise, and `exit` equals the process's exit code. What a person must read before a prompt, the prompt and the wait's progress line MUST go to stderr. Exits 2 and 16, and exit 1 before preflight has passed, print no document; a harness or network fault after it keeps exit 1 and prints the document with the step it hit `stopped` and the go command as `next_command`.

**L4-YOLO-089 Safe to run again, to interrupt and to run at the same time.** A run SHALL decide each step from the ledger and the repository as they are when it reaches the step. A second run with nothing changed MUST record nothing, push nothing and start no judge; it SHALL ask the forge for a run only when the review is still missing. A run interrupted at any point SHALL leave the ledger as the commands it ran left it, and the next run SHALL go on from there. Concurrent runs SHALL be serialised by the plan ledger's lease (L4-YOLO-006): when a command `go` runs loses the lease, `go` SHALL read the plan again and decide again, at most three times, and MUST NOT record a write twice; the fourth lost lease SHALL stop the run with exit 28 and the go command as the next command.

**L4-YOLO-090 Agents run the agent-allowed steps; the MCP tool is read-mostly.** For an agent caller (`l4.actor.actor`), `l4 yolo go` SHALL run preflight, the push of the hand-off (L4-YOLO-082), check, review and findings, and SHALL accept only with `--accept-findings --yes` where `l4 yolo accept` lets an agent accept (`yolo.review.accept_by_agents` true at `origin/<base>`). It MUST NOT prompt, MUST NOT force-accept and MUST NOT activate; at a person's step it SHALL stop with exit 27 and the person's exact command. No configuration key SHALL change these rules. The MCP server SHALL offer the tool `l4_plan_go`, which runs `l4 yolo go PLAN --reason TEXT --json --no-push [--wait DURATION]` as an agent; it MUST NOT offer `--accept-findings`, `--force`, `--yes` or `--local`, and its description SHALL say that it may ask CI for a review (judge tokens), may wait, never pushes, accepts or activates, and that an agent MUST NOT run a `next_command` whose `next_by` is `person`.

**L4-YOLO-091 Documentation of the one command.** `docs/yolo-mode.md` SHALL have a section "One command: `l4 yolo go`" with the steps, the flags, the stop codes, the JSON document, re-running, what an agent's run does and that `go` activates (`l4 yolo status` is the read-only view). The runbook's procedure 12.2 SHALL start with "Or simply: `l4 yolo go`". The skill's `operate.md` SHALL give `l4 yolo go <id> --reason "…"` as a person's first step of the plan runbook and the agent's use (`--json`, a bounded `--wait`, exit 27 hands the person `next_command`, never `--force`); `plan.md` SHALL name it in the hand-off. The CHANGELOG's `## 0.4.19 (unreleased)` section and the SPEC SHALL name the command.

**L4-YOLO-092 A task that names a forbidden file is refused at intake.** The intake of a unit (plan check, review, activation, `go` and the CI review; and the start of a unit before it implements, OpenSpec and Kiro) SHALL refuse a unit with the blocker `forbidden_path` when a pending required task's own text names a file-like path (an extension, no trailing `/`) that does not exist in the tree checked and that a glob of `odd.forbidden_paths` matches (`extra_forbidden_paths` applied), unless the task's line says not to touch it ("do not", "don't", "never", "must not" or "without" before the path, a `./` before it not hiding it) or that a person delivers it ("a person commits", "committed by a person", "a person adds"). A token whose first segment looks like a host name (`github.com/org/repo/...`; `.github/...` is still checked) and a `..` path give nothing. A file exists when the revision checked tracks it (`git ls-tree -r` of the revision, `git ls-files` for a working-tree check, `HEAD` of the unit's worktree at the unit start); an untracked or ignored file on disk does not count, and the disk answers only when git cannot be read. The message SHALL name the task, the path, the glob and the fixes: an explicit `odd.forbidden_paths` list on the base branch without that glob (there is no exclusion syntax; not offered for a contract glob), a person's commit of the path on the base branch first, or rewording the task (for example `Do not create <path>`; a person commits it). The same match for an existing file, a directory token, a file the revision tracks one directory deeper (a monorepo) or a mention in the design, proposal or spec deltas SHALL be a warning and SHALL NOT refuse the unit. On the plan side the blocker SHALL apply only to a unit in the phases none, `intake` and `ready`; for a unit already implementing the same text is a warning, so that re-activation, `accept --force` and the CI review are not blocked. At the unit start the blocker is a reject reason (`unit.rejected`, exit 14, before any agent step), and a unit already implementing is not rejected. The offline plan validator of the skill does not run the rule (0.4.40, change 90).

**L4-YOLO-093 A unit whose setup fails in CI stops its plan; a local refusal does not.** When the run that a plan step started for
the current unit of an active plan ends with exit 3 in a CI job (a failed `gates.setup`, an unusable sandbox),
the harness SHALL record `unit.setup_failed{unit, run, detail}` in the plan's ledger, and the next plan step SHALL stop the plan
with `setup_failed` instead of dispatching a run at every trigger until `limits.max_runs`. A local refusal of L4-SEC-041
returns before the refresh, the plan step and any lease: it records no `unit.setup_failed`, and the plan is not stopped.

**L4-YOLO-094 A task deliverable that a test glob covers is a warning at intake.** The intake of a unit (plan check, review, activation, `go` and the CI review; and the start of a unit before it implements, OpenSpec and Kiro) SHALL warn with `test_path` when a pending required task without the human `[test-infra]` tag names a path that a glob of the effective `tdd.test_globs` or `tdd.test_support_globs` (both with their `extra_*` lists) matches and that a scope-exempt glob (`verifier.evidence.scope_exempt`: `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG*` by default) also matches: documentation that a default glob such as `**/fixtures/**` covers, which green may not write and which the test-path freeze of L4-IMP-006 (7) restores after every green step, so that the unit escalates. A file token is matched as written; a directory token (no extension) counts as a file directly in it; a glob token with a file pattern (`docs/client/fixtures/*.json`) is shown as its directory and matched as a file with that pattern, so `**/fixtures/*.csv` does not match it. A path with a source-code extension (`CODE_SUFFIXES` of the diff coverage; test code under `docs/` is red's work) is not documentation and gives nothing. The match SHALL use the matcher the freeze uses (`l4.implementer.guards._matches`), so intake and freeze cannot disagree. The message SHALL name the task, the path, every glob of the two lists that matches (test list first, then the support list, the wording following the count) and the fixes: a person tags the task `[test-infra]` (the freeze then lets it write the path), or the base branch's `tdd.test_globs` and `tdd.test_support_globs` leave the glob (all of them) out. A line that says not to touch the path ("do not", "don't", "never", "must not" or "without" before it), a ticked task, a `../` path and a token whose first segment looks like a host name give nothing, as for forbidden paths. The rule SHALL NOT refuse the unit or change an exit code, in any phase: on the plan side the warning is in `UnitInfo.warnings` in every phase (`l4 yolo check`, `check --worktree` and `go` print it as `warning: test_path: <unit>: …`, exit unchanged), the unit start logs it (`log.warning`, no `unit.rejected`) in the intake phases only, so that a unit already implementing is not warned at every run, and the CI review logs every intake warning of the plan's units, `forbidden_path` and `test_path`, whatever its outcome. The offline plan validator of the skill does not run the rule, and the freeze and the verifier do not exempt scope-exempt paths (that would weaken the tamper protection). A consumer's unit (2026-10-30) delivered `docs/client/fixtures/*.json`, green's write was restored twice and the unit escalated; a person narrowed the globs on the base branch (0.4.44, change 100).

## 13. Memory and lessons

**L4-MEM-001** `lessons.md` format (one section per lesson; the harness is the only writer):

```markdown
<!-- l4:lessons v1 — harness-owned; propose changes via .serena/memories/inbox/ -->
## L-3f9a1c2e · Playwright selectors must use data-testid
- **Scope:** `web/**`, task kinds: ui
- **Source:** verifier finding F-002 (openspec:add-login round 1), 2026-10-03
- **Dedupe key:** e2e-selector-brittle
- **Supersedes:** L-77b0d415
Use `getByTestId` with `data-testid` attributes; text selectors broke on copy changes twice.
```

**L4-MEM-002** Promotion: a lesson is created or reinforced automatically only from (a) a verifier finding whose fix
unit later passed, (b) a guard violation repeated across runs, (c) a human-edited lesson, or (d) a feedback item with `Lesson: yes` addressed in a PASS round (L4-FBK-009).
Agent `lesson_proposals` go to `.serena/memories/inbox/<run-id>/` and are promoted only by a human (`l4 lessons promote`, L4-KG-013) or when they match
an existing dedupe key. Caps: `memory.max_lessons`, `memory.max_bytes`; overflow archives the least recently
reinforced lessons to `_archive/` (ignored by Serena via `ignored_memory_patterns`).

**L4-MEM-002a** Lesson IDs are `L-<first 8 hex of sha256(dedupe key)>`, so lessons created on parallel unit
branches never collide and merge cleanly. Agents see the lessons of the base branch plus those of their own unit
branch; lessons from other open units arrive when those units merge.

**L4-MEM-003** Injection: lessons whose scope matches the task's paths/kinds (plus all unscoped lessons) are
injected through the strongest channel per adapter — Claude `--append-system-prompt`, Kiro agent `resources`,
otherwise the prompt's lessons section — always wrapped in `<l4:data kind="lessons">` (lessons are information, not
instructions, wherever they are placed), and their IDs recorded in the ledger (`lessons.injected`).

**L4-MEM-004** Serena (`memory.serena.enabled`, default on, never required): pinned `serena-agent==1.7.0` (latest release, MIT;
`main` is 2.0.0.dev0 under GPL-3.0-or-later with breaking changes [V, PyPI + repo, 2026-10-03]); started per job as
`serena start-mcp-server --context <claude-code|codex|copilot-cli|ide> --project <worktree> --enable-web-dashboard false
--open-web-dashboard false --mode one-shot --mode no-onboarding` [V, research/05] with a per-job `SERENA_HOME`
(Serena rewrites its config at runtime; `base_modes: [editing]` to avoid interactive questions);
`.serena/project.yml` sets `read_only_memory_patterns: ["(?!inbox/).*"]` and an `initial_prompt` that embeds
`harness/lessons` [V-run, research/05]. MCP client timeouts MUST tolerate cold start (OpenCode ≥ 20 s; Codex
`startup_timeout_sec = 30`). Serena is never required: if it fails to start, the run continues without it (lessons
are still injected through the prompt) and logs a warning; Kiro runs MUST NOT list Serena under
`--require-mcp-startup`. A `kiro-cli` run starts no MCP server at all: its harness agent's `mcpServers` is empty, so
Serena has no context for it and is never started for it; `ide` is OpenCode's context.

**L4-MEM-005** Memory changes are committed separately (`chore(memory): …`, `L4-Phase: lessons`) so they are
visible at the merge gate.

### 13.1 Experience graph (manual)

A person reads the recorded history of one repository's units across units: what keeps failing, what followed each
lesson, and how one unit got where it is. The person can turn a recurring, recorded mistake into a lesson through the
inbox and `l4 lessons promote`. Everything is manual. Nothing reaches an agent, a prompt or a run path unless a person
promotes a lesson. The decisions are in `openspec/changes/experience-graph/design.md` (D1..D10).

**L4-KG-001** Manual only, outside every run path. `l4 kg build`, `l4 kg report`, `l4 kg why` and `l4 kg propose` SHALL run only when a person starts them.
- No module outside `src/l4/kg/` MAY import `l4.kg`. The only link MUST be the handler string in `commands.py`.
- `l4.memory.promote` and `l4.memory.inbox` MUST be imported only by `l4.memory.cli`.
- The `l4 kg` commands MUST NOT call a model, a forge API or the network.
- They MUST NOT run `git fetch`, `git push` or any git command that writes a ref, the index or a tracked file.

**L4-KG-002** Failures are contained, with the existing exit codes. An `l4 kg` command SHALL exit 0 when it finished, with every skipped input counted and shown. It SHALL exit 2 for a
usage error: an unknown id, no repository, a refused `--out`, or a cache root inside the repository. It SHALL exit 1
for an internal error. A failure MUST change no ref, no tracked file, no ledger and no `.l4/` file, and MUST NOT leave
an index that a later read takes as complete.

**L4-KG-003** A derived index under the cache root. The index SHALL be written to `cache_root(environ, repo) / "kg" / <first 16 hex of sha256(resolved repository path)>`,
in a folder with mode 0700, and never inside the repository. It SHALL hold:
- `nodes.jsonl` and `edges.jsonl`: sorted keys, sorted lines, LF, UTF-8;
- `manifest.json` (`l4/kg-manifest@1`): the harness version, the read refs with their shas, the counts, the skips,
  and the sha256 of the two other files.

No file MAY hold the build time. The same refs and the same harness version MUST give byte-identical files. `report`,
`why` and `propose` MUST build the index first when it is missing, incomplete, or built from refs that have moved.

**L4-KG-004** Inputs are committed git objects, never fetched. The build SHALL read with `ls-tree` and `cat-file`, with the existing size caps and symlink rules, from:
- the base ref (`refs/remotes/origin/<forge.base_branch>`, else `HEAD` with a warning): the OpenSpec `changes/<name>/`
  folders, every `changes/archive/<date>-<name>/` folder, and the Kiro `.kiro/specs/<name>/` folders;
- the local unit branches `refs/remotes/origin/<branch_prefix><fw>/<name>`, each with the unit folder and its
  `<name>-fix-<n>` siblings;
- the local lock refs, merged with the branch copy as `merge_ledgers` does;
- the local attempts refs `refs/l4/attempts/<fw>/<name>/<n>`, each one as its own attempt.

The build SHALL read `.l4/ledger/*.jsonl`, `.l4/evidence/round-*/verdict.json`, `memory.lessons_file` and its
`_archive/`.

A corrupt, oversized, unreadable or non-regular input MUST be skipped and counted by reason, and MUST NOT fail the
build. An attempts ref that a `unit.restarted` event names and that is not local MUST be counted as
`attempt_not_local`, and the report MUST print the fetch command. The build MUST NOT fetch.

**L4-KG-005** Typed nodes and edges, each with its source. The graph SHALL have the node and edge types of design D4. Every edge SHALL carry `src`, which is
`<sha10>:<path>#<seq>` for a ledger event or `<sha10>:<path>#/<json pointer>` for a `verdict.json` field.

A lesson SHALL be linked to a finding pattern only through its dedupe key:
- a `LESSON_RULES` key links to the recurrence key of that rule's `finding_title`;
- a `kg-*` key links to the pattern it was proposed from;
- any other lesson has no finding link.

The lesson's `Source` line MUST NOT be parsed for links.

**L4-KG-006** Recurrence across units by normalised text, labelled approximate. Recurrence SHALL be counted in distinct units, never by finding id, with the normaliser of design D5:
- **A finding's key** is the normalised title and the normalised criterion alias without its capability part. The
  second part is empty for a Kiro alias or when there is no criterion.
- **An attempt failure's class** is the first line of its `reason`, cut before the first `:` or ` (`, normalised, and
  cut to 120 characters.

Every report section that uses a key MUST say `approximate`.

**L4-KG-007** Blame from recorded fields only. Each finding, question, stop and attempt failure SHALL get exactly one blame value from design D6: `security`, `spec`,
`environment`, `verifier`, `agent`, or `unknown`. The first matching rule wins. A record that no rule matches MUST be
`unknown`. No blame MAY come from a model or from free text.

**L4-KG-008** Lesson outcomes as recorded, as a heuristic. For each lesson, the report SHALL show:
- its injections (from `prompt.rendered{task, lessons}`), by units, runs and tasks;
- the `task.attempt_failed` of the same run and task after the injection, by failure class;
- the findings in later rounds of the same unit and attempt whose key is the lesson's linked key (L4-KG-005);
- a status: `never injected`, `injected, nothing followed`, or `injected, followed by <n> failure(s)`.

The section MUST state that it shows what followed a lesson, not what the lesson caused.

**L4-KG-009** `l4 kg report` with n on every line. `l4 kg report [--out PATH] [--min-units N]` SHALL write markdown with the sections of design D8, in its order:
coverage, lessons, recurring attempt failures, recurring findings, gate candidates (at least `max(N, 3)` units),
spec-gap hotspots, profiles by role, and stops. N defaults to 2.
- The profiles section MUST count what the records show (runs per profile; for implementer profiles the failed
  attempts, the tasks with a failed attempt and the first-round PASS share) and MUST say that it gives no
  first-attempt pass share, because a task that passes at its first attempt leaves no record.
- Every line that carries a number MUST name its *n*, and an empty section MUST say `none (n = 0)`.
- Lines are sorted by count, then by key.
- The output goes to stdout by default. `--out` inside the repository MUST name a git-ignored path, else the command
  exits 2.

**L4-KG-010** `l4 kg why ID` explains one record. `l4 kg why ID` SHALL accept a unit id, `F-<8 hex>`, `L-<8 hex>`, a run id, or `<unit>#Q-<n>`.
- **For a unit,** it MUST print the timeline of design D9, oldest first. Each line ends with its `src`. The last line
  holds the facts: stops by code, a spec edit since the last stop, and the attempt number. It names
  `l4 status --unit ID` for the next command.
- **For any other id,** it MUST print the 1-hop neighbourhood, with `src` on each edge.
- An unknown id MUST exit 2 with the accepted forms.

**L4-KG-011** Redacted, local and per repository. Every text field SHALL pass `redact_text` and then `scrub_for_commit` before it enters the index, a report, `why`
output, or a proposal. The index and reports MUST stay on the person's machine. No command MAY read the index of
another repository, or combine repositories.

**L4-KG-012** `l4 kg propose` writes drafts for a person, never lessons. `l4 kg propose [--min-units N] [--dry-run]` SHALL write, for each pattern of design D10 that no lesson or
`LESSON_RULES` rule covers yet, `.serena/memories/inbox/kg-<YYYY-MM-DD>/<L-id>.md` and `<L-id>.evidence.md`.
- **The draft** is a lessons v1 file with one section, where the id is `lesson_id(dedupe key)`. Its body ends with a
  `TODO(person):` line.
- **Allowed text:** a draft MAY quote only failure classes, deterministic finding titles, gate names, guard rule names
  and globs. It MUST NOT quote a judge finding, a question, an answer or an agent's output.
- **What it must not touch:** the command MUST NOT write `lessons.md`, stage, or commit.
- **Ignore warning:** it MUST warn when git does not ignore the inbox folder.

**L4-KG-013** `l4 lessons promote ID` (builds L4-MEM-002's human promotion). `l4 lessons promote ID [--from DIR] [--yes] [--no-commit]` SHALL move one inbox proposal into `memory.lessons_file`
through `apply_candidates`, with origin `human_edit`. An existing dedupe key MUST be reinforced. The caps MUST hold.

It MUST refuse with exit 2, writing nothing, when any of these is true:
- `memory.enabled` is false;
- the proposal is not exactly one valid v1 section, or its id is not `lesson_id(dedupe key)`, or a glob is invalid;
- the proposal still has a `TODO(person):` line, or an empty body;
- HEAD is detached or on a branch under `forge.branch_prefix`;
- anything is staged;
- the lessons file in the work tree differs from HEAD, or has parse problems;
- there is no terminal and no `--yes`.

It MUST print the lesson and its scope before it writes. Unless `--no-commit` is given, it MUST commit only the
lessons paths as `chore(memory): lesson <id> promoted [skip ci]`, with the person's git identity and no `L4-*`
trailer, and then delete the proposal and its evidence file.

**L4-KG-014** Nothing changes for a repository that does not use it. This change SHALL add no configuration key, no doctor check, no ledger event, no lifecycle edge, no prompt change and
no CI template change. Every configuration that validates today MUST still validate. `l4 lessons list` and
`l4 lessons lint` MUST keep their output. Existing tests MUST keep their assertions. Only the command tables of the
dispatch tests MAY gain rows.
