## 18. Security requirements

**L4-SEC-001** Agent processes MUST receive an allow-listed environment: their own credentials, `PATH`, `HOME`,
locale, proxy variables, `L4_RESULT_PATH`; **never** `L4_FORGE_TOKEN`, trigger tokens, App tokens, or other profiles'
credentials. Gate commands (`setup`, `build`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `e2e`, `extra`) execute code the agent wrote
and MUST receive the same kind of allow-listed environment (no harness or LLM credentials at all); when the harness runs
in CI they also receive the CI's identity variables of L4-SEC-040, which agents never do. Adapter-set variables
are part of the allow-list: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_*`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`,
`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES`. `XDG_DATA_HOME` MUST NOT be redirected for OpenCode (credentials live in
`~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`) [V, spikes/02]. Both environments carry `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, so a Python
import by an agent or a gate leaves no `__pycache__` in the worktree (a stray one under `.l4/` was a protected-path
violation).
The harness's own CI/CD secrets (`L4_FORGE_TOKEN`, a judge API key such as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) MUST also be unreachable
for **every other CI job of the project** (HB-2): the hand-off commit runs the project's own `test` job, which executes
code an agent wrote. On GitLab they are therefore CI/CD variables scoped to the environment `l4` (never `protected`: the
harness job also runs on `l4/**` branches, and protecting would expose them to every job on those branches), and the CI
template's `l4` job declares `environment: {name: l4, action: prepare}`; `scripts/forge/gitlab_bot_token.py` and
`scripts/forge/gitlab_ci_var_from_mintkey.py` take `--environment-scope` (default `l4`). Doctor has no check of a
variable's scope: GitLab's variables API returns the value together with `environment_scope`, and a check MUST NOT read
values [I, from GitLab's API documentation; not tested live]. Whether the project's other jobs really cannot see the
variable is proven by a presence-only probe job (`[ -n "$L4_FORGE_TOKEN" ]`), not by doctor. On GitHub the same holds
for the secrets of the environment `ci.github_environment`: only a job that names the environment receives them, and
the generated `l4` job is the only one that does (L4-PRV-027).

**L4-SEC-002** Repo-supplied (and user-level) agent configuration MUST NOT take effect. Per adapter: claude
subscription implementer: `--setting-sources "" --disable-slash-commands` + `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` +
`--strict-mcp-config` + protected paths (agents cannot add hooks or MCP servers), subscription judge and reader:
`--safe-mode`; claude api_key: `--bare`; Codex `--ignore-user-config --ignore-rules -c project_doc_max_bytes=0` plus doctor
ENV-009 (`$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md` is injected regardless [V]); OpenCode: `--pure` **and** an empty `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` **and** `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG`,
`_CLAUDE_CODE` and `_EXTERNAL_SKILLS` **and** an explicit `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (`--pure` alone loaded user config
and MCP servers [V]); Kiro an explicit harness agent [V flags, research/02]. Every CLI leaked user configuration under
the former flag set [V for all three, spikes/01–03: Claude without `--safe-mode` ran user SessionStart hooks that
injected text; OpenCode `--pure` loaded the user's `opencode.jsonc`, started Serena, and a hello wrote a file; Codex
injected `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md` despite `--ignore-user-config --ignore-rules`]. Whether `--safe-mode` also suppresses
**project** `.claude/settings.json` hooks is moot for the implementer (it runs with no settings source, and the
sandbox masks `<wt>/.claude`: HB-X1 [V live]); the protected-path guard (L4-IMP-006) covers the rest. A profile may opt in to repo config with `options.allow_repo_config: true`.
Repository **guidance files** (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.agents/**`, `.kiro/steering/**`,
`.opencode/**`, `opencode.jsonc`, and the folders the sandbox masks: `.hermes/**`, `.kiro/hooks/**`, `.kiro/prompts/**`,
`.kiro/skills/**`) are loaded by the CLIs as instructions, outside the `<l4:data>` blocks. Under L4 no
adapter loads them (table in §8.3, "Repository guidance under L4"). Those written by members are trusted like spec

`.opencode/**`, `opencode.jsonc`) are loaded by the CLIs as instructions, outside the `<l4:data>` blocks. Under L4 no
adapter loads them (table in §8.3, "Repository guidance under L4"); the steering that applies reaches the implementer as data, read by the harness (L4-KSP-010). Those written by members are trusted like spec
files (L4-SEC-003); those written by an agent step are protected paths (L4-SEC-004). **Residual:** a CLI that is
not *loading* a file can still *read* it with its file tools (Codex may open `AGENTS.md`): that is allowed, the file is
member-written and trusted like the specs, and it is not a way for an agent to change it (L4-SEC-004).
A judge-mode call (a call with no file tools: the verifier judges, the clarifier, the S1 stand-in, the audit) MUST
start in an empty directory below the step's private directory, so that no repository guidance is loaded into the
independent check; the sandbox starts the process in that directory (L4-SEC-005). A Codex judge also runs with
`-c project_doc_max_bytes=0`, so a guidance file found above that directory is not injected either; what it loads of
its own accord is the four OpenAI vendor system skills of `~/.codex/skills/.system` (the CLI's own, not the
repository's) [V live, HB-X1].

**L4-SEC-003** Text from untrusted sources (issue/PR comments by non-members, external URLs) MUST NOT enter prompts.
Spec files and `questions.md` are trusted only as far as their pushers are (members only, L4-CI-003); answers and quotes
enter prompts as `<l4:data>` (L4-CLR-006).

**L4-SEC-004** Protected paths (contract list, which includes the repository guidance files of L4-SEC-002, every
`.l4/` directory at any depth and the spec root `openspec/**` and `.kiro/specs/**` (HB-3: the archived specs are the
verifier's pass-to-pass baseline, a sibling or archived change is another unit's contract), + `odd.forbidden_paths`) changed by an agent MUST be reverted; only the run's own ledger
is the harness's to append to (L4-IMP-006), and a ledger of another unit, which would fold into that unit's state once
the branch is merged, is a protected path like the unit's own. The contract list matches in any case (`Agents.md` and
`.Claude/settings.json` are what a CLI opens as `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/settings.json` on a case-insensitive file
system); `odd.forbidden_paths` keep their case. Code an agent wrote and a gate runs (a test, or production code the
tests import) is the agent's too: a protected path it changes at any depth (`src/pkg/CLAUDE.md`, a migration) MUST be
put back after the gate, with `guard.violation{phase: gate}`, before anything is committed. Every directory that the
sandbox covers with a tmpfs (L4-SEC-005, `sandbox.base.GUIDANCE_DIRS`, mirrored in `scripts/runner/sandbox-probe.sh`) is on
the contract list, `.hermes/**`, `.kiro/hooks/**`, `.kiro/prompts/**` and `.kiro/skills/**` included, and a test fails
when the two lists differ (SCN-SEC-50 to SCN-SEC-53). A `.gitattributes` file at any depth is on the contract list, and
the root one is listed literally beside the root guidance files, so an edited `.gitignore` cannot hide it: git attributes
decide what a diff shows, and `*.py -diff` made the judge's diff and step 1's `-U0` scans read `Binary files a/x.py and
b/x.py differ` for every Python change, an added `# noqa` included (a `diff=` driver or `working-tree-encoding` changes the
bytes they read too). [V, 2026-10-31: reproduced with the verifier's own diff arguments, `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`
and `-U0`.] A person's `.gitattributes` on the base branch or on the unit branch is the owner's choice and is not read
differently. Changed
by a human on the unit branch, they are allowed but the PR body MUST list them. Authorship is per commit: a protected
path counts as changed by a human only when every commit of the unit's range that touches it is not the harness's
(author = the bot identity and a non-empty `L4-Run` trailer); a path a harness commit touched too stays a violation.
Listed paths go to `verification.md` ("Protected paths changed by humans"), which the PR body links, and to the step-1
note. The same attribution lets a skip marker or a test deletion that only people's commits made, and a file that
only they changed (the scope check), be listed instead of blocked or held. Labels that change harness behaviour
(`l4:resume`) are honoured only when set by a member with at least Developer/Write access, as the forge's own record of
who set them says (a commit's author is text anyone can write, so no commit is such a signal), and never when set by the
harness's own user (L4-CI-004).

**L4-SEC-005 Sandbox.** An environment allow-list alone does not contain code running as the same OS user: it can read
`/proc/<ancestor pid>/environ`, `.git/config`, credential files and the runner's files. The harness therefore runs two
kinds of sandbox (bubblewrap with `--unshare-pid --proc /proc`, a container, or a separate OS user — `sandbox.mode`):
- **agent sandbox** (one per agent run): the worktree read-write; the shared `.git` directory **read-only**; a private
  writable temp dir that holds `$L4_RESULT_PATH`; **only that profile's** `sandbox.credential_paths` bind-mounted
  read-write (logins, OAuth refresh and session stores for resume, L4-IMP-010); that profile's credential env vars; no
  other profile's credentials, no forge/trigger/App secrets; network allowed (LLM APIs);
- **gate sandbox** (every gate command, test, build, `serve`, scanner run on the worktree): the worktree read-write,
  `.git` read-only, an **empty home** (L4-SEC-030: a tmpfs over the real home, the tool paths of L4-SEC-032 read-only), the runner cache
  hidden (L4-SEC-031), the environment read-only unless the command is `gates.setup` (L4-SEC-035), no credential paths
  and no credential env vars at all; network allowed unless
  `gates.network: none`.
Both kinds (HB-X1; the gate runs agent-written code) cover, after every bind, each **existing** one of `.claude`,
`.agents`, `.codex`, `.opencode`, `.hermes`, `.kiro/steering`, `.kiro/agents`, `.kiro/settings`, `.kiro/hooks`,
`.kiro/prompts` and `.kiro/skills` of the worktree with a tmpfs: no switch of Codex removes the repository skill roots, and these are
contract-protected paths an agent step has no use for. A missing path is skipped (bwrap cannot create a mount point under
a read-only root, and would create the directory in the real worktree), and so is a symlink (bwrap resolves it:
`.claude -> /etc` would cover `/etc`; residual: a guidance directory committed as a symlink to another directory of
the repository is not covered, so Codex loads its skills; member-written, L4-SEC-003). `.kiro` as a whole is never covered (`.kiro/specs/**` is the spec root) and
`.serena` is not (Serena reads its project file and memories). The masks come after every bind, not just the
worktree's: a later bind of a path at or above the worktree (a `sandbox.caches` path such as `$L4_CACHE/worktrees`
is valid) would put the host directories back [V live: a parent bound after the mask ran the repo's hook]. The mask
is per mount namespace: the host worktree is unchanged. Mirrored in `scripts/runner/sandbox-probe.sh` (planted `.claude`/`.agents` canary).
`mode: user` (a separate OS user) cannot separate two profiles' logins inside one user's home: with more than one
profile that has `credential_paths`, it REQUIRES `sandbox.user_per_profile` (one OS user per profile), otherwise doctor
fails. Both sandbox kinds get the per-unit cache mounts of `sandbox.caches` (keyed by the repository key, L4-SEC-034, read-only except for `gates.setup`, with a
private scratch cache for every step, L4-SEC-039) with their environment variables (per-unit
caches so that agent-written code cannot poison another unit's cache). A new unit's `uv` cache is a **copy** of the
project's seed (`$L4_CACHE/seed/<hash of the origin URL without credentials>/uv`): the seed is filled by `gates.setup`,
unchanged, on a detached scratch checkout of the base branch's head, under a lock and only when the base's `uv.lock` or
the setup commands changed; it is copied, never shared, into a unit cache that is new, and is never mounted into a sandbox
that runs an agent or agent-written code. A failed fill is `cache.seed_failed` and the unit downloads as before.
`UV_LINK_MODE=copy` is set when a `uv` cache is mounted. `HOME` inside a sandbox is a tmpfs over the real home
holding only the mounts above, and the runner cache is a tmpfs too (L4-SEC-030, L4-SEC-031). `mode: auto` picks `bwrap` if available, then `container`, then `user`; `none` is refused unless
`sandbox.allow_none: true`, which doctor reports as an accepted risk on every run.
An agent run can write its own profile's credential paths, and some host-side calls of `l4 probe` read them outside
the sandbox. So each such call ignores what an agent could have planted there: the Claude Code hello runs with
`--safe-mode`, the Codex hello with `--ignore-user-config --ignore-rules`, and OpenCode's `auth` step (v1 and v2) and
hello with an empty config directory and the disable switches (the v1 hello also with `--pure`). Known gap, assessed
2026-10-24 in the 0.4.28 review: the OpenCode hello still uses the real `~/.cache/opencode` and
`~/.local/share/opencode`, which an OpenCode agent run can write, and whether a tool-less hello loads code from them
is not recorded [U]. Running the hello inside the agent sandbox closes it when a release touches the probe.
**Container-daemon sockets (HB-1).** A read-only bind does not stop `connect()` on a unix socket: with
`--ro-bind / /` alone, a runner user in group `docker` reached `/var/run/docker.sock` from inside the sandbox, with or
without `--unshare-net` (root on the host through `docker run -v /:/host`) [V, live on `l4-runner`, 2026-10-05].
Both sandbox kinds MUST therefore cover `/run` with a tmpfs (and `/var/run` when it is not a symlink into `/run`, or the
directory it links to otherwise), and put back read-only only the file `/etc/resolv.conf` points to when that file is
in `/run` (Ubuntu: `/run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf`), so name resolution keeps working; `/run/user/<uid>` (dbus,
podman, gpg sockets) is never put back. Doctor `SANDBOX-002` runs a probe with the real argv in both network modes and
fails (exit 3) when a daemon socket is reachable. Residual, stated in the docs: a daemon socket outside `/run` (for
example under the runner's home) stays reachable, abstract unix sockets (dbus, X11) are isolated only by `--unshare-net`,
which gates get with `gates.network: none` and agent sandboxes (network on) do not, and removing the runner user from
the `docker` group stays a human decision (`prereqs.sh` PRQ-19 warns).
Doctor `SANDBOX-001` probes both
kinds: from the gate sandbox no credential path of any profile, no ancestor environment and no harness secret is
readable; from profile A's agent sandbox no credential path of profile B is readable. Residual risk, stated in the
docs: code an agent runs inside its own sandbox can read that agent's own credential, so profiles SHOULD use
dedicated logins/keys with provider-side spend limits. OpenCode `external_directory` and Claude path rules are
heuristics, not confinement [V, spikes/01, spikes/02]. The agent CLIs work inside bubblewrap on the reference runner
(bubblewrap 0.6.1, as the runner user): under `bwrap --ro-bind / / --dev /dev --proc /proc --tmpfs /tmp --unshare-pid
--unshare-ipc --share-net --die-with-parent` with only the worktree and the CLI's own state dirs writable, claude
(`--permission-mode acceptEdits`, without `--safe-mode` or `env -i`), codex (with its own sandbox nested inside bwrap)
and opencode (`opencode/big-pickle`) were each asked to implement a function and run `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` after
a `uv sync` outside the sandbox; each exited 0, edited the code so that the tests, re-run by the probe afterwards,
passed, and changed no test file [V, runner/sandbox-probe-2026-10-03.txt; whether the agent itself ran the gate inside
the sandbox is not recorded, I]. That probe profile still left `/` readable, so the production agent profile
MUST also hide the other profiles' credential paths (e.g. a tmpfs over each) as required above. Whether browsers
(Playwright/Chromium) and container-backed `serve` commands work inside bubblewrap is [U] and is settled by the spikes
of delivery change 0 (§21) before the sandbox is declared GA.

**L4-SEC-006 Harness-side tools never execute repository-controlled code.** Everything the harness itself runs outside
a sandbox on an agent-controlled tree MUST be hardened:
- the OpenSpec CLI comes from the harness-owned prefix (L4-OSP-001), never `npx` or the worktree's `node_modules`;
- every harness git invocation uses `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c protocol.ext.allow=never`,
  and commits use `--no-verify`; the shared `.git/config` is hashed before each agent/gate step and any change is
  reverted and logged (`guard.git_config`);
- test reports are parsed with hardened parsers (XML without external entities — e.g. `defusedxml` — and size limits;
  JSON/YAML safe loaders only);
- scanners (gitleaks, semgrep) and any other third-party tool run in the gate sandbox with harness-owned configuration.

**L4-SEC-007 Outgoing commits are scanned for secrets before every push (HB-4).** Before every push of a unit branch
the harness MUST read the lines added by the commits the forge does not have yet (`git log -p` over `HEAD` minus the
remote unit branch and the remote base branch, so a secret an earlier commit added and a later one removed is still
found, and what was merged in from the base is not ours) with the redactor of L4-OBS-002: the values of the configured
secrets (`value:<NAME>`) and the token shapes (`anthropic-key`, `gitlab-pat`, `jwt`, `private-key`, ...). It needs no
external scanner. On a hit nothing is pushed, one `guard.secret {path, kind}` is recorded per path and kind (never the
value, not even in redacted form), `breaker.tripped{reason: secret_in_push}` is recorded, and the unit **halts** with exit
13 and `exit_reason` naming the paths: through the `breaker_or_budget` edge in `implementing` and `fixing`; in any other
phase the phase is unchanged and only the exit code says halted. The run's final ledger is not pushed either, because it
would carry the same commits, so the halt is visible in the run's console and `outcome.json`, not on the forge. There is
no allow-list: a fixture that must look like a key is written so that the shapes do not match, and an implementer step
that writes one loses its attempt before this scan is reached (L4-SEC-008). This scan is in addition to
the gitleaks step of verifier step 1 (L4-VER-002), which runs later and on the net diff. Residual: only the known token
shapes and the configured values are found; the harness's own pushes of the ledger lock ref (redacted ledger) and the
archive branch (files moved by the harness) are not scanned.

**L4-SEC-008 An implementer step's changes are read for secrets before any gate or commit.** A step that writes a
token shape into a test fixture should lose its attempt, not halt the unit at the push with no advice. After an
implementer step (red, green or single) returns and the protected paths are put back (`agent_step` in `implementer/tdd.py`), the harness
MUST read the lines that the worktree adds to `HEAD` with the redactor of L4-OBS-002, as L4-SEC-007 does for outgoing
commits (`secretscan.worktree_secrets`). These are the added lines of a tracked file and every line of a new file,
never the run's ledger. On a hit the attempt fails before any gate runs, and its changes are discarded. One
`guard.secret {path, kind, task, phase, attempt}` is recorded per path and kind, never with the value, and
`breaker.tripped` is not. The failure, which the next attempt's prompt carries, is `the change holds text shaped like a
secret: <path> (<kind>), …. Nothing of this attempt is kept. Never write a secret value. A test that needs a value
shaped like a token builds it at run time from parts, with the prefix split (for example "mk_" + "agent_" + "A" * 24),
so that no file holds the whole shape: the harness refuses to push one.` The attempt counts as any failed attempt does
(L4-IMP-017 escalation, the attempt limits). The contract template says the same rule up front. The push scan of
L4-SEC-007 stays: it is the last net for what the step check does not see (a gate or a harness step that writes a file).
Residual: a deleted file, a symlink, a binary file and a new file over 2,000,000 bytes add nothing to the step check.

**L4-SEC-020 Harness file operations in a worktree never follow a link.** After agent-written code has run in a worktree
(an agent step or a gate), every read, write and removal that the harness makes there MUST refuse a path with a symbolic
link at any component below the worktree root, and MUST never follow one: the variant writes and restores of the
zero-value runs and of the run at the red commit's code, their report restores, the removal of earlier reports, the
bytecode removal, the production guard, the red scope and the audit (`l4.fsutil`: `read_inside`, `write_inside`,
`unlink_inside`, `linked_component`, `remove_link`). The check is made at the moment of the operation, relative to
directory descriptors opened without following links (`O_NOFOLLOW`), never as a check before the gate. A file is written
as a new file in its own directory and renamed over its name, so a symbolic link, a hard link or a FIFO in its place
neither receives the bytes nor blocks the harness. A link at the end of a path to be removed is removed itself. A file
that the harness varies is taken by its real path inside the worktree, resolved before the gate: a link the repository
commits (`src/app -> ../lib/app`) keeps working, and a target whose real path is outside the worktree or under the test
globs is not varied. `restore_to_base` removes a link at or above its path, checks a path that was a directory at the
base out as that whole directory, and runs `git rm -r --cached` for a path that is new, so a directory a link replaced
cannot make a guard raise. Before the commit of every red, green and fix-chore attempt the harness MUST refuse a symbolic
link that differs from the step base and points outside the worktree (an absolute target, or one that climbs above the
root), unless the base holds the same link: `guard.violation{phase, rule: "link outside worktree", path, action:
refused, target}`, the attempt is discarded and fails with a reason that names each link. A link that stays inside the
worktree is not refused (SCN-SEC-40 to SCN-SEC-45, SCN-SEC-48, SCN-SEC-55, SCN-SEC-56). Known gap, assessed
2026-10-24 in `openspec/changes/replay-restore-confined/design.md` D4: the remaining `git checkout <rev> -- <path>`
restores rely on git, which replaces a linked folder instead of writing through it, and on the sandbox ending every
process of a run, so no agent can swap a link in during the restore. The Serena project file
(`.serena/project.yml`) is read and removed by name. Both convert to the descriptor-confined restore when a release
touches them.

**L4-SEC-021 A planted link is removed, recorded and halts the unit; nothing is written through it.** A symbolic link
found on the path of an operation of L4-SEC-020 after a gate, at or above a production path in red's production guard,
or on a gate's report path MUST be removed itself and recorded as `guard.violation{phase: gate, rule: "planted link",
path, action: removed, where, target, points_to}`, and the write MUST be made once more into a real directory. A write
that still fails, or whose sha256 read-back differs, is recorded as `rule: "restore failed"`. No exception leaves a
restore. A recorded `planted link` halts the unit at once, as a secret in a push does (L4-SEC-007): the attempt's changes
are discarded, `PlantedLink` ends the step (never out of a `finally`), `breaker.tripped{reason: "planted_link", task,
links: [{path, points_to, where}]}` is recorded and the unit takes the halted edge with the code `planted_link` and a
detail that begins `task <k>: a gate run put a symbolic link at <paths>`; the fix loop halts the same way. A recorded
`restore failed` fails the attempt before its commit, with a reason that names the paths, and the run goes on to the next
attempt. In the verifier a recorded refusal is a blocker (`a gate run planted a symbolic link in the worktree`, or `could
not restore a file after a gate run`) and the round ends FAIL (SCN-SEC-41, SCN-SEC-46, SCN-SEC-47, SCN-SEC-49,
SCN-SEC-54).

**L4-SEC-030 The real home is hidden in both sandbox kinds.** Every bwrap sandbox, agent and gate, MUST cover the runner
user's real `$HOME` with a tmpfs right after the base flags (`--ro-bind / /`, `--dev`, `--proc`, `--tmpfs /tmp`, the
`/run` masks, the namespaces) and bind back, after it, only what L4-SEC-005, L4-SEC-031 and L4-SEC-032 name. `HOME` in
the child environment keeps its path (the CLIs find their logins at `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, and shims and virtual
environments carry absolute paths into the home): inside, it is an empty writable tmpfs plus those binds. A `$HOME` that
is `/`, not absolute or not an existing directory MUST make the sandbox unavailable (exit 3): the harness then does not
know where the user's files are. Any other file of the home, a git, SSH, gh, docker or netrc credential included, MUST
NOT be readable (sandbox-security-2). The argv order of both kinds is: the base flags; `--tmpfs <home>`; `--tmpfs
<cache root>` (L4-SEC-031); the tool paths and, for a setup gate, the setup paths, `--ro-bind` each (L4-SEC-032,
L4-SEC-033); the masks over every other adapter's login and over the runner's scratch directories; the agent's own
login paths read-write; the worktree and the step's temp directory read-write; the cache mounts; the main repository's
`.git` read-only; the read-only environment directories and the empty tool caches of a gate that builds nothing
(L4-SEC-035); the repository guidance masks (HB-X1) last. `mode: user` and `mode: container` are not built (M2) and
MUST meet this requirement when they are. Mirrored in `scripts/runner/sandbox-probe.sh` and `ci-probe-m15.sh`
(`root:DIR` and `tool:DIR` arguments), which tests/unit/sandbox/test_probe_parity.py diffs against the Python.

**L4-SEC-031 The runner cache is hidden in both sandbox kinds.** Every bwrap sandbox MUST cover the runner cache
`$L4_CACHE` (L4-CFG-005) with a tmpfs, after the home's and before any bind, when it exists, is not `/` and lies outside
`$HOME` (inside the home it is covered already), so that under it only the step's own worktree, private temp directory
and cache mounts are visible. Other units' and projects' step directories, worktrees, unpublished run files, the seed,
the probe's key directory and the lock files MUST NOT be visible (sandbox-security-4).

**L4-SEC-032 Tools under a hidden root stay usable, read-only.** After the tmpfs of L4-SEC-030 and L4-SEC-031 the sandbox
MUST bind read-only each existing tool path under the home or the runner cache, and the credential masks MUST come
after them, so no tool bind re-exposes a login. `l4.sandbox.home.tool_paths` derives them, in this order, dropping a
duplicate, a path inside an earlier one, a path inside the worktree or the main checkout, and a path that is or holds the
home: (1) each entry of the sandbox's PATH and, for a symlink entry, its resolved path; (2) the `node_modules` of an
entry ending in `node_modules/.bin`; (3) for each symlink directly inside an entry whose target is a file under a hidden
root outside that entry, the target file itself (Claude's native install is one file), or its package directory when it
lies in a `node_modules` (the directory below the innermost `node_modules`, two levels for an `@scope`): never the
directory around a file and never the project around a `node_modules`; (4) `$L4_HOME`; (5) uv's Python
and tool directories (`$UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `$UV_TOOL_DIR`, else under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share`), never
`~/.local/share/uv` as a whole (uv keeps `credentials/` there); (6) the corepack home (`$COREPACK_HOME`, else
`~/.cache/node/corepack`); (7) the harness's own gate plugin directories (the evidence plugins reach every test gate
through `PYTHONPATH`; a harness run by `uvx` lives in the uv cache); (8) `~/.serena`, agent kind only; (9)
`sandbox.tool_paths`. Every path derived by (1) to (8) is vetted: one that is, holds or lies inside a login path
of any adapter or a well-known secret location of the home (`~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.docker`, `~/.kube`,
`~/.npmrc`, `~/.pypirc`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.cargo/credentials*`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.claude*`,
`~/.codex`, `~/.gnupg`, cloud CLI configs) is not bound and is reported as skipped. A tool under the home that none of these
reaches, or that needs the files beside its target, fails inside the sandbox ("command not found"): the fix is a
`sandbox.tool_paths` entry.

**L4-SEC-033 Configured home paths are checked at load.** `sandbox.tool_paths` (both kinds) and `sandbox.setup_paths`
(only the gate sandbox of a `gates.setup` command, for a registry login such as `~/.npmrc` or `~/.netrc`) are lists of
`~/`-relative or absolute paths, bound read-only when they exist. An entry that is `/` or `~`, contains the runner cache,
or equals, contains or lies inside any adapter's credential path, built-in or configured, MUST be a configuration error
(exit 2) that names the key and never the path; what needs the environment (the runner cache, an absolute entry that
reaches a login once `~` is expanded) is checked where the paths are expanded and ends the run with exit 2 the same way.
`setup_paths` hands a registry login to setup code an agent can influence (a build backend hook, a `postinstall` script):
that is the owner's accepted risk of keeping the key, and doctor `SANDBOX-004` warns whenever it is set.

**L4-SEC-034 Every per-unit directory carries the repository key.** Per-unit directories under `$L4_CACHE` MUST include the
repository key of L4-WTR-001 (sandbox-security-1): `units/<key>/<fw>/<name>` for the step temp directories (`agent-tmp`,
`gate-tmp`), `excludes`, the agents' raw streams and the merge-base checkout; `pending-unpublished/<key>/<fw>/<name>`;
and `{unit}` in `sandbox.caches` is `<key>/<fw>/<name>`, so every existing configuration is keyed with no edit. The
harness MUST NOT write or remove anything of the earlier layout (`units/<fw>/<name>`, `pending-unpublished/<fw>/<name>`),
except that it moves a run file of it that belongs to this repository to the keyed directory and publishes it as usual (it
records this repository's key in `run.started`, or, written before 0.4.18, a CI link whose project path is the path of
`origin`; the commits a file names prove nothing, every clone has them); any other run file stays and is named in one warning per run. A new keyed uv cache is new and gets
the project's seed copy.

**L4-SEC-035 Gates that do not build the environment cannot change it.** The gate sandbox of any command other than
`gates.setup` MUST bind read-only each existing environment directory of the tree it runs in (`.venv` at the root and
every `node_modules` that git tracks no file in), after the cache and git binds and before the guidance masks; each
`node_modules/.cache`, `node_modules/.vite`, `node_modules/.vite-temp` and `node_modules/.vitest-cache` MUST be empty at
the start of every such gate (a tmpfs under bwrap, and the harness empties them before each gate in every mode, in the
workbench's gates, in the post-merge check of L4-YOLO-009 and in the gate dry run alike, each before it builds the
gate's sandbox: vite
loads pre-bundled modules from `.vite/deps`, and Vite 5 and later bundle a TypeScript config into `.vite-temp` and
tolerate only `EACCES` there [V, Vitest 5.0.5 / Vite 6.4: ENOENT mkdir under a read-only node_modules]; Vitest 5's
module cache is `.vitest-cache`, on by default and read back in later runs [V, Vitest 5.0.5: one file per run fails at
file level with `mkdir` `.vitest-cache` under a read-only node_modules]). Setup gates
and agent sandboxes keep them writable. A tool that writes elsewhere inside `node_modules` in a test gate fails read-only
and belongs in `gates.setup`.

**L4-SEC-036 An environment an agent step or a gate changed is rebuilt (implementer-2).** No guard looks at `.venv` or
`node_modules`, `git clean` keeps them, and `uv sync --frozen` leaves a `.pth` or `sitecustomize.py` that no installed
distribution owns [V, uv 0.10.0], so a file planted there decides every later gate. After each passing `gates.setup`
command the harness MUST record, in memory, a manifest of the tree's environment directories: the `lstat` of every entry
(kind, mode, size, mtime, ctime, inode, link target; a directory by kind, mode and inode only, because its own times move with
every child and with the tool-cache reset before each gate) without following symlinks, the tool caches left out. After every
agent step and every other gate it MUST compare the environment with the manifest; a directory that differs, is new or has
no manifest MUST be removed, so that the next `gates.setup` builds it again, and the worktree's `setup_at` is cleared. It
records one `env.rebuilt` (`{tree, dirs, phase, added, changed, removed, reason: changed|created|unverified, declared,
planted_more}`, counts for the three lists) and, for each added or changed path that no install explains, one
`guard.violation` (`rule: "environment"`, `action: "removed"`, `phase`), at most 20 together with the notices (the rest is
`planted_more`). A path is explained by an install when a lock file (`uv.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Pipfile.lock`,
`package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`) changed in the same
step (`declared`) and, under `.venv`, a `RECORD` of the current environment lists it with a matching sha256. **A dependency
upgrade without a lock-file change** (owner decision Q4) is reported as a non-failing `guard.notice` (`rule:
"environment"`) instead of a violation when a dependency manifest changed in the same step: a `requirements*.txt` in any
way, a `package.json` in `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`,
`bundleDependencies`, `overrides` or `resolutions`, a `pyproject.toml` in `[project] dependencies` or
`optional-dependencies`, `[dependency-groups]` or `[tool.uv]` (compared with HEAD, parsed); a Python startup hook
(`*.pth`, `sitecustomize.py`, `usercustomize.py`, `*.pyc`) stays a violation unless a `RECORD` lists it and the install
was declared by a lock file. The rebuild happens in every case. The classification only decides how a removal is
reported; the removal is the protection. A project with no `gates.setup` never gets a manifest: every environment a step
or gate leaves is removed (`created`), so a test command that builds its own environment builds it in every gate.

**L4-SEC-037 A workbench's gates run on an environment it built.** The first `gates.setup` command a workbench runs in a
tree MUST first remove that tree's environment directories when the workbench holds no manifest for it
(`env.rebuilt{reason: "unverified"}`), so the verifier, a fix unit and any workbench built after a fallback never run
gates on an environment an earlier step left. A run's first setup in a new worktree removes nothing.

**L4-SEC-038 Doctor SANDBOX-003 proves the home and the runner cache are hidden.** Doctor `SANDBOX-003` MUST plant
canaries (a file in `$HOME` outside every credential path, a credential file in another unit's step directory, a lock
file, and a secret beside each of two symlinked tools in a PATH directory of its own, one a shim into a project's
`node_modules`; each holding a random marker only) and run them through the real gate and agent argv; a readable canary MUST fail
the check (exit 3) naming the path and the kind, never the content, and the canaries and the probe directory MUST be
removed. It is skipped when bwrap is absent or `sandbox.mode` is not `auto` or `bwrap`.

**L4-SEC-039 Package caches are read-only except for setup, and the verifier has its own.** A cache an agent step or a
gate could write came back in every environment rebuilt from it: `zz_marker.pth` in `UV_CACHE_DIR/archive-v0/<id>/` survives
`rm -rf .venv; uv sync --frozen` into site-packages [V, real uv], and the manifest of L4-SEC-036 trusts what setup built.
Every agent sandbox and every gate sandbox except that of a `gates.setup` command (and the uv seed's fill) MUST therefore
mount the per-unit package caches of `sandbox.caches` (`uv`, `pip`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `go`, `gobuild`) read-only, and the
step MUST work in a private scratch cache: the cache variable (`UV_CACHE_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`,
`pnpm_config_store_dir`, ...) names a directory under the step's private temp directory, empty at the start of the step and
of every gate and removed at the end, so that `uv add`, `npm install` and `pnpm add` still work. Removing a scratch cache
first makes its read-only directories writable, because Go extracts every module it downloads with 0o555 directories and
0o444 files, which a plain removal leaves behind (the next step's `mkdir` of the scratch then fails with
`FileExistsError`), and makes a directory it cannot open or list readable and removes it whole (a test suite can leave
a directory with mode 0o000 in the temp directory); it changes modes only inside the removed tree and never through a
symlink, so that a link an agent planted cannot point the change of a mode
at a file outside the scratch, and the next step's scratch is empty. A removal that still fails stops the run at the
start of a step, naming the path, and is a warning at the end of a step or a gate. Only `gates.setup` writes
the shared cache. One exception, gates only: `GOMODCACHE` is read where it is, because Go's module cache is read-only by
design and a test gate with `gates.network: none` has no other source (an agent gets a scratch for it too). The
verifier's workbench (L4-VER-010) MUST build from caches of its own, at the same configured paths with the namespace
`verify` after the repository key (`units/<key>/verify/<fw>/<name>/...`), emptied at the start of each verification round
and shared by every workbench of the round; its first `gates.setup` rebuilds the environment from them (L4-SEC-037), and
the manifest baseline of the round is taken only after that rebuild. The cost is stated: every step and gate starts from an
empty cache, the verifier downloads once per round (a new uv cache is first copied from the project's seed), and a test gate
that needs a download setup did not make belongs in `gates.setup`. For Go that means every module and its checksum:
`gates.setup` MUST run `go mod download all` and `go mod verify` (doctor `SANDBOX-005` warns when a Go project's setup has no
`go mod download`), because `GOMODCACHE` and the checksum database cache are read-only in the other gates; a tool with a
cache of its own (golangci-lint: `GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE`; anything under `~/.cache`) points it at `.l4-out/` in the gate script.

**L4-SEC-040 Gates see the CI's identity variables.** When the harness runs in CI (`CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` or `GITLAB_CI`
is `true` in its environment), every gate process (setup, build, lint, typecheck, test, e2e, coverage check, a
`repository-ci:<job>` step) SHALL also receive those of `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `GITLAB_CI` that the harness's
environment sets, with that value, when the value fully matches a short word (1 to 16 letters, digits, `_`, `-`); a
gate's own setting wins. A value that is not a short word MUST NOT be passed, and `l4 run` SHALL log once per such name
the WARNING `the gates do not get <NAME>: its value is not a short word (at most 16 letters, digits, '_', '-')`, never
the value. No colour variable (`FORCE_COLOR`, `NO_COLOR`, `PY_COLORS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `TTY_COMPATIBLE`)
is passed, in CI or out of it: with them pytest writes ANSI codes into its logs and JUnit XML, which the harness's own
readers of gate output do not expect. Agent processes MUST NOT receive the three variables. No other variable of the CI
is passed (not `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_PATH`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `RUNNER_TEMP`,
`CI_JOB_TOKEN` or any `CI_*`). Outside CI the gate environment SHALL be unchanged; `CI=true l4 run` opts in on a
person's machine, and `l4 run` then logs one INFO line `the gates run with <NAME=value, ...> from this environment, not
from a CI job: tools behave as in the repository's CI` (when neither `GITHUB_ACTIONS` nor `GITLAB_CI` is `true`).
`run.started` SHALL record `gate_env_ci`, the sorted names the gates get, when there is one. The runner probe's shell
twin (`m0_gate_env`) SHALL build the same environment, with `LC_ALL=C` for its character class.

**L4-SEC-041 A local run that cannot sandbox refuses before it touches anything.** Outside a CI job (L4-CLI-004), `l4 run`
(also `--unit`) and `l4 verify` SHALL check that a sandbox can be selected (`l4.sandbox.select.sandbox_refusal`, which reuses
`select_sandbox`) before they refresh refs, run follow-ups, take a plan step, take a lease or make a worktree. When none can
be, they SHALL exit 3 (`doctor_failed`) with the reason on stderr and nothing recorded: no ledger line, lease, worktree, ref or
plan event, and the plan is not stopped. `sandbox.mode: none` with `allow_none` selects nothing and runs; `none` without
`allow_none` is refused up front; a mode that does not exist yet (`user`, `container`) keeps its usage error; `--dry-run`,
`l4 retry`, `l4 resume` and `l4 simulate` are not checked. On macOS the message SHALL replace the Linux-only bubblewrap hint
by the ways out and name the refused command (`l4 run` or `l4 verify`): a Linux machine or VM with bubblewrap, letting CI run
it (`l4 ci start`, or `l4 retry` for a halted or escalated unit), or `sandbox.mode: container` once it exists; Linux keeps the
bubblewrap hint. In a CI job the check stays where it was, in the run: a runner without a sandbox still records
`unit.setup_failed` (L4-YOLO-093). [V, a local `l4 run --unit` of a plan's current unit on a host without bubblewrap took the
lease, made the worktree and the ledger, failed to select a sandbox, and the recorded setup failure stopped the plan for
everyone]

**L4-SEC-042 A Python file that a unit changes must be UTF-8.** After every agent step (red, green, a chore of any kind, a
refactor, a test chore, and a replayed held step), a Python file (`.py`, `.pyi`) that the step added or changed SHALL be put
back to the step's base (a new file removed), recorded as `guard.violation{phase, rule: "python encoding", path, why,
action, task, attempt}` (`action` is `restored` or `removed`), and SHALL fail the attempt with the reason `the step wrote a
Python file that declares an encoding other than UTF-8: <path> (<encoding>)[, ...]; it was put back` (at most five paths
shown) and the advice `Python files must stay UTF-8: do not add a coding cookie that names another encoding. The harness put
the file back: write the change again without the cookie (a file that already declared another encoding must be converted to
UTF-8, or left unchanged).`, when its declared encoding is not `utf-8`, `utf-8-sig` or `ascii` (`tokenize.detect_encoding` on
the first two lines, `\r\n` and a lone `\r` counted as line ends, as the compiler does; every spelling of UTF-8 or ASCII
counts as that encoding, and ASCII is a subset of UTF-8 and hides nothing), or when it is `unreadable`. The rule is on the
file, not on the cookie the step added: a pre-existing non-UTF-8 Python file that a step changes is put back too. The guard
runs in `agent_step` and in `replay_step`, right after the gate-configuration guard and before any result is read, so a
`blocked` or invalid result does not excuse the file; the ledger restore and the environment check of the step still run
when the guard raises (a restore that fails raises to the attempt). No file is read whole and none is skipped by size: at
most `COOKIE_PREFIX_BYTES + 1` (64 KiB + 1) bytes are read, from the work tree through a reader that never follows a link
and from a blob by a stream that stops after them. When the prefix ends inside line 1 or line 2: if that line, after
`[ \t\f]*`, starts with `#` or is blank, the file is `unreadable` (a comment or blank line longer than the prefix, behind
which a cookie may sit) and is a violation like any other encoding; if it starts with code, no cookie can sit on it (and none
on line 2 after a line 1 of code), so the file is decided from the complete lines before it and the byte-order mark, and the
cut bytes are never decoded. A Python file that cannot be read (a directory without read permission, a FIFO or a device; any
`OSError` other than a missing file, or a file that is not regular) is `unreadable` too and put back like the rest, with the
`why` `the harness cannot read the file (<error>)`; a missing file, a link (left to the link walk) and a directory give no
verdict.

A Python-named symbolic link is followed inside the work tree (a chain, a linked directory; at most 40 links). When the
link, a link on the way or the file it ends at changed in the step, the file it ends at is checked the same way, and on a
violation every changed path of the chain and the file itself are put back, one `guard.violation` each, whose `why` names
the link and the file. The file a link ends at is matched to the changed paths by file identity (`st_dev`, `st_ino`), not by
name, since a file system that ignores case or Unicode normalisation gives one file several names; a changed path that was
removed cannot be the target of a link that still resolves. A link that does not end at a regular file of the work tree
(dangling, a directory, a loop, outside the tree) is not followed: Python cannot import it as a file, so it cannot hide
source.

The verifier SHALL report ONE blocker that lists every Python file the unit's diff (base..head) adds or changes, whoever
committed it, that is not UTF-8 in this sense, in the last integrity row of step 1, `python encoding` (at most five rows are
shown, then `(+N more)`), with the title `a Python file declares a non-UTF-8 encoding` and the detail `<path>: <encoding>[,
...]. <advice>` (the finding reads `a Python file declares a non-UTF-8 encoding: <path>: <encoding>[, ...]. <advice>`), the
advice reading `Python reads the cookie and the harness and the judge read UTF-8, so code can hide behind a comment. Convert
each file to UTF-8 and remove the coding cookie (a link must end at a regular file of the repository)`. Every git path and
link target is decoded with `os.fsdecode`, so names that are not UTF-8 stay distinct and a link finds its own target; a name
is shown with its invalid bytes as `\xNN`.

The verifier follows every Python-named link of the tree at head the same way. A link is touched by base..head when the
link, a link on the way or its target is added, changed or deleted (a target that is renamed, case only included, counts as
deleted), or when its target, folded for case and Unicode normalisation (`NFC`, `casefold`), is the folded name of a changed
path. A touched link is checked at the file it ends at (`<link>: <encoding> (link to <file>)`); when its literal target is
not a regular file of the tree and was not deleted, the one regular file with the same folded name is taken for it (a
literal regular target wins over a folded twin). A touched link that ends at no regular file of the tree at head (dangling,
a directory, a loop, outside the tree, a target that was deleted or renamed, several files with the same folded name) is the
row `<link>: link that cannot be checked`; this also applies when only a link in the chain changed. A link that base..head
did not touch is not looked at. The note of the check never says that a file is UTF-8 that it did not read.

The verifier's test writer SHALL refuse generated test code (audit and e2e) for which the bytes it would write (the marker on
line 1, then the code) declare another encoding, with the reason `the test declares the encoding <encoding>; write UTF-8
without a coding cookie`, and `write_test_file` SHALL refuse to write such a file (`ValueError`).

A file with no cookie, a `utf-8` or `ascii` cookie or a byte-order mark is unaffected, and so is a file that is not Python.
Not covered [I]: a file that a gate run writes is checked only by the verifier row, before merge (the step guard runs after
the agent, not after the gates); `.gitattributes` is not frozen (`*.py -diff` would show a diff as binary to the judge and
`working-tree-encoding` makes the work tree bytes differ from the blob, both a separate change); extensionless scripts with a
Python shebang, `.pyw`, files loaded through `runpy` and tracked `.pyc` files; a pre-existing non-UTF-8 Python file must be
converted to UTF-8 on the base branch before a unit can change it (a step that changes it is put back, a commit that changes
it is a blocker); `Git.blob_prefix` and `stream_blob` read the object stream without a timeout (a partial clone could block
on an object it has to fetch), only the wait for git to exit has one; the verifier's link walk costs one git call per hop
for every Python-named link at head (linear: 1,500 links take about 11 s), and links the diff did not touch are not looked
at but their texts are still read to walk them; and a link whose chain or directory components differ in case from git's
names is not followed by the verifier (only the final target is folded). [V, adversarial review 2026-10-30, with the
harness's own pure functions: a red step that adds `# coding: utf-7` as line 1 of a pre-existing test and `  # +AAo-    return` to a line of it leaves `tamper.compare` empty and the skip-marker scan silent, because the harness and the judge
read the file as UTF-8 and see a comment, while Python reads a newline and a `return`; the test passes against a broken
product, and red's own new test still fails by assertion, as red requires; `openspec/changes/python-file-encoding/`]

## 19. Non-functional requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| L4-NFR-001 | `l4 doctor --ci` and `l4 plan` complete in < 30 s on a repo with 200 units (excluding `--live`, `--adoption` (GATE-001 runs the test suite), `--sweep` and the `install` actions of `--fix`, L4-DOC-002). |
| L4-NFR-002 | Harness overhead per task step (excluding agent and gate time) < 5 s. |
| L4-NFR-003 | Deterministic: given the same repository state, config and fake adapters, `plan` output and simulation event sequences are byte-identical (timestamps excluded). |
| L4-NFR-004 | Runtime dependencies limited to: `pydantic`, `pyyaml`, `httpx`, `jsonschema`, `typer` (or `click`); optional extras `[laya]`, `[serena]`. No LiteLLM library dependency (heavy deps; a compromised release shipped in 2026-03 [D, research/04]). |
| L4-NFR-005 | CI and live runners: **Linux** (bubblewrap, container or sandbox-user isolation). macOS is supported for local development only (`sandbox.mode: user` or `container`; doctor reports the reduced isolation); a local `l4 run` or `l4 verify` there refuses up front while no sandbox can be selected (L4-SEC-041). Windows best-effort (line endings handled by L4-TMW-001). |
| L4-NFR-006 | Every `[U]` fact in §8.3 has a contract test or a `LIVE-*` doctor check before the adapter is labelled GA. |

## 20. Testing strategy for the harness itself

1. **Unit tests** — parsers (tasks.md OpenSpec/Kiro, questions.md, lessons.md) with golden files including CRLF, tabs,
   optional tasks, nested numbering; byte-safety property tests (random marker flips change exactly one byte);
   state fold; aggregation truth table (§10.4) exhaustively; exit-code severity ordering; redaction.
2. **Contract tests** — each adapter parses recorded raw outputs (success, max-turns, schema output, usage limit,
   429, auth failure) for the pinned CLI versions; recorded via `scripts/record-cli-fixtures.sh` on a maintainer
   machine.
3. **Template lock** — `src/l4/templates.lock.json` pins the body sha256 of each implementer template (contract, red,
   green, single) and the system text of the judge and clarifier prompts to their version; `tests/unit/test_template_lock.py`
   fails when a body changes without a version bump (or a bump without `python -m l4.templatelock --write`). A template
   change that passes the lock is not thereby shown to be no worse: run `l4 eval --compare` (item 6).
4. **Simulation** — all built-in scenarios (§17) in CI on every commit.
5. **Live** — opt-in pipeline against the reference environment (architecture §15): the dummy GitLab repository
   `example-group/dummy-agentic` on runner `l4-runner` (tags `agentic`), plus a GitHub test repository; seeds a small
   app with an OpenSpec change and a Kiro spec; exercises: probe + fallback (Codex window artificially excluded via
   config), red/green, a forced clarification, a forced verifier failure → fix unit → PASS → archive → MR ready.
6. **Eval set and regression gate** — `l4 eval` (§20.1) runs a fixed seed set through the real implement and verify
   paths, one profile per role, and writes a scorecard; `l4 eval --compare` is the gate. Run it on every template
   version bump, every CLI pin bump and before a free model leaves a chain, and commit the scorecard as the next
   baseline under `docs/eval/` when the gate passes or the regression is accepted with a note.

### 20.1 `l4 eval` (M1.14)

**L4-EVAL-001** The seed set MUST live in this repository (`tests/eval/seeds/`: a base project and units, each with an
OpenSpec change, `expected.json` and a `reference/` of red and green files), and `seed_set_sha256` MUST change with any byte of it.
**L4-EVAL-002** Every seed unit MUST be a change the harness detects, with every criterion covered by a tagged reference
test; the base gate MUST be green on the base and on each reference green and red on each reference red.
**L4-EVAL-003** One unit (`add-late-fee`) MUST carry a designed defect that its own tests do not see and a hidden check
(never copied into a worktree) does, with expected judge verdict `NEEDS_HUMAN`.
**L4-EVAL-004** A cell MUST run one profile per role with no fallback, on `forge.type: local`, with System One,
fix rounds and the clarifier off, keeping of `--config` only the profiles and its `sandbox` and `availability` sections
(a slow local model needs the operator's `probe_timeout`); an implementer and a judge of the same vendor, or an
undeclared vendor, make the cell `invalid` before any agent call.
**L4-EVAL-005** A cell MUST start from a fresh bare mirror and clone of the seeded base, with fixed commit dates and
nothing that gives the answer (`expected.json`, `reference/`).
**L4-EVAL-006** A judge cell MUST get its implementation from a deterministic `command` profile that replays the
reference through the real implement path.
**L4-EVAL-007** A cell MUST run the real `l4 run` as a child process with a private `L4_CACHE`, touching nothing under
the repository's `.l4` or the user's cache; a cell timeout makes it `invalid`.
**L4-EVAL-008** The score MUST be read from the child's ledger: an implementer cell passes when red and green ended ok
(and the reference judge, if it ran, said PASS); a judge cell passes when its round-1 verdict is the expected one.
**L4-EVAL-009** Errors MUST be classed `schema`, `rate_limit`, `unavailable`, `timeout`, `login`, `setup_cold` or `other`;
the classes `rate_limit`, `unavailable`, `login`, `setup_cold`, a cell timeout, an `l4 run` exit 1, 2 or 3 (`harness_error`: the model was not measured) and a model under test that never ran (an implementer run halted before its first agent step: `baseline_failed` or `halted_before_agent`; a judge never called: `judge_not_reached`; the cell's reference, the fixed judge or the replay, unavailable: `reference_unavailable`) make a cell `invalid` (left out of every rate), `schema` and an agent timeout count as failures.
**L4-EVAL-010** Cost MUST be the sum of the reported `budget.cost`, `null` when none was reported, `0.0` only for a profile declared free.
**L4-EVAL-011** The scorecard MUST be canonical JSON (`l4/eval-scorecard@1`), deterministic for the same cells, with
per-profile aggregates (`pass_rate = pass / (pass + fail)`).
**L4-EVAL-012** The scorecard MUST record the environment: harness commit, every template version and hash, CLI
versions, the uv and OpenSpec versions, models, vendors, options and the kept `--config` sections without secrets, seed
hash, k, timeout, machine.
**L4-EVAL-013** A markdown form of the scorecard MUST list invalid cells under their own heading.
**L4-EVAL-014** `l4 eval` MUST refuse without `--impl` or `--judge`, without `--ref-judge` for an implementer cell,
and for an unknown unit or profile (exit 2); cells MUST run one at a time.
**L4-EVAL-015** A rate limit or an unavailable endpoint MUST stop the profile for the rest of the run (an unavailable reference stops the cells of its role instead, never the profile), and `--resume` MUST skip cells already measured (`pass` or `fail`) on the same seed set in the same environment; an `invalid` cell runs again.
**L4-EVAL-016** `scorecard.json` and `scorecard.md` MUST be rewritten atomically after every cell, and no file of the run directory may hold a raw prompt or an unredacted log.
**L4-EVAL-017** `--idle-check` MUST gate every cell on a command's exit code (no shell, output dropped); past `--idle-wait` the cell is `invalid: runner_busy` and the run stops with exit 12.
**L4-EVAL-018** The harness MUST open no socket for `l4 eval`; the scratch setup is `uv sync --frozen --offline`.
**L4-EVAL-019** `l4 eval --warm-cache` MUST be the only path that reaches an index, and it MUST be refused with `--impl` or `--judge`.
**L4-EVAL-020** The whole path MUST be testable end to end with the scripted fake adapter in every role.
**L4-EVAL-021** `compare` MUST report per profile the deltas and a status `ok`, `regressed`, `improved`, `new`, `gone`
or `unrated`; `regressed` when the pass rate drops by more than `--max-drop` (default 0.20), when a judge's
agreement drops by more, or when a judge passes a designed-defect unit the baseline did not miss (at any threshold,
also when the baseline has no rated cell for it or the profile is otherwise `unrated`).
**L4-EVAL-022** Only cells present and rated in both scorecards MUST enter a rate; a profile more than half `invalid` in either scorecard is `unrated`.
**L4-EVAL-023** The report MUST start with the environment diff; scorecards of different seed sets or schemas MUST be refused (exit 2) unless `--allow-seed-change`, which reports deltas only.
**L4-EVAL-024** `--compare` MUST exit 0, 15 (a regression, a newly missed defect, or with `--require-all` a missing profile) or 2 (a missing or invalid file, an incomplete scorecard, or nothing compared: no profile rated in both); with `--new` it runs no agent, and `--new` without `--compare` or `--baseline-dir` is exit 2.
**L4-EVAL-025** `--baseline-dir` MUST pick the newest complete scorecard of the same seed set that started before the new one (never the new scorecard itself or a copy of it), and say how to make one when there is none.
**L4-EVAL-026** `l4 doctor` MUST carry a warning row `EVAL-001` when a template differs from the newest baseline; it never fails doctor.
**L4-EVAL-027** `docs/eval.md` MUST state what the eval can and cannot see and the practice of §20 item 6.

## 21. Delivery plan (OpenSpec changes for this repository)

### 21.0 This repository's own CI

The harness repository checks itself with GitHub workflows (L4-ACT-006, L4-ACT-007):
- **`checks.yml`:** ruff, `scripts/check_spec.py`, gitleaks over every commit and the files, the publication scrub, and
  the unit suite in 8 shards (`scripts/dev/shards.py`: a deterministic split by test file). The shards run on pull
  requests to `amaster`, nightly when `amaster` moved, and by dispatch, not on every push, to protect the private
  repository's minutes (about 32 runner-minutes for a run) [V: run 38312211032, 103–355 s per shard]. One summary check
  fails when any shard fails.
- **`action-selftest.yml`:** the action from the checkout with source `action`, then `l4 --version` and
  `l4 doctor --adoption` on `tests/fixtures/py_tdd`.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`:** the repository's own `github-actions` pins.
- **`release.yml`:** on `src-vX.Y.Z`, the slim release commit on branch `release`, the tags `vX.Y.Z` and `v0`, and a
  GitHub release (scripts/dev/release_commit.py). The `release` branch is separate so that no consumer downloads
  `docs/live/` on every job.

Built in this order; each change is a unit the harness itself could later run (dogfooding):

| 113 | `own-test-repair` | a unit's own new test that fails with an error of its own gets a narrow repair step whose edit a person accepts. `l4.verifier.repairs.repair_candidates` derives the candidates from the stored round and git (the red commit of this unit added the test, no person's commit changed it or what it uses, a kind other than `assertion` or `not_implemented`, every repository frame of the traceback in test files, a browser test only with a usage error); `l4.verifier.fixunit` makes a `repair` chore (marker `repairs` in `.l4/fix.json`, re-derived by the step) only when every failing id of a finding is a candidate. `l4.implementer.repaircheck` is the pure structural check (`check_repair`); `_run_repair` (in `l4.implementer.tdd`) runs the step with the single-repair prompt, the scope re-derived from git, the check, the gate the tests failed in as must-pass, the proofs (`_repair_proof`: zero values for a unit-gate test, the base code built for an e2e test) and the static gates. An agent's step that passes is not committed: `_repair_proposal` captures it (`held_patch.capture`), `held_patch.repair_blobs` gives the blob pair of each file from `expected_state` and refuses a file whose text before or after the patch changes under `redact_text` (alone or the two read together) or holds a character a view does not show (`_unshown_reason`; `held.unshown_in` names by Unicode class what `str.isprintable()` rejects, except tab, newline, a carriage return before a newline and a leading byte order mark, and the default-ignorable characters it accepts), `_repair_proposal` refuses a saved patch whose text (decoded, uncut) changes under the redaction or has a line longer than `held.MAX_LINE_CHARS` (a cut would take a redaction mark away), and then a question whose title or Context holds a redaction mark (`[REDACTED`) or changes under the redaction as a whole, and `held.Check` `repair` (`held_question` routes to `_repair_question`: the tests, their failure, the runs that took place (`ExtraRun.made`, `e2e-repair-base`), how each was proved, the suppressions the saved result declares, the diffs, options `accept` and `retry`, the person-only line) holds the task with no attempt counted. `held.accepted_overrides` counts an `accept` of a `repair` question only with `by: human`; `held_patch.find_replay` records `held.accept_ignored{by}` once for another actor and runs the step again as an agent's; the delegate's pass escalates such a question without a model call and `questions_cli` refuses an agent whatever `clarifier.answer_by_agents` says. A person's accept replays the saved edit with no agent, every check runs again, `_repair_drift` compares the changed files with `held.recorded_repair_blobs` (the step base is the recorded before, the work-tree file the recorded after, hashed without line-ending conversion) and the commit (staged with `core.autocrlf=false`, `core.safecrlf=false`) carries `L4-TDD: exempt` and `task.repaired{question, patch_sha256}`; the done record has no notes and the suppressions of the saved result, which the question shows. `loop._raise_held` commits the saved step with the same exact staging, so its `patch_sha256` holds after a fresh checkout. The views read the lines git and Python count (`text_lines`, `_python_source` with the class chain of the id), every shown line (`_indented`, `_cut`, `_file_diff`, the failure line) goes through `escape_unshown` after redaction (a line that gets an escape has its backslashes doubled) and is cut once (`cap_line` keeps a line that already ends in its cut note), and `FIELD_SHAPE` of the redactor stops at a line end (every question and the judge). `integrity._repair_acceptance` (`_accepted_why`, `_repair_problems`) lets `check_test_paths` accept the files of a `task.repaired` only as the edit a person accepted (five conditions, the replay after the answer); `traceability` counts a repaired test as proved by the event while the file has the `sha10`, and the judge sees the test before and after. Amends ci-evidence D11 (a plain fix chore still may not change a test). Limit: the structural check and the proofs are a filter, not the boundary; a person reads the diff (L4-IMP-091, L4-VER-073; `openspec/changes/own-test-repair/`) | the unit tests (`test_repair_step`, `test_repair_person_only`, `test_repair_check`, `test_repair_candidates`, `test_repair_probes`, `test_held_question_unchanged`, `test_held_views`, `test_redact`, `test_repair_escalation`, `test_repair_integrity`, `test_traceability_repair`, `test_fixunit_repair`, `test_questions_agents`) |
| 114 | `judge-schema-break` | a judge's reply whose only break is an over-long list of free text is kept, and a judge whose reply still breaks the schema gives way to the next independent judge. `judge_repair.FOLDED_LISTS` (`riskiest_assumptions`): `_walk` folds a list of strings longer than its `maxItems` N into its first N − 1 items and the rest joined by newlines (a list in another field, with an item that is not a string, or shorter than `minItems` is left as it is), so `run_judge` keeps the reply as `repaired` with one call. `ladder._ask_judges`: a `schema_invalid` result of a prompt that is not a follow-up calls `vc.next_judge("schema_invalid", None)` (the `skip` branch, no cool-down) and asks the new judge the same prompt with its `criteria` and `rebuild`; a `WaitingCapacity` from it ends the loop with the discarded result, so `judge_body` holds the round as before (exit 11, never `waiting_capacity`); a `schema_invalid` batch of `_ask_batches` gives the next judge the whole prompt; a follow-up and a timeout keep their rules. A consumer's unit of 25 criteria had its judge's reply to part 1 of 2 discarded twice for more than three riskiest assumptions; part 2 and the chain's other judges were never asked and every criterion became a verdict question (L4-VER-074, L4-VER-075; `openspec/changes/judge-schema-break/`). Limits: a judge that breaks the schema on every prompt costs the next judge's call for each part, in every round; `verification.md` names only the judge that gave the final answer and counts its replies, so a discarded judge shows in the ledger's `verify.judge` rows only | the unit tests (`test_judge_repair`, `test_judge_chain`, `test_judge_length_split`, `test_judge_step_followup`) |
| 115 | `transient-retry` | a capacity wait is bounded by a transient failure: when nothing in a required chain is usable and a profile was skipped for a failure of the `transient` class (a probe step or `hello` that timed out, an unreachable provider), `retry_after` is the earlier of the earliest cool-down's end and the park plus `availability.default_cooldown`, so one cooling profile (credits used up, 24 hours) no longer sets the time for a chain whose other profiles were back in minutes. `fallback._Walk.transient` (recorded in `_probe`, dropped by `forget`), read by `_nothing_usable`. A chain that only timed out waits the default too, so its park is not fix-only and an outage no longer stops the plan with `capacity_needs_fix`; a failed login, a refused or wrong `hello`, a missing binary, an unsupported version, a constraint and `serves` keep L4-AVL-007. Limits: a model that hangs at every hello is probed again at each trigger after the wait, up to `max_runs`; the delegate (optional) keeps L4-DLG-013 (L4-AVL-013, L4-AVL-007, L4-YOLO-035, SCN-AVL-33..36; `openspec/changes/transient-retry/`) | the unit tests (`test_fallback`, `test_yolo_cycle_capacity`) |
| 116 | `delegate-batch` | the verdict questions of one round share a delegate call: the due verdict questions of one target folder with the same askers are asked in batches of up to `delegate.batch_size` (5; 1 asks one per call), each question first passing its own checks; one call with `delegate-batch@1` and the reply `l4/delegate-batch@1`, one `l4/delegate-result@1` per question, each checked and written on its own; a batch of N needs N answers' cost left and gets N times `max_cost_usd_per_answer` as its budget, is shortened to fit the money and `BATCH_MAX_CHARS`, and its cost is recorded once with a share on each result; a question whose batch timed out or failed is asked alone next; `max_questions_per_run` counts questions. `_Pass.run` forms the batches, `_ask_batch` asks one, `prompt.build_batch_prompt`, `batch_schema`. Limits: a batch's timeout costs each of its questions an attempt; the answers of one call can share a misreading (each is still checked on its citations); other kinds are one call each (L4-DLG-028, L4-DLG-003, L4-DLG-004, L4-DLG-005, L4-DLG-009, SCN-DLG-127..133; `openspec/changes/delegate-batch/`) | the unit tests (`test_batch`, `test_prompt`, `test_pass`) |

The self-hosting proposal's L4-SELF-014 (a boolean to require a plan) is `yolo.hold: ["*"]` (L4-ADO-011): every spec is then opt-in by plan, and no new key is added.

## 22. Open questions and decisions

Maintainer answers of 2026-10-03 are marked **decided**.

| # | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Where is the harness repository hosted? | **Decided (2026-10-12): a private GitHub repository.** Adopting repositories fetch it at run time by commit (`harness.repository`, `harness.commit`; `uvx --from git+<url>@<sha>`, L4-GHP-010), through a read-only deploy key, so no harness code enters their history. `l4 init --vendor` remains for air-gapped runners. [V: public dummy repository, runs 38173604230 and 38173836160.] Earlier decision (2026-10-03): local only, `--vendor`. |
| Q2 | Bot identity for commits and the forge token owner. | **Decided (2026-10-03):** GitLab project access token `l4-bot` (Developer, `api` + `write_repository`, 1 year) stored as the masked, unprotected, raw CI variable `L4_FORGE_TOKEN`; created and rotated reproducibly by `scripts/forge/gitlab_bot_token.py` (on `example-group/dummy-agentic`: token id 62, bot user 60, expires 2027-10-03). The maintainer authorised the agent to create as many tokens as needed on `example-group/dummy-agentic`. GitHub: a GitHub App (still open, with Q5). |
| Q3 | Agent authentication on `l4-runner`. | **Decided: mixed** — subscription logins for Codex and Claude Code (quota probing, per-profile credential mounts, `max_concurrency: 1`), API keys for OpenCode/OpenRouter and the judges. Observed 2026-10-03 [V, runner]: Claude Code (subscription **`pro`**) and Codex are logged in as the runner user (logins moved from the admin user, PRQ-17); OpenCode's free `opencode/*` models and the local `magnitude` provider need no login; Kiro is not logged in; no API key is configured on the runner yet. The OpenRouter key used by the spikes had a negative balance (every call 402) [V, spikes/05]; whether the runner will use the same account is U. Spike 05's Claude quota figures came from a Max plan, not `pro`. |
| Q4 | Laya checkpoint for v1: fine-tuned `typed-decisions` or base `english`? | Open — default `typed-decisions` if its license and size fit the runner. |
| Q5 | Is a GitHub test repository available for parity live tests? | Open — default: a private one under the maintainer's account, created in change 13 (`live-validation`). |
| Q6 | Sandbox on the reference runner. | **Decided: bubblewrap**, installed on `l4-runner`: bubblewrap 0.6.1 works for the runner user (PRQ-04), and claude, codex (nested sandbox) and opencode ran inside it [V, runner/sandbox-probe-2026-10-03.txt]. Doctor `SANDBOX-001` (change 11) still has to prove the per-profile credential separation of L4-SEC-005. |
| Q7 | Archive timing. | **Decided: post-merge archive PR** (`archive.mode: post_merge_pr`, default). `on_approval` stays available as an opt-in. |
| Q8 | Job timeout of the agentic projects. | **Decided: 180 min**, set by the maintainer in the GitLab project settings (the harness never changes forge settings); `max_iterations_per_unit: 30` stays as the generic default. |
| Q9 | Independent verification and fallback on the reference runner. | **Decided (2026-10-04):** M0/M1.1 pair a Codex implementer with a tool-less Claude Code judge/clarifier (CLI judge, L4-FAC-003) [V, live pipeline 2530]. When Claude Code (subscription `pro`) is exhausted, the harness falls back to **Codex or OpenCode** (maintainer). Reference chains: `implementer: [codex, opencode-free, claude-code]`, `judges: [claude-code, opencode-free, codex]`, `clarifier: [claude-code, codex, opencode-free]`. The independence constraint (L4-VER-001) still applies to judges: a judge whose vendor equals the implementer's is skipped. OpenCode Zen models do not disclose the served vendor, so the `opencode-free` profile carries an operator-declared `vendor:`; a verdict from it is reported in `verification.md` as `independence: declared (unverified)`. Implemented with fallback chains in M1.2. |
