#### SCN-SEC-56 (+) A link inside the worktree, and one the base already held, are not refused · L4-SEC-020
- **Given** a red step that adds `tests/alias.py` as a link to `test_discount.py`, and a repository whose base commit
  holds `vendor` as a link to an outside directory that a step leaves as it is
- **When** the step has passed its gates and is about to be committed
- **Then** no `link outside worktree` violation is recorded and the commit is made; the same name pointing to another
  outside target is refused

### 23.16 Non-functional (NFR)

#### SCN-NFR-01 (+) Plan is fast on large repositories · L4-NFR-001
- **Given** a fixture with 200 OpenSpec changes
- **When** `l4 doctor --ci` and `l4 plan --json` run on a CI-sized machine
- **Then** each completes in under 30 s.

#### SCN-NFR-02 (+) Harness overhead is bounded · L4-NFR-002
- **Given** a simulation with zero-latency fake adapters and gates
- **When** 20 task steps run
- **Then** the mean harness time per step is under 5 s.

#### SCN-NFR-03 (−) No unapproved runtime dependencies · L4-NFR-004
- **Given** the built wheel
- **When** its declared runtime dependencies are listed
- **Then** they are a subset of the approved list (extras excluded); `litellm` is absent.

#### SCN-NFR-04 (+) Linux CI; macOS unit tests · L4-NFR-005
- **Given** the harness CI matrix
- **When** the full test and simulation suites run on Linux and the unit tests on macOS
- **Then** all pass.

#### SCN-NFR-05 (+) macOS for local development · L4-NFR-005
- **Given** a developer's macOS machine without bubblewrap and with `ci.platform: local`
- **When** `l4 doctor` and `l4 run --dry-run` run
- **Then** both work; LOCAL-001 warns that `l4 run`/`l4 verify` will refuse on this computer and names the ways out, and
  the exit code of `l4 doctor` is that of the other rows; with `sandbox.mode: user` LOCAL-001 reports the mode as not
  built yet (`select_sandbox` exits 2 for it); SANDBOX-001 is not registered, so no row of that id is printed.

### 23.17 Security (prompt sources)

#### SCN-SEC-05 (−) Untrusted text never reaches prompts · L4-SEC-003
- **Given** a PR comment by a non-member containing instructions, and an issue linked to the unit
- **When** prompts are rendered
- **Then** their recorded sources are only harness templates and files at the unit branch head; neither the comment nor
  the issue text appears.

### 23.14 Eval set and regression gate (EVAL)

#### SCN-EVAL-01 (+) The seed set is whole and hashable · L4-EVAL-001
- **Given** `tests/eval/seeds/`
- **When** it is loaded
- **Then** it has the base project and four units, each with one task, two scenarios with distinct WHENs, `expected.json` and red and green references; `seed_set_sha256` changes with a byte of `expected.json` and not with the place of the directory.

#### SCN-EVAL-02 (+) No seed can rot · L4-EVAL-002, L4-EVAL-003
- **Given** each unit with its reference applied
- **When** the base gate runs
- **Then** it is green on the base and the reference green and red on the reference red; the `add-late-fee` reference passes its own tests and fails the hidden check.

#### SCN-EVAL-03 (+) A cell has one profile per role · L4-EVAL-004
- **Given** an implementer cell and a judge cell
- **When** their configs are rendered
- **Then** the implementer chain, or the judge chain, is exactly the one profile, with the local forge and no fallback; a same-vendor cell is `invalid: vendor_veto` with no agent call.

#### SCN-EVAL-04 (+) The reference replays through the real implement path · L4-EVAL-005, L4-EVAL-006
- **Given** a fresh workspace and the `eval-reference` command profile
- **When** `l4 run` takes the unit
- **Then** red and green are harness-made commits with trailers and a ledger, and the unit reaches `implemented`.

#### SCN-EVAL-05 (+) An implementer cell is scored from the ledger · L4-EVAL-007, L4-EVAL-008, L4-EVAL-010
- **Given** ledgers with retries, a breaker trip, a block and a verdict
- **When** they are scored
- **Then** pass, fail with the halting phase, attempts per phase, cost (`null` when unreported) and tokens are as the ledger says.

#### SCN-EVAL-06 (+) A judge cell is scored against the expected verdict · L4-EVAL-008, L4-EVAL-009
- **Given** a judge that holds back the defective unit, one that passes it, and one whose reply breaks the schema twice
- **When** they are scored
- **Then** the first agrees, the second has `missed_defect`, the third fails with error class `schema`, not `invalid`.

#### SCN-EVAL-07 (+) The scorecard is deterministic · L4-EVAL-011, L4-EVAL-013
- **Given** the same cells in two orders
- **When** the scorecards are built
- **Then** their canonical JSON is byte-identical and valid against `l4/eval-scorecard@1`; `pass_rate` leaves `invalid` cells out.

#### SCN-EVAL-08 (+) The environment is recorded without secrets · L4-EVAL-012
- **Given** profiles whose options hold a planted secret
- **When** the environment is captured
- **Then** it holds the harness commit, template versions, CLI versions, models and seed hash, and no secret.

#### SCN-EVAL-09 (+) The command refuses what it cannot run · L4-EVAL-014
- **Given** `l4 eval` with no profile, an implementer without `--ref-judge`, or an unknown unit
- **When** it runs
- **Then** exit 2 with a message that names the problem; a dry run prints the matrix and writes nothing.

#### SCN-EVAL-10 (−) A 429 stops the profile, a resume skips what is measured · L4-EVAL-015, L4-EVAL-016, L4-EVAL-017
- **Given** a profile that is rate limited on its first cell, and an interrupted run
- **When** the run continues
- **Then** its other cells are `invalid: skipped_after_rate_limit` and never started; `--resume` runs only the unmeasured cells; a busy `--idle-check` past `--idle-wait` ends the run with exit 12; no file of the run holds a raw prompt or a secret.

#### SCN-EVAL-11 (+) The harness opens no socket · L4-EVAL-018, L4-EVAL-019
- **Given** a socket-denying process
- **When** the matrix is built, configs rendered, cells scored, the scorecard written and two scorecards compared
- **Then** nothing fails; a cold uv cache is `invalid: setup_offline_cache_cold` naming `l4 eval --warm-cache`, which is refused together with `--impl`.

#### SCN-EVAL-12 (+) End to end with the fake adapter · L4-EVAL-020
- **Given** the scripted fake adapter as implementer and judge
- **When** `l4 eval` runs a unit, a wrong-status retry, a 429 and a designed-defect judge cell
- **Then** the scorecard matches the golden file and no agent CLI was started.

#### SCN-EVAL-13 (−) A lost cell or a missed defect regresses · L4-EVAL-021, L4-EVAL-022
- **Given** an old and a new scorecard where one of four cells is lost, or a judge now passes the held-back defect
- **When** they are compared with the default `--max-drop 0.20`
- **Then** the profile is `regressed`; a profile mostly `invalid` is `unrated` and does not fail.

#### SCN-EVAL-14 (−) Different seed sets are not compared · L4-EVAL-023
- **Given** scorecards with different `seed_set_sha256`
- **When** they are compared
- **Then** exit 2 "the scorecards measure different seed sets", unless `--allow-seed-change`, which reports deltas and never `regressed`; the report starts with the environment diff.

#### SCN-EVAL-15 (+) The gate has an exit code · L4-EVAL-024, L4-EVAL-025, L4-EVAL-026, L4-EVAL-027
- **Given** two scorecard files
- **When** `l4 eval --compare OLD --new NEW` runs
- **Then** it exits 0, or 15 on a regression, or 2 for a missing file, and starts no agent; `gone` profiles do not fail unless `--require-all`; `--baseline-dir` picks the newest baseline of the same seed set; `l4 doctor` warns (EVAL-001) when a template changed since the baseline.

### 23.18 Adoption kit (ACT, SKL)

#### SCN-ACT-01 (+) A private repository of the same owner needs no key · L4-ACT-001
- **Given** a private repository of the harness owner, and the harness repository's Actions access `user`
- **When** a job runs `uses: <owner>/l4/.github/actions/l4@<sha>` and then `l4 --version`
- **Then** the job succeeds with source `action` and no secret configured.

#### SCN-ACT-02 (−) A public repository cannot use the private action · L4-ACT-001
- **Given** a public repository
- **When** a job uses the private action
- **Then** the job fails at "Set up job" with `Unable to resolve action … not found`, as GitHub documents.

#### SCN-ACT-03 (+) A public repository with a deploy key · L4-ACT-001
- **Given** a public repository with a copy of the action and `L4_HARNESS_SSH_KEY` in its environment `l4`
- **When** the copy runs with source `repository`, the harness's SSH URL and a pinned commit
- **Then** `l4 --version` succeeds, and the key file no longer exists after the install step.

#### SCN-ACT-04 (−) A bad commit stops before any download · L4-ACT-001
- **Given** source `repository` and `commit: main`
- **When** the action runs
- **Then** it fails with `::error::commit must be 40 hex digits` and exit 2, and fetched nothing.

#### SCN-ACT-05 (+) A warm job builds nothing · L4-ACT-002
- **Given** a previous job with the same harness source and catalog
- **When** a job runs the action
- **Then** both caches are hits, nothing is installed, and `l4 --version` follows the restore.

#### SCN-ACT-06 (+) A harness upgrade keeps the CLIs warm · L4-ACT-002
- **Given** warm caches for harness commit A
- **When** the workflow moves to commit B with the same catalog
- **Then** the harness cache misses and is rebuilt, the CLI cache hits, and `doctor --ci --fix` installs no CLI.

#### SCN-ACT-07 (+) The sandbox is ready on ubuntu-24.04 · L4-ACT-003
- **Given** a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 job with the action and `self-provision: auto`
- **When** the action runs
- **Then** the log has `[HSU-99] OK summary` with bwrap usable, and the repository holds no `.l4/bin/` file.

#### SCN-ACT-08 (+) A fresh adoption holds only config, the workflow and evidence · L4-ACT-004
- **Given** a repository without L4
- **When** `l4 init --ci github --action --harness-ref v0.3.0` runs
- **Then** the new files are `.l4/config.yaml`, `.github/workflows/l4.yml` (with `uses: …@<sha> # v0.3.0`) and
  `.serena/project.yml`, and `l4 doctor` passes its pin check.

#### SCN-ACT-09 (−) A drifting pin is reported · L4-ACT-004
- **Given** an action-mode workflow with source `repository` whose `uses:` sha and `commit` input differ
- **When** `l4 doctor` runs
- **Then** the pin check CFG-006 fails and names both shas.

#### SCN-ACT-10 (+) Upgrade by version · L4-ACT-005
- **Given** an action-mode workflow at `v0.3.0`
- **When** `l4 upgrade --harness-ref v0.4.0` runs
- **Then** the workflow is re-rendered from the config with the template of the harness that runs it and the new pin:
  the `uses:` line is `@<sha of v0.4.0> # v0.4.0`, an older template's steps are replaced by the current ones, and a
  second run changes nothing.

#### SCN-ACT-11 (+) One release · L4-ACT-006
- **Given** a tag `src-v0.3.0` on a commit whose checks passed
- **When** `release.yml` runs
- **Then** `release` gains one commit with only the release paths, `v0.3.0` and `v0` point to it, the release names
  the source sha, and its notes start with the CHANGELOG section of 0.3.0.

#### SCN-ACT-12 (−) A failing shard fails the check · L4-ACT-007
- **Given** a pull request with one failing unit test
- **When** `checks.yml` runs
- **Then** exactly that shard fails, and the summary job fails.

#### SCN-ACT-13 (+) A seed unit end to end through the action · L4-ACT-008
- **Given** the dummy repository adopted with `l4 init --action` and one seed unit
- **When** the workflow runs on a push
- **Then** the unit reaches a ready PR, and the step timings show a warm job's action step under 15 s with both caches
  hit.

#### SCN-ACT-14 (−) A tag without a dated CHANGELOG section is refused · L4-ACT-006
- **Given** a tag `src-v0.3.1` whose `CHANGELOG.md` has `## 0.3.1 (unreleased)` (or no 0.3.1 section)
- **When** `release.yml` runs
- **Then** it fails before it builds or pushes anything, `release` and the tags are unchanged, and the error names the
  dated heading to add (`## 0.3.1 (YYYY-MM-DD)`).

#### SCN-SKL-01 (+) Installed from the repository · L4-SKL-001
- **Given** a Claude Code session with read access to the harness repository
- **When** the person runs `/plugin marketplace add ciprianiacobescu/l4` and
  `/plugin install l4@l4-harness`
- **Then** the skill `l4` is listed and loads.

#### SCN-SKL-02 (+) The feedback kind is chosen right · L4-SKL-002
- **Given** the request "the base URL is hard-coded; make it configurable"
- **When** an agent with the skill turns it into a command
- **Then** it runs `l4 feedback add --kind config --env <NAME> --at <file:line> --text …`, not `refactor`.

#### SCN-SKL-03 (−) A refactor that breaks tests is not sent as refactor · L4-SKL-002
- **Given** the request "rename `calc` to `compute`; the tests call `calc`"
- **When** an agent with the skill chooses the kind
- **Then** it chooses `behaviour`, with `--when`/`--then`, and says why.

#### SCN-SKL-04 (+) One command installs the skill for the agents that are present · L4-SKL-003
- **Given** a home folder with `~/.claude` and `~/.kiro`, and no Codex or OpenCode folder or CLI
- **When** `l4 skills install` runs
- **Then** `~/.claude/skills/l4/SKILL.md` and `~/.kiro/skills/l4/SKILL.md` equal the package's copy, each folder has
  `.l4-skill.json` with the running version, nothing else is written, and the output names the two targets.

#### SCN-SKL-05 (+) A rerun after an upgrade updates the skill in place · L4-SKL-003
- **Given** the install of SCN-SKL-04 made by an older `l4`, its files unchanged
- **When** the newer `l4 skills install` runs
- **Then** both copies hold the new files and the new version, and `l4 skills status` says `current`.

#### SCN-SKL-06 (−) An edited copy is not overwritten · L4-SKL-003
- **Given** an installed copy whose `references/plan.md` a person edited
- **When** `l4 skills install` runs without `--force`
- **Then** that target is refused with the edited path named, the others are installed, the exit code is 2, and
  `--force` replaces it.

#### SCN-SKL-07 (+) A team installs the skill into the repository · L4-SKL-003
- **Given** a repository checkout
- **When** `l4 skills install --project --agent all` runs
- **Then** the four project folders hold the skill, ready to commit.

#### SCN-SKL-08 (−) An old installed skill is named by doctor · L4-SKL-003
- **Given** `~/.claude/skills/l4/.l4-skill.json` with a version older than the running `l4`
- **When** `l4 doctor` runs
- **Then** SKL-003 warns with the fix `l4 skills install`.

#### SCN-SKL-09 (+) The operate reference starts with origin, then the runbook and the table · L4-SKL-004
- **Given** the skill's `references/operate.md`
- **When** it is read
- **Then** its first section after the title states that origin is what counts, then holds a numbered runbook of ten steps that names `yolo_preflight.py`, "at most two rounds" and "a person activates", then an error table whose rows include `review: --record records what CI and l4 yolo activate read`, `activate: the review of <plan> is stale against origin/<base>`, `cannot judge` and `did not answer within`, and every `l4 …` command in that section resolves to a command of the CLI

#### SCN-SKL-10 (+) The skill hands a person's steps to a person · L4-SKL-004
- **Given** `SKILL.md` and `references/operate.md`
- **When** they are read
- **Then** `SKILL.md`'s rules say to run `scripts/yolo_preflight.py <plan>` and do its `Next:` line, and that activating and `--force` are a person's (print the command and stop); `operate.md` gives `l4 yolo activate <plan> --reason` and `l4 yolo accept <plan> --all --force` only as commands for the person

#### SCN-SKL-11 (+) A pushed, admitted plan with no review gets the review command · L4-SKL-005
- **Given** a clean clone at `origin/main` with plan `p1` pushed, a `claude-code` judge whose `claude` is on PATH, and a harness that admits the plan and reports no review
- **When** `python3 -I yolo_preflight.py p1` runs
- **Then** every check is `ok`, `skip` or `info`, the last line is `Next: l4 yolo review p1 --worktree --record`, and the exit code is 0; with no judge CLI on PATH the line is `Next: l4 yolo review p1 (CI reviews origin/main at its next run; then run this script again)`

#### SCN-SKL-12 (−) A dirty tree or an unpushed commit fails with its fix · L4-SKL-005
- **Given** an uncommitted edit of a unit folder, and in a second case a committed, unpushed plan file
- **When** the script runs
- **Then** the first prints `FAIL  clean-tree` and `Next: commit the changes git status lists, then git push origin HEAD:main`; the second prints `FAIL  head-is-origin: origin/main (<o7>) is 1 commit behind HEAD (<h7>)…` and `Next: git push origin HEAD:main, then run this script again`; both exit 1 and do not call the harness

#### SCN-SKL-13 (−) A judge that cannot judge and an OpenCode v2 fail in the harness's words · L4-SKL-005
- **Given** a `command` profile in `roles.judges`, and in a second case an opencode profile with an `opencode` on PATH that prints `opencode v2.0.32`
- **When** the script runs
- **Then** the first fails `judge-roles` with the text of L4-CFG-006 (without ` at $`); the second fails `opencode` with `opencode 2.0.32 is OpenCode v2; this profile runs v1 (opencode-ai 1.x)` and `Next: l4 doctor --fix (it installs opencode-ai@1.18.34 user-locally), then run this script again`; both exit 1

#### SCN-SKL-14 (+) An agent with a READY review is told to hand activation to a person · L4-SKL-005
- **Given** every check ok, a current review with every subject READY, and `CLAUDECODE=1`
- **When** the script runs
- **Then** `caller` is `agent (CLAUDECODE)` and the last line is `Next: a person runs: l4 yolo activate p1 --reason "<why>" (stop here: activation is a person's decision)`, exit 0; for a person in a terminal it is `Next: l4 yolo activate p1 --reason "<why>"`

#### SCN-SKL-15 (+) A subject past two rounds is accepted by whoever may, and the output is stable · L4-SKL-005
- **Given** a current review whose subject `openspec:add-greeting` is NEEDS_REVISION, `findings --json` giving `accept_available: true` for one caller, and for another an `accept_refusal` whose fix starts with `a person runs:`
- **When** the script runs for each caller, with and without `--json`
- **Then** the first `Next:` is `l4 yolo accept p1 openspec:add-greeting --reason "<what the implementer should do>"` (with ` --yes` for an agent, which has no terminal to confirm on; availability follows the caller kind and the target's `accept_by_agents`), the second is that refusal's fix followed by ` (stop here)`; `--json` prints `schema: l4/yolo-preflight@1` with `checks`, `next` and `exit`; the script imports only standard-library modules

### 23.19 Operator commands (OPS)

#### SCN-OPS-01 (+) An escalated unit at the fix-round limit needs no flag · L4-OPS-001
- **Given** a unit escalated with `fix rounds used 3/3`
- **When** `l4 retry --unit U --reason "spec corrected" --no-run` runs
- **Then** `budget.extended{fix_rounds: 1}` and `unit.retried` are recorded, the unit is back in `verifying`, and the
  push is `chore(<name>): retry [skip ci]`.

#### SCN-OPS-02 (+) A unit that waits for capacity from `fixing` continues · L4-OPS-001, L4-OPS-009
- **Given** a unit in `waiting_capacity` that was parked from `fixing`, with no `retry_after`
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** the unit is back in `fixing`, and `l4 plan` says `implement`.

#### SCN-OPS-03 (−) A unit that waits for an answer is refused · L4-OPS-001
- **Given** a unit in `awaiting_human` with the open question Q-002
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** it exits 2 with `retry: U is awaiting_human: answer Q-002 in questions.md on l4/<fw>/<name>, then push`, and
  records nothing.

#### SCN-OPS-04 (+) The retry starts the workflow on GitHub · L4-OPS-002
- **Given** a halted unit on GitHub and a forge token that may dispatch workflows
- **When** `l4 retry --unit U --reason TEXT` runs
- **Then** a `workflow_dispatch` run of `l4.yml` on the base branch starts, and the output says `run started on <base>`.

#### SCN-OPS-05 (−) A refused start still exits 0 and says how · L4-OPS-002
- **Given** a token that may push but not start pipelines
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** the retry is pushed, the output names the command that starts a run, and the exit code is 0.

#### SCN-OPS-06 (+) A reworded requirement reaches an escalated unit · L4-OPS-003
- **Given** an escalated Kiro unit, and a person's commit to `requirements.md` on its branch after the escalation
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** the unit is in `implementing` (`spec_edit_since_stop`), and the next verification judges the reworded
  requirement.

#### SCN-OPS-07 (−) A change outside the unit folder does not count · L4-OPS-003
- **Given** a halted unit, and a person's commit after the halt that changes only `src/`
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** the unit goes back to the phase before the halt, not to `implementing`.

#### SCN-OPS-08 (+) A poisoned unit starts over with the corrected spec · L4-OPS-004
- **Given** an escalated unit whose branch has a person's correction to `requirements.md`
- **When** `l4 restart --unit U --reason "start over" --no-run` runs
- **Then** `refs/l4/attempts/<fw>/<name>/1` holds the old head, the PR is closed, and the new branch has the corrected
  `requirements.md`, the base's task boxes, no `.l4/evidence`, and a ledger with `unit.restarted`; `l4 plan` says
  `implement`.

#### SCN-OPS-09 (−) A person's push during the restart wins · L4-OPS-004
- **Given** a person pushes to the unit branch after the restart read its head
- **When** the restart pushes the new branch
- **Then** the lease fails, the restart exits 1 with `the branch moved: run l4 restart again`, and the PR stays open.

#### SCN-OPS-10 (+) A non-convertible finding is named · L4-OPS-005
- **Given** a FAIL round whose only finding cannot become a fix task, with fix rounds left
- **When** the unit escalates
- **Then** `phase.changed` has `reason: no_convertible_finding` and its `detail`, and the note headline is
  `### Escalated: <detail>`.

#### SCN-OPS-11 (+) The halt cause is in the table · L4-OPS-006
- **Given** a unit halted by `max_task_attempts`
- **When** `l4 status` runs
- **Then** its row shows `halted` and the cause cut to 60 characters, and `l4 status --unit U` ends with `Next: l4 retry
  --unit U --reason TEXT`, after an `Or: add the label l4:retry` line.

#### SCN-OPS-12 (+) The same crashed test twice stops the loop · L4-OPS-007
- **Given** round 1 failed with the test gate's `INTERNALERROR` and no report, and a fix round ran
- **When** round 2 fails with the same gate and exit code
- **Then** the unit is escalated with `same_failure` after round 2, and no second fix unit is written.

#### SCN-OPS-13 (−) A different failure gets its fix round · L4-OPS-007
- **Given** round 1 failed on test A and round 2 fails on test B
- **When** round 2 ends
- **Then** a fix unit is written as before.

#### SCN-OPS-14 (+) A member's restart label starts the unit over · L4-OPS-008
- **Given** an escalated unit with an open PR, and a member adds `l4:restart`
- **When** the next run's sweep reads it
- **Then** the restart of L4-OPS-004 runs, and the same run's `l4 run` implements the unit again.

#### SCN-OPS-15 (+) A secret halt can be retried · L4-OPS-009
- **Given** a run whose outgoing commits contain a secret
- **When** the run ends
- **Then** the remote branch has no new code commit, its ledger shows `halted` with `secret_in_push`, and `l4 retry`
  after the person's correction is accepted.

#### SCN-OPS-16 (+) A closed PR is not a dead end · L4-OPS-009
- **Given** an `in_review` unit whose PR a person closed without a merge
- **When** the next sweep runs
- **Then** the unit is `abandoned`, and `l4 restart` on it is accepted.

#### SCN-OPS-17 (−) The resume label survives a manual run · L4-OPS-010
- **Given** a halted unit whose PR carries `l4:resume`
- **When** `l4 run --unit U` runs with a forge token
- **Then** it exits 13, the branch head is unchanged, and the label is still on the PR.

#### SCN-OPS-18 (+) A laptop retry needs no project setting · L4-OPS-011
- **Given** a clone whose `origin` is `git@github.com:o/n.git`, a token, and no `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
- **When** `l4 retry` runs
- **Then** it acts on `o/n` and does not exit 2.

#### SCN-OPS-19 (+) A failure under coverage reaches the fixer · L4-OPS-012
- **Given** a fix task whose test passes without coverage and fails under the coverage plugin
- **When** its green step runs
- **Then** the gate fails in that step, and the attempt's retry prompt carries the gate log.

#### SCN-OPS-20 (+) A spec push to an escalated unit starts it again · L4-OPS-014
- **Given** a unit escalated with `fix rounds used 3/3`, and a person's push that edits `proposal.md` on its branch
- **When** the next run starts
- **Then** `budget.extended{fix_rounds: 1}` and `unit.retried{reason: "spec edited"}` are recorded, the unit is in
  `implementing`, and no `l4 retry` was needed.

#### SCN-OPS-21 (+) A spec push to a verified unit is verified again before the hand-off · L4-OPS-014
- **Given** a `verified` unit, and a person's push that rewords a requirement before the hand-off
- **When** the next run starts
- **Then** the unit goes to `implementing`, then to `verifying`, and it is not handed off on the old verdict.

#### SCN-OPS-22 (−) Answers are not a spec edit · L4-OPS-014
- **Given** a unit in `awaiting_human`, and a person's push that changes only `questions.md`

### 23.24 L4 as an MCP server (MCP)

#### SCN-MCP-01 (+) A client connects and lists the tools · L4-MCP-001
- **Given** `l4 mcp serve` started by an MCP client in a repository
- **When** the client sends `initialize`, then `notifications/initialized`, then `tools/list`
- **Then** the server answers with its name `l4`, its version and the tools capability, and lists every tool with a description and an input schema

#### SCN-MCP-02 (−) A malformed request gets a protocol error · L4-MCP-001
- **Given** the running server
- **When** a line that is not JSON, or a call of an unknown method, arrives
- **Then** it answers -32700 or -32601 and keeps serving

#### SCN-MCP-03 (+) A read tool returns the command's output · L4-MCP-002
- **Given** a repository with a delivery plan `p`
- **When** a client calls `l4_plan_status` with `plan: p`
- **Then** the server runs `l4 yolo status --json -- p` with `AI_AGENT=l4-mcp` and returns its output and exit code

#### SCN-MCP-04 (−) An agent rule still refuses through the server · L4-MCP-002
- **Given** a repository whose base config does not set `clarifier.answer_by_agents`, and an open verdict question
- **When** a client calls `l4_question_answer` for it
- **Then** the CLI refuses it as for any agent, and the tool returns that refusal with `isError: true`

#### SCN-MCP-05 (+) A plan is checked before the push through the server · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** a working tree with a new plan file `multitenancy` and its specs, not pushed
- **When** a client calls `l4_plan_check` with `plan: multitenancy, worktree: true`
- **Then** the server runs `l4 yolo check --worktree -- multitenancy` and returns its findings and order

#### SCN-MCP-06 (+) A stopped unit is debugged through the server · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** a unit that halted on a task
- **When** a client calls `l4_status` with the unit, then `l4_unit_events` with `type: task.attempt_failed`
- **Then** it gets the unit's cause and next step, and the failed attempts with their reasons

#### SCN-MCP-07 (−) Activation is not a tool · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** the running server
- **When** a client lists the tools
- **Then** no tool runs `l4 yolo activate` or `l4 yolo cancel`, and `l4_plan_status`'s description names `l4 yolo activate <plan> --reason "…"` as a person's command

#### SCN-MCP-08 (+) A client is configured and other servers stay · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** a client user configuration file that already lists another MCP server and an entry `l4-shop`
- **When** `l4 mcp install --client <that client> --repo /work/billing` runs
- **Then** the file adds `l4-billing` with the command `l4 mcp serve --repo /work/billing`, and still lists the other server and `l4-shop` unchanged

#### SCN-MCP-09 (−) An unparseable configuration is not overwritten · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** a client configuration file that is not valid JSON (or TOML)
- **When** `l4 mcp install` runs for it
- **Then** it exits 2 naming the file and writes nothing

#### SCN-MCP-10 (+) Two IDE entries serve two repositories · L4-MCP-005
- **Given** two servers configured as `l4 mcp serve --repo /work/shop` and `l4 mcp serve --repo /work/billing`
- **When** a client calls `l4_status` on each
- **Then** each runs in its own repository and its result names that repository

#### SCN-MCP-11 (−) A repository the instance does not serve is refused · L4-MCP-005
- **Given** a server started with `--repo /work/shop --repo /work/billing`
- **When** a client calls `l4_plan_status` with `repo: /etc` or `repo: other`
- **Then** the call is refused with the list of the repositories it serves, and nothing runs

#### SCN-MCP-12 (−) No repository, no guess · L4-MCP-005
- **Given** a server started without `--repo` in a folder that is not a git repository with `.l4/config.yaml`
- **When** a client calls any tool
- **Then** the result is an error that says to start the server with `--repo PATH`

#### SCN-MCP-13 (+) A unit's ledger events are read, filtered and cut · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** a unit whose ledger holds three events of type `task.attempt_failed` and others
- **When** `l4 status --unit U --events --type task.attempt_failed --last 2 --json` runs
- **Then** it prints `l4/events@1` with the newest two of them, `total: 3` and `shown: 2`, redacted, and writes nothing

#### SCN-MCP-14 (+) A unit's verification.md is read from its branch · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** a unit branch on origin that holds `verification.md`
- **When** `l4 status --unit U --verification` runs
- **Then** it prints that file; for a unit without one it says `no verification.md`

#### SCN-MCP-15 (+) A plan that is not pushed is refused without `worktree` and admitted with it · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** a plan file `.l4/plans/p1.json` and its unit folders only in the working tree (the command is L4-YOLO-034's)
- **When** a client calls `l4_plan_check` for `p1` without `worktree`, then with `worktree: true`
- **Then** the first result is an error because origin has no such file; the second prints the order and exits 0, and nothing is recorded

#### SCN-MCP-16 (+) A committed project file serves a worktree a session starts in · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** `l4 mcp install --client claude-code --project` committed its `.mcp.json`, and a git worktree of the repository in which the client's session starts
- **When** the server starts with that file's arguments in the worktree and a tool is called
- **Then** the file holds no absolute path and the result names the worktree

#### SCN-MCP-17 (−) An entry of another repository is not replaced · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** the entry `l4-app` serves `/work/app`
- **When** `l4 mcp install --repo /oss/app` runs
- **Then** it exits 2 naming both paths and `--name`, and writes nothing

#### SCN-MCP-18 (−) A symlink in the repository is not followed · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** a repository that commits `.mcp.json` as a symlink to a file outside it
- **When** `l4 mcp install --client claude-code --project` runs
- **Then** it exits 2 and the file outside is unchanged

#### SCN-MCP-19 (−) A stopped call leaves no descendant running · L4-MCP-002
- **Given** a command whose descendant ignores SIGTERM
- **When** the call times out or is cancelled
- **Then** after the grace period the whole process group is killed, also when the command itself already exited

#### SCN-MCP-20 (+) The protocol is UTF-8 under a non-UTF-8 locale · L4-MCP-001
- **Given** the server started with `LC_ALL=C` and Python's UTF-8 mode off
- **When** a client sends `initialize` and `tools/list`
- **Then** both are answered, as UTF-8, with the `…` of a description intact, and the server does not die

#### SCN-MCP-21 (+) A write tool says what it writes · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** the tool list
- **When** a client reads the description of a write tool
- **Then** it says what it writes, whether it pushes to origin and that CI may be running; `l4_plan_review`'s also says that it costs judge tokens and takes minutes

#### SCN-MCP-22 (+) Progress rises with every notification · L4-MCP-001
- **Given** a call that carries a progress token and runs long enough for several notifications
- **When** the server sends them
- **Then** each `progress` value is greater than the one before

#### SCN-MCP-23 (−) A number that is not finite is refused · L4-MCP-003
- **Given** the running server
- **When** a client calls `l4_plan_resume` with `extend_cost` NaN or infinity
- **Then** the call is an error and nothing runs; `l4 yolo resume --extend-cost=nan` itself exits 2

#### SCN-MCP-24 (+) The printed Claude Code command is shell-quoted · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** a repository whose path holds a space or a quote
- **When** `l4 mcp install --client claude-code` prints its `claude mcp add` line
- **Then** the line, split as a shell splits it, gives the exact `l4 mcp serve --repo <path>` arguments

#### SCN-MCP-25 (+) Instances for different repositories can be told apart · L4-MCP-005
- **Given** two servers, one per repository
- **When** a client reads each `initialize` result and `tools/list`
- **Then** `serverInfo.title`, `instructions` and every tool description name that server's repositories and no other

#### SCN-MCP-26 (−) A file of the repository named like a dependency does not run · L4-MCP-002
- **Given** a repository that holds a `yaml.py` (or `click.py`) whose code writes a marker file
- **When** a client calls `l4_status`
- **Then** the marker is not written: the command ran with `-P`, and the setting is not in the environment of its children

#### SCN-MCP-27 (+) A descendant gets the grace to clean up · L4-MCP-002
- **Given** a call that times out, whose descendant needs one second to clean up after SIGTERM while the command exited at once
- **When** the grace period is longer than that
- **Then** the descendant finishes its cleanup; one that ignores SIGTERM is killed when the grace ends

#### SCN-MCP-28 (+) Cursor's project entry names the workspace folder · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** `l4 mcp install --client cursor --project`
- **When** the file `.cursor/mcp.json` is read
- **Then** its entry runs `l4 mcp serve --repo ${workspaceFolder}`, holds no path of this machine, and a second install is not refused

#### SCN-MCP-29 (−) A Kiro project entry is refused · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** `l4 mcp install --client kiro --project`
- **When** it runs
- **Then** it exits 2 with a hint to use the user scope (`--repo PATH`, one entry per repository), and writes nothing

#### SCN-MCP-30 (+) Codex gets the forge token variable · L4-MCP-004
- **Given** a repository whose `.l4/config.yaml` sets `forge.token_env: MY_FORGE_TOKEN`
- **When** `l4 mcp install --client codex` runs, with a user-listed `env_vars` already in the entry
- **Then** the entry's `env_vars` holds the user's variables and `MY_FORGE_TOKEN`

#### SCN-MCP-31 (−) No progress follows the response · L4-MCP-001
- **Given** a call with a progress token and a very short heartbeat
- **When** the call completes, many times over
- **Then** no progress notification is written after its response

### 23.24 Sandbox isolation (SEC, PRV)

#### SCN-SEC-70 (−) Agent-written tests read no credential of the home · L4-SEC-030
- **Given** a runner home that holds `.git-credentials`, `.netrc`, `.ssh/id_ed25519`, `.config/gh/hosts.yml` and `.docker/config.json`, and a working bwrap
- **When** a gate of a unit runs a command that reads each of them
- **Then** every read fails inside the gate sandbox

#### SCN-SEC-71 (−) An agent sandbox sees its own login and nothing else of the home · L4-SEC-030
- **Given** the home of SCN-SEC-70 plus `~/.claude.json` and `~/.codex/auth.json`, and a claude-code implementer
- **When** a command in its agent sandbox reads every one of these files
- **Then** only `~/.claude.json` is readable

#### SCN-SEC-72 (+) The tmpfs over the home comes before every bind · L4-SEC-030
- **Given** a gate spec and an agent spec whose worktree, temp directory, caches and git common directory all lie under `$HOME`
- **When** the bwrap argv is built
- **Then** `--tmpfs <home>` follows the base flags, and every bind of those paths comes after it

#### SCN-SEC-73 (−) A home of `/` is refused · L4-SEC-030
- **Given** `HOME=/` in the harness environment
- **When** a gate is wrapped in bwrap
- **Then** `SandboxUnavailable` is raised (exit 3) naming `HOME`, and no process starts

#### SCN-SEC-74 (+) A runner cache outside the home is covered and the step's directories come back · L4-SEC-031
- **Given** `L4_CACHE=/var/cache/l4` and a gate spec of a unit in it
- **When** the bwrap argv is built
- **Then** `--tmpfs /var/cache/l4` follows the home's tmpfs, and the worktree, the step's temp directory and each cache mount are bound after it

#### SCN-SEC-75 (−) Another unit's step files and the lock files are not visible · L4-SEC-031
- **Given** a runner cache outside the home with a file in another unit's `agent-tmp`, another project's worktree and a file in `locks/`, and a working bwrap
- **When** a gate and an agent of this unit read them
- **Then** every read fails, while the unit's own worktree and caches are readable

#### SCN-SEC-76 (+) User-local tools are bound read-only · L4-SEC-032
- **Given** a home with `~/.local/bin/uv`, a symlink `~/.local/bin/claude` to `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.288`, `$L4_HOME/npm/node_modules/.bin` on PATH and `~/.local/share/uv/python`
- **When** the agent argv is built
- **Then** `~/.local/bin`, `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.288` (the file, not its directory), `$L4_HOME`, `~/.local/share/uv/python` and the harness's plugin directories are `--ro-bind` entries, `~/.local/share/uv` as a whole is not, and no tool path is bound twice

#### SCN-SEC-77 (−) A tool bind never re-exposes a login · L4-SEC-032
- **Given** a PATH entry `~/.local/share/opencode/bin` and a codex agent spec
- **When** the argv is built
- **Then** that entry is not bound (it lies inside a login path) and is named among the skipped paths, and nothing under `~/.local/share/opencode` is visible

#### SCN-SEC-78 (+) Tools under the home run in both sandbox kinds · L4-SEC-032
- **Given** a working bwrap, a home outside `/tmp` with a script in `~/.local/bin` and a symlinked tool whose target is under `~/.local/share`
- **When** a gate and an agent sandbox run both tools
- **Then** both exit 0 in both kinds

#### SCN-SEC-79 (+) A setup gate reads the registry login, a test gate and an agent do not · L4-SEC-033
- **Given** `sandbox.setup_paths: ["~/.npmrc"]` and an existing `~/.npmrc`
- **When** the argv of a setup gate, a test gate and an agent is built
- **Then** only the setup gate's argv binds `~/.npmrc`, read-only

#### SCN-SEC-80 (−) A tool path inside a login is refused · L4-SEC-033
- **Given** `sandbox.tool_paths: ["~/.codex/bin"]`
- **When** the configuration is loaded
- **Then** loading fails with exit 2 naming `sandbox.tool_paths`, and the message does not contain the path

#### SCN-SEC-81 (−) Two projects with the same unit name share no directory · L4-SEC-034
- **Given** two repositories with different `origin` URLs, one runner cache, and a unit `openspec:add-login` in each
- **When** a workbench is built for each and project A resets its agent temp directory
- **Then** the unit caches, `agent-tmp`, `gate-tmp`, `excludes` and every cache mount differ, and project B's result file is still there

#### SCN-SEC-82 (−) A unit of another project is not handed this project's uv cache · L4-SEC-034
- **Given** project A's unit `add-login` that wrote a file into its uv cache
- **When** project B's unit `add-login` mounts its caches
- **Then** B's uv cache is new (it gets B's seed copy) and does not hold A's file

#### SCN-SEC-83 (−) One project's unpublished run file never reaches another project's lock ref · L4-SEC-034
- **Given** project A kept an unpublished run file of `openspec:add-login`
- **When** project B's run of `openspec:add-login` starts and publishes what is unpublished
- **Then** B's unpublished files are empty and nothing is pushed for A's run

#### SCN-SEC-84 (+) A run file of the earlier layout is adopted only by its own repository · L4-SEC-034
- **Given** two run files in `pending-unpublished/openspec/add-login`, one whose `run.started` records this repository's key and one that records another key, and a clone of this repository that has every commit either file names
- **When** the run starts
- **Then** the first is moved to the keyed directory and published, the second is left in place, and one warning names its directory

#### SCN-SEC-85 (−) A test gate cannot write into the environment · L4-SEC-035
- **Given** a working bwrap and a worktree with `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages` and `node_modules/pkg`
- **When** a test gate writes `zz.pth` into site-packages and changes `node_modules/pkg/index.js`
- **Then** both writes fail, and a setup gate in the same worktree can write both

#### SCN-SEC-86 (+) A uv project's tests run on the read-only environment setup built · L4-SEC-035
- **Given** a working bwrap, uv on PATH and a uv project with no dependencies
- **When** the setup gate runs `uv sync --frozen` and the test gate runs `uv run --frozen python -c "print(1)"`
- **Then** both gates pass and `.venv` was read-only in the test gate

#### SCN-SEC-87 (+) The tool caches start empty and writable in every gate · L4-SEC-035
- **Given** a worktree whose `node_modules/.vite/deps` holds a file from an earlier gate
- **When** the next test gate starts, under bwrap or under `sandbox.mode: none`
- **Then** `node_modules/.vite`, `node_modules/.vite-temp` and `node_modules/.vitest-cache` are empty directories the gate can write, and under bwrap its argv has `--tmpfs` over each after the read-only bind of `node_modules`

#### SCN-SEC-88 (−) A `.pth` planted by a green step does not make green pass · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** a red task whose green step writes only `zz_l4.pth` and a pytest plugin that turns failures into passes into `.venv` site-packages, the production code left a stub
- **When** the green phase runs
- **Then** green fails on the stub, the plant is gone, and `guard.violation{rule: "environment"}` names `zz_l4.pth`

#### SCN-SEC-89 (−) Plants that survive `uv sync --frozen` are removed by the harness · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** uv on PATH, a synced uv project, and `zz_planted.pth` and `sitecustomize.py` written into its site-packages after the manifest
- **When** `uv sync --frozen` runs again, and then the harness compares the environment
- **Then** both files survive the sync, the harness reports both as planted and removes `.venv`, and the next sync builds it without them

#### SCN-SEC-90 (+) A dependency the agent declared is installed again with no violation · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** an agent step that changes `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` and adds a dist whose files its `RECORD` lists with their hashes
- **When** the step ends
- **Then** `env.rebuilt{declared: true}` is recorded, `.venv` is removed, and no `guard.violation` is recorded

#### SCN-SEC-91 (−) Under `sandbox.mode: none` a gate's plant is removed after the gate · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** `sandbox.mode: none`, `sandbox.allow_none: true`, and a test gate whose test writes `sitecustomize.py` into `.venv`
- **When** the gate ends
- **Then** `.venv` is removed, `guard.violation{phase: "gate", rule: "environment"}` names the file, and `setup_at` is cleared, so no later gate runs on the planted environment: the next `run_setup` builds it again, and a gate before that runs without it and fails rather than passes

#### SCN-SEC-92 (−) A changed installed package is removed with `node_modules` · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** an agent step that edits `node_modules/vitest/dist/index.js` and changes no package manifest or lock file
- **When** the step ends
- **Then** `node_modules` is removed, and `guard.violation` names `node_modules/vitest/dist/index.js`

#### SCN-SEC-93 (−) An environment a gate created is not left for the next gate · L4-SEC-036
- **Given** `gates.setup: []` and a test gate whose command creates `.venv`
- **When** the gate ends
- **Then** `.venv` is removed with `env.rebuilt{reason: "created"}`

#### SCN-SEC-94 (−) The verifier never runs on the implementer's environment · L4-SEC-037
- **Given** a worktree whose `.venv` an implementer workbench built, with a file added to it after its manifest
- **When** the verifier's workbench runs `gates.setup`
- **Then** `.venv` is removed first with `env.rebuilt{reason: "unverified"}` and built again, without the file

#### SCN-SEC-95 (+) The first setup in a fresh worktree removes nothing · L4-SEC-037
- **Given** a new worktree with no environment directory
- **When** the implementer's first `gates.setup` runs
- **Then** no `env.rebuilt` is recorded and the manifest is taken after the setup

#### SCN-SEC-96 (−) A readable canary fails the check · L4-SEC-038
- **Given** a fake runner whose agent sandbox reports the home canary readable
- **When** `SANDBOX-003` runs
- **Then** it fails naming the canary path and `agent`, prints no canary content, and no canary is left on disk

#### SCN-SEC-97 (+) The real argv passes the check · L4-SEC-038
- **Given** a Linux runner with a working bwrap
- **When** `l4 doctor` runs `SANDBOX-003`
- **Then** it passes and no canary is left on disk

#### SCN-SEC-98 (+) The check is skipped without a bwrap sandbox · L4-SEC-038
- **Given** `sandbox.mode: none` with `sandbox.allow_none: true`
- **When** `SANDBOX-003` runs
- **Then** it is skipped with a reason that names the mode

#### SCN-SEC-99 (−) The login and unit lock files are not readable in any sandbox · L4-SEC-031
- **Given** the login lock file of `l4.agents.gate.lock_root` and the unit lock file of `UnitNames.flock_path`, both existing, a runner cache under the home and one outside it, and the gate and agent specs of a unit of any adapter
- **When** the bwrap argv is built (and, with a working bwrap, a command in each sandbox kind reads both files)
- **Then** neither file is visible at its path in either kind, and the login lock directory lies under no adapter's credential path

#### SCN-SEC-100 (−) In a GitHub job the gates get the CI's flags and the agents do not · L4-SEC-040, L4-SEC-001
- **Given** a harness environment with `CI=true`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, `FORCE_COLOR=1`, `PY_COLORS=1`,
  `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `RUNNER_TEMP` and `CI_JOB_TOKEN`
- **When** a gate and an agent step are started
- **Then** the gate's environment has `CI=true` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` and none of the other seven; the agent's has
  neither flag; `run.started` has `gate_env_ci: ["CI", "GITHUB_ACTIONS"]`

#### SCN-SEC-101 (−) A test that only CI fails now fails in the unit's gate · L4-SEC-040
- **Given** a unit whose test of a command's help text fails when `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set and passes otherwise
- **When** its test gate runs in a GitHub job, and again on a person's machine with no CI variable
- **Then** the gate fails in the job, as the repository's CI does, and passes on the machine as before

#### SCN-SEC-102 (−) A value that is not a short word is not passed and is named · L4-SEC-040
- **Given** a job with `CI=true`, `GITLAB_CI` set to a 40-character token, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=/tmp/x` and a third case with
  `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true\n` (a trailing newline)
- **When** `l4 run` starts and a gate runs
- **Then** the gate's environment has `CI=true` and none of the refused names, and the run's log has the WARNING once
  for each refused name, without any value

#### SCN-SEC-103 (+) Outside CI nothing changes, CI=true opts in, and no colour variable is ever passed · L4-SEC-040
- **Given** a person's shell with `CLICOLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=1`, and no `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` or `GITLAB_CI`
- **When** a gate runs, and again with `CI=true` set in that shell
- **Then** the first gate's environment is the 0.4.20 environment, with no `gate_env_ci`; the second has `CI=true` and
  neither `CLICOLOR` nor `FORCE_COLOR`, `run.started` has `gate_env_ci: ["CI"]`, and the run logs the INFO line once

#### SCN-SEC-104 (+) A test gate loads a Vite configuration · L4-SEC-035
- **Given** a worktree whose `node_modules` holds no `.vite-temp`
- **When** a test gate under bwrap runs a command that creates `node_modules/.vite-temp/x.mjs`, as Vite does when it bundles a TypeScript configuration
- **Then** the command succeeds, the gate's argv has `--tmpfs <worktree>/node_modules/.vite-temp` after the read-only bind of `node_modules`, and after the gate the real `node_modules/.vite-temp` is an empty directory

#### SCN-SEC-105 (+) A test gate writes Vitest's module cache · L4-SEC-035
- **Given** a worktree whose `node_modules` holds no `.vitest-cache`
- **When** a test gate under bwrap runs a command that creates `node_modules/.vitest-cache/<key>`, as Vitest 5 does with its default module cache, and an agent step later writes a file into `node_modules/.vitest-cache`
- **Then** the command succeeds, the gate's argv has `--tmpfs <worktree>/node_modules/.vitest-cache` after the read-only bind of `node_modules`, after the gate the real `node_modules/.vitest-cache` is an empty directory, and the environment check after the agent step reports no `guard.violation` and no `env.rebuilt`

#### SCN-SEC-106 (+) The post-merge check empties the tool caches after a fresh install · L4-SEC-035, L4-YOLO-009
- **Given** a profile whose setup gate creates `node_modules` with a stale `.vite` entry and a symlink at `.vitest-cache`
- **When** the next gate runs
- **Then** the four tool caches are real empty directories, the symlink's target is untouched and the profile passes

#### SCN-SEC-107 (−) A local run on a host without a sandbox touches nothing · L4-SEC-041
- **Given** a plan whose current unit is U, `sandbox.mode: bwrap` and a machine where no sandbox can be selected, outside a CI job
- **When** `l4 run --unit U` runs
- **Then** it exits 3 before any lease, worktree, ledger line, follow-up, ref refresh or plan event, and the plan is not stopped

#### SCN-SEC-108 (+) The macOS refusal names the ways out · L4-SEC-041
- **Given** the same run on macOS
- **When** it refuses
- **Then** the message names a Linux machine or VM with bubblewrap, `l4 ci start` (and `l4 retry` for a halted or escalated unit)
  and `sandbox.mode: container` once it exists, and the refused command (`l4 run`); on Linux the bubblewrap hint stays

#### SCN-SEC-109 (+) `l4 verify` refuses the same way · L4-SEC-041
- **Given** a machine where no sandbox can be selected, outside a CI job
- **When** `l4 verify --unit U` runs
- **Then** it exits 3 before it reads the unit, with a message that names `l4 verify`; `sandbox.mode: none` with `allow_none`
  runs, and `CI=true` alone does not exempt the run

#### SCN-SEC-110 (−) Red cannot hide a return in a pre-existing test · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** a pre-existing `tests/test_a.py::test_existing` and a red step that adds `# coding: utf-7` as line 1 and
  `  # +AAo-    return` to a line of `test_existing`, plus a new failing test
- **When** the step ends
- **Then** `tests/test_a.py` is put back, `guard.violation{rule: "python encoding"}` is recorded and the attempt fails with
  the advice

#### SCN-SEC-111 (−) Green cannot hide code in a product file · L4-SEC-042
- **When** a green step writes `src/app/x.py` with a `# coding: utf-7` cookie
- **Then** the file is put back (removed, as it is new) and the attempt fails, as in SCN-SEC-110; so does a fix chore, a
  refactor, a test chore and a replayed held step

#### SCN-SEC-112 (−) The verifier blocks such a file from anyone · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** the unit's diff adds `# coding: utf-7` to `tests/test_a.py` in a person's commit
- **When** the integrity checks run
- **Then** a blocker in the row `python encoding` names `tests/test_a.py: utf-7` and the fix; a commit of the harness or of
  a unit step blocks the same way

#### SCN-SEC-113 (+) UTF-8 files are unaffected · L4-SEC-042
- **When** a step writes a file with no cookie, with `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-`, with `# coding: ascii`, or with a
  byte-order mark
- **Then** nothing is put back and the verifier reports nothing

#### SCN-SEC-114 (+) A non-Python file is unaffected · L4-SEC-042
- **When** a step writes `docs/a.md` whose first line reads `# coding: utf-7`
- **Then** nothing is put back and the verifier reports nothing

#### SCN-SEC-115 (−) Padding over a size limit does not hide a cookie · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** a step that writes SCN-SEC-110's test file padded to more than 8 MiB, or a file whose first line is a comment of
  9 MiB followed by `# coding: utf-7` on line 2
- **When** the guard and the verifier run
- **Then** the first file is put back as `utf-7` and the second as `unreadable`, and the verifier reports both (neither
  file is read whole or skipped); a file whose long first line is code is not a violation

#### SCN-SEC-116 (−) A link to a cookie file is followed · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** `pkg/x.py` is a link to `notes.txt`, which holds `# coding: utf-7` and hidden code, and the step adds both; or
  the link is in the base and the step only changes `notes.txt`; or the link goes through another link or a linked
  directory
- **When** the guard and the verifier run
- **Then** the changed paths of the chain and the file are put back, one `guard.violation` each whose `why` names the link
  and the file, and the verifier reports `pkg/x.py: utf-7 (link to pkg/notes.txt)`; a touched Python-named link that ends
  at no regular file of the tree is reported as `pkg/x.py: link that cannot be checked`, also when its target was deleted,
  was renamed (case only too), has several folded matches, or when only a link of the chain changed. A link that names
  `NOTES.txt` while git tracks `notes.txt` finds it on a case-insensitive file system, at the guard (by identity) and at
  the verifier (by folded name; a literal regular target wins over a folded twin). A dangling, directory or loop link is
  not followed by the guard: it cannot hide source

#### SCN-SEC-117 (−) The test writer refuses a cookie · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** a reply whose code is `# coding: utf-7` and a test with a hidden `return`
- **When** the writer checks the reply (audit or e2e)
- **Then** the reply is invalid with the reason `the test declares the encoding utf-7; write UTF-8 without a coding
  cookie`, and `write_test_file` raises instead of writing the file

#### SCN-SEC-118 (−) Names that are not UTF-8 stay distinct · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** `a.py` is a link to `\xff.txt` (a utf-7 file) next to a clean file named U+FFFD, or `test_\xfe.py` (utf-7) and
  `test_\xff.py` (clean) in one commit
- **When** the verifier runs
- **Then** the link is resolved to `\xff.txt` and `test_\xfe.py` is checked and reported; neither is merged with the other
  name, and a name is shown with its invalid bytes as `\xNN`

#### SCN-SEC-119 (−) A file the guard cannot open is put back · L4-SEC-042
- **Given** a step writes a utf-7 test into a directory without read permission
- **When** the guard runs
- **Then** the file is put back as `unreadable` and recorded; a directory, a link and a missing file give no verdict

#### SCN-SEC-120 (+) A `.gitattributes` file at any depth is a protected path · L4-SEC-004
- **Given** the paths `.gitattributes`, `src/.gitattributes`, `web/app/.gitattributes` and `.GitAttributes`, and the lookalikes
  `.gitattributes.bak`, `docs/gitattributes.md` and `src/x.gitattributes`
- **When** the protected-path rules match them
- **Then** each of the first four is protected by `**/.gitattributes` (any case), and no lookalike is

#### SCN-SEC-121 (−) An agent's `.gitattributes` is put back, also behind an edited `.gitignore` · L4-SEC-004
- **Given** a step that writes `.gitattributes` (`*.py -diff`) and `src/.gitattributes`, and one that also adds `.gitattributes`
  to `.gitignore`
- **When** the protected-path guard runs
- **Then** both files are removed with `guard.violation{rule: "**/.gitattributes", action: removed}`, a production change of the
  same step stays, and the root file is removed although the edited `.gitignore` names it

#### SCN-PRV-100 (−) A unit's key files are not readable from another unit's sandboxes · L4-PRV-040
- **Given** a working bwrap, unit A's provider key file and credential-loader file written by the real `write_key_file` and `write_credential_file` into A's private directory, and unit B of the same project
- **When** a gate and an agent sandbox of unit B read both files
- **Then** every read fails, and the files hold their values on the host

#### SCN-PRV-101 (+) The private directory is 0700 and the key file is gone after the step · L4-PRV-040
- **Given** an opencode profile with a custom provider and a fake process runner
- **When** an agent step runs once to an end and once to an exception
- **Then** during the run the private directory and `opencode-config` are 0700 and the key file is 0600, and after each run no key file and no credential file is left

#### SCN-PRV-102 (−) A key file left by a killed run is gone before the next step · L4-PRV-041
- **Given** `agent-tmp/opencode-config/provider.key` and `agent-tmp/credential` left in a unit's directory
- **When** the next run builds the unit's workbench
- **Then** both files are gone before the first gate or agent step

#### SCN-PRV-103 (−) The hello's key directory is hidden from every sandbox · L4-PRV-041
- **Given** a probe context whose working directory is the runner cache, and a gate spec of any unit
- **When** the hello writes its key and the gate argv is built
- **Then** the key's directory is under the runner cache, has mode 0700, and the argv covers the runner cache with a tmpfs and binds nothing above or at that directory

#### SCN-PRV-104 (+) A run that ends normally leaves nothing for the next workbench to remove · L4-PRV-041
- **Given** an opencode agent step with a provider key that ended normally
- **When** the unit's next workbench is built
- **Then** no key file or credential file was there to remove, and the private directory exists with mode 0700

#### SCN-PRV-105 (+) Doctor warns while setup_paths is set · L4-SEC-033
- **Given** `sandbox.setup_paths: ["~/.npmrc"]`, with or without bwrap on the machine
- **When** doctor runs

### 23.28 GitHub Copilot CLI (FAC, PRV, OCG)

Scenarios SCN-FAC-22 to SCN-FAC-51, SCN-PRV-129 to SCN-PRV-140 and SCN-OCG-15 to SCN-OCG-16 (change 67, `copilot-cli`). The adapter scenarios run on a recording process runner and the recorded streams under `tests/fixtures/recorded/copilot-cli/1.0.102-byok/`, `1.0.102-firstcalls/` and `1.0.102-notoken/`; a `Fetcher` serves the tarballs. No scenario needs a token or the network, except SCN-FAC-49, which is the release gate of L4-FAC-022.

#### SCN-FAC-22 (+) Every Copilot run has the common argv, its prompt on stdin and a private home · L4-FAC-013
- **Given** a `copilot-cli` profile with `model: claude-sonnet-5.5` and an implement-mode request with a preset session
  id, run with a recording process runner
- **When** the adapter runs it
- **Then** the argv after the executable starts with the common flags of this requirement in that order, with that
  session id and `--model claude-sonnet-5.5`, the runner's `stdin` is the prompt and no argv entry holds it
- **And** the environment's `COPILOT_HOME` is `<step>/copilot-home`, which holds exactly `settings.json` with the four
  keys, the environment has `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` and `XDG_CACHE_HOME=<step>/xdg-cache`, and
  `<step>/xdg-cache/copilot/pkg` is a link to `<L4 home>/copilot-cache/copilot/pkg`
- **And** a file left in `<step>/xdg-cache` by an earlier run is gone

- **When** a judge call is made for each
- **Then** each argv holds `--model auto` and no adapter error is raised

### 23.29 OpenCode v2 (OCV)

Scenarios SCN-OCV-01 to SCN-OCV-28 (change 68, `opencode-v2`). They run on the recorded v2 outputs under `tests/fixtures/recorded/opencode/2.0.32/` and on fake process runners. No scenario starts an `opencode` or `opencode2` binary, needs a key or reaches the network. Each [U] row of L4-OCV-013 that has code (every row but U8, whose fallback is a rule for the operator) has a test that pins its fallback by name. No scenario here has been checked against a live run (design E8).

#### SCN-OCV-25 (−) An unrecorded provider form stays refused · L4-OCV-013
- **Given** no recorded v2 run with a custom provider key file
- **When** a `cli_major: 2` profile sets `options.provider`
- **Then** the configuration is refused with the `provider_refused` message

#### SCN-OCV-26 (+) The v2 adapter is announced as experimental · L4-OCV-013
- **Given** a role chain whose selected profile is `cli_major: 2`
- **When** it is selected twice in one run
- **Then** one `agent.experimental` event names the profile

#### SCN-OCV-27 (−) A v2 profile in roles.delegate is refused at load · L4-OCV-014
- **Given** `roles.delegate: [oc2]` where `oc2` is an `opencode` profile with `options.cli_major: 2`, and the same
  profile in `roles.judges`
- **When** the configuration loads, and separately when the v2 adapter is given a read-only request
- **Then** the load fails with the L4-OCV-014 message naming `oc2`; without `oc2` in `roles.delegate` it loads; the
  read-only request raises `AdapterError` and no process starts

#### SCN-OCV-28 (−) ci.cli_versions holds opencode2 at major 2 only · L4-OCV-002
- **Given** `ci.cli_versions: {opencode2: "2.0.32"}`, and another configuration with `{opencode2: "1.18.34"}`
- **When** each configuration loads
- **Then** the first loads and `opencode2`'s effective pin is `2.0.32` from `ci.cli_versions`, and the second is a
  configuration error naming OpenCode 1 and L4-OCV-002

## 24. Definition of done

### 24.1 For each delivery change of this repository (§21)

A change is done when **all** of the following hold — checked by the change's own `tasks.md` and by an independent
reviewer of a **different vendor** than the implementer (a third vendor is always reachable through OpenRouter) before
it is archived:

1. Every requirement the change touches has passing automated tests, and every scenario of §23 mapped to the change
   in `tests/scenario_matrix.yaml` is automated and passing.
2. Tests were written first (red commit before green commit per task), and no pre-existing test was weakened.
3. `ruff`, `mypy --strict` on `src/`, and the full test suite pass on Linux in CI (unit tests also on macOS).
4. Public interfaces (CLI flags, config keys, schemas, file formats) match this SPEC exactly; deviations are
   amended in SPEC.md in the same change.
5. Documentation for users (README sections, `l4 --help` text) is updated.
6. `openspec validate <change> --strict` passes and the change is archived.
7. No `[U]` fact the change depends on remains unverified (spike report, contract test or doctor live check).

### 24.2 For the harness v1 release

1. All changes 0–13 of §21 are done (24.1).
2. All built-in simulation scenarios (§17) pass on Linux.
3. The live test (§20.4) passes end to end on the reference GitLab (17.5.2 CE, runner `l4-runner`) **and** on a
   GitHub repository.
4. The success criteria of §25 are measured and met (or explicitly waived by the maintainer with a reason recorded in
   `docs/decisions.md`).
5. `l4 init` + `l4 doctor` succeed on the three fixture stacks of §25 (Python/uv, Node/TypeScript + Playwright, Go).
6. A tagged release `v1.0.0` exists and `uvx --from git+<repo>@<sha of v1.0.0> l4 --version` works on a clean runner.

### 24.3 For a unit processed by the harness (what "done" means in a target repository)

The harness may move a unit to `in_review` only when the **evidence package** shows:

1. Intake passed (spec valid strict, criteria present, oracle configured, no forbidden paths).
2. Every non-optional task is `[x]`, with a red→green commit pair, a recorded human-tagged exemption, or a
   `pre_adoption` mark.
3. Verdict PASS from the deterministic aggregation (§10.4): all gates green; non-vacuous tests; every criterion passed
   by discriminating, adequate evidence **or accepted by a named human** (listed with who and why; judgment-only
   passes exist only when traceability is switched off and are listed explicitly); no blocker/major finding open.
4. All questions answered or dismissed, with who answered (human / clarifier) visible.
5. Fix units (if any) verified; the repository's own CI green on the hand-off head.
6. `verification.md` lists profiles used and every fallback, cost, guard events, exemptions, and links to artifacts.
7. Nothing was pushed outside the unit branch, its WIP branch, its lock ref, its verified tags, and the harness's own
   PR branches (bootstrap unit, post-merge archive PR).

With the default `post_merge_pr` mode the human merge of the code PR is the sign-off and the archive follows in a
harness PR (L4-ARC-007); with `on_approval` the unit reaches `archived` only after a member's approval (L4-ARC-001).
The human merge is the final gate for code; the harness never merges code under `merge_policy: human`.

## 25. Success criteria (measurable)

Targets are proposals for the maintainer to confirm; each has a measurement method. Benchmarks that judge the verifier
use defects and correct units **written by someone other than the implementers of the harness** (a person, or an agent
of a different vendor working only from a defect catalogue), so the system under test is never its own oracle.
Statistical bounds use the rule of three (0 failures in n ⇒ the true rate is below 3/n at 95 % confidence).

| ID | Criterion | Target | How measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC-01 | Scenario coverage of the spec | 100 % of MUST requirements have ≥ 1 scenario; 100 % of scenarios automated; every Then-clause phase and exit code consistent with §12.0/§2.2 | `scripts/check_spec.py` + `tests/scenario_matrix.yaml` |
| SC-02 | Simulation suite | 100 % pass, deterministic across 2 runs | harness CI |
| SC-03 | **False PASS rate** (most important) | 0 of ≥ 20 on the tampering subset (deleted/skipped/weakened tests, result-forcing hooks, gate-config weakening, vacuous or import-only tests, over-tagged tests) ⇒ < 15 % at 95 %; ≤ 1 of ≥ 60 overall | Seeded-defect benchmark: ≥ 60 units with known defects (also unmet criteria, flaky tests, secrets, out-of-scope changes, UI defects only Playwright catches) |
| SC-04 | False FAIL rate | ≤ 15 % | ≥ 30 correct units in the same benchmark |
| SC-05 | Autonomy on the live benchmark | ≥ 70 % of units reach `in_review` with no human action other than answering `product` questions; mean human touches per unit ≤ 1.5, where a touch = one human commit or label (verdict questions count) | live benchmark of ≥ 10 units, chosen **before** the run, on the reference GitLab and GitHub repos |
| SC-06 | Fallback correctness | 100 % of quota/limit situations select the next usable profile without spending a request on the exhausted one, and log it | SCN-AVL-02/08/09/11/12/16 + live test with Codex excluded via `min_remaining_percent: 101` |
| SC-07 | Restartability | 100 % of 20 random SIGKILL points resume with no lost task, no duplicate commit, no double-applied marker | chaos simulation `crash-mid-task-resume` parameterised over kill points |
| SC-08 | Loop safety | 0 runaway loops: every halted unit stops within the configured budgets | budget scenarios + live benchmark ledger audit |
| SC-09 | Safety | 0 pushes outside the allowed refs (§24.3-7); 0 secrets in committed files or logs | fake-forge assertions; gitleaks over the test artifacts |
| SC-10 | Portability | `l4 init` → green `l4 doctor` in ≤ 10 minutes per fixture stack (Python/uv, Node/TS + Playwright, Go), without editing harness code | timed run on clean Linux runners |
| SC-11 | Overhead | harness overhead ≤ 5 % of unit wall time; probe spend ≤ $0.05 per run | ledger timings and costs from the live benchmark |
| SC-12 | Comprehension | a person who did not build the harness answers 5 standard questions ("phase? what blocks it? who answered Q-2? why did round 1 fail? what did it cost?") correctly for 5 live units from the unit folder alone | blind review |
| SC-13 | Clarifier auto-accept precision | ≥ 95 % of auto-accepted answers judged correct by a human; 100 % of auto-accepts audited during the live benchmark | live benchmark audit |
| SC-14 | False NEEDS_HUMAN rate | ≤ 25 % of correct units reach `awaiting_human` because of verifier disputes | correct-unit benchmark |
| SC-15 | Cost and time per unit | median and p90 USD per unit and time from spec merge to `in_review` reported; targets set after the first baseline run | ledger |
| SC-16 | S1 calibration | Laya accuracy and expected calibration error on the harness's own labelled verdicts reported per release; auto-accept stays disabled for a repo while ECE > 0.1 | `laya-evals` over `s1-calibration.jsonl` |
| SC-17 | Lessons work | the rate of findings repeating an existing lesson's dedupe key falls between the first and second half of the live benchmark | ledger + lessons |

## 26. Spec self-consistency rules

1. Every `L4-*` requirement with MUST/MUST NOT is referenced by ≥ 1 scenario in §23 (SC-01).
2. Every config key referenced anywhere in this document exists in §3.2 (the schema is generated from §3.2's
   reference configuration and unknown keys are errors).
3. Every state named anywhere appears in the lifecycle of architecture §6 and in `l4/state@1`.
4. Every exit code used anywhere is in §2.2, and every phase or exit code named in a scenario's Then-clause matches
   the §12.0 table (checked by `scripts/check_spec.py`).
5. Changes to this document go through an OpenSpec change of this repository once change 1 lands.
